title: Our National treasure.
text: The National Art Theatre is one of the historical tour destination in Lagos. It is an ideal tourist destination for Private and Group tours. It is educative for the children and it is a place of history and an architectural master piece.

title: Great Picnic Atmosphere
text: Went picnicking and met quite a large number of other people out there with the same intention as ours. Didn't have access to the Art Gallery but the front view art work made a tremendous piece of great background for some nice pictures!

title: Beautiful Landscape
text:
Why bother going into the half functioning theater when there is enough beauty on the outside? The sculptures, the trees, the carvings on the walls, the architecture, the lakes, the submerged bridges, and roads, the lawns, the thick bushes, the horses, the picnickers, etc.

I did see a play there (Altine's Wrath) and it was thrilling. If there isn't a performance going on, just walk around the premises, it's relaxing. Or pack a picnic basket and find a quiet corner with your gang. Lovely place! (And they wanted to sell it off for a mall).

title: great building
text: i enjoyed the two hours there. looks as if the place is being fixed up. impressed at the lack of litter. gardens are pretty and the saying "far from the maddening crowed" is so true.. very piecefull... will be back

title: Nothing for 100 Naira
text:
We could not go into the theatre because a politician was there. We could only enter to a gallery which had very poor exibition. None of our questions about the pictures were answered, the same information was told us about them that we read next to the pictures. The worst gallery ecperience I have ever had.
1000 naira/person were charged for admission, we got no receit. Probably this was the same pocket support we had to give to some policemen and immigration officers.

title: NATIONAL ART THEATRE
text: The National Arts Theatre is the primary centre for the performing arts in Nigeria. The monument is located in Iganmu, Lagos State. Construction was completed in 1976 in preparation for the Festival of Arts and Culture in 1977.Between 1975, and July 2009, the National Theatre has been managed by six successive Administrators. In August 2009, a new General Manager assumed the headship of the National Theatre Management with a new vision.

title: Iconic Landmark in Lagos State
text: This Landmark is  embodied with so much history, being the first place Nigeria celebrated the biggest Tourism event, Festival of Arts and Culture in 1977 (FESTAC77). Built by a Bulgarian company and today its still use for a lot of cultural activities and events.

title: Coming Back
text:
I was happy to see that stage plays are coming back and people are embracing the idea.

It will be nice to make the National Theater environment more attrative to encourage turm out for activities held at that venue

title: The African Art Lives On
text: i was there watching the Musical Concert the atmosphere is great enough car park for everyone and its free also European dishes for breakfast/Lunch /Dinner ..Adequate security Personal for every one in the Theater and very clean and spacious Bathroom for ladies and Gentlemen .it must see

title: memory re-enact
text: it is one place a like going. it creates a warm welcome for people who history, culture and arts. I hope the management of the theatre would work on retouching some fading wall paints at the exterior.

title: What a waste of a beautiful and priceless treasure
text: Everything that should make a place great fun is there.  The movie theatre, arts theatre, artifacts, spaces for restaurants and eateries etc etc.  But corruption reigns supreme and the place is run down by the government people handling things.  My heart bled when I discovered the National Arts Theatre - what corruption can destroy.

title: nice place
text: This is one of the landmarks in Lagos State, a very prominent structure in the heart of the city. Well maintained but is neglected by people. also has cultural museum near by.

title: National Theatre built like a General's Hat
text: The National Theatre is one of Africa's greatest Landmarks rumored to be built like a General Ibrahim Babaginda's Hat. It is supposed to host plays, musical shows and cultural events, unfortunately, it is a relic, it has been neglected and the MUSON Centre now play's the roles the National Theatre ought to play. To me, it is more like an artifact, and I hope it isrejuvinated.

title: Neglected Masterpiece
text: This is one of Africa's best cultural and entertainment masterpieces.  The space and the idea behind the construction is amazing.  But equally amazing is the level of neglect this edifice has been subjected to.  Stinking corruption and mindless selfishness of those under whose care the facility is left is confounding.  It just takes one purposeful leader with integrity to restore the glory of Africa that is the National Arts Theatre.

title: Master piece nice place to visit
text:
This is a place for entertainment. It is well design to accommodate different forms of entertainment. Many school groups, cultural troops, dance groups etc come here for entertainment and presentation for international visitors ensure you have a guide and stick to your tour schedule and group so that you do not get missing.
Many years ago(1978) as a student of Queens college Yaba Lagos, we came for a musical concert here and I lost my group. It took three concerned vigilant older men to redirect me to my group. Thanks to my school uniform too

title: Haggling for unique hand crafted items to remember my trip
text: Elegushi International market is vibrant market place with hand made , baskets, wood carvings, unique art and paintings. A variety of African jewelry, figurines, leather goods and clothing  are available. Prices are negotiable.

title: Nigerian Market Shopping
text: Very good experience! Left with bags full of momentous including clothing, placements, fans, leather clutches  jewelry, etc….. Prices were beyond reasonable. It was hot so buy a handful of colorful fans upon arrival and use one to try and keep cool. I wish I could have returned another day without my children for more targeted shopping. Beautiful artwork and carvings but no room in suitcases to bring home. Felt safe and it was an amazing outing!

title: To buy pieces of Art and crafts
text: It's one of the most authentic art and craft market in Africa! It is a great place to visit. Very reasonable prices.

title: Lots to browse through
text: It was wonderful to see items being handmade right before your very eyes. Pride is put into their work.

title: Neat and budget friendly
text: The market has almost everything..The market is neat,farm produce are fresh and budget friendly.one of the best!

title: Art and Clothing
text: Great safe place to stop and shop while in lagos. TIP- never accept the first offer haggle haggle haggle! They will eventually sell to you

title: Vacation
text: A sight to behold, the spot and the attendant were quite accommodating and courteous. I can't wait to visit again

title: Sight seeing
text: It’s an open market for crafts and arts.. it’s totally free just get your purse ready to buy pieces you will love to keep..

title: Business
text: Simply best of the rest, absolutely wow and a wow, would be referring u here cos its just a safe place

title: Best Market for Gifts for your foreigner Visitors
text: The market provides you with options of items to buy for your visitors from other countries. It offers several ranges of arts, clothing and accessories that will make your visitor show off to their friends of their visit to Nigeria. The prices are appropriate, the place is clean and secure.

title: Très grand marché
text: On trouve de tout reste à faire quelque kilomètres pour trouver quel que chose, j ai recherché le marché chinois, mais j ai pas trouvé

title: Best of Art and Craft
text: I was at the market for 2hrs, brought all of great and valuable Art and Craft. So, many lovely collections at different store. But you need to know how bargain out here.

title: faszinierender afrikanischer (Handwerks-) Kunst-, Gebrauchsartikel- und Souveniermarkt
text: Sehr umfassendes und faszinierendes Angebot an afrikanischen Kunst- und Handwerksartikeln. Von Schmuck zu Schnitzereien, Korbwaren, Bildern, Stoffen und Taschen..... ein nicht endend wollendes Angebot. Unbedingt zu empfehlen. Handel nach afrikanischer Tradition ist ein muss....

title: buy all food items
text: get all food items here and be satisfied with what ever you buy there. It is sure you will get things there

title: A treasure Trove
text:
I visited thearket to purchase Afeican prints but I was blown away by the amazing choice of treasur there
Canons were there!Beads,paintings,sculptures, semi precious stones,antiques,african vintage material,its definitely a place I will always go back to.

title: Arts, crafts and paintings
text:
Nice market to purchase arts, crafts and paintings. 

Watch out though, you would need to haggle to get a fair price for your purchase. 

Negatives: After a while, you notice that almost everyone is selling similar stuff so getting something unique might be rare. 

It rained earlier the day we went so the roads into the market were largely inaccessible.

Overall, good place.

title: Intersting Hidden Gem
text:
Lovely art Market, with just about anything in art and craft you are looking for. Shame the access road is so bad, but once you do arrive, you are greeted with endless rows of creative designs in clothing, furniture, home decorations, etc.
Good prices too. Be prepared for a good haggle, as initial asking process tend to be inflated 150%. A good guide is the cut the price in 3 and work your way up from there. But good  hidden gems if you take the time to look. I love my trips  here.

title: Art & Craft Market
text: You get to access lovely arts and craft and you must also be smart when bargaining cos the sellers intend to inflate the prices assuming everyone that comes to patronise is a tourist.

title: great day out
text: great art market with wonderful paintings,sculptural and handcraft pieces if you know what you're   looking for

title: El primer museo del país para dar voz a las etnias que se encontraban en él.
text: Aquí podemos encontrar las famosas máscaras Gueledé muy logradas, sin ser las mejores de una cultura que debería tener una colección propia y una serie de ilustraciones de sociedades secretas muy representativas de lo que es el vudú en Benín. Sin ir más lejos, más allá de la leyenda, el considerado fundador de Porto Novo es el creador de la sociedad secreta de Zangbetos que aquí aparece.

title: Buen guia y muy interesante
text: Este museo nos ha parecido un museo ilustrativo de las etnias africanas y de sus costumbres y la explicación del guia fue bastante buena.

title: Peu de moyens, peu d'objets
text:
Le Musée, dont l'entrée est gratuite (!) est abrité dans une jolie bâtisse coloniale qui vaut en elle-même le détour mais les collections sont tout de même assez décevantes : de malheureux objets posées sans arrangement et couverts de poussière (le manque de moyens n'empêche pas de dépoussiérer de temps en temps, surtout que les touristes ne se bousculent pas...). Certains objets n'ont rien d'authentiques et ne valent pas mieux que ceux que l'on voit sur les marchés. 
À la fin de la visite on vous mène vers un petit local où quelques tissus de coton tissé sont en vente, le tout présenté par un enfant (en semaine y a pas école?!)
Bref, malgré les efforts de notre guide de bonne volonté, la pauvreté du projet saute aux yeux. Dommage car il y aurait tant à faire!

title: Free, wonderful guide, nice short stop.
text: Very knowledgeable and friendly guide. Museum has moderate content but provide very interesting information about history and tradition.

title: Disappointing
text: A few masks, a few stories, nice building. We came with natural hunger to learn about the various tribes in the country, and met a small, rundown, neglected set of masks and a bit more. So disappointing ,

title: Benin historiamuseo Porto-Novossa
text:
Kohde sijaitsee Porto-Novon keskustassa. 

Isohko rakennus, jossa kaksi kerrosta museon käytössä. Ilmainen sisäänpääsy (vapaaehtoinen maksu oppaalle) sisälsi käyntimme aikana ranskankielisen oppaan, joka opasti läpi museon. 

Jos ranskankieli ei suju on heillä tarjota englanninkielinen kirjanen oppaaksi kierrokselle. 

Naamioita, mallinukkeja, päähineitä, käyttöesineitä...

Jos kaupungissa vierailet on kohde toki käytävä katsastamassa mutta mitenkään järisyttävän hyvä kokemus ei ole kyseessä. Toki saat paremman kuvan kohdemaasta. 

Sisäpihalla kangaspuut, joilla valmistettuja kankaita mahdollista ostaa muutamalla eurolla.

Kuvaaminen kielletty sisätiloissa. 

Pieni osa näyttelyesineistä omasi englanninkielisen kuvauksen. Kirjassa kohteet oli kaikki englanniksi lueteltu. 

Ei lapsiystävällinen.

title: musee ethnographique de porto_novo benin
text: situe en pleine ville de porto_novo au benin,le musee ethnographique de porto_novo est la deuxieme musee de porto_novo apres le musee honmè.il accueille beaucoup de tourisques et visiteurs tous les jours

title: Quirky and interesting
text: We walked in and found an excellent guide that took us around the museum. Fascinating collection and great overview of Benin, the history and culture. Definitely the best musuem in Porto Novo and on my top 5 for Benin.

title: A place to learn about the people of Benin republic
text:
This is a good idea and when I bring people on a trip with Anago Osho Adventures, the first thing I do is to make the tourists learn about the different culture and way of life of the environment people.

The museum is rich with information but the management need to promote the place more for everyone to benefit from the rare collections.

title: Interesting history and museum
text: This museum is simple but provides an interesting history of Benin. Our guide spoke English and was helpful, but there was another person who walked around with us to turn the lights on and off which seemed unnecessary. Definitely worth a visit if you're in the area as it's a small space but provides a good amount of history.

title: For one hour in history
text: Stopped there with a friend after a moto tour of the town. The history is revealed again but it is strictly forbidden to take photos

title: Faut bien
text:
Très peu de monuments et musée au Pérou. Donc quand on en voit un il faut en profiter. 
La ville a été délaissée par ses propres politiciens qui avaient peur que le président leur prenne leur électorat. Ils refusaient tous projets venant de l'état. Bilan une ville sans équipements ,peu de routes. l'attrait réside dans la personnalité d'habitants qui soulèvent la dignité de la ville.

title: Et à la fin, le drame
text: Un sympathique petit musée : la collection n'est pas très grandes mais il y a quelques belles pièces. Le guide s'est démené pour rendre la visite vivante et n'a pas été avare d'explications mais... à la fin il nous emmène voir deux métiers à tisser traditionnel dans la cour dont l'un est activé par un enfant. Pas très normal dans un musée national.

title: Une perle
text:
Cette maison d'habitation au riche passé aujourd'hui transformée en musée ethnologique, par son architecture et l'histoire de ses occupants nous apporte des éléments qui nous aident à mieux comprendre la richesse historique du Benin 
Notre guide par son humour et ses commentaires a été une aide précieuse 

Une visite indispensable

title: la ville de porto_novo au bénin
text: c'est vraiment très formidable d'aller au bénin pour visiter des lieux historiques on peut y aussi visiter d'autres villes du bénin

title: This is a MUST to understand the religious/cultural history and customs of Benin
text: It is small museum; we were only allowed to visit the downstairs of an old house converted for this purpose.  So it won´t take you long.  But you see masks and disguises used in traditional dances and ceremonies.   Unfortunately, photos are not allowed.

title: Overview of local culture and history
text: Although it is only a small exhibit in French, the guide did an excellent job of explaining each piece in clear English. We got a very good overview of the history and culture of the country. As always, the more you ask, the more you learn and get out of the tour.

title: The Benin's history and the museum where understands a tradition
text:
At a 2-story museum, a contracted guide guides me.
Photography is prohibited in the inside.
I arrive by car from Cotonou for approximately one hour.

title: Marchez sur les traces de Tintin (L'Oreille Cassée)
text: Ce musée est un passage incontournable lors d'une visite à Porto-Novo. Les guides sont sympathiques et la collection particulièrement intéressante (bien que limitée faute de place si je comprends bien). Cela me semble un bon aperçu de la culture locale.

title: Visite à faire avec un guide
text: Visite très intéressante pour peu que vous ayez un guide qui connaisse l'histoire. Un passage à faire après le temple des pythons

title: Top 5 Things To Do In Lagos
text: I personally love going to Lekki Market to shop for dresses made with Ankara fabric, interesting local art work, or other furnishing pieces.  It is hands down one of my favorite places to visit in Lagos.   It is also a great stop when I am hosting visitors to Lagos, because they can get fabric in the market and find tailors to sew it into whatever creations, buy ready-made pieces, wood carvings, raffia goods, get their market haggling experience, etc.  Prices are usually reasonable (after you have done a bit of bargaining, of course).  And I love the variety of options that can be found here.  The market is relatively organized, but be prepared for the noise of generators, if the power is out.  The road leading to the market is in really terrible condition, and even worse when it rains so be wary of going there in a sedan car.  There is also a N200 charge to park your car in the lot so make sure you have spare cash.

title: Your regular art market in West Africa
text:
Souvenirs can be cheap if you are good with haggling. Ankara fabrics made into bags, purses and notebook covers. You can also easily get your emergency tailor to sew simple dresses.

The market which consists of stalls for raffia bags and beautiful art works is not that much of a big deal. Market is not easily accessible as the road is in dire need of repairs.

title: Lekki the best to shop local
text: Am amazing experience show casing local talent for art, beadwork, wooden carvings, local fabric, handbags and so much more. Friendly environment open to negotiations on prices. Much cheaper than purchasing at the airport. What a lovely experience will go back next time I am in Lagos!!!!

title: Not much here
text:
If you’re thinking souks in Marakesh or the bazaar in Istanbul this is nothing like these. 

We were done in 45 minutes.  Everybody selling the same things.  Beautiful Nigerian fabrics made into purses, bags and notebooks.  

If you want cheap souvenirs for friends at home you’ll find them here.  They really do NOT bargain which I found surprising after visiting other bazaars. 

Worth a very quick trip.  Wear trainers as it’s mucky and muddy.

title: Very different Wooden art and African paintings
text:
This place is amazing for art lovers . You will get plenty of options for home decor (Wooden artifacts and painting). We bought lot of small wooden arifacts ) . I took some to India as well
But do remember to negotiate well!

title: Antiques and a lot more
text: Roads are very bad leading to the market. But lots of African art and lots more which I shall not mention. Can buy things like pearls, paintings, get African clothing stitched. Lots of bargaining. Much. Enter than buying from one of the hotels. Much cheaper. Road leading to market is very bad so a good vehicle is needed.

title: Amazing artwork and unique finds but poor setup...
text:
The Lekki Market is AMAZING if you're looking for unique gifts and original artwork. Canvas art is of very high quality, prices are reasonable considering the talent and they will roll them and pack in a tube for easy travel. You can negotiate a bit but don't insult the artists- they are very talented and could command much higher prices if they had a better setup. Getting there is a huge turnoff, the Lagos State officials should be ashamed- can the Ministry of Art and Culture not build a large open-air facility for the artists to have stalls and properly display there work? This is something they have done very well in countries like Senegal, Burkina Faso, Tanzania and Madagascar. Something simple but clean, organized and easy to access for tourists and visitors. On the day I visited, there was so much standing water that we had to go back and switch cars. The potholes are insane, the area lacks ambiance for tourists and there isn't any signage. When we arrived the Japanese Embassy delegation decided to not even get out of the car because the generators were running and blowing black smoke on you at the entrance. Not a very nice welcome. 

The art is amazing, local and ambiance not so much.

title: Lekki Market
text:
The road to the Lekki Art Market was quite rough and it didn't help that it had rained the previously day. On getting there we were a bit confused as we couldn't easily spot a sign telling us we were at the right place. Inside the market, we were able to spot nice African inspired items, good for gifts. We also walked pass where some of the bags sold in the market are sold. 

When going here, you need to go with your bargaining skills so the traders don't take advantage of you. I always started by bargaining from less than half the price they mention first

title: Shopping for African Artwork
text: The road ushering us to the Lekki Art Market was quite rough. We needed a gift for a speaker at our event and felt that a good artwork will suffice. The market is not large but still has a good collection of paintings, bronze work and wood carvings. We finally settled for a wood carving of a Saxophone. We also discovered that prices were much lower here than most art galleries in the area.

title: A place to kill time for 1/2 day
text: After traveling to many countries within Africa.  It appears that each market around the continent are selling the same stuff.  As it's the same here.  Most vendors welcome you to take photos and associate with you.  But this one particular lane with wooden carvings and furniture, I was yelled at for talking videos.  Other than that, my experience here is okay.

title: Number 1 arts and craft shopping center
text: This is one of the few places I must take my clients to visit in during our Lagos City tours for esquisite creative art works. Just that now a days it takes a while to see something new as they all now sell same stuffs. So it takes a while of walking the entire market to get a few things that are totally unique and cheap.

title: Buy groceries and craft work
text: The Lekki Market is located at the Victoria Island extension/ beginning of Lekki. It is an ideal place to buy souvenirs, art work, beads, paintings and most importantly food.

title: Lekkie market
text: If you're looking for a taste of rich African culture, Lekkie Markets the place to go to.  Experience African talent and craftsmanship at the Lekkie Market.

title: Gifts & Souvenirs
text: Something we will always remember Nigeria with are the gifts and souvenirs we were able to buy at affordable prices. Don’t be afraid to haggle, it is expected !!

title: City Tour of Lagos with our international tourist and friends.
text: This is an excellent and unique stopping point for series of souvenirs, artworks, painting, beautiful beads, artefacts, tie & dye fabrics for both locals and various visiting tourists when showcasing part of what Lagos has to offer. Most tourist took much time here picking trending stuffs....

title: A Challenging Experience
text: On my first visit, we were literally swamped by sellers and hadn't even left our vehicle. I guess my being "oyibo" didn't help. I appreciate this is the Nigerian way but it was a little intimidating being followed, led, pushed and pulled to stores to buy. My husband is Nigerian but even he found it hard to direct them away.  Needless to say, I didn't wish to stay long. I had hoped to buy many traditional items and fabrics but went home disappointed.

title: Average market place though
text: Here you get luxury and meet class that flutters the Lekki community. Buy here and meet the 'bigs' in Lekki

title: A definite visit for a true African market
text: Jam packed with all sorts of interesting art and handmade articles, masks,etc.  It can get overwhelming but definitely worth a visit.

title: Local treasures
text: Great local market experience but you must not be shy of bargaining. We picked up some nice artifacts

title: Typical Lagos Market with the added bonus of a craft section
text:
This is a market i have been too very often. It is a typical market that sells the usual items you will find around Lagos. However, it is cleaner than most Lagos markets and that is a plus. The road leading to the market has been fixed and so access is a lot easier than it used to be.

It is a very safe and sane space. It is also not far from the beaches along the coastal line of Lagos. You feel the usual Lagos bustle but the market is far from crowded and the stalls are well set out.

The craft section is a big attraction of foreigners and expats. The downside of its popularity is that the crafts have become a lot pricier than they used to be. The good news is that this is an old fashion market (it is not a superstore with fixed prices) and it is a game of negotiation so when the seller goes high, you should start with a counter offer that is at least 50% lower than the asking price. Be prepared to haggle on price as this is the most fulfilling part of the experience.

Enjoy your visit to this quaint and niche market.

title: I was there to give lecture on drug abuse.
text: I found sukur kingdom very attractive and much historical monuments. Enriched with african culture and believesn some organisations shrine to see

title: Great events centre
text:
Easy to locate.
This more of events hall for multi-purpose use.
I presume because of it's affiliation to the Musical Society of Nigeria, the acoustic in the halls are above average.
These halls  host  recitals, theatres, live plays, social events, board meetings  etc
The halls come in diffrent capacity
•	Shell Nigeria  Hall            Maximum 1,000 seats
•	Agip recital hall                Maximum   258 seats  or 80 box seats
•	Function rooms                Maximum 150 persons 
•	Board room 1                    12 persons
•	Board room 2                    24 persons

Limited parking within, however more parking across the road. This venue is used more by corporates.
Prices may range from $200  to circa  $5,000 per event

title: Event place
text: The event halls have different carring capacities. The parking space is big and secure. The facility is well maintained.

title: The Muson Centre
text: From musical theater to concerts to Fundraising shows or recitals, Muson centre is the IT place for all things Music and more in Lagos. For those with a taste for  Live performances ,stage plays and everything Music,be sure to visit the Muson centre. There is always a program or two going on.

title: Want to listen to Classical music?
text:
This is the go-to place for Classical music in Lagos. MUSON stands for the Musical Society of Nigeria and they run a music school on the premises. You should try to catch the annual MUSON week in October and there are also Christmas & Easter performances by the MUSON Orchestra & Choir which are always well attended.

If you are in Lagos at the right time you might even get to see one of the now increasingly rare stage plays.

The Halls also serve as venues for shows, meetings and even Church services so not all events there are musical events.

title: A First Class Event Place.
text: A great place for events hosting. Good soundproofing and sound reproduction is very great. However a local band will show itself especially with low quality musical equipment.

title: Venue for good classical music
text: The MUSON Centre will always live up to expectations as a very good place to listen to good classical music. The other function rooms also play host to several events. The venue is likewise central somehow to link to Victoria Island and the Mainland; there are options of how to navigate round

title: Very comfortable place
text: I've been privileged to watch recitals, small concerts, plays and shows in this place for the last 23 years of my life. It has always been a pleasant experience. It's smack in the middle of a busy part of Lagos but don't let that deter you. There's ample parking space most times and it's a secure location. Check out any events happening there and go have fun!

title: Amazing centre
text: This place is used for a lot of different activities especially activities connected with arts. I love how it is set up. You might want to find out what activities they have lined up for your enjoyment.

title: Interesting play at Muson Center
text: Saw a thought-provoking but funny play at the Muson Center. The theater hall was comfortable and well designed. Good view of the stage from all seats. Forehall also good location for before and after reception. All in all a great location for an outing.

title: Events
text: Muson centre is a multi-purpose center with some halls for hire (agip hall, shell hall etc.). I've attended quite a number of shows (SARO, stand up 9ja etc.) there.

title: For the finer things
text:
If you're one that enjoys the finer things like 'live theatre' and the likes. This is the place to catch em. The halls are large and comfy,especially the Shell Hall. 
It's also a good place to host conferences and meetings.

title: Good to host conferences,seminars etc
text: I attended a conference in one of the halls shell hall precisely. The hall is big and very fit for that purpose

title: Lovely!
text: The Muson Centre is a great multi purpose center. Located on the Marina, Onikan, it is home to a fantastic restaurant, a great music hall which presents music, recitals, plays, concerts, etc The centre is also a venue for weddings. Lovely!

title: Electrifying
text: The Muson Centre is electrifying. Whether for musical, stage drama, meeting  etc, it is a promise assured. Regular visits all year round.

title: Nigerian Broadway Show
text: The Muson Center is the place to be if you love ''Live theater''. This the second time I will be attending a musical at the center. The first was  ''SARO'' and the second is ''WAKAA". It's a great place to watch a live stage performance. Both performances  were electrifying. The costumes, the music, the singing, the choreography, the lighting, Really wonderful.

title: Moving tour of infamous fortress, part of the transatlantic slave trade
text: A tour of Elmina Castle is a must for any visitor to Ghana who is interested in history and an understanding of the infamous slave trade. Dating from 1482, this is the oldest surviving fortress in sub Saharan Africa that housed captured slaves headed for the Americas.  To take a guided tour of the “castle” and its slave dungeons, including the Door of No Return, is both fascinating and incredibly moving, affording insights into the horrific slave trade in ways that cannot be appreciated through books or even films.

title: Haunting
text: Elmina Castle was one of the hundreds of holding prisons for black men, women and children who had been kidnapped and were about to be shipped to other parts of the world as slaves, never to return to their home and families.  Our excellent guide gave much information about this trade and what it would have been like for these people. It horrified and haunted us. I had heard quite a bit about the slave trade, but not fully understood the size and horror of this mass kidnapping and displacement of people, over so long a period of time and by so many countries occupying Africa at the time. This important part of history warrants greater acknowledgement and understanding.

title: Important, interesting, and underdeveloped attraction
text: Historically important and interesting site. While clean, the location is somewhat neglected and unkept. So much potential to develop and maintain the site further. Heat is a major issue in both indoor and outdoor areas. Air condition should be installed, and exhibits better maintained. So much potential and many things could have been presented in appealing exhibitions and visuals, but there is no investment in upgrading the facility and its exhibits in what seems to have been a very long time. The tour guides however do a great job at presenting enough information without overloading visitors, while creating drama and interest throughout the visit.

title: Haunting
text: This was my second visit to Elmina Castle.  I think my one gripe is that they need to have organised tours at set times. I also think that group sizes should be limited to a certain number. I was disappointed with the toilet facilities. This is a place that is extensively visited and there is no need to have toilets which are substandard. Great guide and very informative.

title: Elmina Castle and "The Door of No Return"
text:
Elmina Castle, in Ghana, was built by the Portuguese to protect the gold trade in 1482. Although the castle had different ownership over time, from the Portuguese, to the Dutch, and finally the British, it became a major center for the transatlantic slave trade. In the center of the Castle was the Catholic Church.

Elmina Castle, like other castles on the gold coast, were used to hold captured/ kidnapped enslaved Africans before they were loaded onto ships and sold in the Americas as a new workforce.

At this Castle, I was able to see the "Door of No Return" where my ancestors left their homeland to never return again. Our tour guide was outstanding!

title: Elmina Castle - A Day Trip to Take
text: If you are interested in the history of slavery, Elmina Castle is a must see.  This is not a joyful experience, but yet one that is a worthwhile visit.  The Castle was the largest of the several slave embarkation points along Ghana's coast.  As a reasonably well preserved landmark, there are guides available once you get there.  After an hour or two of walking around the castle, you will be thinking about how this human cruelty ever happened.  The exit known as the "doorway of no return" will prompt your thoughts to families with loved ones, children included, who, after months in dungeon quarters, were split apart and never saw each other again.   The only downside was the drive to get there.  With road disarray and construction, it took 3.5 hours to go 100 miles with a hired driver.  At least the continuous scenes of life along the roadside provided a view that was never boring.

title: Atmospheric
text: This castle is a strangely European piece of architecture reflecting the Portuguese, Swedes, Danes, Dutch and British that successively exploited this piece of Africa. It is amazingly well preserved with a Portuguese chapel dominating a claustrophobic, whitewashed courtyard. It is minor miracle these places survived to give one of few pieces of evidence for the transatlantic slave trade. Essential to visit alongside the Cape Coastal Castle nearby.

title: Must See
text:
Pay a visit Elmina Castle if you’re in the area.

The first European structure in sub-Saharan Africa, Elmina Castle towers over the Gulf of Guinea’s blue waters on one side and the bustling fishing village on the other. When the Portuguese erected this fortress in 1482, they built it to last. 540 years later the battlements stand strong and the hardwood floors and rafters are worn smooth with the passage of time. 

Spend an hour or two walking freely about the bastions and interior spaces. The sea breezes and commanding views provide ample incentive for reflective pauses. There’s even a small restaurant in the northeast corner where visitors can take refreshments and watch the townspeople’s fishing boats venturing to and fro. 

I traveled to Elmina castle with a local and we didn’t pay an entrance fee or hire a guide, but guides were standing ready to provide a tour. If visitors do some light reading prior to arrival, it’s quite a nice experience to do alone, at your own pace.

My only regret is that the government of Ghana doesn’t put a little more funding towards the maintenance of the window fittings and other small aspects of the building. Elmina Castle is a monument to engineering and exploration, as well as a testament to man’s cruelty during the colonial period.

title: Cape Coast Castle – A Journey Through History
text:
Cape Coast Castle, located on Ghana’s central coast, is one of the most significant historical sites in West Africa. This UNESCO World Heritage Site stands as a powerful reminder of the transatlantic slave trade, offering visitors a deeply emotional and educational experience.

Historical Significance

Built by the Swedes in the 1650s and later controlled by the British, Cape Coast Castle was a major hub for the transatlantic slave trade. The castle’s dungeons, where enslaved Africans were held before being shipped to the Americas, leave a haunting impression. Walking through these dark, airless rooms gives a chilling glimpse into the suffering endured by countless men and women.

Tour Experience

Guided tours are available, led by knowledgeable guides who provide a detailed and moving account of the castle’s history. The Door of No Return, through which captives were forced onto slave ships, is one of the most powerful stops on the tour. However, there is also the Door of Return, symbolizing the resilience of African descendants who revisit their ancestral homeland.

Architecture & Scenic Views

Beyond its somber history, the castle itself is an impressive structure, featuring whitewashed walls and breathtaking views of the Atlantic Ocean. The contrast between the beauty of the surroundings and the tragic history within the walls adds to the site’s emotional impact.

Museum & Exhibits

The on-site museum provides valuable context with artifacts, documents, and displays about the slave trade, Ghanaian culture, and colonial history. It’s a great addition to the tour, helping visitors gain a deeper understanding of the past.

Verdict

Cape Coast Castle is a must-visit for history enthusiasts, students, and anyone seeking to understand the impact of the transatlantic slave trade. While the experience can be heavy and emotional, it is an important reminder of history and resilience. The only drawback is that the site can get crowded during peak tourist seasons, and some areas could use better maintenance.

Final Thoughts

A visit to Cape Coast Castle is not just a tour—it’s an unforgettable lesson in history, humanity, and remembrance. Highly recommended for anyone traveling to Ghana.

title: Basilique de l'Immaculée Conception , Une oeuvre des Missionnaires Catholiques en 1909 .
text:
Cette basilique de Ouidah , dite de " L'Immaculée Conception " , qui date de 1909 ,  a été longtemps Cathédrale de la Colonie du Dahomey instituée en 1884 , avec Ouidah comme capitale . Elle est le fruit de la persévérance des Missionnaires venus au Bénin dès 1884 .  En 1954 , elle perd son statut de siège du vicariat apostolique au profit de Porto Novo , qui devient capitale de Dahomey . Elle devient basilique en 1989 ; 

La construction de cette basilique dans le style " néo Gothique " a été faite de 1903 à 1909 , grâce à la participation de toute la communauté de Ouidah y compris celle de confession Vaudou , du fait de cette solidarité africaine unique en son genre !!

En arrivant cette basilique se remarque . La façade comporte un clocher de section carrée , mais inachevé , encadré par deux contreforts ouverts de lancettes en vitrail , le tout peint en gris clair . Le porche à la base du clocher , est encadré par une haute portée en arc de plein cintre à voussures peintes en blanc . Le haut du clocher est ouvert d'abats sons , et il est décoré de corniches peintes . Une petite statue d'Evêque ( peut être Monseigneur Dartois initiateur de cet édifice) se trouve au devant du clocher . 

En entrant , on découvre la nef unique , en forme de croix latine , qui est à cinq travées éclairées par des baies géminées à vitraux surmontées d'oculus . Le transept est peu saillant et ouvert de vitraux dans le style de la nef . La voute est de style lambrissé ( bois)  et est portée par des structures métalliques , ce qui lui donne une légèreté de bonne facture . 
Le choeur est placé dans une abside quadrangulaire ouverte de vitraux historiés . L'autel avec ses décorations simples , est placé contre le mur pignon sous une voute débordante en berceau . Une statue de la Vierge Marie au dessus de la croix , constitue les seules ornementations .

La visite de cet édifice est instructive sur le style de l'époque coloniale française , qui reprend celui des édifices français , mais avec des touches de couleurs d'inspiration africaine .  L'utilisation de matériaux légers , métal et bois , est déjà à la mode . 

A l'extérieur , une grotte réalisée en pierre de taille , sert pour les cérémonies en l'honneur de la Vierge notamment le 15 Aout

title: The Elmina Castle Experience marred by leeches outside the walls!
text:
There were 5 of us in the group and the cost of entry & tour totalled £11.96 converted to £ which I thought wasn't bad at all. A warning to everyone, as soon as you arrive in the castle parking area you're pounced on by the street sellers! It's quite unnerving especially if you have senior citizens within the group. They were like leeches & hounds. Note: don't give them your name when they ask, I worked out that what they'll do is get a shell from the sea which is of course free. Write a welcome note on the shell and charge you the earth for it claiming the money which can be accepted in Dollars or sterling will be donated to a local school? they even had badges on lanyards, not sure stipulating what though! probably a discount card of some sort? I was surprised they didn't have high visibility bibs on to give it the full official effect!. This all happens when you're on the tour of course. I'll come back to this afterwards.

The tour guide started, they tried to pack as many visitors into the group which I felt lessoned the experience as I had questions, lots! well, if I'm travelling this far I want to know things as well. Personally I felt the tour was rushed because there was always another group behind us ready to enter the areas of the castle. 

The stories were horrendous, makes me think the English can't be the worst slave traders as the castle was ruled by the Dutch & the Portuguese and after by the English. The slave quarters were a sight to see, I'm not surprised the ruler of the castle died young, what with the diseases going around back then. Imagine being a slave and being a sex slave to the ruler? unimaginable.

There were a lot of places to buy souvenirs but pricy in my opinion, especially the books. I think I'll read about it online. Watch out for the steep stairs, not very disability friendly but then again, the country hasn't moved pace with other countries in the world and there's no rush for it. If you've seen the roads, so called footways and general infrastructure you'll know what I mean.  

After the tour was over we walked around and I thought to myself "Why don't they give this place a lick of paint and do a little bit of maintenance? it was falling apart  especially with the salt in the air. The washrooms weren't clearly signed, I thought we'd had to use the corner until we saw a sign on top of some stairs. You could tell a place by it's toilets and it wasn't great but what alternative was there?. 

Exiting the draw bridge we were mobbed by the leeches and hounds, it was terrible. The castle car park should be out of bounds to these things. It got so bad it caused arguments in the group as one of the senior citizens were hounded so much he was confused about how much to give so he just whipped out £10 but they jumped on him and wanted more. We had to detach him from the mob and usher him into the vehicle for his own safety. I did give them £5 but then they came out with all the teary eyed puppy dog stories of "I need to feed my family" "my  children needs to go to school" "Brexit, Covid, War in Ukraine!" hey, the Tories are always using that line so I'll jump on the band wagon whilst I still can!. 

What these leeches will do is thrust a form in front of you showing amounts of previous donations from previous visitors, obviously high amounts to persuade you to part with money. When I handed over £5 the cheeky leech said "you should double it, it'll help the children". Yeah right, more like help him. I told him where to go and it was all that I had but he still badgered me until I closed the car door on his face, he continued through the window. It was one of the worst experiences on my travels, nothing in comparison to the street sellers, they're tame in comparison to these blood suckers.  

I doubt Elmina Castle's management team will take any notice. Going by the state of the buildings the things outside are the least of there worries, it's just about getting as many through the door as possible. 

One time thing for me, I wouldn't dream of entering the car park if you paid me. Only way to get around this is be dropped at the entrance of the castle by the draw bridge. If security woke up and did their job probably they'll keep the leeches & hounds from trespassing & vastly improving the experience otherwise, a thumbs down from me but the tour was educational and an interesting insight into the tragic things that happened behind these walls.

text:
What can I say?
This was a heart wrenching experience. And it wasn't even my first time yet I felt the same sense of sorrow and trepidation as the first time I visited about 20 years ago. 
It was also a time to feel pride for the bravery of my ancestors. Those who fought to end this phase of inhumanity and evil. Evil that was inflicted even with a so-called church on the premises. 

Kwamena was our tour guide and narrator. Excellent work, Kwamena. He told the story well, with the perfect amount of detail and expression. He also looked out for our safety, ensuring that the children especially were secured away from potential hazards such as when he opened the floor flaps to the water wells and dungeons. 

There are several excellent books being sold on site, at the entrance and at the end of the tour, along with souvenirs. Even Shea butter and shittor! We got the children some hand flicked drums which has kept their attention since!

There is a small museum on site as well. 

Beware the hecklers in the car park who will harass you to buy their paintings. I requested a shell that they design with your name and it makes a cute little souvenir but agree the price at the start and if they get grumpy, walk away. They are nice people but they're a bit too much.

Overall, this place is a must-see for all visitors and locals alike. Thank you, Kwamena.

title: Elmina Castle, A walk back in time
text:
We also went up to their chapel and the offices; was quite a solemn experience. Then took us to the male and female dungeons where our people were overcrowded, slept, died, defecated, and for the females menstruated. Many died before the ship arrived due to starvation and inhumane conditions. On the grounds of the dungeons, you will see what they wore, the awful stench would hit your noses but what got me sad was when he got to the door of no return; a small metallic gate.

Now I had a problem because I did not see any food vendor or an eatery, aside from the several souvenir shops for people to buy from. I had the same problem at Afadjato. I would strongly suggest they put up an eatery for visitors to have good local food to enjoy as all of that adds to the beauty of the site. We were there for more than 2 hours and did not see any sign of a food vendor on the premises, rather we had to go into town for something to eat. Then again, I had snacks in my bag and that served us well till hunger set in and we left to the next place.t. Just outside the premises you will have a lot of options to pick from so we did that and had our fill

I recommend an eatery be set up outside the castle

title: Touts detract from visit.
text:
With all respect the castle tour is worth it, however, much the same style if you will have likely visited Cape Coast.

Perhaps things may have been a changed since I was last there, however, my visit was completely sullied by the touts outside who hounded me to the main door and then waited to follow me from the main door. By far the most aggressive touts I encountered in Ghana, who made me feel very unsafe and I would would just advise caution if you plan to visit. 

If you opt otherwise, there are multiple other castles to visit, including at Cape Coast where touts were much more manageable - and the tours were very informative, interesting and sad.

title: Heart Touching Experience
text: Heart Touching Experience. Once you get to Elmina, to visit the castle is a must. I and my husband visited caste 2 times during our stay, everytime with different guide but it was really impressive. The story is really heart touching, specially in these times. Human beings should learn from the past and Elmina Castle belongs to this learning for 100%.

title: Emotionally tour around Elmina!
text: We had a good guided tour around Elmina Slave Castle. Built in 1482, this was the hub of the Portuguese (1482-1637) and Dutch slave trade (1637-1872) on the Gold Coast. Under the rule of the Dutch West Indies Company, around 30,000 slaves a year passed through Elmina’s door of no return. It was a very emotional and sobering visit, especially the secret staircase from the women's cells to the Governor's bedroom.

title: Our people suffered
text: Being from Surinam we know how the slaves were brought in. Elmina was very confrontating. They suffered so much.

title: Elmina Castle
text: Elmina es una ciudad situada en la costa atlántica de Ghana. Fue el primer asentamiento europeo en el Oeste de Africa y en la actualidad cuenta con una población de unos 20.000 habitantes. Los portugueses fueron los primeros en ocupar Cape Coast en 1555, lugar al que llamaron Cabo Corso. La Compañía Sueca de África construyó un fuerte en 1653, primero de madera y después de piedra, y lo llamaron Carolusburg por el rey Carlos X de Suecia. Cape Coast, es otra de las ciudades destacadas, conocida como Oguaa es una ciudad de habla Fante, posee un precioso castillo que data del siglo XVII. Fue construido por los suecos y se convirtió rápidamente en el centro de operaciones de la posterior incursión británica. También famosa por su Universidad enfrentamientos entre las potencias europeas para conseguir su dominio. En 1663 fue tomado por los daneses, luego por los holandeses y finalmente pasó a poder de los británicos, que en 1757 reconstruyeron el castillo, dañado por los bombardeos. Todos los ocupantes tuvieron a su vez que combatir contra los nativos del lugar. Imprescindible la visita.

title: Elmina Castle Tour - Ghana
text:
Wanted to share details of the our Elmina Castle Tour, we were staying locally at the Lemon Beach Resort, we didn't have the time to book an official tour but glad we didn't as the tour conducted by the Guides at the Castle was amazing, informative (whilst very harrowing)  engaging and very interesting. 
We took a local taxi to the site and walked up to the Castle, the entrance fee is 40 GHC (cedis) for adults and 30 for students. The guides take you around and share so much information starting from the arrival of the Portuguese in 1471, the Dutch and then the British. The Tour lasts about 1.5 hours. A must for anyone visiting the area.

title: Ouidah - is on the future UNESCO site
text: Ouidah is very impressive. the history, the museum, the sites, the people, the restaurant, everything about Ouidah is magical.

title: Well worth a visit
text:
It is well worth walking the whole of the Route des esclaves. You can start from the Ouidah Museum of History and end at the gate of no return. The museum itself has some fascinating images showing the assimilation that took place from west African slaves bringing food, dance, and culture over to the Americas. The artifacts and images from the slave trade are horrific and it really makes you think about the dreadful conditions these people were forced into. Well worth the time to tour around. 

Entrance is free although, at the end of the tour, you donate what you want to the guide. Guides can be conducted in both French and English.

title: Une partie triste de l'histoire de l'humanité
text: Même si triste, il faut connaître et se souvenir de cet partie de l'histoire afin que jamais quelque chose de semblable ne se reproduise

title: Incontournable...
text: Si vous êtes blanc à faire avec l'humilité et le devoir de recueillement qui s'impose ici, le musée comme tout autre lieux de mémoire au Bénin aurait besoin d'une bonne réhabilitation, mais la visite reste incontournable et les différents guides restent très compétant.

title: A faire mais assez décevant

Il faut se documenter avant la visite et discuter du sujet après.
Intéressant pour les plus jeunes car cela permet d'initier une discussion sur les relations sociales en Afrique et le rôle des européens sur ce continent.

title: The Black Holocaust

You actually feel some of the pain and anguish as you hear the story which is told by a group of well educated guides in detail who invite questions and challenges to the message. Our guide was excellent in so much as he wasn’t shocked by the questions he was asked during our tour.
Definitely worth a visit.

title: A stark reminder of man's inhumanity
text: You must visit but be prepared, this is one of the worst reminders of man's inhumanity. Yes the slaves were bought from the winning side in tribal wars and sold to the slavers, some walked here from as far away as Chad and Mali. The conditions we kept them in is appalling. The dungeons have no light and the slaves were kept in uncleaned conditions for up to 10 weeks.  It reduced some in our small group to tears.

title: One of Humanity's Worst
text:
The debate whether this was a castle or prison is settled once you walk 'the room of no return'. There's literally a slide (image 2); one can only imagine how they shoved them into this room, then narrowed down so they couldn't turn around or fight back (like they do with cattle; image 1) but pushed into one direction, which is where they were loaded onto the ships. To call this a prison, even seems too much of an epitaph for this all but slaughterhouse.

Building a church inside, then proceed to do all God forbade, if only hypocricy at its worst was the worst of this.

text:

Downside was the tour guide who gave the tour a strong overlay of her own religious views. Happy for someone to tell me they are a born again christian, but giving me god’s view of the slave trade is not very informative.
The tour had a strong element of being designed to produce an emotional impact. It is certainly an emotionally impactful place, but I also felt that a rather crude over-emphasis on emotional impact during the tour detracted from the overall experience.

title: La Porta del Ritorno
text:
Mercoledì 3 agosto 2022 
La visita a Cape Coast Castle ti svuota, è un tuffo nell'orrore, perpetrato per centinaia di anni dall'uomo bianco, da trafficanti senza anima che hanno commerciatoaltri uomini, ignari dell'orribile destino che li attendeva, costretti ad abbandonare la propria terra di origine ed i propri cari. 
Immaginare, come in un incubo, di essere costretti a camminare per giorni e giorni per essere deportati, vivere per mesi in spazi angusti senza luce, senza cibo, né acqua, in attesa di attraversare la cosiddetta "porta del non ritorno" ed essere poi imbarcati, costretti ad una nuova disumana esistenza, al servizio di padroni sfruttatori. 
Eppure serve per non dimenticare, per avere grande rispetto di una razza che è stata perseguitata, schiavizzata e che nonostante tutto questo, a distanza di generazioni, a volte riesce a ritornare in questi posti, in una sorta di pellegrinaggio, riuscendo ad attraversare la “Porta del ritorno” a Cape Coast castle, per avere memoria di tutto quello che in un tempo lontano è successo. 
Nel 2019 il Governo del Ghana, per commemorare il 400° anniversario della tratta degli schiavi, ha lanciato una campagna chiamata l'Anno del Ritorno" con lo slogan "Bentornato a casa", operazione volta ad incoraggiare gli afrodiscendenti a tornare in Ghana alla ricerca delle proprie origini. 
Un bel messaggio, nel segno del perdono, della speranza e della pace. 
La visita a questo posto è una esperienza da vivere, anche se è molto dura, tanto da restare impressa in maniera indelebile nell'anima!

title: TOUCHANT
text:
Petit musée simple et touchant.  Un incontournable de Mindelo,  ne pas manquer.3 euros l entrée. 
Quelques effets personnels de la diva aux pieds nus,  robes , documents personnels, photos et autres .  Appareils audio murales pour écouter la musique de Cesaria sur place. Sa  vie est retracée sur de grands panneaux. 
Bonne visite !

title: Desapontamento - Cise, merecias bem mais!
text: A simplicidade da Diva dos pés descalços merecia bem mais do seu amado São'sente. Saí daquela casinha a que chamaram Núcleo Museológico Cesária Évora com um sentimento de tristeza e injustiça. Senti um certo abandono à "grandeza" que ela foi para o mundo, para o seu povo, no papel que teve na projeção mundial da cultura Cabo-verdiana, a doce Cize.

title: Honteux.
text: Aucun respect des horaires d'ouverture pour un musée trop petit, ne mettant pas assez en valeur le talent de cette grande artiste : il en résulte un goût de tristesse et de gâchis.

title: Il semblerait que ce beau bâtiment soit en travaux
text: Malheureusement ce magnifique bâtiment, ancien palais du gouvernement est encore fermé.nous sommes restés 10 jours et n’avons pu y entrer

title: Nucléo Museologico Cesaria Evora
text: Fermé et encore fermé. Que passa ? On a fini par trouver un minuscule musée pas loin de là. Aussi modeste que la vie de Cize comme ils l’appellent là bas. Mais beaucoup de vidéo très intéressantes et instructives. Entrée 3€. Rua Guerra Mendes

title: Passionnant et sans prétention.
text: Si l’extérieur ne paye pas de mine et ne paraît pas engageant, on est vite pris par l’histoire de ce personnage qui a vécu dans cette maison. L’émotion n’en est que plus belle!

title: A small overview of the city's history
text: A very modest display, but it's still worth stopping to familiarize yourself with what's on display. Fresh works by local artists are also presented here.  A very modest display, but it's still worth stopping to familiarize yourself with what's on display. Fresh works by local artists are also presented here. No fee!

title: a not miss in Cabo verde
text: this is the famous Cesaria Evora museum , the house where the greatest singer lived while alive. We were even able to talk to her living brother.

title: Sehr schönes Museum, viele Exponate
text: Wer die Musik von Cesaria Evora kennt und mag, sollte unbedigt das Museum besuchen! Man sieht viele Utensielen aus ihrem Leben aber auch original Fotos und Kleider die sie bei Konzerten trug!

title: Nice insight into Cesaria's life
text: Interesting details of Cesaria's life. Record covers, dresses she wore at concerts, many pictures on tour of with friends and family...

title: Pamiątki po Cesarii Evora
text: Warto zobaczyć pamiątki zebrane przez fana Cesarii. Niestety rodzina Cesarii nie zdołała stworzyć musem. W muzeum polski akcent- zdjęcie Cesarii z Kayą - ze wspólnego koncertu.

title: Authentiquement vôtre
text: Petit musée au cœur de la ville dédié à la star de Mindelo et du Cap Vert. Une collection assez éclectique dont la présentation ne manque pas d'un charme que je qualifierais de joyeusement désuet. Rien d'époustoufflant mais cette visite reste néanmoins un des instants des plus touchants de mon séjour au Cap Vert.

title: Prachtige Afrikaanse kunst
text: Het deel over Cesaria Evora was het voor ons niet echt waard te bezoeken. Maar de Afrikaanse kunst die tentoongesteld stond was prachtig, zeker een bezoek waard.

title: Magnifique
text:
2 collections, Cesaria Evora d’un côté - à être la.... - et l’art africain de l’autre avec un premier étage à ne pas manquer. Des objets magnifiques.
Il faut y faire un tour.

title: Voor Afrikaanse kunst een must-see!
text: Als je van Afrikaanse kunst houdt, moet je hier echt naar binnen! Het is klein, maar zeer de moeite waard. Prachtige maskers in alle soorten en maten en een aantal sculpturen. De andere kant van het museum is ingericht met alles over locale heldin zangeres Cesária Évora. Niet echt bijzonder, maar je krijgt wel een gevoel van haar indrukwekkende oeuvre. Mensen vinden 7 euro entree misschien wat duur in verhouding, maar je houd daarmee wel het prachtige gebouw en cultuur mee in stand.

title: The African Art Rooms upstairs were stunning.
text: There was an art exhibition downstairs to the left and the Cesaria Evora Tribute to the right. We had to pay 8 euros each to see all exhibits which for us was well worth it having got access to the many rooms abovej which contained the most amazing wealth of african art in all its intricate carving.there was witch doctors masks both fearsome yet often comical expressions Musical instruments inlaid with colourful mosaics .Strange but beautiful statues and artifacts.A throne that was symbolic with elephant tusks six foot high ...which I was assurred were made of wood.Somewhere in the depths of my mind the ensemble of the throne and tusks I felt I had seen them before Shaka Khan King of the Zulus...maybe the film crew borrowed it .It was all set in sunlight and airy rooms painted white walls of an old portuguese palace. Nothing like our dull and sunless victorian Museums.But maybe thats changed since I was a child. I thoroughly recommend you see this exhibit  it was glorious.

title: Small but fascinating and moving memorial to Cesaria Evora
text: I visited this museum to pay homage to Cape Verde's most famous person.  It is situated in an ordinary house in a side street (not her original house I don't think) and contains personal items such as her dresses, hair curlers, favourite coffee mug and ashtray as well as awards and decorations from her singing career.  The story of her life is told in Portuguese, English and (I think) French.  There is a very moving film of her funeral procession when all the local musicians accompanied her coffin to the cemetery playing 'Sodade'.  Also you can listen to a wide selection of her songs on audio.  The museum is excellent value and should be better known.  Perhaps they could have more of her CDs on sale, though I did buy one.

title: Découverte incontournable
text: D’abord il y a le palais rose qui domine, et témoigne du passé colonial. À l’intérieur, 3 expositions différentes de l’art local contemporain lumineux, une collection d’objets d’art africain remarquable, l’évocation touchante de la vie de Cesaria Evora.

title: Le Palais Rose
text: Très belle demeure, les expositions proposées étaient des peintures de 3 talentueux artistes cap verdiens ainsi que la vie musicale de Cesaria Evora a l'étage se trouvent des sculptures africaines (colons) d’ailleurs j’en ai acheter un en souvenir. Très belle exposition il faut y aller

title: Emotional moments!
text: I was very excited when I visited the museum by seeing the photos, dresses that Cesaria Evora wore at her concerts. The personel was very helpful by giving information and answering to some of my questions. There was another exhibition with African objects. I felt very grateful and lucky that I had the chance to visit Mindelo and the museum!

title: Per respirare un po' di cultura locale
text: Interessante Sao Vicente, i suoi mercatini, i luoghi in cui si parla della cultura locale. Sicuramente da visitare.

title: Bom para conhecer sua cultura
text: o centro cultural de Mindelo, vale a pena conhecer para se saber um pouco da culrura do local. Tem apresentações de teatro  noite.

title: Precisoso e fundamental para entender a historia da cidad e
text:
O Centro Cultural do Mindelo, antiga alfandega, é um edificio belissimo e fundamental conhecer para entender a cidade e a importancia do Porto Grande do Mindelo em toda a historia da cidade. 
Hoje em dia e um centro de exposições com direcção de Tony Tavares e também as suas exposições são, em geral, muito boas.

title: Well worth a Visit
text:
The museum was well set out with local artefacts, and some fabulous fabric work 
....a combination of hand made carpet, collage and embroidery with wool.  Stunning and very clever.
The souvenir shop sold some local paintings ...excellent  .....and some interesting local souvenirs.  We watched some Portuguese based dancing and singing that took place at the museum.  The three man group was great as was the singing, .and the dancing was a combination of jive, and sometimes exceedingly suggestive but with taste!  Each island in the group has its own dance, not necessarily music, so each dance was very different.   Sitting in the courtyard tasting the local grog ...43% proof....it was very pleasant indeed!

title: ambachten, kunst en muziek, eten en drinken
text: In het gratis toegankelijke Centro Cultural zijn ambachten, lokale kunst en andere produkten te zien en te koop. In het weekend zijn er hoogwaardige muziekuitvoeringen met niet alleen de lokale muzieksoorten maar ook gastoptredens, ik heb bijvoorbeeld een groep uit Mali en Senegal gehoord en gezien. De concerten zijn vaak van 19:00 tot 20:30, dus een prima manier om het wachten op het diner te verkorten. Ik ben er iedere dag wel een uurtje geweest, het restaurant is simpel maar lekker en niet duur.

title: versteckte Künstler
text: Eine unscheinbare Tür in einer Bretterwand öffnet den Zugang zum Centro Cultural. Die Künstler fertigen hier ihre Figuren für den Karneval. Das Ganze mutet etwas  chaotisch an. Coole Aufbauten und Sujets.

title: Patrimônio cultural
text: Local reúne exposições de artistas locais, espaço para apresentações teatrais, local para leitura e para fazer um lanche. Localizado no centro da cidade.

title: Worth it for the Carnival display
text: I was not impressed with the building generally, but we were lucky enough to visit it just after a special Carnival exhibition had been set up. This displayed several of the actual costumes worn during carnival, as well as a rolling film of some of the highlights of the 2016 carnival. It is definitely worth visiting for this if the exhibition is still running.

title: Not impressed with the exhibition
text: This is a large building across the road from the seafront. It is quite large with high ceilings which make the whole building cool. There is an exhibition space as you come in with a shop on the right, and a library further back on the left and a theatre/lecture room at the rear behind a central courtyard. Public toilets were very welcome.

title: An overview of a day in Mindelo as a cruise port
text:
We have been to Mindelo twice now, both as a one day port of call whilst on a cruise. We have had a pleasant time on both occasions, though if you are seeking glamour and modern shopping centres this is not the port for you. If however you like to explore every port and seek out what it has to offer, you can certainly enjoy your time here. The scope of the excursions offered from the ship (or rather the lack of) give a good indication of what you might expect here.

It is a short walk along the port road, though a minibus shuttle has been offered each time we have visited.As you walk along the coast road you will see fishermen and as you reach the town, they will be gutting and selling fish on the beach. It is a very laid back place and understand that unemployment is extremely high and so many people 'hanging around'.

Still on the waters edge you will find a small fishing museum 'Museu do Mar' (based on the style of the Belem Tower in Lisbon) which is certainly worth a look and then next along is the fish market, which can be interesting to see what different countries have on offer.  There isn't really anything if you continue on further, but if you now head inland you will find the market square, which has a differing number of stalls depending on the day. You will see many beautiful blue and white art tiles, also as seen in Portugal.

 If you now take the street parallel to the coast road, you will find a rather nice gallery/craft shop and also the church. Onward and then to the right you will find an indoor market (can't quite remember but it may be the old town hall) and also see the beautiful colonial architecture of the pink palace, Palacio do Povo (Peoples palace). The University is located behind this, accessed to the right as you look at the Palace.

Back down to the harbour and you will find the cultural centre - a small affair but easy to walk into, friendly staff, local music playing (CD not live) and some interesting artwork on display (though it does change so may just depend how you catch it). They also sell stamps so you can send your postcards much cheaper than on ship.

Back on the waters edge where the shuttle bus departs is a tourist centre, which offers a very pleasant stop for a beverage! Our first visit was at the weekend and a local performing group entertained us for a hour or so, but our subsequent visit was a weekday and this did not occur. We enjoyed a very pleasant lunch. The wind breaks were much appreciated on the breezy and cool January day, which was quite a contrast from the blazing hot sun we experienced thee previous time in April.
Some fellow passengers felt ill at ease here and if looking at the photographs this may apply to you, perhaps consider booking one of the ships excursions so that at least you see a little of the island.

title: Bom
text: È bom conhecer muitas vezes tem esposicao de arte nao so o batimento è estilo antigo lindicimo tem atracao de teatro a noite

title: Always changing
text: This is a very central building and easy to walk into and there was no admission fee.  The first time we went by there was nothing really going on, but with a lot of activity of changing paintings and art work.  Several visits later there was a band playing inside and then a choir.  The craft/souvenir store has some same same items but also offers unique one of a kind (or at least we did not see duplicates at other stores) trinkets.  Worth while to check this building out as you pass by each time.

title: Great spot for local crafts
text: The center is located in an interesting old building across from the waterfront and houses an excellent little shop with local handicrafts. On this barren windswept island, recycling reigns and you'll find wallets made from colorful local coffee bags, bracelets made from aluminum can pull-tabs and jewelry crafted from K-cup coffee containers. And it's all really attractive! You can also purchase local coffee and rum, along with CDs of famed singer Cesaria Evora, a native daughter.

title: музей ремесел
text: если интересно узнать, чем занимались люди на острове, кроме рыбалки - зайдите в музей на центральной площади города и походите по прохладным залам,любуясь на незатейливые произведения ткачей, гончаров и других ремесленников. Цена билета смешная, а впечатление очень милое. Дополните его поездкой на целый день на соседний остров Санту Антау на персональном джипе за 80$ на всех и вы будете иметь полное впечатление о жизни островитян. Обязательно попробуйте сахарный тростник, купите бутылочку сахарного сиропа - альтернатива кленовому- вкусный сувенир в дополнение к магнитику с ракушками, для мужчин больше подойдет национальный продукт перегонки - ром. а после всех экскурсий полюбуйтесь на пляже местными девушками с фигурами статуэток, виндсерферами и тинейджерами, выполняющими акробатические трюки прямо на песке.

title: Preciosidade arquitectural
text: Situado bem no Centro da cidade do Mindelo, a uma distância de cerca de 15 metros do mar, com uma excelente vista para a Baía do Mindelo, uma das mais belas do Mundo, segundo uma classificação da Unesco, o CCM (Centro Cultural do Mindelo), é uma preciosidade arquitectural, estilo colonial, onde funcionou a antiga Alfândega do Governo colonial Português. É um espaço cultural multifunções com uma interacção formidável com a Cidade e sua população.

title: Un bel mercato etnico africano.
text:
Nel centro città di Mindelo troverete un mercato all'aperto che, oltre ad ospitare numerosissimi venditori senegalesi raccoglie nelle sue "casette / negozio" molte altre etnie africane. Potrete trovare coloratissimi foulard provenienti dal Benin, oppure statue in legno Togolesi, o ancora dei magnifici "Boubou" del Ghana, eccetera eccetera. 
I prezzi non sono sempre buoni ma, come un po' dappertutto in Africa, tutto va discusso. Alla fine vedrete che acquirente e venditore si accordano quasi sempre.

title: A visiter
text: Franchement je ne suis pas très musée, et bien ce petit musée sans prétention  est à voir. On ne peut pas rester insensible à cette collection d'art africain et on est agréablement surpris alors qu'il ne bénéficie pas de beaucoup de publicité dans les guides.

title: Art,collection  et culture locale
text: Mérite le détour dans cet ancien palais pour 8€ une expo de peintres cap verdien,une collection d'art africain remarquable evec de superbes "pièces et bien sûr un hommage émouvant  à la Diva au pieds nus qui retrace avec profusion de "fotos" intimes et ses principaux "tours" dans le monde..Très agréable dans cette atmosphère coloniale..A voir !

title: A voir
text: Beau résumé de l'icone du Cap-Vert.Une exposition photo riche,énormément de tenue portées par Cesaria.Le tout à un prix modéré de 500 escudos.

title: Importante per la storia di Sao Vicente
text: Cesaria Evora ha viaggiato in tutto il Mondo ed è stata, non solo grande musicista ma ambasciatrice della sua Terra che deve a lei molto. Il Museo merita senz'altro di essere visto per celebrare una delle figure più importanti di Capo Verde. In un'area separata dell'edificio invece, è possibile accedere anche a una collezione privata di arte africana da tutto il Mondo

title: Musée original...
text:
car situé dans l'ancien palais du gouverneur, d'un joli rose malabar, on peut visiter 3 expos très différentes d'un coup (8€ par pers.): celle consacrée à Cesaria Evora (gloire locale et internationale), celle qui propose des tableaux d'artistes capverdiens et une magnifique expo d'objets d'art africains (masques, tam-tam, armes...). Le tout, dans un joli espace clair et bien entretenu. 
Comptez au minimum 30 minutes de visite. Il existe des fiches d'informations en français.

title: Interessante
text:
In questo bel palazzo coloniale, in passato casa del governatore ci sono due musei interessanti, uno e' il museo Cesaria Evora dedicato alla cantante di Mindelo.
Ci sono centinaia di foto, scritti, strumenti e alcuni suoi vestiti che indossava durante i concerti.
Il secondo museo e' una esposizione  di arte capoverdiana e africana.

title: African Art Museum
text: Excellent Museum. Small but filled with african art fom different West African  countries. It is also part og¡f the Museum devotde to Cesarea Evora that I do not visited

title: Exposition africaine remarquable
text:
2 expos, une sur C Evora que nous n’avons pas choisie et une sur l’art africain de toute beauté.
Des masques, des statues, des portes....un ensemble remarquablement mis en valeur.
A voir absolument pour 500 CVE par personne.

title: Een charmant, klein museum, relatief prijzig voor het gebodene
text: Een leuke, kleine tentoonstelling van allerlei herinneringen uit het leven van Cesaria Evora. Foto's, jurken, cd's en ga zo maar door. Stel je er niet teveel van voor, dan is het leuk. Als je de zangeres niet kent, is bezoek niet zinvol.

title: piège à touristes

Everything you can think of is here, weither you are looking for magnets, fabrics, objects made with different leaves (cane...), books, music, lamps and lampshades, jewels, ceramics, food, soaps, alcohol... I bought all my gifts for my friends in this store as, on top of it, the staff is very useful, nice and knowledgeable. Definitely the place to come to in Mindelo for all your gifts!

title: BUSINESS IS BUSINESS
text:
Revente sans âme de superbes produits et créations artisanales locales. Leurs articles sont revendus 4 fois plus cher du prix bradé par l'artisan. On est très loin d'un commerce équitable, parcontre leurs articles sont d'authentiques productions artisanales.
Personnel sans âmes, boutique de luxe, prix très élevés, pour exemple vous pourrez acheter un authentique Pilon à un local entre 1500 et 2000 escudos max, quand vous en payerez entre 8000 et 12000 escudos chez cap vert disgn.

ownerResponse.text:
Bien dommage que ce message soit anonyme... Les pilons anciens ne sont pas destinés aux Capverdiens. Quant aux touristes, ils ont beaucoup de difficultés à les emporter dans leurs sacs à dos ou dans leurs bagages limités à 20 kg. En fait, ils témoignent d’une tradition capverdienne d’origine africaine et leur prix est dissuasif. Il en va de même pour les moulins de pierre et les pots anciens en terre cuite. Nous ne tenons pas à vider le Cap-Vert de ses richesses, ni à le brader ! 
À noter en Europe, les pilons sont vendus 280 Euros (28.000 Escudos).

title: Rapport qualité prix déplorable
text:
La boutique est belle, il y a beaucoup de choix, mais les prix sont parfaitement indécents pour le Cap-Vert. 

Allez plutôt faire vos achats sur les marchés pour aider les commerçantes qui se lèvent à l'aube, plutôt qu'engraisser cette boutique attrape touristes

ownerResponse.text:
Madame,
Sachez qu'offrir 450m2 de showroom dédiés exclusivement à l’artisanat de toutes les îles du Cap-vert ne peut être comparé à des vendeurs de rue sans lieu ni charge… Que vous nous décriviez comme "attrape touristes" est insupportable au regard de notre démarche désintéressée, 100% équitable, et du nombre de familles que nous faisons vivre depuis plus de cinq ans.
Bonne route !
