title: Un lieu authentique pour acheter de l'artisanat.
text: J'adore. Ici, on fabrique les choses que l'on vend, du moins presque toutes. Il est possible de voir les artisans travailler le cuir, le bois, le tissu ou l'argent. Il faut négocier, bien sûr, mais les prix sont raisonnables. L'ambiance est amicale, sans trop d'insistance.

title: Sympathique
text: Habitant à Thiès pour quelques mois, je me rends souvent au village arti. Très globalement, les vendeurs sont très agréables. Il y en a toujours quelques exceptions qui cherchent à imposer des prix élevés. Mais généralement, les vendeurs proposent de bons prix (à condition de négocier un peu  rekk 🙄) ! :)

title: Un lieu de flâneries très accueillant
text:
C'est un véritable village d'artisans. Ce ne sont pas que des vendeurs ou revendeurs comme dans d'autres villages artisanaux du pays. Ici nous voyons bon nombre de véritables artisans, que ce soit dans le cuir, le bois, l'argent, les tissages ou la couture!
Cela fait 12 ans que je le fréquente régulièrement, et il y a toujours de la nouveauté et quelque chose d'original. Plusieurs des artisans sont devenus de véritables amis au fil du temps...

title: Excellente adresse
text: Je vous recommande cette adresse. Magasin très chic et les prix restent raisonnables par rapport aux rares boutiques de souvenirs à Mindelo. Un large choix de cadeaux ou de souvenirs. Je me suis fait plaisir 😊

placeInfo.name: Capvertdesign+Artesanato
placeInfo.address: 10/12 Rua da Luz Centre Historique, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 1054 Cape Verde

title: best souvenirs
text: Probably the best shop on the islands to buy souvenirs! All made on Cape Verde, for different prices...

placeInfo.name: Capvertdesign+Artesanato
placeInfo.address: 10/12 Rua da Luz Centre Historique, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 1054 Cape Verde

title: Très belle boutique
text: Belle boutique avec des choses originales. Vous y trouverez quelque chose pour offrir à l'un de vos proches. Ils ont un large choix de décoration traditionnelle.

placeInfo.name: Capvertdesign+Artesanato
placeInfo.address: 10/12 Rua da Luz Centre Historique, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 1054 Cape Verde

title: Artesanato & Design
text:
Conceito interessante. Artesanato de qualidade com design contemporâneo oriundo de vários pontos do arquipélago. 
Os preços são um pouco mais elevados do que em outras lojas, mas aqui não se compra gato por lebre.

placeInfo.name: Capvertdesign+Artesanato
placeInfo.address: 10/12 Rua da Luz Centre Historique, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 1054 Cape Verde

title: Showroom Design e Artesanato do Cabo Verde
text:
Boa qualidade, bom gosto e sensibilidade seriam os adjetivos que usaria nesta descrição. Para mim melhor local de comprar lembranças de Cabo Verde não somente de Mindelo mas de todas as localidades e ilhas. A proprietária escolhe as peças pessoalmente e quando esta na loja tem o bom tom de atender com alegria. 

Cabe lembrar que não estamos falando de uma loja de lembrancinhas, mesmo as tendo, estamos falando de um showroom de design e artesanato e isso tem seu custo, mas sinceramente acho que vale. 

Iria a algumas outras ilhas antes de voltar para o Brasil, mas não me arrependi de comprar presentes para a família lá. Uma observação de uma olhada no andar de cima da loja que se encantará com alguns artistas de Cabo Verde expostos e já no térreo atenção para confecção local ( lindo corte).

placeInfo.name: Capvertdesign+Artesanato
placeInfo.address: 10/12 Rua da Luz Centre Historique, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 1054 Cape Verde

title: Venda de artesanato local
text: Uma belíssima loja de venda de artesanato local, genuíno caboverdeano e de boa qualidade artística, que contrasta e ainda bem com a venda de outros artesanatos que se dizem caboverdeanos e não são.

placeInfo.name: Capvertdesign+Artesanato
placeInfo.address: 10/12 Rua da Luz Centre Historique, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 1054 Cape Verde

title: Great shop, with original capverdian artesanto articles
text:
Loved the shop, it has variety and a wide price range.
I was able to find souvenirs for family and friends.

placeInfo.name: Capvertdesign+Artesanato
placeInfo.address: 10/12 Rua da Luz Centre Historique, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 1054 Cape Verde

title: Sehr schönes Kapverdisches Kunsthandwerk
text: Ein tolles Geschäft auf zwei Etagen mit sehr schönen Möbeln und Kunsthandwerk. Es lassen sich aber auch kleine Souveniers zum Mitnehmen finden. Wir haben einen sehr schönen Bildband gekauft.

placeInfo.name: Capvertdesign+Artesanato
placeInfo.address: 10/12 Rua da Luz Centre Historique, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 1054 Cape Verde

title: Acquisti
text: Bellissima esposizione di oggetti artigianali gioielli oggetti per la casa... non le solite "cineserie" ma originalità e ottima fattura caratterizzano gli articoli di questo negozio. Buon shopping!

placeInfo.name: Capvertdesign+Artesanato
placeInfo.address: 10/12 Rua da Luz Centre Historique, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 1054 Cape Verde

title: Boutique très sympa
text: Souvenirs à tous les prix ... vaut le détour ... accueil très sympathique mais ça ce n'est pas exceptionnel au cap vert !!

placeInfo.name: Capvertdesign+Artesanato
placeInfo.address: 10/12 Rua da Luz Centre Historique, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 1054 Cape Verde

title: Une belle boutique
text:
Incontestablement une belle boutique !  Agréable à visiter et bien agencée
accueil aimable.  j'y ai trouvé un joli livre sur le cap vert ( l'Archipel par ses habitants)
Il faut noter que l'artisanat du cap vert n'est pas exceptionnellement riche ( par rapport à d'autres pays ) aussi il faut chercher ! il y a pas mal de petits souvenirs d'intérêt moyen.  Mais il y a aussi de jolies pièces voir des pieces magnifiques comme ce mortier avec son pilon ! superbe ! j'avais bien envie de craquer mais l'encombrement et le fait que nous avions plusieurs transferts sur d'autres iles m'ont dissuadé . j'ai été un peu déçu au niveau peintures , aquarelles etc  choix limité ... mais c'est incontestablement la boutique de Mindelo ou il faut passer !

placeInfo.name: Capvertdesign+Artesanato
placeInfo.address: 10/12 Rua da Luz Centre Historique, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 1054 Cape Verde

title: Beautiful building & shop
text:
This shop has a beautiful, light architecture. Owned by a french couple, it only sells original, Cape verdian items, made by local people, in every price range. 

I loved it and went there twice to by some small souvenirs. And to look...

placeInfo.name: Capvertdesign+Artesanato
placeInfo.address: 10/12 Rua da Luz Centre Historique, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 1054 Cape Verde

title: Souvenirs pour tous les goûts, toutes les bourses
text:
Cette boutique de souvenirs artisanaux (qui plus est) est très riches en articles de déco ou fonctionnels (cuisine, vêtements,...) Dommage que nos valises aient été trop petites & que nous voyagions par avion car on aurait bien ramené qq meubles ou tableaux d'artisans/artistes locaux ! 
Accueil sympathique & chaleureux.

placeInfo.name: Capvertdesign+Artesanato
placeInfo.address: 10/12 Rua da Luz Centre Historique, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 1054 Cape Verde

title: Wonderful Selection
text: Such a joy to see such a selection of arts and crafts ...many local.  Paintings, artwork, clay work, basket work ....something for everyone.  French spoken and helpful if you can speak the language. Didn't find the staff over helpful, but they certainly packed everything well, and can certainly recommend a visit.

placeInfo.name: Capvertdesign+Artesanato
placeInfo.address: 10/12 Rua da Luz Centre Historique, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 1054 Cape Verde

title: Excellent selection of local art and craft
text: This large store hosts a wide and varied selection of local items and is perfect for that souvenir or gift for someone special.  The staff are warm and friendly,too and prices are good.

placeInfo.name: Capvertdesign+Artesanato
placeInfo.address: 10/12 Rua da Luz Centre Historique, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 1054 Cape Verde

title: Un espace inattendu
text:
On ne s'attend pas à Mindelo de trouver une boutique si spacieuse et moderne, fourmillant d'objets de toutes tailles et sorte, tant pour la déco que pour des petits cadeaux souvenirs,  le tout fabriqué SUR PLACE !
C'est un vrai Bonheur que de déambuler dans cette "boutique-loft"où rien ne dénote, tout donne envie !
Pour couronner le tout, un accueil souriant et adorable !
Passage obligé !

placeInfo.name: Capvertdesign+Artesanato
placeInfo.address: 10/12 Rua da Luz Centre Historique, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 1054 Cape Verde

title: Moderno
text: A melhor loja para comprar artigos com design local, mas muito caro, o que leva as pessoas a comprar noutros locais, mas vale a pena visitar...

placeInfo.name: Capvertdesign+Artesanato
placeInfo.address: 10/12 Rua da Luz Centre Historique, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 1054 Cape Verde

title: Artesanías y productos de diseño
text: Es una tienda grande, que usa materiales locales para diseños más modernos. Tienen textiles que usan la "manta da Terra", textil artesanal. Hay productos de Coco, piedra volcánica, cuadros de artistas locales. Vale muchísimo la pena visitar la tienda. Los precios son razonables

placeInfo.name: Capvertdesign+Artesanato
placeInfo.address: 10/12 Rua da Luz Centre Historique, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 1054 Cape Verde

title: Authentisches Kunsthandwerk von den Kapverden
text: Als wir nach einem Ort suchten, um auf den Kapverden hergestellte Souvenirs zu kaufen, empfahl uns eine Einheimische dieses Geschäft. Hier gibt es die unterschiedlichsten Mitbringsel: Schmuck, Geschirr, Spielzeug und sogar Möbel - um nur ein paar zu nennen. Die Verkäuferinnen waren sehr nett, und man konnte mit Kreditkarte bezahlen. Hier ist auf jeden Fall etwas für jeden Schenkenden und zu Beschenkenden etwas dabei.

placeInfo.name: Capvertdesign+Artesanato
placeInfo.address: 10/12 Rua da Luz Centre Historique, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 1054 Cape Verde

title: Local para compras
text: Ótimo para os viajantes que desejam comprar as tão desejadas lembranças da viagem. Oferece várias opções de artesanato local.

placeInfo.name: Capvertdesign+Artesanato
placeInfo.address: 10/12 Rua da Luz Centre Historique, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 1054 Cape Verde

title: Nice
text:
Very interesting structure that is in wonderful shape. Its quite Portuguese as is resembles a structure in Lisbon. 

Houses a museum of naval artifacts.

placeInfo.name: Torre de Belem
placeInfo.address: Avenida de Republica, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 2110 Cape Verde

title: Museo do Mar
text: Replica of the famous tower in Lisbon right next to the fish market. Inside there is a maritime museum with some finds that were recovered from ships that sank off the islands.  English descriptions only on the first two floors. There is a beautiful view from the roof. Entrance fee 3€ or 300 escudos.

placeInfo.name: Torre de Belem
placeInfo.address: Avenida de Republica, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 2110 Cape Verde

title: Décevant
text:
La visite se fait en quelque temps. Pensez à bien arriver à l'heure d'ouverture pour ne pas rester bloqué dans les escaliers plutôt étroits.
Il n'y a que très peu d'explications, seule la vue vaut peut être le détour.
Les détenteurs d'une Lisboa Card bénéficient d'une file d'attente rapide à la billetterie.

placeInfo.name: Torre de Belem
placeInfo.address: Avenida de Republica, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 2110 Cape Verde

title: schöne Aussicht von der Dachterrasse
text: Der Turm ist an der Küstenstraße nahe dem Fischmarkt ein Blickfang. Das Museum ist einfach, aber es lohnt sich, hineinzugehen, weil man dann den super Ausblick von der Dachterrasse aus genießen kann.

placeInfo.name: Torre de Belem
placeInfo.address: Avenida de Republica, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 2110 Cape Verde

title: MIndelo's Museum of the Sea is a real "Must See"
text:
Mindelo's Museum of the Sea is a gem -- located in the repurposed Torre de Mindelo national monument (which was modeled after Lisbon's Torre de Belem), the museum chronicles northern Cape Verde's rich maritime history.  

Featured exhibits include such themes as whaling, warships, migration, bio-diversity,  aquatic archeology and even music!

The museum also offers for sale books, mostly in Portuguese, about Cape Verde.

placeInfo.name: Torre de Belem
placeInfo.address: Avenida de Republica, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 2110 Cape Verde

title: Magnífico
text: Faz-nos lembrar a partida das caravelas de Lisboa….Cidade lindíssima. Gente hospitaleira. Parece que estamos em Portugal.

placeInfo.name: Torre de Belem
placeInfo.address: Avenida de Republica, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 2110 Cape Verde

title: Kopia wieży z Belem k. Lisbony
text: Znane miejsce w Mindelo, przy nabrzeżu. Warto się przejść. Piękny widok na nabrzeży, łodzie, rybacy sprzedający świeżo złowione ryby, panowie siedzący na nabrzeży, rozprawiający, grający w karty, lokalne planszówki.

placeInfo.name: Torre de Belem
placeInfo.address: Avenida de Republica, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 2110 Cape Verde

title: Tour de bélem
text: On a l’impression que c’est la tour d’un château qui est au bord d’une plage. La vue en haut de la tour est magnifique. Je vous conseille de monter tout en haut en une seule fois pour éviter d’attendre entre chaque étage. Près de l’entrée on peut voir les prisons et l’emplacement des canons

placeInfo.name: Torre de Belem
placeInfo.address: Avenida de Republica, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 2110 Cape Verde

title: klein museumpje met goed uitzicht op de baai
text:
Een mooi verzorgd museum met een mooi uitkijkpunt bovenaan. 
Voor 2000 escudos p.p. krijg je toegang tot het museum. Er staan enkele curieuze items maar ook foto's met uitleg over de walvisjacht, de oorlog, muzikanten, etc. Kortom een kijk in de geschiedenis van Kaapverdië

placeInfo.name: Torre de Belem
placeInfo.address: Avenida de Republica, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 2110 Cape Verde

title: Pessima imitazione
text: Non mi è piaciuta, ammirevole l’idea, nonostante sia  il monumento più “grande” e vistoso nei paraggi è comunque estremamente più contenuto dell’originale portoghese.

placeInfo.name: Torre de Belem
placeInfo.address: Avenida de Republica, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 2110 Cape Verde

title: En famille février 2020
text: Une petite réplique à visiter pour 200 Escudos en plein cœur de Mindelo. Belle vue sur les marchés de la ville une fois sur la terrasse. A faire

placeInfo.name: Torre de Belem
placeInfo.address: Avenida de Republica, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 2110 Cape Verde

title: Museum
text: Der etwa 100 Jahre alte Turm ist kein architektonisches Schmuckstück, ist durch Einheimische durchaus belebt und beherbergt ein Meeresmuseum.

placeInfo.name: Torre de Belem
placeInfo.address: Avenida de Republica, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 2110 Cape Verde

title: A not to be missed museum of the sea.
text:
A museum of the sea; with many old pictures of how the port looked , when it was an important coaling station for shipping. The history of the visiting whaling ships needing local people to work upon them.
Don't miss the fine views of the harbour and town, from the top of the building.

placeInfo.name: Torre de Belem
placeInfo.address: Avenida de Republica, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 2110 Cape Verde

title: Mooi gerestaureerde toren van waaruit je een mooi uitzicht hebt op de haven van Mindelo
text: Deze authentieke toren is prachtig gerestaureerd, met dank aan een subsidie uit Portugal. Vanaf deze toren heb je een prachtig uitzicht op de haven van Mindelo. De lokale bevolking legt er een kaartje en op de rand bij het strand wordt de versgevangen vis schoon gemaakt.

placeInfo.name: Torre de Belem
placeInfo.address: Avenida de Republica, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 2110 Cape Verde

title: Digna de ver
text: Es uno de los lugares de más interés de Lisboa.Las vistas son espectaculares puesto que está en plena mar.se divisa el oceanográfico y otros lugares de interés como el monumento a la reconquista

placeInfo.name: Torre de Belem
placeInfo.address: Avenida de Republica, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 2110 Cape Verde

title: Très décevant
text: On a mis du temps à comprendre ce que c’était tellement elle est petite! (Surtout quand on a vu la tour de Bélèm du Portugal). En plus de cela, impossible de monter à l’intérieur malgré que nous étions dans les heures d’ouvertures: une vraie déception! Aucune raison de se déplacer pour cela!

placeInfo.name: Torre de Belem
placeInfo.address: Avenida de Republica, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 2110 Cape Verde

title: a copy of the BelemTour of Lisboa
text: Just a copy of the Belem Tour of Lisboa, nothing special here. It is close to the sea and the city center.

placeInfo.name: Torre de Belem
placeInfo.address: Avenida de Republica, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 2110 Cape Verde

title: Unspektakuläres Fotomotiv am Hafen
text: Am besten macht sich der Torre de Belem als Hintergrund für ein Hafenfoto. Auf dem Weg zum Fischmarkt kommt man direkt daran vorbei. Es lohnt sich jedoch nicht, extra wegen diesem Gebäude nach Mindelo zu kommen.

placeInfo.name: Torre de Belem
placeInfo.address: Avenida de Republica, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 2110 Cape Verde

title: niet de moeite waard
text:
zeer oud geëtaleerd. niet alles in het Engels vertaald. Zit weinig logica in, gaat met name over de walvisvangst. 
Gebouw zelf is meer de moeite waard dan het museum gehalte.
Bovenop de toren kun je mooi over Mindelo uitkijken, dat is wel de moeite waard.

placeInfo.name: Torre de Belem
placeInfo.address: Avenida de Republica, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 2110 Cape Verde

title: Réplica pouco fiel
text:
Quem conhece a Torre de Belém fica muito decepcionado com esta réplica muito pouco fiel.
Infelizmente não tive tempo de visitar o museu.

placeInfo.name: Torre de Belem
placeInfo.address: Avenida de Republica, Mindelo, Sao Vicente 2110 Cape Verde

title: Super!
text: Très bon magasin d'art artisanal et FairTrade. Tout est fabriqué sur l'île, les produits cosmétiques sont également de très bonne qualité. Toutes les vendeuses étaient parfaites!

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art
placeInfo.address: Rua 1 de Junho Predio Plaza, Santa Maria, Ilha do Sal 4111 Cape Verde

title: Muito giro tudo e causa linda. Compensa e recomendo
text: Muito giro tudo e causa linda. Os produtos são tradicionais e especiais. Tem desde produtos cosméticos como decorativos e com utilidade

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art
placeInfo.address: Rua 1 de Junho Predio Plaza, Santa Maria, Ilha do Sal 4111 Cape Verde

title: Negozio artigianale
text: Personale molto gentile e disponibile, la ragazza che ci ha serviti parlava bene italiano. Abbiamo comprato caffè del luogo e un liquore tipico, tutto eccellente! Consiglio vivamente questo negozio se volete portarvi a casa un souvenir artigianale.

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art
placeInfo.address: Rua 1 de Junho Predio Plaza, Santa Maria, Ilha do Sal 4111 Cape Verde

title: Lovely fair trade shops
text: Lovely shops in Sal with fair trade  products to support local artisans. Includes local liquors as well. Visit more than one as they have different products

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art
placeInfo.address: Rua 1 de Junho Predio Plaza, Santa Maria, Ilha do Sal 4111 Cape Verde

title: As nossas compras
text:
Djunta Mo Art, uma loja sustentável com produtos locais e de cariz solidário, da qual, ficamos ainda mais fãs.
Sem dúvida a melhor loja para comprar souvenirs.
Adorei o atendimento. Super simpáticas e atenciosas.
Recomendo ❤️ 

Maria e Diogo

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art
placeInfo.address: Rua 1 de Junho Predio Plaza, Santa Maria, Ilha do Sal 4111 Cape Verde

title: Lovely shop ♥️
text: We were looking for some native made art and luckily found this amazing shop on the main turist street of Santa Maria town. Great selection of wares and amazing staff. I definitely recommend this little shop 👍🏾

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art
placeInfo.address: Rua 1 de Junho Predio Plaza, Santa Maria, Ilha do Sal 4111 Cape Verde

title: Da farci un salto!
text:
E’ un negozio molto carino, con prodotti creati da artigiani capoverdiani.
Ci sono moltissime idee molto graziose, etiche, di fair trade, che cercano di opporsi alla concorrenza cinese nell’ambito dei souvenir.

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art
placeInfo.address: Rua 1 de Junho Predio Plaza, Santa Maria, Ilha do Sal 4111 Cape Verde

title: Netter Laden
text:
Netter Laden mit nettem Personal.
Man wird weder aufdringlich dazu aufgefordert den Laden zu betreten, noch wird man drinnen bedrängt oder zum kaufen überredet. Es wird gefragt, ob man hilf ebenötigt odernur schauen möchte und kann sich dann im aller ruhe umsehen. 
Es gibt einen Taste-Stand für die diversen Liköre an dem man freundlich beraten wird.

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art
placeInfo.address: Rua 1 de Junho Predio Plaza, Santa Maria, Ilha do Sal 4111 Cape Verde

title: great present
text: We  just came back from our trip and got a beautiful colorful totebag as a present for our daughter and she loves it so much. It’s very good quality with a pocket inside and a cute button. everyone was so nice! Thank u!

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art
placeInfo.address: Rua 1 de Junho Predio Plaza, Santa Maria, Ilha do Sal 4111 Cape Verde

title: Volle Empfehlung
text:
Toller Laden mit nachhaltigen und fair trade Artikeln. Tolles Projekt, dass der Bevölkerung zu gute kommt. Die Produkte sind schön gemacht und nicht so ein Ramsch, den man sonst überall aufgeschwatzt bekommt... 
Personal war freundlich und unaufdringlich. Bezahlung war auch in € kein Problem.

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art
placeInfo.address: Rua 1 de Junho Predio Plaza, Santa Maria, Ilha do Sal 4111 Cape Verde

title: Fair trade, no scams
text: The place to buy locally produces goods in Sal. Actual local goods and a good purpose. Polite service, no pressuring.

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art
placeInfo.address: Rua 1 de Junho Predio Plaza, Santa Maria, Ilha do Sal 4111 Cape Verde

title: Skvělé nakupování.
text:
Je to nádherný obchůdek se skvělou obsluhou. Holky jsou milé a příjemné.
Koupili jsme několik dárků a byli jsme moc potěšení jak nás obsloužily a přijaly od mé ženy jako dárek pár obyčejných náramků že skla. Zde je svět plný emocí a krásných výrobků. 
Určitě se tam jednou vrátíme. 
Renata a Anton Czech Republik.
Děkujeme.

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art
placeInfo.address: Rua 1 de Junho Predio Plaza, Santa Maria, Ilha do Sal 4111 Cape Verde

title: Fair trade and craft beer
text: Small shop in the main pedestrian street. Wide range of fair trade souvenirs and other stuff including excellent craft beers

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art
placeInfo.address: Rua 1 de Junho Predio Plaza, Santa Maria, Ilha do Sal 4111 Cape Verde

title: Artesanato de verdadeiros artesãos Cabo-Verdeanos
text: Loja muito acolhedora, funcionárias simpáticas e muito produtos e artigos artesanais naturais de Cabo-Verde.

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art
placeInfo.address: Rua 1 de Junho Predio Plaza, Santa Maria, Ilha do Sal 4111 Cape Verde

title: Muy recomendable
text: La tienda está situada al lado de la playa, me atendieron muy bien, los productos son naturales y de calidad, encuentras alimentación, cosmética, regalos y joyería artesanal. Muy recomendable, la atención de las dependienta muy amable. Si quieres contribuir al comercio justo esta es tu tienda.

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art
placeInfo.address: Rua 1 de Junho Predio Plaza, Santa Maria, Ilha do Sal 4111 Cape Verde

title: Loja de produtos regionais produzidos por cooperativas locais
text: A loja oferece boas opções em produtos alimentare e bebidas locais, além de artesanato, produzidos por cooperativas caboverdianas, com certeza um local a ser visitado se procura produtos regionais ou pequenas prendas. As geleias produzidas com frutas das ilhas são maravilhosas, já testamos todas, nenhuma deixou a desejar!

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art
placeInfo.address: Rua 1 de Junho Predio Plaza, Santa Maria, Ilha do Sal 4111 Cape Verde

title: Fair trade
text:
Place whith fantastic customer service, explaining everything bout the objects we wanted to buy.
Great prices for fair trade.
must visit

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art
placeInfo.address: Rua 1 de Junho Predio Plaza, Santa Maria, Ilha do Sal 4111 Cape Verde

title: Such a wonderful experience
text:
🇪🇸Mis padres fueron de vacaciones a Cabo Verde decidieron pasarse por esta tienda para comprar unos souvenirs. La atención excelente y los productos que tienen son preciosos. Realmente vale la pena apostar por el comercio justo y local. Además, ellas son majisimas y su trabajo es delicado. Muchas gracias!

🇬🇧My parents went on vacation to Cabo Verse and decided to go to this shop to buy some souvenirs. The customer service was excellent and the products that they have are beautiful. Investing in local and fair trade is worth it! Besides, they are very nice and their work is done delicately! Thanks!

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art
placeInfo.address: Rua 1 de Junho Predio Plaza, Santa Maria, Ilha do Sal 4111 Cape Verde

title: Fantastic shop for souvenirs and gifts! Fair trade and supporting local craftspeople.
text: Amazing little shop filled with fantastic, locally made gifts to take home as souvenirs or gifts. The staff were really friendly and helpful. I loved the fact that purchases support local producers and many of the items are made with recycled materials. Support the local economy and shop here!

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art
placeInfo.address: Rua 1 de Junho Predio Plaza, Santa Maria, Ilha do Sal 4111 Cape Verde

title: Souvenirs
text: Gostei do conceito da loja, em que os produtos vendidos eram feitos em Cabo Verde. Estive duas vezes na loja da Rua 1 de Junho e a simpatia das funcionárias foi imensa.

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art
placeInfo.address: Rua 1 de Junho Predio Plaza, Santa Maria, Ilha do Sal 4111 Cape Verde

title: Art centre with pedigree
text: I was invited for a cocktail at this centre and was really impressed; I never new it existed despite my long stay in Lagos. It is tucked in a quiet part of old Ikoyi. Art lovers will be glad to visit.

title: Great shop for gifts
text: Great fair trade shop in the heart of Santa Maria  with some beautiful gifts for all my family back home. A welcome non-pushy shop compared with others in Santa Maria

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art
placeInfo.address: Rua 1 de Junho Predio Plaza, Santa Maria, Ilha do Sal 4111 Cape Verde

title: The ONLY place to buy genuine Cabo Verde crafts & souvenirs
text:
Very friendly and welcoming staff. You felt immediately at ease when you entered the shop, and the assistant was very knowledgeable and helpful. She told you the background of any of the items for sale, where they came from and how they were made. The shop also has a partnership with the island prison whereby inmates take craft classes and the goods are sold here.

No sales pressure whatsoever. Relaxed and friendly. 

Reasonably priced and genuine locally produced goods. Visit here safe in the knowledge that your money is kept local.

title: Djunta Mo Art
text: Following recommendations I visited both Djunta mo Art shops in Santa Maria. The shop assistants were lovely and did not pressurise you to make a purchase. I love the fact that their items are made on the islands of CV by a cooperative and profits are ploughed back into the cooperative. I appreciate that all souvenier shops and stalls have to make a living but a lot of their products are imported from the likes of China so therefore not authentic to CV. Go and take a look, their products are not expensive.

title: A Laid-Back Lagos Icon with Real Afrobeat Spirit
text:
Visited: Wednesday 13th August 2025

We dropped into the New Afrika Shrine on a midweek night while in Lagos visiting family, and ended up catching a free rehearsal by Femi Kuti & The Movement—a real treat for first-time visitors.

Entry was free and we walked straight in—no queue, no ID check. The place had a relaxed, almost hippie vibe: murals, pool tables (₦500 a game), small stalls selling jewellery, food, merch even vapes, plus a big stage upfront. At the back, TVs were showing the Tottenham v PSG game on mute while the band played. There was a noticeable whiff of weed in the air, and we were even asked a few times if we wanted to buy some (even by security)—so be aware that anything goes here. Cats wandered about which we were sure to keep away from as we didn't want to catch anything!

We arrived late but caught around 90 minutes. The sound wasn’t perfect—muddled at times—but it was fun seeing the band fine-tune their set. Toward the end, dancers pulled a few willing participants from the crowd onto the stage, which really captured the communal energy the Shrine is famous for. On a busy night the tables and chairs would likely be cleared for standing space, but during rehearsal it was easy to sit anywhere and still have a great view.

Drinks were good value. While my cousins ordered beers, I asked for a whiskey and Coke and was surprised when the server returned with a full bottle of Jameson’s (₦35k ≈ £17)—so we just rolled with it. Service was great: staff were attentive, friendly, and happy to chat. I was even challenged to a few games of pool with one of the bartenders. Merch was also reasonably priced—t-shirts around ₦17k (£8). We didn’t try food, though sellers walked around with snacks; personally, I’d be cautious if you have dietary restrictions like I do.

Cleanliness was questionable: toilets fine (just used urinals), and while the Shrine isn’t polished by any means, it felt comfortable and relaxed (If you have ever been to Nimbin in Australia, it reminded me of the vibe there). Smoking (weed, cigarettes and vapes) is common but the space is large enough that it’s not overwhelming. No issues with mosquitoes, though Lagos realities mean you might see a roach or two.

Outside the venue can feel a little sketchy—“area boys” will approach asking for money when you arrive or leave. They weren’t aggressive, more joking than threatening, and security seemed to keep an eye on things. As with anywhere in Nigeria, just a polite “sorry, no” works if you don’t want to give. Although giving out a few thousand Naira makes everyone happy and doesn't hurt the wallet too much.

Highlights: the welcoming people, live music, and affordable drinks/pool games.

Verdict: 4/5 stars. A must-visit for music lovers, culture/history fans, budget travellers, and anyone wanting to soak up authentic Lagos Afrobeat energy. Come with an open mind, and you’ll have a memorable night.

title: my absolute favorite part of Lagos
text: This was my absolute favorite part of my month in Lagos. Femi Kuti's performance was so passionate. The musicians & dancers were incredibly energetic. I had an absolute blast & my only regret is that I couldn't attend another show while I was there. Visiting the Shrine will be top of my list when I return to Lagos next

title: My expérience
text:
I am giving a 5 star yes ! And that’s because  I use to enjoy the show each time I visit Nigeria I am always there to see femi most especially. 
But yesterday I went to Made show and the way the people at the gate look down on us it was shocking their attitude of discrimination without knowing who we are was awful .I love to be at the front role so I can see the show properly .And I have no Idea that I need to make a reservation online before so on getting there after paying the individual tickets for 3 of us and find out on getting inside that there is no space at the front role where I normally seat when ever am there ! So  i decided to find out how much it cost to use the front role and the ladies at the gate reply was the table are for  VIP so I ask the VIP are the people that paid right ? And she reply pls the tables are not for my type. I was so disappointed with there attitude because I have always love the African shrine. I think they should work on the worker with good manners  thanks . But anyway the new African shrine is still a place to be 👌🏼 when ever you visit Lagos Nigeria 👍

title: Great atmosphere and really fun
text: I was lucky enough to be taken here while on a work trip to Lagos and wouldn’t have missed it for anything. So great to see Femi Kuti (it was a Thursday - I’m not sure how often he plays). Lots of people there and good drinks service. We arrived about 9.30pm and it was in full swing. Great atmosphere - loved it! Interestingly my colleague who is from Lagos has only been a couple of times and said it’s more a thing for tourists. But if you’re a tourist, what’s not to like!

title: Shrine
text: This place was great. I really like the way it was newly renovated. If you have not been there recently try and go.you will love it

title: It's an interesting place to visit.
text: It's a very nice place to be. It's one of the freest place on earth. At the New Afrika Shrine, you're free to do whatever you wish to do as long as you aren't hurting anyone.

title: Name Shrine is misleading some tourist.
text: I recently worked with few tourist from Finland on a brief week day visit to Nigeria. They were so excited when I mentioned the visit to the African shrine while we were at Fela museum though I explained the concept  to them. A lot of them were disappointed when we got there. I asked for feed back and some said they imagined the place to be a voodoo shrine kind of place. While others said they were afraid of the high numbers of young men, smokers hanging around the place even without a musical show as I've explained before.

title: HOME OF ENTERTAINMENT
text:
The new Afrika Shrine is what i refers to an home of fun and entertainment. 
The Afrika shrine alway have collections of performance and the chairman of the place Femi Kuti always perform on Thursdays.

The Afrika Shrine is a place to be anytime one is in ikeja axis of lagos.

title: Homage to Fela!
text: This was a must go for me on my second visit to Lagos, with only a few hours before leaving for Nairobi, I had to check in and drink me some palm wine. It seemed as if they were setting up for a performance but I had a flight early the next day I left at 10 pm. Fun fact that is the only place in Lagos you can smoke weed and not get arrested. I am so going back to expereince the music, next time.

title: Great atmosphere
text: I was with a band who were playing here as part of Felabration. The place is much bigger than I expected and has a great atmosphere. There were a lot of people smoking. The place got very full, there were thousands of people there but that was because it was a special night, the previous night I was there it was not nearly so full and was more chilled. The acoustics are not good which is a pity and when it gets packed it can feel a bit unsafe. Overall I would say that if you are going to be in this part of Lagos or indeed in Lagos at all, you must visit this place, it's an amazing experience.

title: True Nigerian
text:
An absolute must when visiting Lagos. Femi Kuti has a show on every Sunday and I was lucky to have also being able to see him perform with his son. What an amazing energy they have on stage. 
Besides there being signs up that no drugs allowed there is a constant smell of weed but as long as you dont mind that its a great place to hang out.

title: Not Bad I Guess
text: If you don't mind the smell of people smoking weed, then you can spend a couple of hours here just chilling with friends.

title: The BEST attraction in Lagos!
text:
This place is full of dancing, singing, food, drinks and Palm Wine (a local favorite). What I like best about the Shrine is the laid back environment. It is the only place in Lagos where  people  are really relaxed and carefree. 

 When you go to the Shrine be sure to bring your desire to have FUN! The place is not expensive and is open seven days a week. Any night is a good night. However, try and go when  Fela's  son plays. The live shows are supernatural almost a spiritual experience,  

 I go there at least two times a  week when I am in Lagos, However, the best time to go is after 7 p.m..  And this place is really not expensive. Lagos is very very expensive but the Shrine is reasonable and is one of the BEST attractions in Lagos.

title: Lagos Folklore at its peak
text: Live show almost every Sunday. Femi Kuti the host will amaze you with wonderful musical performances. A must visit if you are passing by Lagos Nigeria.

title: Fun night at the shrine
text: Great time great performance, Fela left a great legacy God bless him. Cheap entertainment without fanfare or illusions good time beautiful music. I can't help wondering what it would be like if Fela had been around. Amazingly a safe environment as well.

title: Great music!  Very political environment.
text: Saw Femi Kuti put on a truely great show!  I'm not African but still felt welcome.  Reasonable prices.

title: Exclusive Fun in a rough Environment
text:
Different people from different walks of life... 
African Shrine is for everybody. 
The poor and the poorest, The rich and the richest together and share lighters for smokes.. 
If you 're asthmatic you should try not enter this Marijuana licensed Hub. 
African Shrine nick name :KALAKUTA
The best time to enjoy Shrine is Thursday night, There's always a free show from Femi Kuti (The son of the late legend Fela Kuti).

title: Cool Cape Verdean gifts sources locally!
text:
My wife and I stumbled across this amazing shop, located on the main street in Cape Verde, by chance. Well, it was because my wife had toothache and yes, she was able to buy some local Grogg here and it did help her tooth!

Their mission is definitely "no plastics" and the sustainable gifts come in all shapes and sizes, with not a sign of plastic, mainly made by female entrepreneurs.

We spoke to Elsa on 18 January 2023, who explained that all products and gifts are locally sourced and made in Cape Verde. So they really are pushing a number of the UN SDGs like 
*Nr 5: Gender Equality, 
*Nr 8: Decent work and economic growth, 
*Nr 11: Sustainable cities and communities

Would be a great place to educate your kids (and adults) about these important sustainable goals.

title: L'autentica Capo Verde
text:
Durante la nostra vacanza a Santa Maria ci è stato consigliato di fare un giro da Djunta Mo Art, un negozietto tipico nel cuore della città che offre prodotti 100% capoverdiani. Una volta entrati non abbiamo potuto non apprezzare il grazioso artigianato esposto nonché il meritevole concetto che lo anima. A ciò si aggiunge la gentilezza delle ragazze del negozio, molto disponibili, attente e sempre sorridenti. Il nostro consiglio è quello di acquistare i vostri souvenir da Djunta Mo Art: ad un prezzo onesto, potrete acquistare pensierini autentici e che fanno del bene alla comunità capoverdiana. E sono talmente belli che non potranno non essere apprezzati da chi li riceverà. In vendita a un costo simbolico troverete anche un libro di suggestivi scatti fotografici dell'Isola di Sal il cui ricavato andrà a sostegno dell'associazione Nu Bai.
Che dire, buono shopping 100% capoverdiano!

Особенно заспиртованные рыбы, маленькая акула, осьминог и ещё ряд морских обитателей. Пару корабликов, металлические элементы, ископаемые бивни и зубы, ну и всякие плакаты и фото об истории рыболовства и мореплавания за последние лет 150. И пик этого - круговая смотровая площадка на Миндело и бухту. Лучше город можно увидеть только с гор, наверное. за 1 евро, вполне сходная  себе цена за обзорное фото "Я здесь был!"

title: A museum dedicated to traditional artifacts and other artwork from West Africa
text:
The Théodore Monod African Art Museum (Musée Théodore Monod d'Art Africain) is one of the oldest art museums in West Africa, named after Théodore Monod, a French naturalist. Though small, with very little art, the museum is dedicated to African art and culture, showcasing a diverse collection of traditional African artifacts, masks, sculptures, textiles, and more from Senegal, Nigeria, Guinnea-Bissau, Sudan, Mali, Cameroon, Mauritania and Benin.

If you read the reviews, you'd be tempted not to visit. I've learned, after visiting many countries around the world, that reviews are subjective, based on people's opinions about a country, their experiences and their biases. Often it is also informed by their lack of knowledge and the context of what they are observing. Museums are squarely situated within a country's political context. Factors such as budgeting and funding, cultural diplomacy and censorship have an impact. A museum is not just a building filled with things. There's always a rich legacy to learn about.

There is a restaurant on the premises, behind the museum. We almost missed it, because it is not well advertised. It appears not to get too many visitors. We enjoyed a delicious fish dish. 

This museum has a special meaning for us in South Africa. It is situated on Place de Soweto (a well known township in South Africa), on the corner of Nelson Mandela Road.

title: Beautiful West African art in an old Art Deco building
text:
We had visited this museum during our first visit to Dakar in 1979 and it is little change. The main building is perhaps a little dustier but the quality of the pieces in their collection is still outstanding. There were no other exhibits open higher than the first floor but across the interesting courtyard and cafe out back, in the other building there was a fantastic show of contemporary art on the second floor that was air conditioned and had a price catalogue.
Well worth a visit for both the architecture of the original building and the quality and diversity of its west african collection. If there's a temporary exhibition also happening, that would be even more of a reason to go.

title: Avoid this messy museum
text: Foreigners pay 5000CFA (I gladly pay a higher price to enjoy local art). Unfortunately, there is hardly anything to see. Only the ground floor has beautiful masks etc. to see. The floor upstairs had hardly anything of note and was full of garbage. The building itself is beautiful and worth a visit in, although you can actually just walk around it (without a ticket) and enjoy the architecture and foliage. There is no information in English whatsoever. I met some other foreigners who live here and they thought it was not that bad. Of course in Europe, you would pay double this price to see a museum, but for that, it would be clean, orderly, and have more on offer. There was no information that the other buildings housing contemporary art were closed. IFAN should be ashamed of themselves and go and see how nice the Museum of Black Civilisations is!

title: L'Ifan médiocre

text:

Parco era carino e c era una piccola mostra esterna.

title: Enjoy the Art
text:
There is a good range of art work here, from Senegal and the wider continent. I am surprised by some of the reviews here. There is a higher price for overseas visitors but to me this is good policy. It is still a lot less than you would pay to visit most European galleries. 
The building is a little tired, hence four stars, but the art is great. Yes the titles are in French and there is little explanation but if you come here just to enjoy great carving, brilliant fabrics and moving photography you will not be disappointed. 
I think some people may have missed a whole gallery. Across a courtyard is a second building with contemporary art exhibits. It is great to see ancient and modern together in one gallery.

title: Da NON macare
text: Chi ama l’Africa deve vedere questo museo, in specie per capire nel profondo un’arte molto diversa da quella tradizionale; l’Africa ha una sua storia che sarà bene conoscere, né pare giusto parlare di “arte” solo per quella nota e diffusa nel mondo occidentale; museo quindi da NON mancare: osservare all'interno anche foto e riconoscimenti al Nobel italiano Dario Fo.

title: Worth it if you can read French

They have some interesting artifacts from Abomey, Benin as well as the Dogon people and various tribal groups in Senegal. I thought the museum would be much bigger but it is only one floor and there isn't much to see (20-25 minutes is enough to see everything). For 5000CFA that is rather a poor return. Hopefully the museum may be expanded in the future as there is space for it, as well as, one would think, a rather spacious upstairs area.

title: Must visit for anyone in Ghana
text: Visiting SWOPA is a must for anyone who truly wants to get in touch with ghanaian culture. The rooms are amazing and the food is delicious. The pottery and weaving workshops are highly advisable. The shop offers all kinds of traditional pottery and baskets at very reasonable prices. Having lived in Ghana for a while, I know what the right prices are for things here. Usually when you want to buy something, you have to bargain. Locals will then ask ridiculous prices sometimes because they can see you're not Ghanaian. At SWOPA all prices are fixed and all objects are labeled with their price. This makes for a very pleasant and fair shopping experience. If you are interested in buying traditional art or pottery: this is the place to do so. The people are very friendly and for a small fee, someone can drive you around the mesmerising and peaceful landscape.

title: Rustic and Peaceful
text:
Subject: Sirigu Women's Organisation for Pottery and Art Guest House
Location: Bolgatanga, Upper East Region, Ghana, Africa
Title: Rustic and peaceful
ID#: 290117711

Spent 3 days at SWOPA and had a wonderful time. Took Arts classes in the morning and went on several different tours in the afternoon. My brain if fully expanded. The staff are very accommodating and were eager to help as much as needed. Sirigu is up in the most northern part of rural Ghana and was quite a bit more arid and hot as compared to the coast. Took an afternoon tour off grounds and a walking tour of area painted traditional homes. Albert, our tour guide, was very knowledgeable about the area and history. Faustina, the coordinator of the arts classes was invested in our success and enjoyment of the crafts. 

The guest house facilities were rustic but clean. Round traditional huts with electricity and running water (most of the time) Not a 5 star hotel, but mostly clean and comfortable. The extra 15 cedis was well worth the air conditioning.  Electricity was partially solar powered so even with lights out fans and lights work. Water pressure and warmth was great. Food was ok. Food choices were limited.  I will definitely be going back when others come to visit.   We stayed 3 days which was a good amount of time.

title: Testimony to a simple past
text:
Every effort to preserve the memory of the past must be appreciated, even if it deals primarily with former household items or farming utensils as for cattle rearing or milk processing. What the exhibits mainly tell is the fact that life was very simple on Cape Verde in the old days. The products of basketry and pottery, the gourds, mortars and tobacco pipes all lack almost any kind of decoration. A bit more sophisticated are the musical instruments, among them typical ones like a cimboa and cavaquinhos.

All is labeled in Portuguese and English, with much more detailed descriptions in Portuguese. The small museum is housed in a colonial building on the pedestrianised 'Rua Peatonal' (Rua 5 de Julho) and its exhibits are distributed on two floors, one of them being a kind of cellar.

Entrance fee is 200 Esc (2 €). Inside there is also a souvenir-shop with several books in Portuguese on Cape Verde, but also with Fogo wine, sweets and soaps from the islands. When there we were alone and we had the feeling that this museum is not much visited. It was late morning, but just with our arrival a cleaning woman started to wet wipe all the museum's floors.

title: Musée ethnographique très interessant
text:
Tout d'abord, il faut trouver ce musée, la plupart des guides le situent encore sur la place principale d'Assomada alors qu'il a été déplacé depuis juin 2010 à 5 Km d'Assomada à Chao de Tanque ( prendre la route de Puerto Rincao).
Musée ethnographique présentant les divers aspects de la Tabanka, système d'organisation social original. De nombreux objets traditionnels sont présentés, malheureusement les panneaux d'information sont rédigés en portugais sans traduction en anglais ou en français. Si vous trouvez la porte close, n'hésitez pas à faire le tour du bâtiment et à demander aux femmes qui vivent dans les maisons derrière le musée: elles vous ouvriront le musée, vous accompagneront dans votre visite et percevront le droit d'entrée.

title: Amazing History Lesson (April 2019)
text: This was an amazing experience! If you are a history buff, you'll especially love this museum and this particular piece of history. It's located near the water with a beautiful view and not far from the residence of the country's president. Even if you're not much into history, you'll appreciate learning about Amilcar Cabral and everything that he contributed to the history of Cape Verde and the continent of Africa. He was more than a revolutionary; he was integral to the freedom of this beautiful island from her European colonizers. I was very unaware of Cabral's contribution so this was more than a learning experience. I came away with an education and a history lesson I will not soon forget.

placeInfo.name: Sala-Museu Amilcar Cabral
placeInfo.address: 5, Rua Dr. Julio Abreu, Praia, Santiago CP 280 Cape Verde

title: Small but mighty
text:
Based on previous reviews, I had only allowed myself about 30 minutes to visit this museum. It is physically small but has a lot packed into that space, including an interactive video. If you want to learn about Amilcar Cabral and his significance I would suggest leaving a bit more time as there is plenty of text to read. There are also some very personal mementoes, including Cabral's famous hat and his suitcase.

I learnt a lot and felt quite emotional reading the comments in the visitor book!

If you don't have time to visit I would suggest taking a look at the building, as there is a powerful mural painted on the exterior.

title: Father of the Cape Verdean nationality
text:
While walking in the street between the viewpoint Miradouro do Cruzeiro and the church Nossa Senhora da Graça we encountered this small museum, dedicated to the probably most important person in independent Cape Verde's young history.

There is no entrance fee and no gratuity expected, all the lady in charge showed us was an Amilcar-Cabral-T-Shirt to buy as souvenir. The museum, which opened in 2015, consists mainly of photographs, sorted by themes like education, the fight for independence or Cabral's biography. All is labeled in Portuguese only. But for foreign visitors there is a video shown in English (or Portuguese) about Cabral with people talking, who knew Amilcar Cabral personally. One of them was his daughter, whom we then happened to see in front of the museum, when leaving.

title: Musée Honmé et Palais du roi Te Agbanlin à Hogbonou ( Porto Novo ), Patrimoine en péril !!
text:
Ce musée dit Honmé , établi dans l'ancien palais du roi Te Agbanlin (1710-1760) , de Hogbonou , aujourd'hui Porto Novo ( Sud Est du Bénin) , date de 1725 . A cette époque , le puissant  royaume d'Abomey envahit celui d 'Allada ( centre Sud du Bénin actuel ). Ce qui conduit son roi à se réfugier à Hogbonou où depuis 1600 le frère du Premier roi d'Abomey Gangnihessou (1600-1620) , y a régné. Autant dire qu'il s'agit d'une histoire de famille ,mais qu'importe. 

Le roi Te Agbanlin , à son arrivée, trouve une situation difficile où les musulmans Yoruba venus du Nigéria voisin (Royaume d'Oyo ) , occupent la cité . Ici nous rentrons dans la légende avec l'intervention du Dieu vaudou de la nuit, Zangbeto , qui éloigne les mauvais esprits et du coup les occupants Yoruba sont chassés .( SIC)

La dynastie, qui s'y établie, règnera jusqu'en 1882 quand,  pour se protéger de ses ennemis du royaume du Dahomey associé à celui de Ouidah ( Sud Ouest du Bénin actuel)  , le roi Toffa de Porto Novo (1874-1908) , se met sous la protection de la France . Un accord de protectorat est conclu avec Paris .
Face à cette situation de menace de la part du royaume du Dahomey , la France prend prétexte et engage les hostilités contre le roi Béhanzin d'Abomey . En 1894 la France , qui a vaincu toute opposition , établit la colonie du Dahomey . Le port de Porto Novo est florissant ainsi que la cité . Le royaume  ne sera intégrée à la colonie du Dahomey qu'à la mort du roi Toffa en 1908 .  

La visite est décevante , du fait de la vétusté des lieux et ce malgré les explications du guide. Le palais est construit en terre rouge de la région qui , au fil du temps , lui donne une patine grise , faute de restauration  . Il n'y a aucun meuble les pièces sont vides .L' interdiction de prendre des photos , est de mon point de vue contre productive pour la promotion du site . Ceci étant dit , vue l'état des lieux , ce n'est peut être pas souhaitable pour l'instant . Le gouvernement béninois , conscient de la valeur symbolique et touristique du patrimoine , "devrait" engager un programme de rénovation . Je précise aussi que certaines photos qui apparaissent ne correspondent absolument pas à ce lieu , notamment la photo de couverture . Cela a été signalé , mais rien ne bouge !!

Nous entrons dans chaque pièce par une porte basse , qui oblige à se courber et nous sortons par la grande porte , initialement réservée au seul Roi . 
Les pièces se succèdent , avec des fonctions très précises comme , le vestibule , la salle de réception , la salle de la Reine Mère , etc Puis on accède à la salle du Conseil du Roi , Etrangement , une cour à toit ouvert entourée de coursives , possède une cabane très sommaire en branche en son milieu . C'était paraît il le lieu où le jeune roi commençait son apprentissage et où ,  ensuite il pouvait se retirer pour méditer .
L'espace réservé aux multiples épouses du roi , sous la surveillance de la Reine mère. , est à toit ouvert , avec un bassin central vide au milieu d'une coursive . 
Enfin, nous terminons la visite du palais par un grand espace en herbe rase entouré de gradins couverts pour le roi et les dignitaires  et de banquettes pour les spectateurs . Cet espace était réservé pour les manifestations royales .
A l'extérieur ,on peut voir l'arbre de justice puis le tribunal ,avec les attributs traditionnels . 

Des œuvres d'Art inspirées du Vaudou , sont exposées devant l'entrée , comme le Dieu de la foudre,  un serviteur royal au crane rasé , un laboureur , un étrange personnage style robot Antique ou encore un facteur à vélo , métallique et rouillé . C'est de l'art certes , mais un peu désordonné !!
Le terme " Honmé " désigne " ce qui est à l'intérieur de la porte " par extension " le Palais "

Sa majesté est fort aimable et explique à merveille l'histoire de Porto-Novo et de sa famille.

title: Too expensive
text:
As soon as they knew we were intent on buying, coupled with the fact that I am white, meant that I soon resembled the Pied Piper with about 10 traders following me everywhere thrusting their goods into my face.

I see one reviewer says you should divide the initial starting prices by 4-6. That’s about right. We divided the starting prices by 5, thus offering 20 Cedi for what we were initially told was 100. As we had a good idea of the real cost of these things we refused to budge by one single Cedi from our initial offer. It was accepted; though, ultimately we refused to buy due to the trader's attitude and the fact that we thought we could get it cheaper elsewhere.

There is a good range of products available but if you want the same goods for even less then forget this place and go, instead, to Makola market. For a bag that was initially offered to us for 100 Cedi at the Arts Centre and for which we almost paid 20, we found the very same thing at Makola market for 12 Cedi, which we managed to get down to 7. That’s less than £1 (or $1.25) for a hand crafted bag.

I didn’t see many other customers at the Arts Centre so that’s probably why they hassle everyone so much.

title: Pays to shop around!
text:
A convenient place to visit which is nice and close to Accra however, it is extremely overpriced- and that is coming from someone who is half Ghanaian and visited the place with someone who is a Ga!

I purchased two large giraffes which I fell in love with. I then went to the Art centre in Legon and found them for half the price at a higher quality so it definitely does pay to shop around a bit!

It is definitely still worth a visit as it has various places you can purchase fabrics from.

TIPS AND ADVICE:
Very basic toilets are available for a small fee.
Be careful when purchasing wooden articles- ensure they're bug free or it can be hard to get them through customs.
Look around elsewhere before buying unless you really LOVE the item

title: Off the Rack and From the Runway
text:
Ever wondered how some people turn up looking as if they have just walked off the page of a magazine?  

Part of the answer is whatever they have on is from the runway, or a spin-off from one of the seasons. To simplify, it means someone special made the garments, and then have them fitted for the individual. The last step goes a long way in ensuring that whatever you have on, sits just right and you can go on your life with confidence knowing you present the best of you.

One such talented creative dress designers in Ghana is the founder of the label Christie Brown Ghana. 

Her clothes are a well tailored take on African clothing, and have been seen on celebrities and elegant women in many parts of the world. 

Fortunately, she is never boring or self repeating. She continues to come out with items that get collected over time.

It is beautiful to be authentically African yet cosmopolitan and still turn heads in her outfits and accessories anywhere in the world. 

You will find her salon in Osu, and view some of the selections on Instagram. 

I am grateful for her talents.

title: Amazing architecture but generally shut :(
text: We popped into the NT building as it's impressive architecture we assumed the interior would also be impressive. It's really a mothballed theatre space and wasn't really open. I suspect security staff are allowing opportune tours which you pay for but get very little information or guide. We went into the auditorium ascending the stairs, the ground floor doors where locked. There are some amazing sculptures outside and within the building but little explanation of them. The theatre space is very tired and generally dusty it felt uncared for. There where posters for recent shows but am not convinced it open often which is a shame. This building could be a gem if African theatre was performed here or African choirs, music and dance rather than western high arts. There's clearly a lack of investment in staff and maintenance from the government. Never the less I was glad we looked in.

title: Spectacular performance needs more publicity
text:
We happened to chance upon a performance of Alkebulan's Awakening - a performance of dancing with dances from different parts of Africa.

The performance was a wonderful visual spectacle, showing the experience of pre colonial Africa, the coming of colonial powers, slave trade, slavery n the US, post slavery abuse of black people in the US and then an African awakening. The dancing was energetic, subtle and moving with a combination of African and western music. It was 8 months in preparation and a tremendous experience.

But we stumbled on it totally by accident. The hotel knew nothing about it (and the hotel is across the road). The performance deserved to be publicised so much better.

The actual theatre is well appointed with comfortable seats. It is a little shabby in places but considerably better than many other buildings in Accra.

It is a little disconcerting to buy tickets from a man who simply walks up to you on the theatre steps with no ID or anything else to demonstrate that he is actually selling genuine tickets. He was. But this should be somewhat more professional.

The management needs to think more about how to give these good performances the publicity and theatre environment they deserve.

That place would seriously needs to be redecorated and refurbished.

The outside setting is very beautiful but again could be better exploited..
The parking lot seems safe, we never had any issue. We also felt safe inside the theatre.
We hardly see people wandering around apart from taxi drivers outside the premises. Don't walk home on your own though. Being careful is always better!
I dont think there is anything to visit in the theatre during the day. Unless....
However, you cannot live or visit Ghana and never take the opportunity to go and watch a performance there! If you like theatres magic like me, give it a try.

title: GREAT VISIT - MOVED, NOT CLOSED!
text:
There is a lot of conflicting information here. To clarify: this place has moved to an area near Jabi lake off Ring Road 2, near BNL Life Camp and Nisa Premier Hospital. 
(It used to be across from the Sheraton in Wuse, near the CBD). It is not huge or all that visible off the road, and could easily be missed if you/driver doesn’t know it. A hotel car driver should. Also Google Maps should be able to locate the new location (I tried to attach a pic/map, but it wouldn’t load). 

I visited the new location on Sunday, October 13, 2019 around 11 AM and it was very pleasant - about 6 long rows of small stalls selling a variety of art, beads, carvings, clothes, and other items.  The vendors were warm and inviting, and eager to sell but not pushy. I spent 2 1/2 hours and way too much money, quite happily. Some pictures below. A nice way to spend a few hours in Abuja and pick up some quality, reasonably priced reflections of Nigerian culture. Go!

title: Muy recomendable
text:
Habiendo estado en otros mercadillos del centro de Dakar, sin duda este tiene un encanto especial. 
Se encuentra cerca del mercado callejero de pescado, donde los pescadores desembarcan en la orilla de la playa. También hay puestos de venta de verdura, fruta e incluso ganado. Está muy concurrido por la población local.
El mercado de Soumbédioune se compone de varios pasillos con muchas tiendas artesanales donde poder comprar lo que quieras y sin agobios. Yo buscaba un instrumento típico senegalés pero para profesionales y ahí pude encontrarlo. Todo tipo de souvenirs y productos senegaleses por los que regatear hasta llegar al precio que deseas pagar. Los comerciantes son encantadores y se esfuerzan por ofrecerte algo que sea de tu agrado. Me sorprendió incluso que hubiera vendedores que me hablasen con un español perfecto. 
Sin ninguna duda, recomiendo visitarlo.

En clair, on peut diviser par 3 les tarifs annoncés. Armez vous de patience. Les sénégalais sont sympa donc c'est un plaisir.

title: Puro Senegal
text: Como todo mercado Senegales, prepárese a regatear y pagar sobre un tercio del precio inicial. También saber plantarse y comprar realmente lo que uno quiere y no lo que te ofrezcan. Puedes ver en directo como trabajan la madera, aunque hay que vigilar que no te den gato por liebre. Sacar el dinero en pequeñas cantidades y no mostrar a la vista más de lo que se quiera pagar o será imposible seguir bajando el precio. Puede llegar a ser agobiante, hay que ir con ideas claras, pero es imprescindible para vivir Dakar.

title: Al lado del puerto de pescadores

Interesante sin duda.
Aconsejable

title: Incredibile!
text: Un’esperienza che non si dimentica! Sulla spiaggia dell’oceano ci sono barche, calessi, uomini e cavalli. Il profumo del mare è forte, i pesci sono riversati drittamente sulla sabbia (che pare abbia lo stesso ruolo del nostro giaccio). Le trattative vengono condotte li direttamente: tra barche coloratissime che vanno e vengono dal mare e quelle allineate lungo la spiaggia. È da visitare assolutamente!

title: Aggressive vendors
text: Take care; don't enter if you're all by yourself. The vendors can become quite aggressive if you refuse to take a look at their stuff. It was a horrible experience for me and I went with somebody who knows the local culture.

title: Marché artisanal de Soumbédioune
text: A NE PAS CONFONDRE AVEC LE VILLAGE DES ARTS ! Ici vous trouverez de tout mais attention il faut négocier. On trouve des sacs et des chaussures en cuir, en croco, en serpent faits sur place, des sandales, ceintures, des souvenirs en tout genre. Des bracelets, bagues en argent. Des bijoux fantaisie, des sacs en wax et cuir (tissu coloré), des nappes en batik, des paniers...

title: Un monument emblématique
text: C'est un monument emblématique de la ville de Dakar qui domine cette ville cette statue haute de 52mètres est faite de bronze et de cuivre. Le monument représente un couple et son enfant, dressés vers le ciel. Il est officiellement inauguré le 3 avril 2010 lors des cérémonies du cinquantenaire de l'indépendance du Sénégal.

title: A Positive Tribute to African Going Forward with a View
text: One of the tallest statues in the world, this tribute to freedom shows a man standing with a woman and a child pointing forward. Former President Wade called this  "an Africa emerging from the bowels of the earth, leaving obscurantism to go towards the light". The child points to going forward, The walk up incudes 186 steps with convenient stopping points and a bench for resting and enjoying the view. You can also come up by car in a road that is unseen form the front of the statute. During the dry season, the area is very windy, very windy. You can walk up to the base of the statue for a view of the city. The restrooms at the top are closed. Two eateries at street level open for lunch. This significant sculpture is an essential part of every trip to Dakar.

title: Un lieu de mémoire
text: La maison des esclaves de l'ile de Gorée est un incontournable de cette ile cette maison daterait de l'année 1776, elle reste un emblème symbolique pour le pays on nous retrace ici l'histoire de l'esclavage leur traitement et comment ils vivaient parqués dans des cellules très petites et indignes d'un être humain on ressent  beaucoup de souffrance en ce lieu

title: Uma realidade cruel e verdadeira. Poder tocar nestas paredes dá um aperto imenso no coração.
text: A casa dos escravos situada na ilha de Goreé é hoje considerada como um museu. Aqui a história é agoniante fazendo que se engula em seco várias vezes tais foras as atrocidades aqui praticadas. Pequenos espaços destinados aos muitos escravos que por aqui passaram. Eram divididos consuante o género, peso, rubostez física, doenças, virgindade (no caso das meninas). Aqui as famílias eram separadas para sempre. Existem uma porta ( a porta sem retorno) onde os escravos eram vendidos para nunca mais voltarem...

title: Une vraie gifle !

title: Manque des respect!

title: A step back in history
text:
We visited La Maison des Esclaves as part of our TUI day trip to Dakar and Goree Island whilst staying at the RIU Baobab in Ponto. Took a few photos

It was a great day out with a look back into the history, a day out definitely worth doing

title: Reflection
text:
We toured the place on our own as we wanted to take our time
Great respect to Senegalese government for making this a museum lest we forget.
While in there you reflect on what happened in that time at that place and hope it never happens again

title: Eerie
text: A stark reminder of dark times. The island is full of history, this building too with the door of no return. Perhaps more could be done with information boards from other languages but the place itself is well kept.

title: Awful experience
text: Went with an English Guide and was horrified to find halfway through the tour he was publicly lambasted by the Curator who had been giving a loud talk in French to everyone. He didn't like our guide trying to speak to us in English. The Curator was so unbelievably rude in front of so many people. It's about time this place moved with the times and started to label pictures and information in English and if they don't like English guides at the sane time, they allocate specific times for them.

title: A very poignant location and a reminder to us of cruel human behaviour
text: Visited and was very moved by the location. We had a guide who was able to give us an historical account of the House of Slaves. My only complaint was when we visited it was very very busy and some of the property has been damaged. Although it was still a very poignant visit despite the crowds of people there.

title: Lieu à visiter impérativement au Sénégal
text:
Située sur l’île de Gorée, la maison des esclaves est un lieu à visiter impérativement pour comprendre la tragédie de l’esclavage. Je vous conseille d’être accompagné d’un guide qui vous donnera de précieuses informations. 
Nous avions la chance d’avoir comme guide Babacar originaire de l’île de Gorée, avec une culture extraordinaire concernant son île et son pays. 
Merci à lui!
Une visite chargée en émotions qu’aucun mot ne peut décrire !

title: IL FAUT VISITER !
text: Le voyage en bateau navette qui part du port et arrive à l’Ile de Gorée est très folklorique . La visite de la maison des esclaves est intéressante, notre guide était instruit . Il faut aussi se promener dans l’Ile. Les ruelles,  les fleurs c’est très sympathique . Abstraction faites des faits historiques , on pourrait avoir envie de rester quelques jours. Il y a un petit hôtel et évidemment plage populaire

title: Overrated
text: It's an important part of history that should not be forgotten but the 'house' itself is not so   worthy. The house has been damaged by visitors. The information panels are old.

title: A faire absolument

title: Not to be Missed!!
text:
My wife and myself lived in Dakar in the early/mid 80s and we are currently paying our first return visit and we went to Goree Island on Sunday.

Unlike Dakar, Goree was largely unchanged including our favourite Restaurant Chez TonTon was still doing a thriving trade (see subsequent Review) and - of course -  La Maison des Esclaves. The latter is really what Goree Island is all about and somewhere all visitors to Dakar should make an effort to see.

The attraction is well laid out and it is difficult not to feel for the 20 million (a third of which never survived the horrendous shipping conditions) slaves who passed through Goree during the 300 years it was actively a key part of the Slave Trade. Indeed the door of no return is one feature of ‘La Maison des Esclaves’ that really sticks in my mind!

This really is one attraction not to be missed!

title: GO BACK IN TIME
text: Visiting this place was very educative albeit a bit sad.  You could literally feel the sadness housed in the building.  And as with all things life, you come away shocked at how above the squalor and pain sits a very comfortable accommodation for .the slave masters who had others below in the dungeons in chains

text:

Unfortunately taking of pictures within the museum itself isn't allowed, hence the lack of pictures here. A visit there starts off with a walk through the courtyard (after paying a N300 entry fee) and its scattering of a few displays of artwork and information boards, followed by a walk through the interior area which turns out to be much more expansive than it appears from the outside. The interior contains a sizable display of different artifacts from several Nigerian tribes. It's mostly a self-guided tour (I.e. no tour guide) but most of the arts on display have small signs attached to them providing basic information about each artifact. 

With some investment to make the place a bit more modern and lively, the museum has potential to be a very good tourist attraction.

title: We were hoping for more (not food — the customer service)
text:
I’d really like to give this place 3.5 stars … because despite the middle and end of our cooking class in Cape Coast (the smells as we cooked, and the taste of the food afterward, were incredible!), we were disappointed with the overall customer service.

Perhaps we started the class in a skeptical mood, which didn’t help. We waited for a long time at the Global Mama’s shop for our class to start and no-one gave us any information as to what was happening. A woman finally arrived — no hello and no introduction — and she told our driver to take us to a secondary location.

The location was a small roadside restaurant in the center of town — very authentic, though we waited and waited whilst the woman continued to serve customers and, well, basically ignored us. There was also incredibly loud music playing and at first we couldn’t hear anything the woman (our instructor? — who knew at that point, still no-one told us what was happening…) was saying.

Finally the music was turned down and the woman began to bring ingredients over to the table at which we were sitting. At no point did she introduce herself or ask our names, despite us being the only people in the class.

The class itself was good, though the woman did most of the work — we really only chopped a few veggies and stirred and fanned the boiling pot of oil. This was disappointing as we were hoping for a more hands-on experience.

Note also there’s no toilet at the restaurant for customer use.

At the end we sat down to eat our delicious meal, asked the woman’s name (she was nice enough, just never made the effort to connect with us), and requested the recipes for the meal we’d made. She smiled and said “Absolutely!”. She sent us a copy of *a* recipe, but not the exact food we’d made. I followed up via WhatsApp and she promised to forward the additional information. Two weeks later, I’m still waiting — she hasn’t responded to my requests, though also hasn’t hesitated to send me random, completely unrelated videos via WhatsApp (very strange).

As I said, the food was amazing — but unfortunately the customer service not so much.

title: Great batik workshop
text:
We had a wonderful experience learning to batik from Mavis! We called the morning that we planned to be in Cape Coast and they were so kind to set up the workshop for us on only a few hours notice. 

Mavis met us at the Global Mamas office (where we paid) and then we followed her to her shop, about a 5 minute walk. She gave us stools to sit on under a shaded tent and told us about the process and what all is involved. We each got to select our favorite symbol to stamp our own fabric in the workshop. She was patient with us throughout the process - it requires practice and talent to do well and I have new respect for the artistry! We each came away with our own piece of batik fabric at the end. Mavis’ explanations were great and the kids in the area entertained us as we worked. 

It is a labor intensive process and takes some time to go through each step to allow the dye to absorb and set, and then to remove the wax and dry the print. Mavis was gracious to speed the process along for us because we had less time than the recommended 3 hours. I would strongly recommend allocating plenty of time (that’s why they recommend 3 hours) to ensure you aren’t rushing the process. 

It was a very hot day, so I recommend bringing water. Part of the process includes boiling water so it was smoky (just based on the direction of the wind) which is to be expected. If you plan to head onward to the airport after (like we were) I recommend scheduling it at a time so you can go back to the hotel and shower after.

text:
I recently spent a couple of hours touring the "slave castle". It's hard to be whistling a happy tune as you enter the castle, once it hits you what happened there. The gravity of its size and its purpose hits you in your soul. At it's height the castle shipped off 4,000 slaves a year, mostly to the Americas.  The tour guides are both friendly and knowledgeable   The visit to this slave castle was definitely worth my time and money (the "tour" is NOT handicap accessible!). 
While the castle was worth the drive, the drive itself is not!  Ghana and a few other countries have this curious habit of placing rather large speed bumps on its major two-lane highways - a lot of them (sometimes 3 or 4, one right after another). There must be close to 100 of them (about every 1/2 to 1 mile) between Accra and Cape Coast. They can rattle your teeth even when driving slowly over them!  And of course, cars pass another on curves or going up hills that will get your heart pumping, depending upon how fast or aggressive your driver is. No, there is not a major hospital with modern technology nearby, in case one of the drivers makes a misjudgment (I saw one such accident on the way to the coast. Thankfully it was not a major head-on collision but it was close enough!

title: eye opening visit
text: Arrived at Elmina Castle in January 2020. I believe is was 40 cedi to enter and take the tour. The tour was provided by an employee, a younger girl who was excellent in providing information about the castle and the early days of the slave trade. The tour was in depth and provided a very eye opening account of what went on in this place. Overall this tour was well done and worth the 3h drive from Accra. This trip and a visit to Kukum National Park is do-able in a day from Accra and back.

title: Fascinating and emotional
text: Everybody should visit the Elmina Castle, one of mayn castle along the coast of Ghana where the slavetrade was organised and slaves shipped to the Americas. Built originally by the portugese in 1482 as a trading place it developed into a main central for keeping slaves until they could be put of ships to go across the Atlantic. Feeling the history of tens of thousands of persons that sufferede the horros inside the castle is very emontional. The price for entry - 40 Cedis - includes a very competent guide that will take you around the main spots. The tour takes about 45 minutes.

title: Touching experience
text: The Elmina castle might bring you to tears when you're taken round and told the stories  of the plight of the slaves that once passed through this place. It's a nice place to be and  has good management, the tour guides ar great and has the history at their finger tips

title: Not a Castle, but a Horrible Dungeon
text: It is hard to give a 5 star rating for this dungeon of horrors.  The rating is for the staff and the country that saw fit to maintain this place so that we never forget the horror that was the transatlantic slave trade.  Every African American who visits Ghana must go to this place and experience what our ancestors experienced.  It is unforgettable.  And let not the irony escape you of the horrors that took place right next to the beautiful seaside setting.

title: Emotional eye opening
