title: Septiembre 2014
text: Gore es una bonita isla , desde la cual embarcaban a los esclavos africanos . En la casa de esclavos , había cosas para separar a madres de hijos , para provocarles la dolor al oírlos por los agujeros . Sus dueños vivían en la parte de arriba ,lo cual es un museo de tanto horror vivido .

title: Goree Island
text:
Goree Island is a monumental reminder of the slave trade and the extent of evil the heart of man can conceive. At the same time, it offers opportunity for reflection and reconciliation. 

It takes you into the minds of the slave master and the salves themselves. It is a place that elicits a lot of emotions 

If you visit only one place in Dakar please let it be the Goree Island.

title: Que d'émotion!
text: Tu ne peux pas aller en vacance au Sénégal sans visiter cet endroit! En écoutant les guides, on a l'impression de retourner dans le passé! J'y ai ressenti beaucoup d'émotion et j'ai une cette sensation que les âmes y étaient encore et je ressentais leur douleur! hummm, un lieu incontournable à visiter! C'est une grande partie de l'histoire de l'esclavage!

title: Incontournable de l'histoire de Gorée
text:
Ce site est à visiter absolument pour ne pas oublier ou en savoir un peu plus sur l'histoire de l'esclavage.
A 15h15 il y a les commentaires du conservateur qui reste à notre disposition pour les questions après.
Ce site est émouvant lorsqu'on imagine les conditions des personnes qui sont passées dans cette maison.
Entrée à 500 FCFA (pour les non résidents)

title: Powerful
text: I've been to former slave ports before and they're always poignant for me. This one is no different. Whereas most if the island is a bit of a meat market this place still holds the feel of somewhere with a chequered history. Worth a visit.

title: Besichtigung mit unsern Besuchern aus der Schweiz
text:
Das Schiff wiederum voll ausgelastet,
fuhren wir das 3. Mal zur Sklaveninsel.
Nicht vergessen, den Pass mitzunehmen.
ID genügt nicht!
Ausserdem Mückenspray und einen Fächer 
In der Regenzeit ist es besonders heiss
Es lohnt sich allemal, einen Guide zu nehmen.
Lohnt sicht für jeden!
Warum nur 4 Sterne? 
Man kann sich an einige Verkäufer auf der Insel einfach nicht gewöhnen.

title: Worth a visit for whatever it is worth :)
text: I was at this museum a week ago with my 8 year old and a 10 year old. The Guide wasn't definitely the best you could get but he made quite an effort. I'd suggest that if you're attending with below 10 kids you do the explaining yourself. The museum is good to get some knowledge of the local cultures that are fast fading away. The Nigerian Government part of the Museum is also a bit interesting especially for the presence of the Car in which a Nigerian President was shot. If you find yourself in Lagos, take a trip there for cultural purposes. Very very cheap entry fee too.

title: Not very well maintained
text: For a NATIONAL MUSEUM a disappointment. The museum is not very well maintained and the curation is quite poorly done.

title: Has seen better days
text: I visited the National Museum during my January 2015 trip to Lagos. I was extremely disappointed by what I saw. First of all, there was no power. Given that this is Nigeria, that in itself was not disappointing...what was disappointing was that the "National Museum" of a country as large as Nigeria did not appear to have an emergency power generator.The attendants indicated no desire to provide any customer service, they appeared to be marking time until 4pm. There were virtually no exhibits to speak about - the one area that they claimed had exhibits could not be accessed if there was a power outage. All the more reason to have a generator! Outside the main museum, the entry to the hut used to store the bullet-ridden Mercedes car of the late dictator, Murtala Muhammed, was being used to wash cars. The entire scene was both comical and sad, and reflective of how rotten the core of Nigeria truly is.

title: Could be such an exciting place to visit . . .
text: . . . but unfortunately enough the entire museum is in a very bad shape, the exhibits are badly conserved and the lighting in some of the (few) rooms is horrible. You are not allowed to take pictures, but ironically you can touch some of the artifacts. Nigeria has a very rich history and deserves a much more appealing "National Museum". The most interesting part is a little shack outside the museum (but being part of it), with a brief historic outline of Nigeria's history after Independence and the original bullet-riddled Mercedes in which president Murtala Mohamed was assassinated.

title: A National Museum
text: This is one of Nigeria's most historical sites and would need to be well maintained for posterity.  It has a rich history of the events that took place right from the slavery days to present day political climate.  I would recommend a visit just to help a tourist understand the history of the country and the variety of cultures.

title: 第４代大統領Murtala Mohammed氏が暗殺された車が生々しい
text: ナイジェリアが国家となる前の時代からヨルバ族　イボ族　ハウサ族がどのように暮らしてきたかが展示されている。ガイドさんが付いてくれて説明してくれる。館内は撮影禁止。別館に第４代大統領が暗殺された際のメルセデスが、そのままの状態で保存されており大変生々しい。一度は訪問しておくと良いかもしれません。入園料は外国人300ナイラ、ナイジェリア人200ナイラ。

title: Enlightening...
text:
As an Expat in Lagos I really wanted to understand the history and dynamics which have shaped this amazing vibrant city of incredible contrast...from run down relics of destruction to high rise chrome and glass splendor, fine hotels and human squalor....I know about the various coups and period of Military rule but I , sadly, did not know much. Our Driver, a fine educated man by the name of Isaac took us to the museum one Saturday and we left very much enlightened.
The Museum will not win any awards and certainly needs to be upgraded and updated but it fulfilled its task in enlightening us....job done!

title: Must see Lagos landmark
text:
I have been visiting the national museum since i was a child and there was a time when my local church (house on the rock) used to hold its Wednesday and Sunday services at the MUSON Center which is opposite the Museum. 
It has great exhibitions from our past and i know that anytime i take out of town visitors who appreciate art to the exhibitions on display, they always leave with that 'wow' feeling. 
i wish they didn't move the Murtala Muhammed exhibition away from the main building into that shed though. i want to assume they had a good reason for doing so.
all in all, its an affordable place to go pay a visit(i paid N100 for a ticket the last time i visited in 2012). You can take your date to the museum instead of the usual cliched cinema/shopping mall. 
I am not sure if the museum kitchen is still function though. it used to serve delicious ,affordable meals back in the day

title: Nigerian history custodian
text: It would amaze you to find artefacts that tells a lot of history at this venue. It is a place often over looked but worth visiting.

title: Amazing recent Exhibit at the end
text:
It's a bit faded and slightly neglected, but let yourself be shown round by one of the enthusiastic guides. They really do add value, Worth wishing them a happy weekend, and where else would you meet a guy called Cosmos?
The main displays concentrate on Nigerian history before the Portugese arrived

The final display is more recent and includes the Nigerian equivalent of Kennedy's limo. This is kept in a shed.

Highly recommended

title: A good visual overview
text: The car in which the President was assassinated was added to the in which the Archduke Ferdinand was assassinated and the uniform in which Nelson was shot ... The Museum is small but gives a good impression of recent events.

title: History of Nigeria in one Building
text: The National Museum is not just your regular museum but one that holds vital information about the history of the country. A great place to take the children. The best part of the trip is seeing the Mercedes Benz Limousine the former  Military President Major Murhitala Mohammed was assassinated in.

title: Interesting but a bit rundown
text:
In all an interesting museum with historical artifacts from the history of Nigeria. Had an exhibition about the traditional life of different groups in Nigeria (with focus on the past of course). Very enthusiastic guide, included in the entrance fee, who actually told things that were not on the labels of the objects. 
At the moment the masterpieces from the Ife culture are not in the museum as they are on loan to other museums across the world as that part is being renovated.

As a national museum it's a bit of a disappointment "is this all?", after all it's the national museum in the countries largest city by far! But it is still a must if you visit Lagos as it gives some insight into the history of the different parts of Nigeria.
Note: the outside has a playground which is not recommended for children as it is too worn down, i.e. dangerous.

title: Learn about Nigeria's ancient civilizations and cultures
text: The museum exhibits Nigeria's ancient civilizations and traditional religions. You can learn more about the different ethnic groups in Nigeria. Moreover, the museum displays Nigeria's government of yesterday and today. Everything is labelled clearly but you can also get someone to show you around for some tips. This is not a European standard museum and you can see that few Nigerians have visited or know about the museum. Still, I think it's worth a visit as you can learn about some old traditions and see some local art.

title: Not to be missed!
text: The memorial complex of Dr. Kwame Nkrumah, the first president of Ghana, is not to be missed if you are visiting Accra. The complex houses both the bodies of Nkrumah and his wife. It is surrounded by beautiful fountains and park.

title: Tourist
text: Tourist visit to learn more about history of Ghana independence and the hero’s/ struggle icons behind the independence

title: Parc historiquement riche
text: Un accueil en musique, un beau mausolée entouré de fontaines et un musée riche en souvenirs de ce 1er président ghanéen m'ont émerveillée...

userLocation.name: Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo

title: Exploring History
text:
Our guide was an interesting and patient story teller.  A significant part of the tour involved looking at many pictures that depict the political history of President Nkrumah.  There are a few pieces of furniture, that belonged to the president.  Unfortunately much of his personal belongings were destroyed in the coup that ousted him. 
This is a great visit for anyone who does not know the history of President Kwame Nkrumah.

title: Very interesting place.
text:
It's a quite and beautiful place. You can see few Nkrumah's belongings and learn about his story. 
The place however has a lot of potential that unfortunately is not exploited, toot bad!!!

title: Interesting Museum and Mausoleum
text:
We visited the Kwame Nkumah Memorial Park as part of a Accra City Tour with Can Do Land Tours.  

This park holds a small museum dedicated to the life of Ghana's first president, Dr. Kwame Nkrumah.  I enjoyed looking at the various photos as I recognized many of the western leaders.

title: A beautiful museum, an African pride
text:
Though the museum itself is quite small, they have preserved numerous artifacts pertaining to the African leader. 
It was great to see a monument that is intentional in its desire to preserve it's national history.

title: Excursion
text: Our company held an excursion over to this wonderful place.....the scenery was splendid. It holds a lot of history.

title: Lots of History
text: I enjoyed my visit here, it was refreshing to know that history is been preserved. Here, you find the car Kwame Nkrumah used during his life time as well as his personal belongings like is shelf, walking stick, books etc. He's also buried in this park. There's a fountain in the park which wasn't functional and I known would be an amazing view if it was working. There is an entrance fee but I can't remember how much I paid.

title: What an experience
text:
It was good being able to see this in person. It is a beautiful monument to Ghana's 1st president. 

Only issue I have with this monument is the upkeep of the park. It seems to be somewhat neglected by those in charge of the upkeep. 

There is a charge to enter, and though I don't know what the revenue looks like, a better effort should be made.

title: Must See
text: The history that’s is in Ghana is rich and is a must see! Loved the museum, although small, still enjoyed the pictures and memorable belongings of Kwame Nkrumah.

title: Interesting Site
text: The Memorial Park is beautiful, peaceful and serene. The museum is extensive in the life of Kwame Nkrumah. A must see.

title: An important stop for any visitor to Ghana
text: The park is off a main street in Accra.  There is ample car parking.   We were taken as guests so I do not know if there is a fee for parking.  The park includes a small museum with a chronology, artifacts and photos from Kwame Nkrumah's life.  Our guide was knowledgeable and did not rush us through the museum exhibits.  The outdoor mausoleum is an impressive edifice.  Around the mausoleum there are sculptures of musicians within the reflecting pools and elsewhere.   There is some but not much shade in order to sit and contemplate the man and his legacy.  Kwame Nkrumah was an extraordinary leader.  The world would be a better place if there were more leaders like him today.  Any visitor to Ghana and Accra should come here to learn and to pay respects.

title: Nice Place with Improvement
text:
The park is always a good place to visit whenever you are in Accra. The place is wearing a good look than our previous visits, just the surrounding has to be kept clean, mostly under the trees. 
Then sits should be provided under the trees for short relaxation after the tour of the place, that will make it more okay. 

In all, it was a cool experience again.

title: Loved the trees that were gifted from foreign leaders.
text:
It's a good place in general, nice way tot see the history of Nkrumah and Ghana. The museum could be expanded upon and have something interactive. But we need more of this in Ghana, so it's worth the visit.

The trees gifted by various leaders that have been planted in the park is a beautiful and very interesting touch.

title: Unique viewing experience
text: The scenery was breathe taking, with a lot of tourist from different continents taking selfies with the monuments. It was a memorable experience for me

title: Guiding Tour
text: Once again I was at the Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park with tourist when I took my group round on a walking tour. So exciting it was but very discouraging to have noticed few things which beautify the park not working. Maintenance culture which seems not to have any place in our dictionary was at play. Well, but that did not take away the rich history of Nkrumah anyway.  The museum has all that is Dr. Kwame Nkrumah. Make sure you take a walk from your hotel to visit Nkrumah park while in Accra. Enjoy your walking tour.

title: Gardens are pretty well kept - definitely worth a short visit
text:
A 10 cedi entrance fee into the gardens (plus gets you into the small but interesting museum). The grounds are well kept although the water features were all completely broken.

The small museum is by far the most interesting (and most informative) part of the site. There are a range of interesting objects as well as numerous pictures of Kwame Nkrumah with various other famous figures including JFK, Mao, and Castro.

Overall, despite not being the most educational site in the world, it's well worth a trip.

title: Slightly disappointing
text: Visited the Park last week and was disappointed at the poor quality of the museum and the attraction generally. We were told (from another review) to visit the museum first, which was best way as it gives background to the Park and the person himself. However the museum was quite dark and the layout/quality of the exhibits could be improved. Then very disappointed with the Park itself - looked tired and not cared for. Also there was no water or fountains working. I think it lacks investment; something that seems to be common across the country. Good to get background about the man and what he did for Africa and Ghana though. Certainly one of the places to visit when in Accra but don’t have high expectations for the overall feel.

title: Worth while
text: First time in Ghana so this was a must see for my travelling party. Very interesting and informative. My only nag was that the water feature wasn't working . I can only imagine how spectacular it would've looked.Definitely worth a visit.

title: Great Experience!
text: We took a 2.5 hour drive from Accra to visit the castles. Our guide was very knowledgeable and covered many aspects of the castle. The tour started with a visit to the museum. We had ample time to check out the museum on our own before starting the castle tour. It lasted for about an hour and was very informative. There is a gift shop that sells books and CD’s about the castles.

title: Life-Changing Experience
text:
Visiting the Elmina and Cape Coast Castles is an essential experience, especially for those (like myself) who live in countries based on a history of enslavement. Our guide, Martin, was excellent and did a wonderful and thorough job explaining the cruel history of this place. Understanding what happened here is essential to understanding the history of my own country, as well as the history of Ghana and other parts of Africa. I will never forget what I learned and experienced here, including standing in the dungeons where so many thousands of men and women suffered and died. I will reflect on this visit for years to come.

(Those who visit, please remember to tip your guides.)

title: A must see for the children of the African Diaspora
text:
This was the third slave stockade I have visited and nothing can prepare you for the emotions which can erupt for the ancestors of stolen Africans.
It is a glimpse into our past...to see an actual "Door of no return". The doors where my ancestors were pushed, shoved and dragged through by their captures and dispersed across the world.

This building is proof to those who lack knowledge that SLAVERY was not a choice for the captives, it was only a choice for the gun toting captors.

title: founded in 1482
text:
Of the several fortified trading posts along the coast of Ghana, which today belong to the UNESCO World Heritage, only the three biggest ones are called castles: Christiansborg of mainly Danish origin in Osu, Accra (not open to the public, since it gets used by the government), Cape Coast (mainly British in its today construction) and St.George in Elmina, which is mainly Dutch in character.

The castles of Cape Coast and Elmina are now museums and they are by far the best preserved (and restored) and also the most visited of all these heritage sites. On top they are only about 13 km apart from each other. If in the area, it definitely makes sense to visit them both.

The castle at Elmina was first built by the Portuguese in 1482, thus 10 years before Columbus had reached the America's. The main reason was to trade in gold, which apparently was abundant here at the 'Gold Coast' (as the old colonial name of Ghana went). In 1637 the castle became Dutch until 1872, when all their properties here were sold to the British. 

In its structure the castle is still mainly a work of the Dutch and there are inscriptions in Dutch language to be seen at different points. From the Portuguese times only the chapel in the courtyard is left, which the Dutch turned into a warehouse and where now a very worthwhile exhibition with photographs and comments about Elmina's past can be seen - with themes like 'Trade, Slave Trade, Religion. Traditional Building, or the Asante in Elmina'.

Unlike at the much more visited Cape Coast Castle, one gets pestered here, when approaching the castle, by a whole bunch of youngsters, who all want to shake hands with you, then get into some kind of business, trying to sell you something, offering guiding services ot asking for supoort for their local soccer club.

At the castle gate I had to pay 40 GHS, thus the same entrance fee is at Cape Coast, only here I was not given a ticket. An aggressive, unpleasant looking official guide wanted to offer me his guiding services, but since - unlike Cape Coast - they are not compulsory, I declined and was quite happy to visit the place all by myself.

Besides the exhibition there are several empty rooms to be seen, but also the dungeons for the slaves. From the parapet are great views towards the beach, the lagoon, Fort St.Jago on an opposite hill and the fishing harbour. The architecture of St:George castle, as it was called by the British, is quite impressive, almost more so than at Cape Coast.

title: Let op!
text: Het kasteel met bijbehorende geschiedenis is uiterst indrukwekkend! Let op: ‘scam’: je stapt uit de taxi en voor het kasteel vragen mensen om je naam, vervolgens vragen ze je om die te spellen. 2min later krijg je een schelp met je naam (een gratis gift..), een seconde daarna staan ze met een lijst naast je met de vraag of je wilt doneren voor het een en ander. Pas hiermee op, met deze ‘gift’ proberen ze je in een lastig hoekje te duwen.

title: Sad history but very interesting
text: If visiting Cape Coast, Elmina Castle is a must see. Very sad history of the slave trade but interesting. Well maintained and we had a very informative guide. Well worth the admission price.

title: Tolle Führung!
text: Eine sehr beeindrucke Anlage.  Unser Führer Martin hat uns wunderbar informiert. In sehr gutem Englisch das auch Nichtmuttersprachler leicht verstehen konnten hat er die Geschichte lebendig werden lassen. Thank you Martin for this wonderful tour!

title: Beeindruckende Anlage
text:
Nachdem wir am Vortag schon Cape Coast besucht hatten, konnten wir beide Burgen gut vergleichen. Elmina ist grösser und „schöner“, wobei wir in Cape Coast einen deutlich engagierten Guide hatten und uns das Schicksal der Sklaven dort stärker berührt hatten. Hier war der Guide sehr lustlos und sein Englisch schwer verständlich. 
Nach der Besichtigung lohnt sich noch ein Blick in den Innenhof hinten mit einigen Souvenirläden. 
Bei den Jungs auf dem Parkplatz fiel uns Peter Cobbina auf, er ist sehr engagiert, interessant im Gespräch und hat uns eine schöne Führung durch Elmina gegeben.  +233556282740, P.O. Box Elmina 311

title: À améliorer
text:
Évidemment le fort St George est un immanquable et le poids de l'histoire impose une visite. 
Cependant, le fort mérite une petite rénovation à certains égards, il souffre la comparaison avec Cape Coast. Prix incluant le guide en anglais, visite en petit groupe durant une grosse heure.

title: If in Ghana-a place must see
text:
Smaller in comparison to Cape Coast Castle but definitely in a better location with three side facing sea.
How can a place so beautiful have such horrid history?
Sad historical monument makes you wonder why human are said to be most intelligent animal?

title: nice place, yet getting too commercial
text: the castle as such is nice. yet, half of the tour is shop hopping, through several shops that are spread throughout the castle, and that are interrupted by the really interesting and good parts.

title: Grim reminder of a terrible past
text: Like Cape Coast (well worth a visit), Elmina tells the story of slavery in Ghana - it's a grim tale of men and women at their best and worst, of greed, suffering, rape, exploitation and hope. People throughout the world can trace their roots back here and for many it must be a pilgrimage to come; for tourists like myself, it is a lesson and a warning lest anything like this should ever happen again. Get a guide to take you round if you can - it's difficult to understand the experience here without one - the spaces will mean little without knowledge of their true function as - for example - a parade ground for officers to choose slave women for their beds. For many, this is a shrine and so it's essential to have regard for the sanctity of the place. Thoroughly recommend - a must-do for us all.

title: Increíble!!!
text: El recorrido de la historia escondida de Elmina Tours es increíble. Recomendaría hacer esto según llegues a Elmina. Sankara dio muchos consejos útiles sobre qué hacer y dónde comer. La gira fue a muchos lugares interesantes y aprendí mucho sobre la ciudad, Ghana y la trata de esclavos que no hubiera conocido sin hacer esta gira. El grupo era bastante grande (sábado) pero hizo un gran esfuerzo para asegurarse de que todos pudieramos escuchar. También fue bueno poder decidir cuánto queríamos pagar. Recomendable 100%!!!

title: toccante
text: le stanze buie, soffocanti ed umide perfettamente conservate dove per settimane venivano tenuti gli schiavi mettono i brividi. In netto contrasto con gli alloggi dei soldati e ancor di più del governatore. Posizione bellissima. Tutto sommato, ben tenuto.

title: World heritage site
text:
This is rated to be the oldest European site in West Africa, established by the Portuguese in the late 15th century. Taken over by the Dutch and then the British, it was a major trading post for centuries, first gold, then slaves. The dungeons are chilling, as are the stories told by the guide. Your guided tour of the castle is part of the entrance fee. 

The building itself is attractive, with many stories, rooms and ramparts, with broad views along the coast and down to the beach and harbour. This is a significant world heritage site, well worth visiting if you are in Ghana. These are several shops inside with fixed prices and good value.

title: Elmina Tours
text:
You must visit Cape Coast and all the castles when you are in Ghana with all its hidden history. Please do this trip with Elimina Tours. Sankara, the tour operator is a great guy and he knows his stuff. The good thing its abosolutlely free but you can tip him what ever you want.

Highly reccomended

title: Bellissimo
text:
Un posto da visitare ancora intriso delle sofferenze patite e della crudeltà se lo uomo.
La struttura architettonicamente parlando e strepitosa sia la posizione sul mare che la costruzione in se
Una visita da fare assolutamente se si viene in ghana

title: Don't miss visiting here when in Ghana
text: If in Ghana, you must visit this historic site.  It is impressive in design and construction but certainly frightful in terms of it’s grizzly history.  Opt for a private tour to understand the design and function of this trading post turned slave castle.  The tour is in English and last about an hour.  If you also visit the Cape Coast Slave Castle, which was built by the British, you will appreciate the differences in this Portuguese/Dutch castle of horrors.

title: Free walking tours
text: I went to elmina castle some years ago I was very impressed. So much so that I decided to go again. This time I went with the free walking tour  with my wife and I was blown away by how knowledgeable the new tour guide was. There was no stone left unturned when it came to detailed information. I highly recommend that when you visit elmina, check out the free walking tour. I promise you that you won't be disappointed.

title: Very educational and moving
text: Visiting Elmina Castle is ABSOLUTELY A MUST!!! I learned so much from this tour about the side of slavery that is not often featured in history class. It is moving to see the place where so many people were tortured and died. The tour guides are amazing and take you on a journey. There are also toilets on site, which is nice. There are cool art gift shops throughout the castle, and these are places you are not pressured to buy (unlike many other tourist areas!). However, when entering and exiting the castle, beware of people trying to sell bracelets and get you to 'sponsor their soccer team or school'. They are persistent, which is frustrating.

title: Very interesting museum
text: Old, not welltained,but very interesting museum. Each one should know about this horrible episode of mankind.

title: Beaucoup d'émotion et une page noire de l'histoire de l'humanité
text: C'est certainement le lieu le plus marquant du Bénin. Ici une grande part sombre de l'histoire de l'humanité s'est déroulé avec le début du circuits infernal de la traite des noirs en Afrique. Le musé est riche en représentation et les explications faite par le guide sont très claires. Aucuns point n'est oublié et la responsabilité de tous les acteurs est mis en évidence. La visite s'est faite avec un ado et un jeune enfant. C'est très important de connaitre cette partie de l'histoire. Autre point très intéressant, c'est la mise en évidence des similitudes culturelles et traditionnelles entre le Brésil et les pays d'Afrique de l'Ouest.

title: Know your history
text:
A lot of history!!! You must hear and see for yourself. The history of the trans Atlantic slave trade and African kingdoms that existed during the time is truly a revealing one.

It's amazing how black communities in the diaspora (in places such as South America and the Caribbean) have preserved certain elements of their culture for centuries and the striking similarities between those cultures and that of certain West African communities today. 

P.S. This museum needs a face lift however... without damaging the history; I felt that it wasn't in the best of shape.

title: Excursion Trip
text:
With about 45 persons that day we drove down to Ouidah from Cotonou, almost an hour.

The road is smooth and free.  Two years before now, we couldn't ply the slave route because it was flooded.  We had to turn back.

If you are going to the point of no return in Ouidah, get a tour guide who should be able to let you know if the route is in perfect state.

What makes this tour site a 'must go' is the story being told about the slave trade way back centuries from the route to the point of no return arc.

title: Emouvant
text: Visite ce site si vraiment tu  aimerais mieux connaitre l'histoire de l'esclavage. C'était purement extraordinaire.

title: History cherished
text:
The museum is rich with antiques and it is encouraging to appreciate the managers for the preservations well done.

However, English speaking guides should be on a stand by for English speaking tourists.

It is a great place for those who value history.

title: Ouidah Museum
text: The museum have a lot of blood chilling history of slavey with lot of historical items  of how slavery was ran way back history.

title: Emotional Journey but Must Have a Guide
text:
My view may be a bit cloudy because it was an emotional place for me. This was a former slave Portuguese Fort that has been turned into a museum and you walk around rooms where pictures describe the unspeakable horrors slaves endured. We were on tour and the guide had arranged an English speaking guide for us who's a decent from a Brazilian slave who repatriated to Benin after slavery ended in Brazil. Of course, he admitted that his great grandfather at the time did not have knowledge of which country his ancestors had come from originally in Africa but he was following the wave of Brazilians who decided to call Ouidah home. 

I can't imagine visiting the museum without a guide because many of the pictures do not come with stories and that means you will miss out on so much. Plus the guide can help take you to the gate of no return which I think is part of the museum and also to other memorials which are there to honor slaves and the lives lost. It's a must do trip but just make sure to bring a guide!

title: No Museum, research the area and history before arriving
text: The Benin Government trying to help their citizens and visitors understand the history of the area and what has occurred here.  This is a monument not museum to the history of what took place here.  Research the trail and spend time to reflect this location and area before coming to the area.

title: The Museum of History of Ouidah has nothing to do with the Gate of No return Monument on the beach
text: The Gate of No return Monument on the beach,  of which there are a number of photographs here, is not The Museum of History of Ouidah. See the actual photo of the building which was originally Fort of São João Baptista de Ajudá built by the Portugese. There is not a lot inside just a few rooms with some artefacts and some explanations in French. Most could be self explanatory without a guide but our guide was quite informative and did add to the experience.

title: Not Great Museum BUT
text: It achieves its effect of making one reflect on Man's inhumanity to Man. The Fort where the .museum is housed was the nub for the slave trade. The Benin authorities should seek international funding to make this Museum worthy of what it is about and to improve the exhibits and their housing. Worth a visit as part of an overall insight into the pernicious and evil slave trade

title: An idiots guide to the Atlantic slave trade.
text: The museum is housed in the old Portugeuse fort that doubled as a slave holding centre on the Benin coast of west Africa. It gives a "no holds barred" account of the way in which the slaves were taken, held, mistreated and eventually made to exit the fort to walk, in chains, down a mile long route to the coast where they would then board the slave ships for the middle passage across the Atlantic to the Americas. Being located in the original fort at Ouidah leaves the traveler with the sense of impending doom and helplessness that the stolen lives must have felt at the time.

title: Eye Opening
text: A eye opening walk through the atrocities that were inflected to the African race for greed. We had an amazing guide Fostine who gave us a thorough historical narrative on the impact of the slave trade and the significance of the monuments and historical pieces. It is a place to visit and I was very happy that a lot of the historical monuments and artifacts were kept in good shape because in a lot of these historical sites things are not archived correctly. It is a beautiful village and you will get your fill with souvenir traders at the actual entrance to the beach Door Of No Return.

title: Très touchant
text: Il est parfois impirtant de connaître et surtout de comprendre l'histoire d'un pays et de tout un peuple.. visite très enrichissante et très touchante. Si vous passez à Ouidah un stop est nécessaire !

text: i think visit to ouidah is must if you came to visit in Benin, the slave route and the musem are intersting locations which you can get short history lesson about the slavery time.

text:
The arch way in the photo is the "Point of Return" on the shore of the sea. Slaves were marched the 4km from Ouidah on the Rue des Esclaves. It is the point of return because the slaves believed there spirits would return even if their bodies did not.
The museum is housed in what was the Portuguese fort which was burned down after independence. Little of the original remains, what you see is mostly a reconstruction. There are few items of real interest inside, some are reproductions.

title: Small but nice museum in an historic building
text: This rather interesting museum is located in the old Forte de São João Baptista de Ajudá. This fort has an interesting history. With its 5 acres (~2 ha), it was at one time the world’s smallest internationally-recognized political unit. It was built on land given to Portugal by King Haffon of Ouidah in 1721, and remained under Portuguese administrative control until Jul 31, 1961. On Aug 1 of the previous year, Dahomey (now Benin) had become independent, and its new government gave Portugal one year to vacate the premises and move on! When the ultimatum expired, the resident Portuguese population of the fort (2 inhabitants, down from 5 in 1921…) tried to set it on fire, rather than surrender it to the new country. The issue only reached closure in 1975, i.e., after the Portuguese revolution of the previous year, when Portugal recognized Dahomey’s sovereignty over the fort. In 1987, the Fundação Gulbenkian of Portugal funded the full rehabilitation of the historic facility, which now houses Ouidah’s Museum of History.

title: History
text: Hmmmmm. This is a must visit if you are in Cotonou. We arrived here and got a volunteer guide to take us around after we paid the official government tariff. Harry our guide was very good and told the stories with a lot of empathy.

title: Most informative castle tour
text: This is a must-go. The tour guide was extremely knowledgeable and informative. Everyone visiting Ghana absolutely should prioritize Cape Coast Castle.

title: Slavhistoria och obehagliga historier
text: Ett slott med hemsk historia om slavar. Ett informativt men hemskt historia om slavhandeln i världen. Stort slott med fin utsikt.

title: Excellent history
text: Excellent tour included on the entrance price. You get an idea of how slavery was in Ghana and really impressed whit the living conditions.  40 GHS for foreigners.

title: Visiting the ultimate sin
text: A must see just for learning the willpower it took to survive the conditions left in. After this my prosperity has changed.

title: To be remembered!
text:
One thousand men in the male slave dungeon and five hundred women in the female dungeon. Cape Coast Slave Castle dungeon was a place of terror and death. Millions of our African ancestors were shipped off to the new World. This place is a must-see for any Visitor to Ghana.

 Cape Coast Slave dungeon, was were thousands of our ancestors were forced to die. It was shocking! I almost cried, seeing what our people had to go through in order to be shipped off to the new world. The tour guide was on point. I really like his narratives. Never should, we repeat this history!

title: Historical, Educational and Memorable Experience
text:
Recently I traveled to Cape Coast from Accra with a group. Our guide was so very knowledgeable and professional.  

It was a sad experience but the guide was so prolific, the information given allowed me to relax and take it all in.

We did a lot on our Ghanaian trip but visiting Cape Coast Castle was a definite highlight.

title: Took some Married Couples there
text:
In December of 2021 , we visited the Cape Coast Castle as part of our 3 days tour to the Western and Central Regions.
It was a moment filled with lessons and a lot of emotions listening to the guide as he explained the history and showed as the various rooms.
For anyone looking for some history on the slave trade, this is one of the best places to learn from.
Do not forget to take a handkerchief along though because you may need to wipe some tears.

ownerResponse.text: Many thanks

title: Interesting historical site  amidst humunguous polution
text: The visit of the castle and slave dungeons was very interesting and left me in a highly emotional state. On the downside, the environs are extremely polluted and we witnessed quite a few indigenes taking  a sh#t  in the rocks adjacent to the castle.There seems to be a total lack of sanitation and environmental conscience here :-(

title: History- A must to hear the Tour Guides explain the Slave Trade!
text: This was an amazing Castle to visit. The Tour Guide was very well spoken in English. I was amazed to discover that in history, it was the Ghanian Chiefs that made the decision to 'sell' his people to the slave traders. All about obtaining trading goods in return. Very sad to see the conditions in which those slaves were kept and treated.  Travelled in Dec  2018 & Jan 2019. I highly recommend purchasing the DVD video and supporting the artists in surrounding shops, they make the most incredible items.  Ghanian people are beautiful people and they do everything to make this tour worthwhile. In addition, I feel the Ghanian Government could employ their amazing  'Dance Troupe Artists',  to put on daily dance displays, (in their traditional fabric costumes,  at the Castle, to reflect the history and culture.  The Government need to step up their support, for International travellers, to give them richer cultural experiences.  Talented Ghanians are crying out for work, give them jobs  so that they can be part of the travellers rich cultural experiences!

title: Cape coast castle tour
text:
It was an emotional tour.
Our tour guide was very helpful and she engaged us in the tour.

It was a 45 minutes tour and i enjoyed it

title: Breathtaking
text:
This is the most heart wrenching place, so much suffering. The irony of a Christian church built over the squalid and inhumane dungeons the African slaves were forced to endure is lost on no one. Every non-African should come here as part of their basic education. Every African should have the experience of reentering the “Door of no return”. 

We were lucky enough to be shown around by  Mark Tetteh who was knowledgeable and had opinions on the subject matter. I was accompanied by my adopted Nigerian daughter, she felt that he talked to every level of understanding.  He also took time for questions and knew the subject matter intimately. 

Go early to avoid both the school parties and hawkers.

title: Sobering experience
text: Well worth a visit! Sobering piece of history. The guide was really informative and very interesting.

title: Critical history lesson
text: As a European I feel obligatory (and interesting) to learn about the role of Europeans in the brutal past Ghana has and how it still has an impact until today. Cape Coast Castle is a great place to learn and feel the history of colonialism.

title: Historic
text: The background for this place is awful. Anywat the place is worth a visit. You could almost feel the struggle the poor slaves went through for so many years ago.

title: Must see and important in understanding the world’s infrastructure
text: Very intense but I feel like it is critical in understanding our place the world and how the infrastructure of our world was built. The tour guides were very helpful and were able to answer all of our questions.

title: Excellent tour.
text: Really interesting and emotional visit. Had a great tour guide, Kofi Eso. He explained the history and significance of the castle with great clarity and closed the tour with a very moving message about the future. Would definitely recommend a visit.

title: An impressive building that has lasted for hundreds of years and looks beautiful.
text: That Cape Coast Castle is one of the monuments in Ghana that reminds our generation of African slave trade history. The building is old but looks very healthy and strong. It's a nice place to visit with a large group of people. I love the landscape and the sea breeze.

title: Great history
text:
Great place to visit and to remember the horror of slavery. The crime against humanity must not be forgotten. 
Besides that the castle has a great atmosphere surrounding it. Go right along the edge of the castle to you get to the fisherman beach. Children play (at least on Sundays where we we there) and view of the bay is super.

title: Lieu chargé d'histoire
text: Une visite très intéressante, dans un ensemble de bâtiments conservant le témoignage d'un passé terrible.

title: Very Moving Experience
text: Totally enjoyed our visit.  The history and actual evidence of the atrocities committed here are truly moving.  A must see destination for anyone visiting Ghana!
