text: It's an active groove with engravements of history of the Osogbo people. I took tour around the place with the help of a guide.

title: Mystischer Ort
text:
Ich bin von Ibadan aus angereist - Bus 2000 Naira und Motortaxi zum Eingang 500 Naira. Die Fahrt nach Osun dauert ca. 2h. 
Am Eingang liegt eine Preisliste aus: Eintritt für Studenten 1.000 Naira, Fotos mit dem Handy 1500 Naira. Mir wurde noch ein Guide empfohlen, aber 8.000 Naira waren mit zu viel. Natürlich versteht man nicht allzu viel, wenn man ohne Guide den heiligen Hain besichtigt. Zumindest sind im Wald viele Skulpturen und Schreine zu sehen. Auf dem Rückweg bin ich zum Fluss und durfte bei einer Zeremonie zuschauen. Nichts für schwache Nerven, da eine Ziege geköpft wurde. Aber nichtsdestotrotz eine interessante Erfahrungen. 
Am Eingnag ist ein kleiner Souvenirshop, welcher eher Schmuck führt.

title: Священный лес
text: Священный для племён йоруба лес. Почитается как место обитания богини плодородия Осун. В 2005г внесен в список Всемирного наследия Юнеско.

title: Ok
text:
The two hour guided walk was tranquil and interesting. The monkeys running around with their babies hitched to their bellies very cute, but they leap and jump yo grab bananas from you! 

I was surprised that the fantastical  and unusual (if not downright weird ) statues  depicting local spiritual beliefs by Austrian  Suzanne Wenger  surrounding the grove resulted in it being inscribed on the UNESCO heritage. To my mind  Nigeria has more impressive sights like the Benin Bronzes and Badagry. I wouldn’t come all the way from overseas to see this, but if in the area  sure…

title: Exciting
text: The view is beautiful as well as the welcoming monkeys although the pay for the camera is a big turn off for me but it is a lovely place to visit.

title: A Groove with Historical Views and Persons On Ground to tell the tale
text:
i visited the groove and saw with my own eyes stories read from books and journals and i met those to give brushes to the history been shed for years.
I was privileged to witness the cleansing process before worshippers were allowed into the groove, i took pictures too to this effect as well.
Nigeria is got an heritage to cling to if properly harnessed.

title: With friends
text: It was a very sunny Saturday and its good to Na at the osun grove although we met none there but I did satisfy my need to visits there and the monkeys are very interesting ones

title: Historical and inspirational
text:
I love the fact that with the osun osogbo a part of our tradition and history is being preserved. The mona monkeys welcome you on arrival. its 1000 naira per person to visit 200 Naira for mobile cameras and about 2000 Naira for digital digital camera. Your fee includes a guide that takes you around the grove. There is a yearly festival in august that attracts visitors and osun worshippers from everywhere.

The Osun Osogbo grove also includes an art village with tye and dye, paintings, wood carvings, drums and other arts and craft. its totally worth a visit

title: Lovely but eerie 😀
text: So once you step into this place, youd have an eerie feeling, seems like all the African gods inhabit this place, decorated with very creative artwork, the grove is a place to be, get close to nature, experience healing and meditation, if you love the African tradition and culture, here is your goto destination. Expect to see monkeys jumping around, and reserve some tips for the praying women at the entrance of the shrine. Feel free to to pray to the river goddess,  and experience walking through the first ever suspension bridge in Nigeria.

title: Worth the visit!
text: This was one of the first sites I visited in Nigeria and it was worth it. Takes you on a journey to the ancient Yoruba civilisation. Beautiful art works, amazing architecture, fantastic landscape and nature. I totally enjoyed myself. I hope this site’s maintenance remains top-notch!

title: An Historical Site worthy visit
text:
Osun groove is a sacred groove that has been in existence for so long a time. At the grove, you have the historical consultant who are on ground to take you round and tell you more about the sacred grove. 

Is a good place to visit for one who believe more in culture and traditions.

title: Very intereesting place to visit
text: Susan Wenger, an artist and Yoruban priestess has transform this spiritual with her modern and magical scupturees.

title: The surviving groove of a people
text:
The Osun Oshogbo groove and the people of the ancient town are indivisible.
The adoration for Osun, the deity of fertility is undeniable. The numerous monkeys along the road to the groove and in the groove are a spectacle to behold as they are used to the people. It is a common sight to see drivers parking their cars to give bananas and other food to these animals who are friendly.
I advice anyone that is going to Oshogbo or to explore the groove or the town to go with a guide because most of the places are unmarked. It has no signage or directions.  
It will do the tourist or visitor so much good to employ the service of  a guide because the guide will take the visitor beyond his or bargain.

title: Simply the best tourist attraction in Nigeria
text:
I was there severally time but the best season is august when the festival take place.
Tradition, religions and Nature become a mix of colours and sounds.
You can choose to enjoy the relaxing side or the learning side.
Everyday you can discover new things and statues, not far from the entrance you can taste good and cheap palm wine.
During the festival you can meet people from worldwide.
you cannot leave Nigeria without one visit at the park.

title: Nice day trip
text: Can easily do this on your own, however I did it with a guide in hopes of learning more about the Yorba culture.  Walk through a tranquil park with interesting sculptures.

title: Breathtaking experience!
text: I strongly recommend going to Osun-Osogbo grove if you are in the area. When entering the grove through the main gate, you can already feel the unique energy that lies within. We enjoyed a 2-hour walk through the grove, visiting two shrines and lots of the sculptures/art work on the premises. It's a truly spiritual and peaceful place.

title: Beautiful
text:
We went to the Osogbo Secret Grove last week. We were accompanied by a priest. The nature and art from Susanne Wenger is really special and beautiful.
One should wear sneakers, long trousers and Moskito spray.

title: Magical, beautiful and beyond words.
text:
This is by far the most amazing place I have entered. I want to thank Doyin Olosun for a very interesting tour in the Grove. 
As soon as you step into this sacred virgin forest, you immediately feel the magic all around you, and you sense how you find peace. Here, no trees are getting cut down or animals caught or hunted. The work of Adunni Olorisa (Susanne Wenger) and the Sacred Art Movement is breathtaking and very unique. Monkeys are jumbing around you, hoping that you might have brought some bananas, prayers are being said and blessings given. This place is indeed very sacred for the everyday life of the devotees of the Orisa religion. 
The Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove is without any doubt a place I would warmly recommend people to experience, with respect for the sacred character of the place.

title: Nigéria 2017
text: Floresta Sagrada de Osun, local cheio de mistérios com o Templo e o Rio Osun e suas sacerdotisas. Em agosto há a festa de Osun, que é visitada por uma multidão de adeptos de orisa. Experiência maravilhosa.

title: Mystical Sacred Place
text:
The Osogbo grove is a serene mystical place and the source of spiritual strength and growth for the Yoruba people including the diaspora. The site, a UNESCO world heritage site has been carefully maintained for tourists and religious devotees. I was impressed by the management and tour guides. 
One could also easily overlook the impressive sculptures on the walls surrounding the grove. Also the grove is home to a number of rare animals, plants and birds. It is a spiritual oasis.

title: Great vibes!
text:
We went there on a Tuesday night, waiting for traffic to die down (Damn Lagos traffic!). The experience was a great one for me, I just loved the vibe! The stage has pictures of iconic blacks in history, paintings of Fela Kuti and there was a DJ there playing Reggae and Dancehall. I believe the guy playing is from Tidal Soundz. 

Everything about the place feels genuine, raw and pure. According to my bf, Fela housed the homeless there where he also provided food for them.

title: FUN FUN FUN
text: It was a great place to visit. Good dancers and music. A lot of people came to enjoy the social environment.

title: Fun place to catch the Afrobeat Crown Prince Live
text:
Very lively place. Free entry on some days and street dudes all over the place, so it's a place to experience being around the ordinary folks. Safe and secure though as no acts of harassment is allowed even though it may look rowdy with lots of people that are usually around.
Drinks are ver cheap and everyone is free and unofficial. Tuesdays are practice days for the Crown Prince himself. Femi Anikulapo Kuti, so going on those days either there is a show or during his practice is the way to go.

title: Huge place for concert
text: Very interesting place if you have never been. Must pay 500 N to enter (2,50 Euro). Outside there are anykind of vendors and inside you can sit down and drink or eat meat. There is nothing inside to see when there are not concerts.

title: For Felabration
text: Nicest  nice food, dance music people friends reggae all sorts of enjoyment all during Felabration in Oct. I am a regular visitor and I have had swell times in Lagos during Felabration at the New Afrika Shrine. It is also known as Femi Shrine. Your imagination gets fulfilled

title: Best experience in afrobeat
text: Run by Fela Kuti’s children and keeping his legacy alive, the New Afrika Shrine is a truly delightful experience in afrobeat.  Sons Femi and Seun Kuti perform whenever they are in town.  We were lucky to be there on a Thursday, when Femi Kuti was performing, having just returned from a tour.  The Shrine is set up in a huge warehouse-like space, which fills up tight as the evening progresses.  Food and drinks are available for purchase, and smoking (not just cigarettes!) is in abundance.  The musicians accompanying Femi Kuti are excellent and enthusiastic.  Most certainly the best and most authentic show in town.

title: Le parcours des esclaves: un devoir de mémoire
text:
La fondation Zinsou, abrîte le premier musée d’art contemporain africain. Le musée Zinsou de Ouidah est d’abord la rénovation d’une œuvre architecturale unique.

Ouidah qui se veut « villes de tous les patrimoines » avec son histoire dense honore les artistes contemporains africains. Cyprien Tokoudagba, Samuel Fosso, Romuald Hazoumé, SolyCissé, le musée d’arts africains de Ouidah vous donne rendez-vous pour une autre facette de l’Afrique. Une facette qui jusque-là ne pouvait être visitée qu’à Paris, New-York, et autres grandes villes occidentales.

Très belle initiative ce musée dont j'ai beaucoup apprécié la visite.

title: endroit au milieu de nul part
text: la porte du non retour fut errigé par rapport à l'esclavagisme de l'epoque. Les portuguais faisait monter en particulier les.youroubas dans des bateaux à cet endroit la. certains se jetaient à l'eau pour ne pas quitter leur terre. le chemin commence à ouida.

title: Nice place
text:
The Ouidah Museum of History contains a small, but very interesting. exhibition of objects related with the history of slavery and the religious and cultural relations between Benin and Brazil, thanks to the trafiic of slaves, brought from Benin in the XVII, XVIII and XIX centuries. 
The local tour guides are very good, well educated and available to answer all questions. 
The Musuem islocated inside na old portuguese fort of the early XVIII century, what is a plus.

title: Histoire du pays
text: Passage obligé pour connaitre un peu l'histoire de l'esclavage par les Portugais et les Français au Bénin. Endroit imprégné d'un passé douloureux qu'on peut encore ressentir.

title: poor but full of history
text: I was reluctant to hire a guide but, that is the best choice. I high recommend NOT to hire the opportunist people that always will surround to you there but hire one at Municipality Turist Office, particularly to Mr. CARLOMAGNO, the most well english speaker guy there. He is the guy who build some of the monuments along the way to reach the slaves-gate (on the pic). (he's kindly, selfless, and he will take care well of your necesities, avoiding thieves). On the  gate there are not too much to see, the beach is nice even looks abandoned. This slaves-rute and a free musem (zinsao... -I'm not sure about the name) is the best (and unique) realy nice thing to know in all the country. Price approx. 20 USD.

title: =D
text:
O Museu conta a história de reis antigos, a passagem dos portugueses e outros povos pelo Benin.

Em muitos aspectos consegui ver familiaridades entre as culturas do Brasil e do Bénin. Vale a pena!

title: Intereesting if sad.
text: Got take on a tour by an amusing local and he jovially explained there was no money in the  treasure box.  Get a book called the Viceroy of Ouidah to find out more about the place and the Da Silvas. Yayi Bonis wife is a DaSilva.

title: Musée décevant
text: Le musée pourrait être bien, si on pouvait le visiter librement, sans la houlette obligatoire d'un guide. On aimerait flâner, lire les légendes, imaginer ou retrouver ce qu'on aura lu, ou ce qu'on lira ensuite.

title: Exposição interessante
text: Gostamos muito desse museu, apesar dele ter o mesmo inconveniente que muitos dos outros que visitamos na Africa: quase nenhuma explicação escrita, por isso a qualidade da visita depende do guia. Dois pontos altos: exposição sobre o paralelo entre a cultura brasileira e a africana; uma exposição sobre as mascaras usadas para certas danças por uma sociedade secreta.

title: Museo molto carino
text: È la storia e le verità di questo Paese. Se siete in Benin e passate di la, andate a vederlo. Vi sono rappresentazioni e quadri molto carini e pieni si significato e valore umano.

title: Interesting photography
text: The museum is very interesting, our guide was too. There is also an exhibition about the parallel between the voodoo culture in Benin and Brazil, with beautiful photographs.

title: Douloureuse route des esclaves
text: Le Musée est un fort portugais qui retrace l'histoire de l'esclavage. Et la présence coloniale des portugais et des français. Possibilité moyennant finance de faire la route des esclaves avec le guide jusqu'à la porte de non retour.

title: Het verleden zichtbaar
text:
Ongeveer 30 minuten met de auto vanaf Cotonou ligt het stadje Quidah, het stadje is nauwelijks bekend in de buitenwereld maar toch bevinden zich hier enkele bijzondere locaties en gebeurtenissen vanuit het verleden.
Volgens de overleving bevindt de oorsprong van VOODOO zich in deze omgeving en is er een VOODOO Museum vlak buiten het stadje, waar men je meer kan vertellen over de rituelen en gebruiken van VOODOO. Advies: neem een vertrouwde chauffeur mee bv vanuit je hotel en fotografeer mensen pas na dat je toestemming hebt gekregen.
In de stad Quidah bevind zich het Portugese Fort waar in het verleden de slaven werden verzameld en door de Portugezen naar o.a. Brazilië werden verscheept, het Fort is nog geheel intact en is nu als museum en dagelijks te bezoeken.   
Na het bezoek aan het museum kan je via de marktplaats naar de kust rijden, ca. 5 km., over dit pad moesten de slaven lopen naar de schepen die voor de kust lagen. Op dit pad staan nog de beelden waarlangs ze moesten lopen om afscheid te nemen van hun land. Ook bevindt zich halverwege dit pad een dorpje waar VOODOO priesters hun rituelen uitvoeren. Fotografeer niet zonder toestemming!
Aangekomen bij de kust staat er nu een monument op de plaats waar de slaven Afrika hebben verlaten, al met al een zeer indrukwekkende locatie.
Langs de kust kan je dan weer terug naar Cotonou.

title: Intéressant mais attention aux propositions des pseudo guides
text: L'endroit est intéressant à visiter mais ne donner aucune suite aux propositions que font certains des guides du musée pour vous accompagner à la fête vaudou par exemple ou pour vous expliquer la route des esclaves... ils ne cherchent qu'à vous arnaquer et à vous soutirez de l'argent.

title: Some interest, but not much presentation
text: There were some interesting pieces on display here, showing the history of the city and the fort, but everything felt run-down and ignored.  Most of the information concerned the Portuguese control of the city and their missionaries; I got very little information on the indigenous people or how they lived.  I just feel like so much more could be done with this place.

title: O.K. aber besser gleich zum Office de Tourisme
text: Das kleine Museum ist durchaus sehenswert. Viel sinnvoller aber ist, sich zum Office de Tourisme zu begeben, um dort gestaffelt nach Länge sich von einem ortskundigen Führer das zeigen zu lassen, was in der Geschichte dieses Jahrhunderte alten Städchen an Orten, Strassenbzügen, Märkten lles noch zu sehen ist. Diese Führung ist wirklich erstklassig unde rspärt langes überflüssiges Lesen in halbgaren Reuseführern.

title: Interessant und gut gemacht
text: Das Museum ist sehr authentisch und übersichtlich. Die Tour dauert ca. 20min. Sehenswert ist die Fotoausstellung.

title: On est mal à l'aise, mais cela fait partie de l'histoire...
text:
On ne peut pas se rendre au Bénin, sans faire une halte à Ouidah et visiter cet ancien fort portugais si chargé de souvenirs terribles...
On s'imprègne de l'histoire de presque un million d'esclaves, de leurs conditions de détention avant leur grand départ pour l'Atlantique ( pour ceux qui arrivaient à survivre...) 
L'ambiance est chargée, pesante, On imagine les souffrances endurées, on en voit les traces, on comprend la bêtise humaine.
Commencez par visiter le fort avec ses casernes, sa chapelle, ses objets conservés dans la résidence.
Puis suivez le chemin de 4 km jusqu'à la plage d'où partaient les bateaux, en passant par la place aux enchères, l'arbre de l'oubli et la porte du non retour.
Imprégnez vous de cette ambiance terrible et, une fois parvenu sur la plage, soufflez un peu. Vous en aurez besoin.
L'endroit est vraiment magnifique.

title: Few Senegalese monuments and plenty from Other African Nations
text:
It’s not truly a Senegalese museum 🇸🇳 it’s more of an African Tribes and their symbolic masks 🎭 each one has a meaning and try to provide some branding value to each tribe. 
It’s quite a small museum if you have like 20-30 minutes it would be something to talk about when you get back home, especially the historic underwear 😊

title: Für Liebhaber
text: Wer sich in afrikanischer tribal art auskennt, kommt hier sicherlich auf seine Kosten. Unzählige Masken aus den verschiedenen westafrikanischen Staaten im Erdgeschoss. Im Obergeschoss dann lauter weitere Gegenstände des täglichen und rituellen Stammeslebens. Alles sehr interessant, man muss sich darauf einlassen. Die 5000 Cfa Eintritt kommen sicherlich dem Erhalt des Museums zu Gute.

title: A part les murs, il ne reste pas grand chose...
text:
J'ai visité l'IFAN il y a 32 ans: Il regorgeait d'objets primitifs, de photos, de masques, d'outils du néolithique etc...
Où tout cela a-t-il bien pu passer???
De plus le prix demandé à l'entrée pour visiter cette coquille quasi-vide, me paraît exorbitant!
Donc à déconseiller dans l'état où il est rendu... dommage, c'était un trésor!

title: Great Museum
text: We visited when only the ground floor was open. It is impressive, given the range of masks on display from various parts of Africa. Well organized, but I wish they kept all sections open!

title: Very manageable museum
text: Lots of interesting art in a decent building --- 45 minutes is plenty of time to visit. Some of the pieces are most impressive; others not so much.

title: Good collection of masks and textiles
text:
I would recommend visiting this museum while in Dakar, but with some reservations.

Pros
-  Very nice space
-  Good collection of West Africa masks and statues
-  Good tribal textiles

Cons
- Relatively expensive - but this museum does not receive funding other than entrance fees
-  Limited explanation of exhibits or maps to show the source of the exhibits - if you do not know the regional Geography you will not understand the source of the exhibits
-  Very few Senegalese masks

title: επισκεψη στο μουσειο
text: έχει εκθέματα αφρικανικής τέχνης και αφρικανικής ιστορίας. Εχει ενδιαφέρον γι αυτούς που αρέσουν να επισκέπτονται μουσεία

title: excellent permanent collection,  terrific  temporary exhibitions, and center for research and discussion about culture
text: The  current leadership has  transformed this museum into a major site for the newest art by local artists, each well-chosen, and cultural center for lectures, symposia, and discussions about local cultural issues.

title: Don't miss this ..
text:
Had a great visit here spending quite a few hours savouring both old and new. The main building houses many very old pieces from various west African countries. The building at the rear shows a contemporary exhibition of textiles. 
Only thing missing is a really good barista and machine, with outdoor seating.

title: a welcome break from the heat
text:
large open space and lovely building. the exhibits were nice but few were from Senegal. most were from surrounding countries. i enjoyed the videos and to sit was a welcome break from the heat (and the street vendors)
there was a temporary art exhibition in a seperate building which i loved most.

title: Small but interesting
text: Its quite expensive at 5000cfa but worth the visit. The bottom floor is mostly masks from west African countries, upstairs is textiles from the same regions. It took about half an hour to walk round. The highlight for us was a free temporary exhibition in the building behind which included art from each of the 54 african countries. The artwork was based on the artist interpretation of light which made for interesting viewing. There was also a film where the artists had 54 seconds to explain their thoughts and process. It was very interesting to hear the diverse approaches.

title: nice art pieces but a little bit outdated museum
text: nice peces of arfrican art but in the whole it is a little bit outdated. an textile exposition, which should be finished in 2017 was still open in 2018. Nevertheless, it was a welcome 2 hours of activity in Dakar.

title: Un musée qui n’est pas mis en valeur
text: Ce musée présente des masques africains et des instruments de musique. Il est dommage que tous ces objets ne sont pas mis en valeur. Les vitrines sont poussiéreuses et les éclairages sont vieillots. Cependant les objets sont beaux et méritent d’etre Mis en valeur. Je crains que ce musée tombe en désuétude s’il n’est plus entretenu. Même s’il ne mérite pas forcément le détour il mérite cependant d’etre Soutenu.

title: Entrée onéreuse pour ce musée
text:
5000 CFA pour les non résidents ! Trop cher pour voir des objets ( parures,masques,bijoux,poteries) exposés au 1r étage qui manquent cruellement de cartels de présentation.
En revanche, les reconstitutions grandeur nature du rdc sont fort intéressantes. Prévoir 1h de visite.

title: Interessante e caratteristico
text:
Il museo é ubicato nel plateau di Dakar, nella parte più centrale e "in" della città.
E' molto grande ed espone numerosi elementi che ben caratterizzano la cultura delle varie etnie senegalesi e dei popoli degli Stati confinanti, spaziando da maschere rituali ad armi e strumenti musicali, sino a piccoli gioielli ed amuleti protettivi. Al piano superiore é presente una selezione di tessuti e vestiti tradizionali.
In una depandance del museo vi é uno spazio espositivo per quadri o opere fotografiche di singoli artisti. L'accesso é compreso nel costo del biglietto di ingresso al museo. Nel mio caso ho trovato una esposizione di ritratti su carta fotografica veramente di eccellente fattura.
Tutta la visita puo' essere svolta in un'ora. L'ho trovata molto interessante e lo considero tempo ben speso.

title: Mooi overzicht Afrika in beelden
text:
Beelden van rituelen van geboorte tot de dood, met alles wat daar tussen gebeurd.
Landen met de kleine verschillen in het ritueel. Iet wat rmmmelige presentatie, entree 5000cfa

title: mooi overzicht d'Art Africain
text: voor 5000cfa kun je dit museum bezoeken, mooi overzicht van rituelen, beelden van leven tot dood. op dit moment ook met kleden.

title: small old museum
text: nice but small mask collection on the first floor. fabric collection on the second floor. museum building is old, colour is falling from the ceiling in many places

title: Normal
text: Bon quoi dire sur cette place c'est plutôt normal un musée a visité sans plus, j'ai payé 5000 FCFA (7.5 euro) pour pouvoir visité trois zones alors que on allons vers la troisième et ban c'est fermé, mais grosso modo ca va comme endroit

title: Beau, mais quel gâchis
text: Musée cher et très décevant. Peu de pièces exposées au rez-de-chaussé, dans deux grandes salles désertes et mal éclairées. Des statues et des masques qui prennent la poussière sous des vitrines mal fermées. Quel gâchis, car ce sont des pièces superbes, venant de diverses régions et très impressionnantes; un nouveau musée est en construction vers la gare, espérons qu'il améliorera les choses.

title: Shamefully engaging with our history
text: Sebastian was an excellent guide and really made you feel a very small bit of how it must have been to be here. Sorry for our history and maybe we should teach more of this in our schools.

title: Emotional und Bedrückend
text: Eine gute Führung. Ich musste öfters mit den Tränen kämpfen, so hat mich die Abscheu betroffen. Unglaublich zu was die Menschheit fähig ist. Ein dunkles und abscheuliches Kapitel auch in der Geschichte von Europa. Es war ein enpfehlungswerter und eindrucksvoller Besuch.

title: Worth the trip, even if out of the way
text: We stopped in Cape Coast en route from Kumasi to the the Accra airport. It is a long way to go but well worth the stop to contextualize a part of Ghana’s long history. Our group was tired after a full week but after the tour, agreed it was worth getting up and out early and taking a 7 hour drive instead of a 45 min flight to be able to take the tour before our departure that evening. Admission was GHC 40 per person for non-Ghana citizens as of Feb 1, 2020. The tour lasts about 45 minutes and is included with admission. Be sure to wear sunscreen and sunglasses or a hat. Water is also a good idea on hot days.

title: Educational and we'll maintained
text:
Very well maintained castle. Both outside and underground chambers.
It is recommended to take a guided tour provided at the entrance.
Takes about 45 mn.
But the overall stay should take arround 2-3 hours depending how deep you want to explore, the fort.
There are many chambers, pathways,  and towers with connecting walls.
Lots of history.
Highly recommended and educational.

title: Interessant und bedrückend
text: Obwohl die Hitze und Schwüle es schwer machte, war die Führung im Castle auf jeden Fall sehr lohnend.

title: Such an important stop
text: This is an important piece of history that needs to be experienced. Pictures and books don't tell enough of the story. Very powerful!

title: Tour with Anthony Bouadi
text: I had one of the best experiences in Ghana whilst at the castle. My tour guide Anthony did a wonderful job guiding myself and other attendees through the tour- a tour that was gut wrenching at times. He took time to explain and answer every question we had, and provided a lot of healing words, as well as brought great clarity/ knowledge about our history. I highly recommend for all tour needs in the Central Region of Ghana.

title: Incredible experience
text: This tour was emotional but necessary. We learned so much about the history of the slave trade and the countries who occupied Cape Coast Castle until it closed. You must visit when in Ghana!

title: Must see
text:
This was possibly one of the most humbling and emotional tours of my life. The learning experience was incredible and the tour guide had this immense storytelling ability that seemed to transcend us back in time. 

Hearing about the conditions the slaves went through and walking on the paths they did from the main entrance, through the male/female dungeons, and finally through the door of no return was heart wrenching. 

This part of history, as distressing and tormenting as it is still is should not be forgotten, in the hope it doesn’t happen again. 

Life altering experience.

title: Nice pictures
text: It was very intresting to see the slaves castle. I actually saw the castle in june 2018 but there was no 2018 dates.

title: An emotional tour for me
text:
Although I am pakeha/abroni/white this tour of the cape coast slVe castle was a very emotional experienxe.
Learning what was done to the 12 million slaves taken from Africa and the estimated million that went through the coast castles was confronting. The suffering of the slaves should never be forgotten and we have an obligation to learn what happened to these people.
I am stunned that i did not know how many were lost to slavery. Surely this is the greatest loss to humankind .
The guides were knowledgable. The castle is reasonably well preserved. We were taken through all the levels from dungeons and the door of no return to the 3rd floor hovenore and european quarters.
You can wander round on your own. I am insure whether this makes a diffrrence to the entrance price of 40 cedis. ($12NZD approx)
It is hot in Ghana so this tour will make you sweat if you are from cooler climates. Take water and a fan. I have been carrying round a wet flannel to cool my self off.
A down side is being harrassed by hawkers outside the castle. Just be firm with your "no" if you are not interested.

title: Cape Coast Castle
text:
This was the second slave fort that we visited on the same day.  These forts are very emotional sights to visit.  When you see the areas where they kept the various slaves and the church located above it, it is very overwhelming.

This fort had a good museum that covered the Atlantic Slave Trade as well.

title: Interessante Geschichte des Sklavenhandels
text: Die Führung war sehr interessant und eindrücklich. Die Räumlichkeiten zu sehen, in denen die Sklaven unter unwürdigen Bedingungen gehalten wurden sind aber auch bedrückend. Auch das Museum ist schön gestaltet, wenn auch teilweise etwas heruntergekommen. Die Führung selbst war etwas lieblos vorgetragen.

title: Hard History Lesson
text: A must see for any member of the diaspora to learn about the history of slavery. It was a humbling and empowering experience all at the same time.

title: Emotional
text: We went at night. Which added a real atmosphere to the castle. We took the tour with torches. I cried as I know my ancestors went through a terrible ordeal. I learned so much. We were able to light candles and leave an offering to the ancestors. Amazing!

title: Whow - one tour that will remain forever
text: Have you ever wondered about slavery? If you think you know a bit about the subject visit this fort and you will learn so much more as well as other interesting facts about the Europeans, trade and slavery for profit. Absolutely mind boggling to know that there were so many millions died shipping slaves around the world.

title: Inhuman reality which is a blot on mankind - A MUST VISIT
text:
This castle is located at a place which is about 180 kms. from Accra & takes around 3 hours (one way) to reach.

Cape coast Castle is a historical monument with a sordid & tragic story to tell.

This was the place where black man & women were captured from the whole of West Africa,, brought here & kept in the basement of this castle for onward shipment to Americas, Europe & the Carribean.

The men & women were kept separately in underground dungeons in the most unimaginable conditions.

In a 800-100 sq.feet chamber approximately 200 men were kept. They ahd to eat there, sleep there & do everything in that chamber only till the time they were shipped abroad.

Of the total numbers only about 65% could survive & shipped out of the castle.

The rest died in that very chamber.

Females were kept seperately & were subjected to continuous sexual exploitation.

One shudders to think that the governor of the castle was staying in the same castle lavishly.

The Britishers built a church just above the dungeon where slaves were kept like animals , were tortured & many even died.

What an irony !!!

title: October
text: There on a weekend off from volunteering. Was very moving and eerie of what the captives went through. From the chains on the walls to the dungeon and the point of no return. Wreaths and bouquets left in the cells was heart breaking.

title: Emotional History
text: It's a tour everyone should do when you visit Ghana or if you are in Ghana. Very very emotional tour. Very educative and informative. Good for school groups, individuals, cooperate, families, solo.

title: Lohnenswert
text:
Sehr interessante Führung mit einem tiefen Einblick in die dunklen Abgründe der menschlichen Geschichte. 
Nichts für sensible Seelen, sehr informativ und auch sehr nahe gehend.

title: Mother Goddess
text:
What a pristine Landmark preserved to perfection. The scultures and grounds are beautiful it was a pleseant beautiful walk through beautiful forest with gorgeous monkeys leading the way. 

It was a spritial high and a great chance to meditate and connect with the energies in the space.  You get a historical tour from a docent guide who gives you a historical narrative of the grounds. A most see space if you in Nigeria.

title: Easter period visit to the sacred grove
text:
Was an interesting outing.

The gate fee cost N200 for adults and free for children.
There was a tour guide at no extra cost. 
At the entrance, there were lots of monkeys (not sure wat specie).

The monkeys are friendly and they love to be fed bananas which we got from a lady who sells them at an affordable and cheap rate of N20 to N100.

Lots of arts, places and history inside the groove itself .....Pictures speaks more than words.

Visit and see for yourself.

title: One of the best tourist spots in Nigeria.
text: I have been a couple of times and each time I come around,I cannot but appreciate the efforts that have come into making it a world class tourist destination.The history behind it authentic and exciting. The location has been  jealousy guarded from the usual onslaught of unappreciative Nigerians.

title: Sacred Indeed
text: Was always scared of visiting but after the visit I realized it was not as scary as I thought. The locals at the site are friendly and I learnt more about the history of the place.

title: Beautiful and Interesting
text:
The entry fee to this place is 200naira and it was worth every Kobo. The monkeys welcome you as you come in and it will be nice if you could at least buy them some bananas. A banana seller is just right around the corner.

The guide was very knowledgeable and the fee paid included the guide. So there is no need to pay more. 

The Osun festival happens around the 2nd or 3rd week of August and we were told that was the best time to visit. 

The artworks were breathtaking and I asked the Osun goddess for triplets and loads of wealth. I hope she heard me. Lol.

title: A must-see for any visitor to western Nigeria
text:
Or perhaps I should clarify a little. It's a must-see for anyone with an interest in African history, art, culture and religion.
The ideal time to visit the grove would be at the culmination of the Osun Festival which holds annually in August. In addition to all that the grove has to offer, the August tourist will have the opportunity to take in a vibrant ceremony whose traditions date back a few hundred years. 
I have toured the grove unassisted in the past but during my recent visits, it's been made increasingly difficult to tour the site without engaging one of the official guides. Their fee is not exorbitant - I think I paid the equivalent of less than $20 for a 3-hour tour (you can spend more or less time depending on how much time you're willing and able to spend at each shrine or statue). 
I was puzzled by the security alert attached to this site by TripAdvisor. I've never heard of anyone's safety or security being compromised in the area. I was lugging a substantial bag of blatantly expensive photographic equipment and should have been an obvious target for miscreants. I remained constantly aware fo my surroundings as I always am in unfamiliar locations and never once sensed or saw a threat. 
The forest and structures within the site would delight any photographer. The ubiquitous Mona Monkeys at the grove's entrance will entertain any nature -lover. Your own prior research or the help of a good guide will ensure that you appreciate the history and cultural significance of this place.

title: Holiday thing
text: Highly recommended for tourists.  It's good to have some banana to feed the friendly baby monkeys. They will welcome you as you enter the gate. The staff are also helpful and you are allocated a guide to take you around and give you the history.

title: Nature, Culture and Arts combined
text:
We hired a guide Toyin to take us through the forest walk which we felt enhanced the overall experience she took us to the art pieces in different locations of the sacred grove. There were amazing finds amid the serene greenery - art pieces in different locations though the sheer dedication of few folks who invested time, effort and funds to maintain and improve this place.  

We ended our tour with a visit to Susanne Weger's house which we highly recommend as well.

Note that there is a camera fee for phone cameras 1000 naira and normal cameras and 3000 naira so plan ahead on who should be the assigned photographer!

title: Touch of nature and close to nature
text: It is an experience worth having in seeing the power of nature and what the Supreme being has given to us to adore HIM

title: Road Trip to Osun-Osogbo Sacred Groove
text:
My trip to the famous Osun-Osogbo Sacred groove was breathtaking as I had so much fun and was also educated about Osogbo and It's people.

The groove is believed to have a supernatural healing powers that cures illnesses, most especially bareness.

There are a few restricted zones in the groove namely: Igbo Ifa (Meaning Forest of Ifa - a god) and the second Ataoja's palace (Ataoja is the title of the traditional ruler of Osogbo land) believed to be the meeting place of the Ogboni confraternity.

Ultimately, the environment is quite serene and the tour guides knows their job as they are prompt to provide answers to questions.

You can also visit astrologers for less that $5 if you want to...."smiles".

I recommend this site to anyone planning to visit Osogbo anytime soon.

Please feel free to ask any question you have an I will try as much as possible to answer them to the best of my knowledge.

Gracias.

title: Serene in a magical way
text: The Osun-Osogbo groove is a UNESCO world heritage site. It is beautiful and serene in a magical way. The sculptures are huge and very intricately detailed. The annual Osun-Osogbo Festival sees this place packed with worshipers and tourists. Visit the groove to feel closer to nature and learn more about the rich history of the Yoruba people.

title: MY CRADLE
text: this is my origin. I have absolutely nothing negative to write about this historical heritage of all Osun origins.

title: Another Visit
text: The last time i was here was in 1985, as with before i have a chaperone as i was travelling via Osun to the North, quite an experience and highly recommended if you are interested in history and mythology

title: one of those truly globally unique places
text: the whole Osogbo experience is very special particularly if you have affinity with local culture.  First, the sacred Grove is magical for two reasons. 1.  that it is still a functioning Shrine for the ancient Yoruba religion - for Osun the Water Goddess - is rare in a country when fundamental Christianity and Islam has destroyed much of the original Orisha and other local Nigerian religious sites.  2 that the outstanding and mystical art of Suzanne Wenger so clearly fraternises with the local environment that they both become as one.  Second, when you are in osogbo make sure you visit Suzanne's amazing house, Nike's gallery and art complex where students learn traditional cultural crafts such as Adire (traditional Yoruba batik).

title: Highlight of My Time in South Eastern Nigeria
text:
The sacred grove was such a sight to see! The artwork was just incredible and the history surrounding it is very interesting. Luckily my fiancee and I were visiting a friend who lives in Ile Ife, and had him as our escort and guide, which made things much easier. To be honest doing anything sans a friend who is a local or native is basically impossible, unless you know the culture and are a seasoned traveler. However the people of Osogbo were very nice and welcoming, if not a bit wary or curious as to our presence as foreigners. My fiancee and I wanted to learn as in depth as we could about the Ifa religion and thanks to our friends and his acquaintances we were able to. 

I lived in Nigeria for over 2 years (In Yola, Adamawa) and my time in Ife/Osogbo and the surrounding areas was the most enjoyable time I had in those two years. I love the Yoruba people, they are kind and warm people and probobly the most sincere you will find in Nigeria. 

This is a place many people will never see and it really is a damn shame, because this part of Nigeria is steeped in history, tradition, and beauty. Love love love the Osun Grove!

title: Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove
text:
One of the fewest UNESCO World Heritage Centre (WHC) in Nigeria, Osun-Osogbo Sacred Grove is a must view place for every traveller.  A place that has its own traditional background which is respected even now by every sorts of people in the town.  Reasonable entry fee with guide, additional charges for Photography...

http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osun-Osogbo

title: OSUN RIVER
text: Yo fui al festival de Osun, me gustó mucho. Les recomiendo que vayan a finales de agosto, que es la fecha del festival. Se hace una procesión desde el templo de Osun hasta el río, ahí se pueden ver los bailes y la música tradicionales y los ritos a Osun, la deidad del rio. La gente es muy amable. Las personas que tocan los tambores les querrán tocar a cambio de dinero como aportación voluntaria, ya es de cada quien si aceptan o no. También hay adivinaciones de los sacerdotes y sacerdotisas. Es un ambiente muy agradable, hay visitantes tanto locales como extranjeros (asiáticos, europeos, americanos, latinoamericanos). También hay mucha seguridad, hay muchos policías ese día porque al evento va el rey de Osogbo. Hay muchas actividades por hacer, muchas cosas qué ver y mucha gente qué conocer. Yo sí les recomiendo la visita.

title: Sacred or secret?
text:
Nice place to visit, admission fee includes a guide, which is very welcome and you will learn a lot about this forest. Somehow they want to rip you off with the photography charge/fee, which is incredibly expensive, so try to make a some kind of a deal.

Recommended.

title: Elmina Tours Free Walking Tours
text:
We discovered Origins Hidden History free walking tours on their website; elminatours.com. We met our guide at Fort Jago at 10am, we were 9 people on the tour. We wanted to explore Elmina Town and meet with the locals, this tour gave us the chance.
We had lots of questions and the guide answered all of them, he was well versed in local history and did a fantastic job. The tour was free but we tipped him $40 for the two of us. They also run a African Traditional Beliefs tour which we will definitely do next time. Highly recommended for detailed information and shocking facts.

title: Ein absolutes Muss bei einem Ghana-Besuch
text: Ein Besuch des Elmina Castle die über Jahrzehnte in erster Linie als Sklavenburg gedient hat ist wohl eine der interessantesten Sehenswürdigkeiten an der Küste. Ich habe die Führung schon zwei mal gemacht und es war immer sehr interessant.

title: Moving teacheable experience
text: Elmina castle was constructed by the Portuguese who wished to pursue their interests in gold and the promulgation of their faith. Somehow (!!!) they ended up trading in human flesh as part of The transatlantic slave trade. There are old artefacts that remain at the castle and a visit is a must for anyone who wants to get a better understanding of the trade and the African diaspora. I travelled with a party of adults and teens to take a tour of the dungeons where human beings were chained oftentimes in close proximity to the slavers’ places of worship. It’s a moving, educational experience. But, and this is a drawback that MUST be fixed, our guide did not speak clearly. He was muffled or too softly spoken, too fast and wouldn’t stop to make sure we’d understood. One member of my party heard nothing but a few dates rattled out so quickly they made no sense to him. What a missed opportunity!! Elmina Castle, please fix this!! Everyone else: please visit.

title: Overshadows Cape Coast Castle
text: The value added to our visit to this paramount attraction was the excellent orientation and commentary by guide and author Ato Ashun. If you can only see one castle on the coast, be sure that it is this one. BTW, the Coconut Grove Bridge House café across the bridge is perfect for lunch.

title: An educational trip - A reality check-up
text:
This tour of Elmina Castle was a reality check for me.  It brought home the horrors of human history.  The tour guide was excellent.  I will recommend.

The only tip is to be careful of the boys outside the castle trying to sell some shells trying to swindle money out of visitors by getting you to sponsor non-existent local football teams.

title: A meeting with the dark part of our common history - and a pledge for acting today!
text:
This castle was built in the 1480s by the Portuguese and soon became an important hub for the Trans-Atlantic slave trade, continuing well into the 19th century under the command of different European powers. The stories told are shocking and humbling - and should hopefully serve to make us better embrace the value of universal human rights and react against today's modern forms of slavery. 

While the international context and drivers behind the slave trade are aspects relatively well covered by the guides, attention should also be given to the local circumstances under which the trade prospered - that is, also reflecting the local rulers' role in the slave trade. This is not a pledge to be "fair" in describing this horrible history - but rather to leave "political correctness" and focus on the factual power relations instead. Only then may this horrendous chapter learn us something.

title: Excellent Tour Guide Explaining The history About The Castle & Area
text: Being out on my full day tour on Monday 20/11/17 with my driver Ben & friend Radak we arrived at Elmina Castle early afternoon & admission fee 40.00 Cedi. Joined a small group of tourists & the young male tour guide was very informative explaining about the history of the Castle going back a few hundred years, shown around different parts of the Castle & reflecting on the terrible past of the prisoners. The guided tour last approximately one hour & you were then free to look around at your own pace taking many beautiful pics especially along the coastline & the historical architectural structure, a very interesting insight about the past & continuous restoration work on-going to maintain the structure for the next generation. A couple of Souvenir shops to browse around with an excellent selection choice of Ghanian postcards & gifts. I highly recommend a visit to the Castle while visiting Ghana.

title: Interresant og lærerikt
text: Guidet tur rundt på slottet. Vi fulgte slavenes vei gjennom fangehull og ut til stedet de ble satt i båter og lastet på skip for ferden over havet. Kunnskapsrik guide og flott slott!

title: An amazing place. Rich in history.
text: What an amazing place. It is really well preserved and the guides share with you not only the history, but what this building means for the people of Africa. Well worth a visit!

title: A piece of special architecture, an area of sadness and well kept piese of a castle.
text:
.Elmina’!!..Not a lot going on but an interesting fishing community with lot of history.
 i have been to all the castle and fort around the coaster part of Ghana and the story seems to be the same,.."The Black man has always worked hard!..the boarders are closed to them even to their colonial masters who benefited massively from them, it sad!..even today the black man still fight on to get basic needs but one-day very soon, we will all understand that blood is red in every animal created..i am too emotional now...sorry.
.before i talk about something, let me just thank the organization for keeping the place well,..Very well preserved castle. The tour guides give an excellent potted history of the castle and its role in the slave trade..
we need love, everyone needs love an acceptance....

title: Molto interessante
text: Molto interessante, vale sicuramente la pena visiterlo, compreso il Fish market di Elmina a pochi passi da lì

title: An imposing structure
text: A substantial castle set immediately on the coast in Elmina village dominating the coastline no doubt adding to the impression of power to those it enslaved. 40GHc entrance fee for foreigners which is just about reasonable given that you have a large structure to explore. You can have a guide and have the history explained to you but that is easy to find or already well known otherwise why are you here? Suffice to say that this predates the more frequently visited Cape Coast castle by around 150 years but shares the common theme of its primary use. Well worth a visit in a easy photographic location. There are the usual scams tried outside where they'll ask your name so it will be on a bracelet when you come out and try to make you feel guilty to buy it or 'sponsor their school'. Just firmly and politely say no and they are not troublesome.

title: Uma experiência marcante
text: Nenhuma pessoa fica imune à experiência de visitar um lugar que lembra o sofrimento de um povo e a marca vergonhosa da escravidão!

title: A piece of European architecture that came to symbolise man's inhumanity to man.
text: Elmina started life as a coastal store house for the early 15th century Portuguese traders in West Africa. It was so  named because of the nearby inland mines. Once the Portuguese traders, in return for their goods, started to accept captured slaves as a form of currency from local warrior chieftains, the store rooms of Elmina  began to be used for holding slaves.  Elmina is small compared to some of the other coastal slave forts but still exudes an immense feeling of pathos as the visitor passes through the same hellish rooms in which hundreds of men, women and children were incarcerated for before their trans-Atlantic crossing. The castle possesses an original "door of no return" through which the slaves would have to pass through onto the boats.

title: Heart rending
text: This is a well kept castle steeped in rather disgraceful behaviour by The Dutch and Portuguese in particular. Different times but how could religious people commit such heinous crimes against humanity. The Gate of No Return is an emotional expetisne. Just gaze  out to sea and think how you would feel leaving everything behind, not knowing what to expect especially after weeks in the inhumane and fetid conditions.

title: Fantastic....Must have a guide
text: We went to the Elmina Castle with a tour group run by Transafrica, a tour group specializing in tours in West Africa. The experience was very educational, moving, and emotional. To see one of the many doors of no return and to learn how the slaves were treated below the church service, was depressing. However, it's an important part of history and the guide's words at the end were thoughtful when he encouraged all of us who had been angered by the inhumane treatment of those who passed through the fort's gates, to not become the thing we hate. So in that way, I think this is a must do.

title: Spannend
text: Ein weiteres der sehr interessanten Sklaven-Forts an der ghanaischen Küste. Eine Führung vermittelt fesselnde Einblicke in die düstere Zeit des Sklavenhandels und die schlimme Rolle der Europäer dabei. Sehenswert!

title: Emotional but worth going
text: We had a wonderful tour guide Korfi, I must say it was not easy when they tell you the happenings of that place, in some places I felt claustrophobic because when you use your imagination to try experience what it was like. As an African you go through the strangest emotions as you go through the castle I felt shock, anger, betrayal and helplessness at some point I felt like crying. It also felt like some of the slaves are still there. Do not get me wrong that was my personal experience and it was worth it for me.

title: et must når man er i Ghana
text: Imponerende fort med skræmmende historie. Inkluderet i entre er en guidet rundvisning. Guiden var generelt godt vidende, men lidt uinspirerende i attitude. Vær opmærksom på at rundvisningen ender med at du bliver ledt ud af en udgang, og derfor ikke kan vende tilbage for at tage fotos eller selv gå rundt, med mindre du aftaler det med guiden

title: Eindrucksvolle Sklavenhändlerfestung
text: Informative Führung, ausführliche Erklärungen, Antworten auf Fragen. Mindestens eine Sklavenhändlerfestung sollte jeder Ghana-Reisende besichtigt haben.

title: Trés important
text: Miroir du Sénégal et de l'Afrique subsaharienne. Plein de vestiges historiques. Mais aussi et surtout lieu symbolique  hébergeant le laboratoire CARBONE 14 du fameux historien et scientifique le Professeur Cheikh Anta Diop.

title: sztuka Afryki
text: Miejsce warte zobaczenia - wystawione oryginalne, wartościowe przedmioty sztuki Senegalu , Afryki Zachodniej.Dostępna jest ekspozycja stała ale są także wystawy czasowe - warto ,choćby żeby porównać  z masówką dla turystów udającą sztukę.

title: Molto interessante, peccato le scarse condizioni in cui versa
text: Come detto nel titolo, questo museo è molto interessante per gli amanti della storia e dell'arte dell'Africa Occidentale, contiene infatti molti oggetti e manufatti provenienti da tutta l'Africa Occidentale, non solo dal Senegal. Peccato che però la descrizione dei singoli oggetti esposti indichi solo di che oggetto si tratta e la regione (o lo stato) di provenienza, mancando interamente altre importantissime informazioni riguardo la datazione e una descrizione più accurata degli oggetti. Manca inoltre anche la divisione delle opere esposte per regione o paese, facendo risultare il tutto un po' confusionario. Di contro è da notare l'estrema gentilezza e cordialità del personale presente, pronto a rispondere alle più disparate domande. Prezzo del biglietto un po' troppo alto per la dimensione del museo e lo stato di conservazione dello stesso; per i non residenti e gli stranieri il prezzo d'ingresso è infatti di ben 5000 franchi. Tutto sommato però una visita in questo museo, se si è a Dakar, è d'obbligo!

title: Da visitare
text: Un museo bello e pieno di cose interessanti, oggetti di grande rilievo e una splendida collezione di tessuti e abiti. Da non perdere assolutamente. Dotato anche di un fornito shop.

title: Mooi gebouw met een aantal interessante maskers
text: Typisch Afrikaans lekker stoffig museum. Leuk om even door heen te lopen. Een aantal mooie trommels waaronder een enorme spleet trommel! Buiten is een tuin met foto's van Senegal.

title: Interesting African Art
text: This museum is small but it is full of different African masks and statues used to ward off evil spirits or for fertility rituals.  It was very interesting.  When we visited, there was an additional exhibit in the building behind the main building on art found carved in rock.  It was amazing to see.

title: For lovers of real African Art
text: The museum offers exhibitions of real quality African Art. It is professionally curated. Organization and ambiance are truly African (poor maintenance and lots of dust). The entrance fee is a little high but still worth it, if art is your passion. It is situated at Plateau, not far from most embassies and the seaside, where you can have a nice drink or meal after the visit in one of the hotels. IFAN always offers special exhibitions during the biannual DakArt.

title: Da vedere
text: Piccolo museo di arte africana della regione occidentale.Interessante raccolta di maschere per ogni tipo di cerimonia. Attualmente al primo piano esposizione di tessuti e delle tecniche tessili.Un po ' caro l'ingresso ma merita

title: Ok. That's the best I can do...
text: Small collection. Check out the photos here and you will have seen most of the permanent collection on the first floor. 2nd floor has temporary exhibition. In any case - you can be in and out in 10-30 minutes...

title: African Art Museum
text:
The museum is small but has a lot of art from other parts of Africa. During our visit, their were two very good exhibits. 
   The textile exhibit featured cloth making mechanisms and clothes produced as collages, tapestry and clothing.
   The second exhibit show cased works of college students in the subject of black/white and dark/light.

title: A ne pas manquer
text:
Ce musée est situé au centre ville de Dakar quartier du plateau à côté de l'assemblée national. C'est un bâtiment de 1936 situé sur un terrain qui dispose de beaucoup d'espace. Le premier directeur de l'IFAN était Théodore Monod, un  savant explorateur français. Je conseille impérativement au visiteur de faire comme moi, de le visiter avec une guide du musée qui fournit toutes les explications sur chaque objet présenté. 
Il est vrai que ce musée nécessiterait d'être agrandi et la présentation des objets devraient pouvoir bénéficier des derniers cris de la muséographie. Mais cela nécessite  un budget d'investissement qui fait défaut au conservateur de ce musée. Dommage car ce lieu de mémoire le mériterait bien.

title: Beautiful building and small collection
text: Посетили этот музей по соседству с прекрасным собором,чтобы увидеть искусство Западной Африки.Но экспозиция довольно скудная,современные работы художников идентичные продающимся в арт деревне.Настоящих старинных артефактов совсем немного.Рекомендую посетить,если больше совсем делать нечего.

title: Bel édifice, belle collection mais peu mise en valeur
text: agréable visite cependant mais il manquait des explications sur la collection permanente plutôt riche. Exposition temporaire de tissus intéressante. Accueil agréable

title: Музей
text: Музей Сенегала удивил. Приличная коллекция живописи, скульптур. Да и в жару укрыться в самый раз. Особо запомнились работы художников-примитивистов.

title: Not to miss
text: Very interesting museum in Dakar, with some wonderful African art. A must see when you are there. Tickets are a bit expensive to get in, and unfortunately the maintenance of the building is not good (dust everywhere, etc.). But still a very interesting landmark.

title: Musée très intéressant et bâtiment non sans intérêt
text: Le musée était fermé il y a deux ans. Il est de nouveau ouvert et est vraiment très intéressant et très bien présenté à mon sens. De plus, le musée est très bien situé.

title: Brilliant
text: Amazing collection of African arts. As with so much of 'traditional' art though there is little info about the creators/artists. But there is some stunning stuff. I wish there had been an English guide or captions. and it needs a cafe in the gardens

title: African art
text: The IFAN museum, also called le Musée de Théodore Monod, is a small museum on Place Soweto, Dakar. The entrance fee is CFA 5.000, about 8 US dollars. The ground floor has collections of African objects not only from Senegal but also from surrounding countries. The first floor houses textile items, both new ones produced by well-known artisans and old items. The visit does'nt take long, since the museum is small, but it is worth seeing.

title: Chwila wytchnienia od zaczepiania na ulicy
text: Małe muzeum. Ciekawe maski, ale ich opis jest po francusku. Jeśli nie znacie tego języka choć trochę, to połowa przyjemności odpada i chyba nie warto wydawać pieniędzy - 5.000 XOF dla "nierezydentow".

title: tres interressant
text: un musée qui reflete bien les cultures de la region, malgrés tout la partie esclavage est trés orientée anti-colon et ne fait pas apparaitre que les premieres traites d'esclaves en afrique etaient intra-ethniques.....Copie a revoir

title: Lovely little shop which supports local charities
text: Got a lovely warm welcome at this great little fair trade shop that sells local arts and crafts and supports the local community including organisations that support women and children in Cape Verde. Lovely selection of local crafts made sustainably and ensuring the is no exploitation of juvenile workers. Make sure to pay them a visit

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art
placeInfo.address: Rua 1 de Junho Predio Plaza, Santa Maria, Ilha do Sal 4111 Cape Verde

title: Negozietto solidale
text:
Sono anni che vado a santa Maria ma non ero mai entrata in questo negozio. Prima della partenza a fine novembre mi sono docummebtata sullaoro attività. 
Tutto ciò che viene venduto è realizzato a mano da capoverdiani: si possono trovare soprammobili, cappellini, liquori, orecchini, borse, bamboline, tante cose sfiziose e particolari introvabili in ogni altro posto. 

Il negozio si trova sulla via principale di santa maria, lo noterete per i colori vivaci della vetrina. 
sostiene anche iniziative benefiche a favore di famiglie bisognose con l associazione nu bai: vengono raccolti materiali scolastici da utilizzare x le borse di studio, ora anche filati x permettere alle donne di creare prodotti artigianali da vendere ed intraprendere un attività, sostiene anche i carcerati fornendo loro prodotti utili.
Tutto può essere consegnato in negozio e poi verrà distribuito. 
Ho trovato grande cortesia da parte dei ragazzi che ci lavorano, sono simpatici e disponibili a illustrare la loro merce. 
Se siete a santa Maria entrate e sostenete la località

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art
placeInfo.address: Rua 1 de Junho Predio Plaza, Santa Maria, Ilha do Sal 4111 Cape Verde

title: Marque page
text: Ma cousine qui a passé des vacances au cap vert m'a ramené un marque page acheté à Djunta Mo Art .Il est très joli , très original et quand je sais le soutien que sa vente apporte à cette association Il a encore plus de valeur à mes yeux

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art

title: Great shop!
text: Lovely shop with perfect gifts and souvenirs. Helpful and friendly shop staff too. Defintely recommended.

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art
placeInfo.address: Rua 1 de Junho Predio Plaza, Santa Maria, Ilha do Sal 4111 Cape Verde

title: 101% Capo Verde
text: Negozio visitato il primo giorno di vacanza durante il giro a Santa Maria. Non semplici souvenir, come ci hanno spiegato, ma solamente prodotti fatti a mano da artigiani locali! Articoli di ogni tipo e per tutti i gusti, un assortimento davvero completo. Aggiungiamo il fatto che supportano anche associazioni non-profit e cooperative di Capo Verde, insomma più di un motivo valido per non uscire dal negozio a mani vuote. Il caso ha voluto che io dovessi fare un regalo una volta andato via però. Per questo motivo, devo ringraziare una delle proprietarie, Gaia, per la sua immensa disponibilità, la sua gentilezza e soprattutto la sua pazienza. Con il suo aiuto e di tutta la sua squadra sono riuscito a fare un regalo anche a distanza!

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art

title: Uma loja única e diferente em Artes Artesanais
text:

E por parte do atendimento (são simplesmente fantástico e te ajudam a encontrar um produto a que procuras)
Uma loja Mesmo top.

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art

title: Genuine souvenirs of Cape Verde
text: In contrast to most of the tat on sale in Santa Maria (and elsewhere) the products on sale in Djunta Mo are genuine souvenirs of Cape Verde, made by local people and sold for their benefit. They are unique and of good quality. It is well worth visiting and supporting.

placeInfo.name: Djunta Mo Art

Qui troverete oggetti handmade with love (borse, astucci, portachiavi, bambole realizzate davvero con amore!), marmellate di banana e papaya, liquori locali e tanto altro ancora! Un negozio al 100% equo e solidale! Io ho avuto il grande piacere di conoscere personalmente anche una delle titolari, Gaia, che non smetterò mai di ringraziare per il tempo che ci ha dedicato..

text: Girando tra i negozietti di Santa Maria siamo arrivati in questo negozio di artigianato Capoverdiano, finalmente ho trovato un posto dove si vendono veri prodotti artigianali e non le solite statuine senegalesi o i gadget cinesi. La commessa mi ha spiegato che oltre la vendita c'è un progetto sociale di volontariato per il sostegno delle famiglie Capoverdiane meno abbienti. È bello vedere che le piccole.cose possono acquistare in valore incalcolabile. title: Regali unici 100% made in Capo Verde
text: Sulla strada principale e pedonale di Santa Maria subito dopo la piazza c'e questo fantastico negozio che racchiude tutto l',artigianato delle varie isole di Capo Verde. Si possono trovare articoli di vario genere dalle borse fatte a mano, ai bijou, alle statuine di foglie di mais e ceramica,tartarughe e bambole di pezza ,ai liquori locali e marmellate fantastiche, calamite fatte con le conchigliee poi creme,saponi naturali e tante altri oggetti utili e carini. Che dire ce n'è per tutti, noi abbiamo preso i nostri regalini e che li ha ricevuti  sono stati tutti entusiasti. Oltre a comprare qualcosa di originale e 100% made in cape verde aiuti anche gli artigiani locali a sviluppare le loro attività. Lo consiglio a tutti  passate a visitare il negozio.

text:
la Promesse ….. 
oui la promesse de revenir au musée ! La promesse d’un avenir … la promesse en elle même peut ne pas s’accomplir, au final c’est une promesse

title: A vibrant celebration of African art and culture.
text:
La Fondation Zinsou is a must-visit for anyone interested in contemporary African art and culture. The collection is beautifully curated, with stunning works by talented artists from Benin and across the continent. The exhibits are thought-provoking and offer a fresh perspective on African creativity and heritage.

This visit was recommended by Orisha Trails, and I’m so glad I took their advice ! They organized my visit seamlessly, and their insights into Benin’s art scene made the experience even more enriching. If you’re in Benin, don’t miss this gem.

title: Small
text: Small, exhibit with some nice masks, pleasant student guide explained the voodoo spirits. 1000 CFA suggested donation. The other museum/fort was closed. I walked 9 miles around town, found little else to do in Ouidah. The 400 year-old baobab tree between the  church and Python Temple was my favorite...

title: Exhibits change frequently, free entry
text:
The entrance is free of charge. There is a suggested donation. But they are not pushy.

Modern art is not really my thing, so this exhibit was not really my thing.
But I appreciate the guides and the foundation's commitment to African artists.

title: Un incontournable pour comprendre art et culture du Bénin
text: Visite très intéressante avec notre guide Primaël. L’entrée est gratuite et les expositions sont renouvelées plusieurs fois par an. L’art était un excellent support pour comprendre la culture et les modes de vie du Bénin, notamment liés au vaudou. Je recommande, même si vous n’êtes pas spécialement sensible à l’art contemporain

title: Nice exhibit
text: The museum looks like it has been renovated recently and it is well maintained. Was surprised to see the variety of art from artists in Benin and different parts of Africa. They are exhibiting really nice pieces.

title: Centre culturel incontournable !
text:
Très bel endroit ! c'est l'association du Contemporain et de l'héritage ! 
le lieu est riche et vivant culturellement !

title: Un musée contemporain dans un lieu historique du Vaudou .
text:
Le musée Zensou de Ouidah est un bel exemple de ce que peut faire une organisation privée pour la diffusion de la culture et de l'art local .
Situé dans une demeure de charme entièrement rénovée ,il présente des œuvres contemporainnes d'artistes africains ou autres. 

La lumière diffuse met en valeur les objets exposés et le guide est très explicite sur leurs signification  et expressions.  Ce musée est gratuit et l'on peut faire un don . Je recommande la visite de ce lieu  ,qui fait honneur au mécénat . Dans le jardin interieur on.peut découvrir des œuvres en rapport avec le vaudou qui est largement pratiqué à Ouidah avec la fête début janvier. La statue du dieu  vaudou Tohossou , dieu de l'eau à trois têtes avec son serpent , ainsi que Mami Wata , la redoutable  animent le jardin au gazon presque british . A voir absolument !!

title: Esposizioni di arte contemporanea
text: Forse il posto che più mi ha colpita in Benin: una bellissima collezione di arte africana contemporanea, allestita in una antica casa padronale nel centro di Ouidah, perfettamente conservata. La guida che ci ha accompagnato era davvero preparata e appassionata di arte. Consiglio vivamente una sosta nella caffetteria che offre deliziosi succhi freschi ed è arredata con grande gusto.

title: Un lieu magnifique, des euvres admirables, une équipe très sympathque
text:
Un musée absolument incontournable si vous passez par Ouidah. 
Layo Primaël, l 'excellent guide présente admirablement les œuvres de l’exposition temporaire et connait bien l'histoire de l'art. Vu , début septembre, des œuvres de grands artistes africains ou européens dont l’accrochage est simple et valorisant.  
Le lieu est d'une grande beauté architecturale. Bravo pour la restauration. Un café-restaurant très stylé, dont les prix accessibles pour tout Européen le sont sans doute moins pour les visiteurs locaux, auxquels le musée s'adresse pourtant grâce à une intelligente gratuité.  Hâte d'y retourner!

title: Endroit a visiter
text: Bonjour , c'est un endroit  historique a visiter. Si vous voulez faire partir de notre groupe de touristes internationaux pour visiter cet endroit et pleins d'autres au Bénin a l'occasion de la fête annuelle du vodoun en Janvier 2020  , contactez moi: +447554783736 .

title: Charming Surprise
text: Was pleasantly surprised by this place. Charming and fun and educational. Yes the cafe is pricey but the ambiance was worth it. Only issue was no running water on day I visited but they had a water barrel.

title: Varie proposte culturali interessanti
text: In questo museo ho visitato una mostra sulla città di Cotonou, con vecchie foto. Esposizione interessante e brava la guida. Ci sono spesso mostre tematiche.

title: Un des meilleurs et authentiques musée du Bénin. Je remercie beaucoup la fondation pour cette merveille!
text: C'est un musée excellent! Avec une équipe très accueillante.  Le bâtiment qui l'abrite est une des plus ancien à Ouidah. Dedans, on y retrouve une collection d’œuvres artistiques provenant de tous les coins du monde. Il me manque des mots. Franchement, c'est une merveille !!!!

title: Beautiful, well kept
text: Beautiful, well kept museum showcasing contemporary African art. The wallpaper and decor in the cafe was too beautiful. Garden very well kept, we watched a mini documentary about the making of some of the art. We also didn't pay to go in. They have a gift shop if you want some souvenirs though I didn't buy any there because they were a bit pricey

title: Building is nicely renovated, the exhibition was so so
text: We loved the way the Afro-Brazilian building was renovated. Really amazing. The exhibition itself was not interesting - the one in Cotonou was much much better. Definitely worth a visit.

title: A ne pas rater
text: Magnifique expo réalisée au Bénin par la jeune artiste Pauline Guerrier. Un travail réalisé après un long séjour au Bénin et notamment des ateliers avec des enfants.

title: Magnifique musée
text: On a hésité à y venir, et nous n'avons pas été déçu. Le batiment est très beau et les expositions sont magnifiques et inintéressantes. Art contemporain mélangeant les traditions anciennes donne de très belles pièces à voir.

title: A unique creative Art museum in Benin Republic
text: The creativity of this place and the dedication of the staffs is worthy of note. The curators are always patient. The site has a English speaking curator. The art shop upstair is very picturesque.

title: très beau musée
text: Ouidah, ville formidablement vivante et chargée d’histoire, a ce très beau musée. Art contemporain béninois souvent. Il est heureux de voir des créateurs s’exprimer librement et être exposés ainsi. De plus les guides du musée vous accompagnent et leurs explications sont intéressantes. L’accueil au bar est très sympa aussi. Mérite le détour.

title: Wool building but fairly small
text: This is a little cheaper to visit that the Louvre ($9 vs $15) but 1/100th the size and a lot hotter. They have a few unique items, but hardly worth the price. You can see the whole two floors in thirty minutes. Very cool deco building in good repair.

title: Relatively small museum with relatively expensive entrance fee
text: This is a relatively small museum with a relatively expensive entrance fee. It took us no more than 35 minutes to see the entire thing. Save this for a rainy afternoon, or if you're in Dakar for along time and looking to check it off your list. There are only a couple museums in the whole city.

title: Une collection réduite dans un lieu néanmoins incontournable plein d'un charme desuet
text: Nous n'allons jamais à Dakar sans passer par le musée IFAN. D'abord, son emplacement en ville permet de passer devant le palais présidentiel depuis la place de l'indépendance  (10 minutes à pied) puis de ressortir en direction de l'agréable avenue Senghor et rejoindre l'Institut de France (ex Centre culturel) à 15 minutes à pied. Ensuite le bâtiment est entouré dans beau jardin avec baobab et flamboyants, ce qui permet de faire une pause verte et aérée non négligeable dans une ville très polluée et embouteillée comme Dakar. A l'intérieur la collection d'oeuvres d'art est un peu décevante par la quantité et par la qualité avec peu voire pas d'oeuvres majeures. Du coup le ticket d'entrée parait un peu cher mais l'accueil est toujours sympathique alors... Certains costumes traditionnels manquent également depuis notre dernière visite. Mais nous aimons toujours autant nous y rendre, car pour ceux qui savent observer, une atmosphère spéciale y règne. D'aucuns pensent que des esprits y vivent et se manifestent la nuit....

title: Hidden treasure of history
text: This museum was a gem to find in the midst of Dakar.  Open space that showcases the history and beautiful art of Senegal and other surrounding countries.  Special exhibit on the national sport of wrestling was a pleasant surprise the day I visited. Not busy at all, but plan accordingly for your visit, they are not open on Mondays.

title: Circuit
text:
A visiter ...c le musée le plus important et le plus fourni de Dakar pour ne pas dire du Sénégal...
Un musée à 2 niveaux représentant  l'ensemble des masques et des différents rites et cérémonies de l'Afrique de l'ouest...
Le seul hic est que l'entrée est chère donc il n'est pas très accessible...surtout aux clients des  tour operators
Il gagnerait de la revoir à la baisse pour recevoir plus de visiteurs...

title: Nice free flowing museum, needs a bit more narration
text: I visited this museum twice, once when they had an outdoor exhibit about Senegalese fighters (only visited the outside as the museum itself was closed) and another time, when I managed to catch during visiting hours.  The entrance fee depends on whether you are a national or not (2000CFA for nationals and 5000 for non nationals if I recall well).  On my second visit, the lower level was filled with artifacts and sculptures from all over West Africa.  It would be great if there was more information/description before each artifact but it was still a great collection (if a bit dusty).  The Senegalese fighters exhibit had now moved to the top Ievel and that was as interesting as the 1st time I saw it.  learned a lot about the fighters and the fighting tradition, something quite unique to Senegal.

title: Музей искусств
text: Старейший и самый солидный музей искусств Западной Африки. Самая богатая коллекция получилась в результате того, что музей курировал первый президент Сенегала. Интересное место.

title: une très belle collection d'objets venant de toute l'Afrique de l'Ouest
Not much to see and certainly no crowd-drawer
text: I was told it is a must to do in Dakar. Well, there is not much to do in Dakar and for sure this small and nice collection of masks is not really worth the efford. But why they charge 7.50 Euros is a riddle for sure, thats the price of the Louvre. Rib off, just one of many in the Senegal, this place is totally overpized. I would not mind, if it would show where the money goes to, but it unfortunately doesn't. So if you have not seen this museum, your life will still go running:-)

title: Una visita obbligatoria
text: Se andate o fate una sosta a Dakar, per quanto breve sia, dovete visitare l'IFAN, luogo depositario della grande arte africana. Molte statue, maschere e oggetti esposti provenienti da vari paesi: le spiegazioni non sono sempre esaustive e sono solo in francese, ma vale la pena fermarsi almeno un paio d'ore. Al piano superiore visitate la mostra fotografica e di oggetti legata alla lotta senegalese, molto particolare.

title: Theodor Monod created this museum... and if it were not for the occasional exhibitions, it would have very little intere
text: This museum has not been taken care of since its creation. Only when there is an exhibition or a "foire" is there an effort made to revive the space.

title: small but interesting
text: this places contains stuff from all over west africa, which is interesting.  Mostly masks and other traditional stuff, covering the full spectrum of life and death. top floor has some pictures of wrestling which is a big sport in Senegal

title: Décevant
text: L'exposition permanente est vraiment réduite. C'est dommage, car elle contient de superbes objets. L'organisation thématique de ceux-ci mériterait un peu plus d'explications, quelques cartes pour aider le visiteur à se repérer sur la provenance. Il y a du potentiel.
