title: Imperdível mas ao abandono
text:
Património importante e fundamental na História da Ilha de Santiago. Foi sujeito a uma recuperação fantástica. Vistas imperdíveis. 

Infelizmente está em fase de abandono que poderá ter consequências nefastas óbvias: Pagamento com cartões avariado (5€/pessoa); os funcionários da bilheteira não fornecem qualquer tipo de informação, e apenas por muita insistência nossa permitiram a visualização de um vídeo informativo bastante interessante. 
Entrada no forte com a grade encostada dando a entender que está fechado mas afinal é visitavel. 
Todos os placards de informações estão tão degradados que não se lê nada. O passadiço dentro do forte, está interdito porque tem uns cabos e uns apoios partidos: algo de facilmente seria arranjado. 

Falta de profissionalismo, abandono e manutenção num ponto turístico tão bonito e importante.

title: Humbling and Sobering Experience
text: Visited the Castle with my wife and 10 years old son and was left numb by the experience. Walking through the entire complex and seeing the sharp contrasts between the dungeons where the slaves were holed up and the lavish, expansive quarters of the slave merchants was too much to bear. What agony and dehumanizing pains my ancestors had to go through with the connivance of greedy and selfish collaborators. The huge irony for us was the Church located on the top floor of the Castle. Highly recommended for all interested in slave trade history. Very knowledgeable tour guide make the visit pleasant and highly informative.

title: Tragically infamous
text: The guided tour of the Cape Coast castle juxtaposes the beauty of the surroundings with the inhumanity of the site.  A UNESCO World Heritage site, this castle is an infamous reminder of the inhumanity of the slave trade. With a small museum on the slave trade, this is a place worth visiting.

title: Offers an opportunity to appreciate the Slave trade - Quite Emotional
text: The Tour of the Cape Coast Castle is an emotional one for any visitor, and coupled with the fact that 2019 has been tagged the 'Year of Return', the significance of the role played by the Slave trade in African history is even more apt.

title: Historical place

A must visit place to get to know more about the history of beginning of slavery. 
You will get also to enjoy the nice views of the ocean.

title: Where I started
text: I’m from the Caribbean. This is where My linage started. It’s a powerful very emotional tour. All the tragedies my ancestors had to endure. It fulfilled my heart to be able to go to where it all began although very sad and tragic. The Tour guides are very very informative and knowledgable. It think it cost 10 Ghana Cedis to enter. There’s also gift stores inside. Take time to reflect as the ocean breeze blow please don’t make this experience all about talking videos and pictures. It should be more than that.

title: Educative
text:
Nice reception 
Very good history and brief of the uses and purposes the Castle served during before and after the abolishing of slave trade

title: A Must See
text:
This is one of the most emotional trips that I have taken in my life. 
The fee to enter is really low. The guide was exceptional and although there were only 4 in my group we got our own guide and so were not rushed and could move around the facility at our own pace. He was able to answer most of our questions.
 Remember to wear comfortable shoes as there's quite a bit of ground to cover.

title: history meets Mystery meets 'his story'
text: A MUST VISIT for all visiting Ghana. A slice of history as u walk the talk and relive a part of the history and unvail the mystery surrounding the castle as you hear your guide's story of the castle - giving a slice of history best learnt lesson. On my way back from KAKUM national park  to accra i visited the place and was mesmerised by its history.. actually entered the cold dungeon where slaves were kept in chains soaked in their own excreta with only a small hole at the top to throw water to wash off the excreta when air was unbearable to those soldiers outside. From there they were taken to Door of no return to board ships to america to work in farms never to return back. Last century some of the dead bodies were brought back home from america and reburried in ghana and then the door was renamed door of return. ...

title: Insight into the past
text: Visited the castle on the return trip from Kakum National Park to Accra. Interesting to see the inside. Have a snack or lunch at the Cape Coast Restautant. Personally I found  the guild was very repetitive in his commentary. We could see how terrible the conditions were and didnt need to hear a dozen time that the chained slaves had to urinate, deficate amd menstrate over themselves and others in the dark crowded dungeons.

title: YEAR OF RETURN!
text:
I guess it's Providence that made it possible that I return to Ghana in 2019, designated by the Ghanaian authorities as the "Year of Return" - and more so, that I return to Cape Coast to see the castle again.

Some of my colleagues had not been there before and were teary on the tour of the dungeons and various parts of the slave house, as the castle guide took us around. It's always a sobering experience...

title: Ghana's must visit #1!
text: Taking a guided tour of Cape Coast Castle and learning about slavery cannot leave a sane person indifferent. So moving and very sad. There are other slave trading forts along the coast but this one is not to miss.

title: One of the many Highlights
text: AMAZING place.  The history is presented very well, with a museum with chronological story that really takes time to tell in pictures and words, so good for adults and kids alike.  This was followed by an in person tour that was derived in a sincere and sometimes chilling fashion, but it was excellent to hear the raw emotion that came through when referring to the relatively recent history.  We visited Cape Coast after we had been traveling in Ghana for a few weeks, and had spent time in the north and east, and this really tied a lot of what we had seen and learned together.  I wouldn't miss it.

title: Important Lessons on Slavery
text: A tour of this Castle will reveal important information about slavery centuries ago. It was also used for Gold trade. It is highly recommended for those who want to know about how Global trade was done in the Atlantic centuries ago.

title: Cape Coast Castle
text:
My partner and I visited this World Heritage Site on Monday and, having paid the modest fee to go inside, we’re allocated our guide, Mavis.  

We couldn’t have wished for a more educated and informative guide than Mavis. 

We spent upwards of two hours at the site in a tour that wasn’t at any staged rushed.  

We were given the time to contemplate the horror of what this place once was.  

It is, ultimately, a place and a learning experience that will stay with for a very long time.  

Well worth the effort.

title: Shocking
text: Must see if you're in Ghana. It's terrible to imagine how they treated slaves. The castle is well preserved. We did a guided tour and visited the museum. The view is wonderful.

title: Knowledge is power
text: Cape Coast Castle is one of about forty "slave castles", or large commercial forts, built on the Gold Coast of West Africa by European traders. It was originally built by the Swedes for trade in timber and gold, but later used in the trans-Atlantic slave trade.

title: Sklaven Burg in Cape Coast (Ghana) - ein Besuch wert
text:
Wir machten uns auf den Weg zur Besichtigung des UNESCO Weltkulturerbes „Elmina Castle“ — einer ehemaligen Sklavenburg.  

Elmina Castle wurde 1482 von den Portugiesen erbaut und ist die älteste von Europäern errichtete Sklavenburg Westafrikas. Im Laufe der Geschichte gehörte sie zu dem niederländischen und britischen Kolonialreich. Ursprünglich wurde die Burg für den Warenhandel zwischen Westafrika und Europa erbaut und erst später zur Sklavenburg umstrukturiert. Noch bis zur Abschaffung der Sklaverei im Jahr 1814 wurden hier ca. 3 Millionen Sklaven aus Ghana, Togo, der Elfenbeinküste und Burkina Faso unter unwürdigen Bedingungen gefangen gehalten. Innerhalb der Festung waren bis zu 600 Männer und 400 Frauen zeitgleich in unterschiedlich großen Kammern inhaftiert. Der einzige Auslass aus der Burg bestand durch die „Door of no return“, das heißt die Sklaven wurden auf Schiffen in die Karibik und nach Nordamerika deportiert.

Das Oberhaupt des Castles war der Gouverneur. Dieser suchte sich Frauen als Geliebte aus. Ergab sich daraus eine Schwangerschaft, waren sie „the lucky ones“, da sie in separaten Häusern untergebracht wurden und somit im Land blieben.

Im Vergleich zu den beengten Zellen, in denen beispielsweise bis zu 150 Frauen auf engstem Raum gefangen gehalten wurden, sind die Privaträume des Gouverneurs großzügig. Von seinen Räumen auf der obersten Ebene an der Spitze der Festung blickt er auf die Soldaten und vor allem auf die Gefangenen herab. Heute genießen wir von hier aus einen fantastischen Blick auf den Atlantik. Über die Mauern der Burg hinaus betrachten wir das Treiben des ca. 200 m entfernten Fischerhafens und des daran anschließenden Marktes. Die Fischer kennzeichnen ihre Boote mit internationalen Flaggen, um da eigene bei der Einfahrt in den Hafen schneller erkennen zu können. Die Eindrücke der Vergangenheit trüben unsere Stimmung, doch wie uns der Guide lehrt, sehen wir dies als Mahnmal der Geschichte, die sich nicht wiederholen sollte.

Letzendlich waren wir alle sehr begeistert von der Burg. Die Führung war super. Sie dauert circa 1,5 bis 2 Stunden. Es gibt auch einen kleinen Shop, in dem man Getränke und Souvenirs kaufen kann.
Toiletten sind auch vorhanden.
Es is definitv einen Besuch wert!

title: Ghana Trip
text: Depressing, sad and educational.  I wouldn't recommend for children under 10 years of age, especially if you have a sensitive child like myself

title: Cape coast white castel
text: It was an eye opening experience of what Africans went through during the slave trade period. I wasn’t myself for a while, still not myself, being so close to where it all happened. Nice cordial tour guides. Worth every penny. Africa needs restitution for what happened to them. A place to visit when in Ghana.

text: Region Aszanti wyróżnia się swym bogactwem które nie bierze się z niczego .Mieszkańcy tego regionu są bardzo pomysłowi  ,przedsiębiorczy i pracowici .Jedną z ich specjalności jest stylowe i nie powtarzalne  tkactwo określane jako Kente.. title: Bonwire
text: All the looms are there to see you can have a go yourself. its all hand made and takes a lot of skill.this was a visit you i really enjoyed.

title: The Colour or Ghana
text: We’ve been living in Ghana for 7 months and one of the key areas I’ve always endeavored to see is the Kente village! If you intend to visit the village over a weekend  be mindful of the fact that most of the village people attend funerals on Saturdays and Sundays or take the weekend off. Don’t take the road to Adawonamase - even though it’s a scenic road as per the video attached, there are no signs to indicate that you are arriving at a Kente village. You will see a few houses where people weave but best is to continue to Bonwire/Bonwei and then you have to ask where the weaving is done. You will arrive at a small Centre where a master weaver takes you through the experience of weaving and explain the various types. This is insightful and one of the better experiences in Ghana so far. Be prepared to haggle but be fair. More can be done to promote the community and the little shops selling Kente. Definitely worth visiting!

title: Real Kente. Real Ghana.
text: We see kente cloth in America all the time so it is a real treat getting to see first hand where and how it's made. You can even try making it yourself. The weavers work hard and want to sell their wares so be prepared for some aggressive haggling. Otherwise, it's a great place to visit to experience the real culture of Ghana!

title: Nothing beats Authenticity
text:
What strikes you most is the warmth of the people and their eagerness to show off their rich history of weaving. A bit of a hike to get there, but worth the trip. Be sure to walk around the village and see more than just one weaving site. 
I would recommend this trip to get another glimpse of what Ghana has to offer.

title: REAL KENTE CLOTH _ BEAUTIFUL
text: This village is absolutely incredible. If you want the real deal kente cloth - you MUST go. I spent two weeks on the Cape Coast, Accra and Kumasi. These prices are the best and you have so many options. Buy everything here!

title: Kente, Cocoa and more
text: This wonderful village was a real surprise. Hands on learning experience with terrific tour guides. You get a chance to do hands on weaving and to walk through a cocoa grove. There is also a chance to learn about the famous soap as well. Fun and educational. Wonderful shop if you want to purchase Kente Cloth where you can learn all of the meanings and even design your own fabric. A must see and do place to visit.

title: Lovely Experience
text: A good place for art lovers. There are works from different artists on different media. Talking with the artists was also very enlightening.

title: Don't go in the morning but go in afternoon or evening
text: We made the mistake of going there on the way in from the airport after an overnight flight. It looks like a very worthwhile place but most of the artists work into the night and thus only one or two of the artists were open when we arrived at 10:30 am.

title: One of the best places I've ever been
text: Despite not many of the studios being open this was one of the most amazing places I've ever been. Super bohemian, off the beaten track and slightly run down but a million miles off the standard tourist trail and market with some of the most amazing artwork I've seen outside of a museum. Sure you can probably bargin hard but I don't know why you would when you can buy very high quality art at a fraction of the price you would in the west. If you love art and are looking for something interesting to do in Dakar this is a must see. As other people have pointed out this is not a chaotic market with standard ware but a truly unique and wonderful place!

title: Not really into art, loved this place
text:
Saturday morning 27th May and this was the first stop on our all day Art & Culture tour of the City of Dakar.

On arrival we were welcomed by a delightful lady, Kane, her personality was as bright and vibrant as her long flowing colourful robe. Throughout the tour her enthusiasm and love of art bubbled over and was refreshing and infectious.

Before we set off on the Tour,  we learnt that the Village was set up in 1977 by the artist El Hadji Sy. The commune, today. is home to 53 studios where artists live and and work in their studios or open spaces.

Hadji Sy believed that art, in whatever form or material, was a personal expression and not an academic subject. His ideology was supported by the Formet President Leopold Sedar Senghor. The Gallery in the Village, which opened in July 2019 is named in honour of the former President (reviewed separately).

The Gallery was the first place we visited where we saw artworks created by the artists. We saw a variety of pieces that were created using many mediums including glass, metal, acrylics, bronze and textiles.

Our very knowledgeable Guide, Kane, told us about the Artists, what material the piece was crafted it and the artist's interpretation.

Outside the Gallery we walked along the open spaces covered by mango and carob trees. There were so many stunning artworks amongst the trees. Around the open spaces were the neat rows of the studios, we did enter a few and met the artists.

The last piece we were shown was a life-sized metal sculpture of a horse. The artist scoured the streets for materials, he believes it is not recycling but the materials have be given a new direction. Our Guide was the artist's granddaughter and she did sn excellent job showing us around and promoting the Village.

We were permitted to take photographs both inside and outside the Galley, but they were for personal use. The photos posted in my reviews are solely to promote the Village, the Gallery and the amazing experience, nothing else.

title: Great for local art - go during the week
text: I really love art so it was cool to see. It was empty on a Saturday and the locals said it is most lively during the week.

title: Hidden Gem
text: Varying levels of craftsmanship but with a little diligence you can find some really amazing artists and art.

title: I went here with SenegalStyle Tours!
text: Oh this is a must see!  I enjoyed it immensely and the tour was much better than going to African markets.

title: A wonderland!
text: for art lovers, this is a real gem nestled in the middle of nowhere! A district of Dakar.Prés of the road leading to the airport. You will meet magicians of color and creativity. Several shops, not paying mine, and behind their doors of treasure without names. I met the great master Daouda Ndiaye in his den of creation. I met the talented Baba Ly and his master paintings. I met Gibril, and his NOn metal works recycled. He insists. He wants to be the starting point, and so and so....

title: Kunst und küsteleisches Ambiente in Harmonie
text: Ein Künsterdorf mit vielen tollen Künstlern. Es lässt sich dort flanieren, staunen, diskutieren. Ein friedlicher Ort voller Kunstschätze die es zu entdecken gilt.

title: le bateau lavoir de Dakar
text: un endroit extraordinaire où l'art foisonne sous toutes ses formes. Peintres sur verre, sur toile, photographes, sculpteurs , des dizaines d'artistes talentueux qui nous font partager leur passion avec enthousiasme. Un magnifique centre d'art. D'ici peu un espace d'exposition commun doit ouvrir.

title: Good idea ... not on Sunday
text:
I was looking forward to visiting this place,  unfortunately I went on a Sunday and there were very few artists present.

Having said that,  the few artists I engaged with were very friendly and open to show and talk about their work.

One recommendation I have for this community of artists is to clean up the common areas.  Make it nice, colorful and welcoming to visitors... They definitely have the collective creative minds to do this.
At the moment it is quite dirty and messy.

title: Coulerfull
text:
.You can watch hwo do the carve...

YOu should spent a couple of hours, to see not just the handcraft, but the workers

title: Nice 👍🏻 If you know how to Bargain Bargain Bargain.
text: Some really interesting art for art and travel collectors. You just have spend money (not much) in every shop you choose to enter. If not interested or not willing to spend some money don’t go inside. It felt like they see it as an offensive act. You will be invited to get into shops. Decide first, which ones you wish to enter!! And Bargain Bargain Bargain... you shall get 40-50% discount on everything. The guy in the shop tells you something is for 10,000 CFA ($18) you go say 5,000, aiming to accept it for 5,500 or maybe 6,000 at the most

title: Gli artisti in persona nei loro laboratori
text:
Come già fatto notare da altri recensori, non è da confondere con altri luoghi molto più turistici e commerciali. 
In questo luogo ci sono i veri e propri laboratori degli artisti e in base al momento in cui si va se ne trovano aperti alcuni o altri, in ogni caso c'è l'imbarazzo della scelta se volete comprare qualcosa. 
Non ci sono "venditori" fastidiosi, ma solo gli artisti che vi lasciano entrare e vedere senza disturbo. L'unica cosa in comune con i venditori è che si può trattare sul prezzo rispetto alla prima richiesta. 
Vale la pena passarci se si vuole comprare un quadro a Dakar.
Fidatevi di google maps... non c'è alcuna indicazione, bisogna entrarci per capire che ci si è arrivati..

title: A découvrir
text: Cet endroit héberge un nombre important d’artistes... Promenez vous à votre rythme, parlez, écoutez... un moment de culture dans une ambiance paisible!

title: LIEU TYPIQUE ET AUTHENTIQUE DE L'ART SENEGALAIS
text:
J'aime aller au village des Arts, voir les artistes à l'oeuvre et discuter un peu avec eux. 
Visite avec un ami venu pour la biénale, nous avons passé un bon moment et la visite de la galerie Shengor était très bien.
Visite qui s'est couronnée par l'achat de 2 toiles ! 
Si vous ne connaissez pas encore cet endroit, je vous invite vraiment à y aller.

title: Worth an hour or so to visit with these artists in their workshops/homes.
text: These folks are super-friendly and happy to show you their art. While the grounds could really use some tending, a visitor just has to look past that to appreciate the paintings, etc.

title: Visit to Village des Arts
text: The market has a wide variety of masks, carvings, jewelry, and fabrics, many of which are very unique. The selection of many of the crafts is more extensive than elsewhere in Dakar. Prices can be a little high to start, but if you negotiate well, they are fairly reasonable. The shop owners are friendly and not too pushy. Definitely worth a visit and very close to several nice hotels.

title: Peaceful and inspiring! not to be confused with village artisanal
text: Amazing place where you will find real artists painting. No hassle. No hard sellers. To the contrary none lf them would adress you unless you do. Sadly this place is being confused by some reviewers  with Village Artisanal which really is unfair as the latter is a very commercial touristic area with no original art creator (and very pushing traders!). Some of the reviewers actually visited Village Artisanal instead of Village des Arts!

title: ψώνια
text: αξίζει να το επισκεφθεί κανείς, γιατί έχει πολύ όμορφα πράγματα να αγοράσεις και εξαιρετικά φτηνά. Πρέπει να κάνεις μεγάλο παζάρι. Τα ίδια πράγματα στο αεροδρόμιο ήταν πανάκριβα, δηλαδή δέκα φορές πιο ακριβά.

title: Colourful market
text: If you like chaos, people try to sell something to you all the time This is your place, , it's very colorful, cheap, many handcrafts,  local artisans, and some areas are full of garbage. It was a little too much

title: Fun chaos
text:
Chaos, loud, pushy, cramped - exactly what we came for.  We visited hoping to find some fabric and a tailor to make some clothes to order.  But they found us.  A guy came up (Mohamed) who took us in turn to a couple of stalls and another man (Cheikh) who got us to the fabrics and the tailors.  We had multiple items made and they were done at a fair price, quickly and fit perfectly.  We had dresses, pants and a mens shirt done.  Mohammed can find what you’re looking for 221-77-679-1723.  Cheikh will help get any item of clothing made with any variety of cloth 221-77-893-4367.  

I’d also recommend the glass painting of Mr Mame Gueye in the Centre Artisinal just north of the marché.  Lots of similar but none as precise.  Some good silver smiths and bead vendors in the Centre as well.

title: Clásico mercado
text: Se trata de una zona comercial con muchas paradas en las que comprar todo tipo de artículos y souvenirs. Curioseando con nuestra guía, dejamos atrás las paradas exteriores y nos adentramos en un pequeño edificio para ver algunas prendas típicas africanas y sin darnos cuenta nos encontramos en un laberinto de estrechos pasillos llenos de ropa hasta el techo, con toda la variedad habida y por haber. Los comerciantes, con una paciencia admirable, te buscan y muestran sus productos hasta que encuentras lo que quieres. Lo único que me entristeció de este lugar, fue ver hombres cosiendo rodeados de género, en espacios hiper reducidos, sin luz natural, con el estrés del vaivén de gente a su alrededor... y entre ellos algún adolescente también cosiendo.

title: horrible
text:
expérience horrible voir traumatisante, avec mon amie blanche  comme moi on se baladait dans la rue et la des "rabatteurs" nous accostent , nous repondons que nous ne sommes pas intéresser que nous voulons visiter , ils ne nous lachent pas et la l'horreur...

Ils nous suivent toute l'avenue principale Pompidou jusqu'au marché pour que l'on visite "la fabrique a tissus", une fois arriver ,les rabatteurs nous font visiter la fabrique, nous demandons les prix, ils nous repondent qu'ils vont faire un prix a la fin, ils parlent wolof entre eux et aux vendeurs. Nous ne comprenons pas vraiment ce qu'il se passe.
Ils nous obligent a acheter et nous font assoir dans un "coin" a la limite du traumatisme.... et nous font directement les encheres a plus de 100 000 francs pour 3 malheureux articles... une honte, alors que ces articles ne coutent pas plus de 3000 francs chacun...
Mais nous etions comme obliger d'acheter et les rabatteurs etaient assez insistant!!! Les vendeurs de la fabrique sont sympathiques mais les rabatteurs sont tres insistant , ils vont abordent n'importe ou dans dakar plateau et vous y emmenent, faites attention. Si vous voulez des souvenirs (tissus etc) je vous conseil d'y aller avec des locaux sans intermédiaire directement aux vendeurs, faites attention il y a aussi beaucoup de rabatteur dans la farbique et aux alentours.

Cet épisode s'est déroulé la premiere semaine de mon sejour et j'ai été traumatisé , apres avoir discuter avec d'autres personnes étrangeres comme moi ils ont vecu la meme expérience voire meme pire (harcellement, insulte si on ne veut pas acheter...)

un conseil surtout si vous etes blanche  : allez y de vous meme , pas besoin de prendre un intermédiaire qui s'emparent de la plupart de l'argent..
Ne surtout pas y aller seul, et négocier meme aux vendeurs

title: The veg was good
text: I really liked Sandaga. The vegetables sold were tasty. The fresh water was good. Thanks for making me feel welcome.

title: Für Abenteuerlustige
text: Wer Lärm, Gestank, aufdringliche Händler und Chaos nicht mag, ist hier fehl am Platz. Für alle andere ist es ein Erlebnis. Ein typischer exotischer Markt. Man muss feilschen, diskutieren, weglaufen usw. War mit einem Einheimischen dort, was das Ganze wesentlich erleichtert hat. Jetzt in Zeiten des Corona sind die Preise sehr günstig. Die Händler verkaufen fast nichts. Unbedingt einen Café Tomba trinken.

title: Cours des orfèvres
text:
Colorful and lively market, plenty of quality good to find. 
I would suggest to go to the ‘cours des orfèvres’ (69, avenue Blaise Diagne) for all this silver and gold. You’ll find jewelry for every taste. It was my favorite part. The craftsmanship is amazing. 

Vibrant et coloré, vous y trouverez des articles en tout genre. 
Je recommande une visite à la ‘cours des orfèvres’ (69, avenue de Blaise Diagne) pour vos bijoux en or ou argent. Il y’en a pour tous les goûts. C’était ma partie préférer.

title: Marché à faire avec un local!
text:
Nous y sommes allés une première fois en "touristes" et avons été tout de suite repérés dès que nous étions au niveau du carrefour!
Nous avons repéré ce qu'on voulait acheter mais plusieurs rabatteurs nous suivaient et insistaient pour qu'on les suive!
Notre premier passage a été fatiguant.
Nous y sommes donc retourné avec un ami de Dakar et avons pu faire nos achats tranquillement sans personne qui nous suivait!
Je recommande pour faire de bonnes affaires là bas si vous achetez en lot des souvenirs ou tissus mais il faut y aller avec un local qui parle wolof et négociera pour vous.
Beaucoup n'aimeront pas le système de rabattage (à la limite du harcèlement) mais c'est une expérience et ça fait parti du charme du séjour.
Ma note est mitigée pour cela!

title: El arte del regateo
text: Se sale de allí con un máster en la materia. Los vendedores son amables, pero muy pesados. Cuando llegue el momento, hay que saber plantarse y pagar siempre menos de la mitad del precio inicial. Hay que entenderlo como algo usual en su cultura. Visita imprescindible si estás en Dakar. Puede resultar agotador pero al final merece la pena. No sacar todo el dinero ni dejarlo a la vista o será imposible bajar el precio.

title: Don't go there
text: Full with extortionists and shady vendors. Don't go there if you don't look like somebody from Senegal, or you will be harassed.

title: Bargain Bargain Bargain...!
text:
It’s and experience you need to have when you’re in Dakar. My take after visiting it for three times for different reasons would be:
First: set a budget in your home currency before going there.
Second: Be a real tough negotiator on every purchase. 
Third: What every price you get from your merchants go for only 30% of the price you initially get, and to achieve that you have to respond by going as low as only 20% of the initial price proposed. 
Fourth: Always pretend you don’t really need the purchase, 
Finally: Don’t get fooled by the seller pretending he won’t sell, they will go after you when you leave the store. 

One of them came after me when he saw me getting into my taxi 🚕 another one sent her daughter after my wife and myself when we were coming back from the Gorée Island.

title: Marché de Sandaga
text: Ici on trouve tissus, souvenirs en tout genre... Un conseil surtout NE PAS Y ALLER SEUL(E) et attention PAS DE SAC A MAIN ; les touristes sont tout de suite repérés,ne regardez pas longtemps une échope ou quelqu'un si vous n'êtes pas intéressés. On les appelle les mouches car ils sont collants, Ils ont tous pour principe de dire "rentrez juste pour le plaisir des yeux" mais en réalité comprenez bien que si vous rentrez "il faut acheter en marchandant beaucoup beaucoup" sinon ils ne vous lâchent plus et vous suivent parfois même. Le prix qu'ils vous annoncent, faut le diviser par 2 voire par 3.

title: Che fatica ma ne vale la pena!
text: Non sei stato in Senegal se non visiti un mercato! Questo è molto bello e vastissimo, trovi qualsiasi cosa. Bisogna essere pronti all’ insistenza dei commercianti e a contrattare fino allo sfinimento.

title: Fuyez
text: Ce marché est une catastrophe humaine... fuyez le, c’est impossible d’être en paix ou se promener si vous êtes touristes !

title: Un grand bazar multicolore et animé
text: C'est à voir absolument si l'on va à Dakar. Extrêmement animé, pleins de couleurs et d'odeurs. Ambiance bon enfant. Les vendeurs insistent pour vendre aux toubabs mais ils restent polis et sympathique si vous l'êtes vous même. Je vous conseille d'y aller avec un ou des amis africains pour vivre de l'intérieur ce marché. Voir le marchandage, rentrer dans les petites boutiques. Il y a de tout. Bien entendu quelques produits pour les touristes mais principalement pour le local. Tissus, vêtements, bijoux, etc.

title: Aucun interet
text: Marchè sans aucun interet, les touristes sont harcelès, nous avons dû partir precipitamment, car un homme alcoolise nous traitait de « racistes » dans la rue  et nous suivait... le marchè en lui meme ne presente aucun interet. De la contre facon et rien d’autre.

title: Fatiguant!
text:
Il est quasiment impossible de se promener seul (lorsque l'on est touriste) sans être harcelé par des rabatteurs. Le marché est riche d'artisanat en tout genre mais gare à vous si vous n'achetez pas! 
Trop de commerçants acariâtres et aigris rembarrent les clients. Après une heure de déambulation, on est finalement fatigué des interactions négatives et du harcèlement permanent. Dommage!

title: Objets faits au Cap Vert
text:
Les produits vendus sont fabriqués par une quarantaine d'artisans  et deux coopératives de différentes parties de l'archipel.
Si vous voulez des souvenirs typiquement capverdiens et pas sénégalais c'est là qu'il faut aller.

title: Really worth a visit
text: Loved this museum.  Had a private tour and the guide was top notch.  I learned a ton, not only about the slave trade, but importantly, Ghana before then.  It was quiet, the exhibits were well put together, and really informative.  It is not a huge spot, can be enjoyed at a leisurely pace in about an hour.  Definitely worth paying for a private tour, guide was well informed with a clear love of his country.  There was also a good, small gift shop.

title: Very enlightening a must visit for an overview of Ghanaian history
text: Interesting artifacts and amazingly knowledgeable tour guide. Nana gave us the most enjoyable and engaging experience during our visit. We would definitely recommend that you visit during your trip. There is a lot of rich history that can be obtained here.

title: It was great being in Ghana. I learnt so much from these beautiful people. A  country excellent for vacationingh
text: Great place, I learnt a lot about Ghana. Ghana is a country rich in culture. Their diversity is their strength. So much to admire in the daily lifestyle of a typical Ghanian.

title: Excellent Overview
text: The gentleman who gives the tours in extremely passionate, engaging and knowledgeable which made the tour interesting as well as informative. Very well versed on the people, customs and regions of Ghana and the differences. This was our first stop on a 7 day tour and it didn’t disappoint.

title: Nice stop
text: This re-opened in 2022 and is a nice way to spend some time learning about the history of Ghana as well as get out of the heat.

title: Great for a rainy or very hot day in Accra
text: They are done renovating and the entry is 30 cds. You see Ghana from the stone age till now. Very well told by our guide. A clear train of thoughts hold the exhibition together.

title: Good overview of history and culture, guided tour essential to get the most out of the visit.
text:
You definitely need a guide to take you around the museum I  order to get the most out of it because the displays are very static. Our guide was energetic, knowledgable and really brought the objectives to life. 

Guided tours start all day as visitors arriveand takes a bit more than an hour. Although not every Ghanain tribe and experience is represented in the collection, this is a great overview of Ghanain heritage and culture. There's a play corner with Lego for younger kids if they get restless. I was there with kids aged 8-16. Exhibition is on 2 floors.

Also it's quite close to Independence Square so it's nice to combine the 2 spots.

title: CLOSED as of Feb 202
text: Very closed as of Feb 2020. Construction was in process and the staff mentioned a possible re-opening in March 2020, but that sounded too optimistic. Everything was boarded up, and even the sculpture garden was filled with trash, and many sculptures were broken. There was no information about the closure on their website, or on the signs outside the museum.

title: Still closed...
text: Still closed as of December 29, 2019. Idris informer is there’s no funds and plan for reopening. He did give us a nice tour of the sculpture garden that took about 30 minutes.

title: nice cool good
text: you can see the old slavery plase nice to go too and u can learn about a long time ago me and my famaly loved it we think u need to go

title: Closed until December
text: The museum is closed until December 2019 due to renovations. It is not on their website. I only found out on the parking lot. I have send them a mail to put it on their homepage. Hopefully they will put that up soon, so you don’t end up before closed doors, like I did.

title: 內部展覽和博物館關閉
text: 我很失望來到這裡。這是因為內部展覽和博物館關閉了。這是為了進行翻新。我在網上，酒店禮賓部和當地的朋友詢問過。沒有任何信息說博物館關閉。既然來了，我在博物館外的花園走走。那裡有各種有趣的雕塑。還有一輛前總統的舊車。已經處於失修狀態。

title: To Re-open by end of 2019
text: Just at the museum today to see what was happening with the re-opening.  Now say "end of 2019" but not much going on.  They do have a nice exhibit in one of the out buildings on Ghanian architecture.

title: Closed when we visited!
text: There were no exhibits on display - we got a chance to look at the sculptures and the first President's car which is on concrete blocks in the yard, in an unbelievable state of disrepair.

title: "Temporarily" closed for renovations
text: The museum has been "temporarily" closed for renovations in ten (10!) years now. I could enter the museum anyways 9 years ago, nice exhibition but don't expect the Smithsonian level. Still patiently waiting for the grand opening after the renovations :D

title: Museum is currently closed for renovation
text: We got a guided tour in the small sculpture garden. It was informative and gave us some insight into the traditions and history of Ghana but I would say the sculpture garden is a must-see.

Though the place is under construction, but you can visit this place free of cost and have a look on these status depicting the people 's life. title: A Little Bit of Everything

title: Gallery, museum and souvenir shop - all in one
text:
We spent about 2 hours looking at modern art, historical objects and great souvenirs. This place has it all. 
We were a little confused because on their website it says that one should "Book to visit" also "for Private-Viewing". But everyone can turn up during the opening hours, and the entrance is free.
This is an amazing place with a nice relaxing atmosphere.

placeInfo.name: Artists Alliance Gallery
placeInfo.address: Labadi Road, Omanye House, Accra Ghana

title: Amazing art, better than museum
text:
The place is big and if you are into local arts - cloth, paintings (mainly modern), wood carvings, masks, straw bags etc, and you wish to see at your own pace and leisure, without any hassle, you arrived to the right place. It is up to a standard of museum and it is for free.
We spent almost 90 minutes just looking at the different artifacts. If you wish somebody to guide you , it is also possible.
Highly recommended, better than any museum we have seen in West Africa. It also gets the see breeze and hence is very pleasant on warm day despite the fact that there is no aircon.

placeInfo.name: Artists Alliance Gallery
placeInfo.address: Labadi Road, Omanye House, Accra Ghana

title: Gallery bezoek
text:
Het is leuk om in de gallery rond te kijken. Er zijn vooral veel schilderijen te zien. Er us ook veel kunst uit o.a. Mali (Dogonmaskers, deurtjes) en uit Burkima Faso. Door de zeer positieve 
 reviews had ik er iets meer van verwacht, maar zeker voor iemand die voor het eerst in Ghana komt, is het leuk om er rustig rond te kunnen kijken.

placeInfo.name: Artists Alliance Gallery
placeInfo.address: Labadi Road, Omanye House, Accra Ghana

title: A Must See!
text:
Don’t miss this wonderful amalgamation of artistic diversity! 
Displaying everything from traditional to contemporary art, artists and artifacts, the place feels more like a museum/cultural center than retail gallery. 

I found myself here on multiple occasions during my visit.
Outstanding!

placeInfo.name: Artists Alliance Gallery
placeInfo.address: Labadi Road, Omanye House, Accra Ghana

title: So many things to see!
text: This three story building was chalk full of so much artwork. There's definitely not even enough space for it all. There are some lovely galleries spaces with paintings and multimedia wall pieces on the top floors and the bottom floor has antiques, wood carvings, glass beads, kente information and crafts, etc etc. I was so happily surprised by all of the beautiful pieces and the prices seem to be pretty fair. No A/C and there were piles of paintings sitting on tables in some places (so I worry about their long term integrity). However, it's definitely worth the visit! I was wowed by the variety.

placeInfo.name: Artists Alliance Gallery
placeInfo.address: Labadi Road, Omanye House, Accra Ghana

title: Paintings
text: A niceart gallery with lovely african paintings, they take orders, located at the beach front, its so peaceful one can spend hours there.

placeInfo.name: Artists Alliance Gallery
placeInfo.address: Labadi Road, Omanye House, Accra Ghana

title: My visit to Artists Alliance Gallery
text: I visited this wonderful gallery while in Ghana this summer.  A friend who resides in Ghana took me and I am so very happy that she did.  There is something for everyone here.  I found several delightful books for my grandchildren, a map of Ghana for myself, and a couple of jewelry pieces.  I intend to return to purchase a couple of the exquisite art pieces on my trip to Ghana in December when I will be able to arrange to bring the piece back home to the states with me. I encourage anyone that likes art, good books and unique jewelry to be sure to visit Artists Alliance Gallery!

placeInfo.name: Artists Alliance Gallery
placeInfo.address: Labadi Road, Omanye House, Accra Ghana

title: Spectacular Gallery With Knowledgeable Professionals
text: As everyone else is saying, yes, this is a great gallery.  If you are in Accra you really need to stop in, even if you are not interested in buying.  They do indeed have nearly everything.....a full room of kente cloth, 2 floors of modern paintings, 4 rooms of antique and replica carvings and masks, Ghanian coffins, and on and on.  The best thing is that they welcome you and then leave you to browse.  When you have questions they are there and have knowledgeable answers....if they don't know, they get someone who does or they call someone.  My wife and I bought a lot of things.....only drawback was they put it on our guide to get us to a DHL office.....they didn't want to pack and ship what we bought......Absolutely great gallery.......

placeInfo.name: Artists Alliance Gallery
placeInfo.address: Labadi Road, Omanye House, Accra Ghana

title: You don't want to miss this treasure!
text: Two days left in Ghana and we just discovered this treasure! If you love art, all kinds of art, you don't want to miss this. There are three floors of amazing displays of the talent of Ghanaian artists; paintings, carvings, photography, furniture, fabrics, jewelry, and more. I was like a kid in a candy store! Another reviewer mentioned the need for a cafe. I wholeheartedly agree. That would be the icing on the cake. I could have spent another hour or so wandering around looking at art and dreaming of how several of the pieces could grace the walls of the multi million dollar home I'll purchase one day (I can dream, can't I)? It would have been nice to have been able to sit for a while and have a bite and a beverage to refuel. There are items for sale throughout the building, so keep your eyes open. And yes, they do take credit cards. Photography is not allowed, and rightfully so; these artists deserve every penny for their talented work! I look forward to returning next time I'm in the area!

placeInfo.name: Artists Alliance Gallery

text: Uma galeria excelente com uma variedade enorme de trabalhhos de arte,kente,bronze,contas e etc.....Tudo é vendável e com uma bela variedade de preços ,é claro que me encantei com as mantas de kente com fio de seda.

title: Etwas für Liebhaber afrikanischer Kunst
text: Das Omanye House ist fast noch so etwas wie ein Geheimtipp. Selbst Taxifahrer kennen es meistens nicht. Dabei ist es ein ausgesprochenes Highlight in Accra. Alleine die Lage des Hauses direkt am Atlantik hat seinen Reiz. Über 3 Stockwerke hinweg finden die Besucher zeitgenössische Gemälde bekannter ghanaischer Künstler ebenso wie die Werke vielversprechender Talente. Im UG werden Masken und Kultgegenstände aus Westafrika gezeigt und auch verkauft. Das Haus hat fast den Charakter einer völkerkundlichen  Sammlung weil auch davon ausgegangen werden darf, dass kein Touristenkitsch sondern echte, traditionelle Arbeiten präsentiert werden. Selbst einige der berühmten "Themensärge" aus Accra werden ausgestellt. Das Omanye ist nichts für Schnäppchenjäger.

placeInfo.name: Artists Alliance Gallery

title: Do Not Miss This When In Accra
text: Just like a national gallery only better. Well presented 3 floors of Aricana from childrens books to beads to major artworks. An attraction in its own right without even purchasing something. But you will.

placeInfo.name: Artists Alliance Gallery

title: Amazing art to view and to buy.
text:
I loved the Artists' Alliance. I had never heard of it until I saw it in a French guide book. 

3 floors of beautiful art, sculptures, fashion, homeware and crafts. I think it's all for sale.

I went on the second day of my trip but returned on my last day to buy some things for my house and some gifts.

It's right on the beach and it's a lovely place to spend an hour or 2.

A little cafe would be a great addition.

placeInfo.name: Artists Alliance Gallery
placeInfo.address: Labadi Road, Omanye House, Accra Ghana

title: Get Your Africana Here
text: Good selection of traditional West African and contemporary Ghanaian art.  Weaving, carving, painting, jewelry, beads.  You name it, they have it.  I am going back for a second look.  Enjoy the breeze off the ocean.  Did I mention, there are three storeys to explore???

placeInfo.name: Artists Alliance Gallery
placeInfo.address: Labadi Road, Omanye House, Accra Ghana

title: Amazing browsing and shopping
text: Three floors of paintings and handicrafts that are almost overwhelming. Modern paintings, tradition style paintings, coffins, masks, kente cloth, cushions, bed linen, amazing iron sculptures, beads, bowls, chairs and stools, rag mats, ETC. ETC ETC. We came away with tables, cushions, clothes and paintings. The only thing that stopped us buying more is our luggage allowance!

placeInfo.name: Artists Alliance Gallery
placeInfo.address: Labadi Road, Omanye House, Accra Ghana

title: Aesthetic awakening
text:
Whether you're a budding artist, one that's been dormant, established or otherwise, this place serves to enthuse, awaken and challenge the perception of the fine arts. Compounding of vibrant colours, free standing artefacts and unique pieces, this gallery depicts the many Ghanaian cultures reminiscing history to contemporary lifestyles.
A definite place to visit, there's no excuse as it's also free...(I'll gladly pay if I had to). 
Had my aesthetic fix for real👍

placeInfo.name: Artists Alliance Gallery
placeInfo.address: Labadi Road, Omanye House, Accra Ghana

title: Great place if you are into local art
text:
This is probably the closest you will come to a National Gallery in Ghana.
All of the art is recent and for sale. You can buy anything from little bracelets up to some very large paintings by some very well known Ghanaian artists.
I was very tempted to buy some paintings and would recommend a visit if you are looking for something local.

placeInfo.name: Artists Alliance Gallery
placeInfo.address: Labadi Road, Omanye House, Accra Ghana

title: One of the most interesting places to visit and shop in Accra
text:
This place should be top of places to visit, it really should. 

It was near my hotel, but the building isn't readily identified as an art gallery and shop. The gallery is in a rather large building by the beach (sounds better than it is, actually, beach very dirty, area appears a bit run-down). Don't think ther eis public transport there, but cabs are reasonable, and you can easily flag a cab on nearby La beach road. 

Plan a couple of hours for the whole thing, perhaps. It is a pleasant space, clean, airconditioned, no pressure to buy, no one will follow you round. On the ground floor, tehre is a large room filled with canvasses and Ga coffins which are displayed nicer than in their crammed workshops in Teshie (where I went, too) . Note that photography is forbidden, like in most places in Ghana where there is stuff for sale. 

Off the main hall are side rooms full of interesting wooden carvings, Kente cloth, and the piece de resistance, beads. There are also some natural cosmetics and little souvenirs for sale. Prices appear reasonable, and are fixed - you will get things cheaper perhaps, in the Arts Centre, but you need to haggle lots. 

There are a further two floors with paintings,w hich I did not have time to see. I planned to come back, but then did not make it, so I have something to look forward to next time I come to Accra. I could happily have kitted pout my whole apartment here, and perhaps next time I will come with a budget so spend on some art - most of what I've seen is very original, appealing, and I understand that the artists sell directly. 

What this place is really lacking is a little coffee shop or cafe... with the surrounding area not really great for visitors (it's hot, you might get a drink somewhere but nowhere shady to sit) it would be great to sit there for a bit with refreshments, then look at more art.

placeInfo.name: Artists Alliance Gallery
placeInfo.address: Labadi Road, Omanye House, Accra Ghana

title: Sublime fondation d'art contemporain
text:
C'est peut-être le seul lieu culturel dont vous entendrez parler depuis l'Europe, et c'est pour une bonne raison!
Installé dans un ancien édifice colonial, le lieu est très beau. Il expose des artistes africains contemporains, même si vous n'êtes pas passionnés ou que vous n'y connaissez rien, cela vaut le détour. Les pièces sont aérées, les œuvres bien exposées, les guides compétents.
Le prix d'entrée est libre.
Ne manquez pas le café-boutique. Possibilité de déjeuner, mais le café est un peu cher. Par contre la boutique vaut le coup d’œil, pas donné non plus mais original. Vous y trouverez : bijoux, divers objets en tissus africains : sacs de toutes tailles, houses d'ordinateur, cravates, nappes, mais aussi coussins, trousses de toilettes et surtout de nombreux catalogues sur l'art africains et les expositions de la fondation.
Un lieu à ne pas manquer, vaut le déplacement jusqu'à Ouidah!

title: Zinsou Fondation Museum
text:
This museum contains paintings of top Artists and have history of different paintings.
A good place to go if you are a lover of Art

title: Seule visite vraiment plaisante...
text: En effet la maison est superbe, bien rénovée et aérée. Les guides sont bien formés et connaissent leur sujet. La collection est sérieuse, méticuleusement choisie et éclectique. Au final, ce fut pour nous la visite la plus plaisante de Ouidah, sans rabatteurs ou charlatans, calme et agréable.

title: Nice building
text: The building itself is a really pleasant structure and exudes a calm and peaceful ambience. The cafe has very good food and service although expensive for Benin at 1500 for a beer and 5000 for a burger and fries or a nice salad. I am not a lover of contemporary art so I think it best to say nothing regarding that aspect here.

title: Molto interessante
text: Bel museo di arte contemporanea situato in un bell'edificio coloniale stile déco. Pesonale accogliente e disponibile

title: the guide is good
text: the guide was good , the art was good , the problem is the language barrier , they only speak french there

title: tres belle surprise
text: quel bonheur d'avoir été déposée par un ami juste à la porte !!  ce fut un régal , conduite par un guide dont on ne peut oublier le nom : Fortune, un trésor de connaissance et un accueil si simple et chaleureux. Le cadre en lui même est un régal pour les yeux

title: Très bon musée
text: Le musée de la fondation Zinsou à Ouidah a été pour nous une très bonne surprise. L'exposition est très intéressante, et le guide très compétent. L'accès à la fondation est gratuite, mais il est possible de faire un don à la fin de la visite. Le musée a également un très bon café avec wifi. Ce musée mérite le détour.

title: Belle surprise
text: On est tombé par hasard sur ce musée et c'était vraiment une belle surprise. Le guide était très gentil et accueillant: de bonnes explications et un bon aperçu de la culture locale. A visiter absolument.

title: Revenir toujours avec le même plaisir !
text: La villa est belle et l'ambiance somptueuse avec ses couloirs ses fenêtres multiples en bois qui s'ouvre sur l'art contemporain africain. Il faut saluer la performance de cette fondation à Cotonou et à Ouidah avec Marie Cécile Zinsou qui défend l'art contemporain envers et contre tout. Ne ratez jamais à Ouidah cette visite et passer un bon moment à déjeuner ou au café sur des palmes en tissus colorés

title: Redécouverte de l'histoire du Dahomey
text: Au travers d'expositions variées (œuvres artistiques, livres...) on redécouvre l'histoire du Dahomey.

title: Lovely exposition of modern African art and a nice café and gift shop also
text: The Foundation selects truly excellent examples of contemporary art from all over Africa.  It is nicely displayed (a small sample, but definitely worthwhile) in the founder's old family home in Ouidah.  The service and food at the café were good, as was the small but tasteful selection at the gift shop.

title: Bravo. Plein la vue!
text: C est tout simplement extraordinaire de déambuler dans cette superbe villa de style colonial et d y découvrir des œuvres d artistes béninois, nigérians, ghanéens.... avec des guides souriants et sympathiques. Petit détour obligatoire au cafe de La fondation et à la boutique, j adore!

title: Deuxième visite, toujours aussi intéressante !
text: Déjà visité en 2015, nous avons vu cette année une nouvelle exposition très intéressante de masques gèlèdé réalisés suite à une commande du musée visant à enquêter sur les demandes du peuple béninois aux candidats à la future élection présidentielle. En outre nous avons pu constater les efforts de sensibilisation à l'art, réalisés auprès des écoliers de Ouidah : quelle chance pour eux. Bravo à la Fondation.

title: Une très belle visite
text: Ne pas manquer à Ouidah, ce musée improbable dans ce lieu, dans le cadre d'une maison ancienne très bien aménagée, une très belle présentation d'oeuvres d'art d'artistes Béninois. Visite passionnante, grâce au talent de la guide, très compétente et intéressante.

title: Exceptionnel
text:
Le lieu est unique et superbe, vrai joyaux patrimonial.
Les artistes présentés sont passionnants, les guides sont accueillants, souriants, je vous recommande vraiment ce musée. Et n'hésitez pas à prendre un café après la visite (on y sert du nespresso!), l'endroit est magique et les articles de la boutique changent de l'habituel centre artisanal où l'on voit toujours les mêmes choses. A ne pas rater !!

title: Nice exhibit in a beautiful setting
text: Came here recently with my wife to see the La Fabrique à Fantasmes exhibit. What a most pleasant experience: the exhibit was very well curated, with a nice mixture of works as far as artists represented, their country of origin, and media used; the setting—a beautifully restored house from the early 1900s—was equally inspiring; the staff was very helpful and friendly; and lastly, the café (reviewed elsewhere) was super charming and cozy. A morning well spent indeed!

title: Mediocre

title: Lovely house, nice art
text: We had a great tour of the museum mainly due to the fact that my wife is fluent in French and translated as the guide took us around. They've done well with the space. Definitely worth a visit if you're in town.

title: A ne pas rater !
text:
Si vous passez à Ouidah, ne manquez pas la fondation Zinsou afin de découvrir quelques échantillons de l'art contemporain africain. Cela a été pour nous une vraie découverte. Avec une salle par artiste de différents pays et les explications très éclairantes de notre guide, nous avons pu comprendre et mieux apprécier les œuvres. Chaque artiste a un style bien à lui, utilisant souvent des matériaux de récupération. La visite est complémentaire de celle faite à Cotonou où la fondation a aussi un lieu d'exposition, consacré à un seul artiste.
L'entrée et la visite est gratuite. On peut terminer par un petit tour au café meublé de façon contemporaine mais avec de magnifiques tissus africains traditionnels.

title: Panorama bellissimo
text:
Purtroppo io avevo un torcicollo il giorno in cui ho visitato questo luogo per cui la salita per arrivare alla fortezza è stata ancora più pesante oltre al sole pieno e la mancanza di una strada.
Ma una volta sopra ho goduto il panorama che ne è valsa la pena. Troppo stanca però non siamo entrati dentro al castello anche perché il ragazzo che ci lavorava ha ammesso che dentro non c'era molto da vedere. Lui è stato molto gentile.

title: Sklavental und Sir Francis Drake
text:
Der Besuch des Forts oberhalb von Cidade Velha ist ein Muss.Es bietet nicht nur einen grandiosen Rundumblick, sondern vermittelt auch Einblicke in die die Zeit des Sklavenhandels und der Freibeuterei. Ein Mitarbeiter führte uns durch das Fort und ließ Geschichte lebendig werden: das tägliche Leben der Soldaten und Offiziere im Fort, die Mühen der Sklaven, um die Zisterne mittels Wassereimern aus dem Tal zu befüllen, englische Kanonen, in denen sogar eine nicht verschossene Kugel steckt. Das Fort galt lange Zeit als uneinnehmbar, bis es schließlich durch eine Gemeinschaftsaktion der Engländer vom Meer aus und der Franzosen von der Landseite kommend eingenommen werden konnte. 
Der Eintrittspreis ist mehr als gerechtfertigt!

title: Not a breathtaking experience.
text:
The fortress is on the way to Cidade Velha. The entrance fee is CVE 500 (EUR 5) and you can use the same ticket to visit São Francisco convent afterwards. 

The site has a little interpretation museum at the entrance.... good to understand a little bit about this place. The fortress itself is... well, an empty fortress. Just the ones you can visit throughout the Balkans (Skoder, Belgrade, Skopje...)

Views are not really impressive either. The cistern is worth, though. Not a place I would recommend but... what else to do while in Santiago?

title: Gut erhaltene Festungsanlage mit fantastischem Panorama
text: Die Besichtigung der sehr gut erhaltenen Burg ist beim Besuch der Cidade Velha sicherlich ein Muss. Der Anstieg vom Dorf aus ist zwar durchaus reizvoll aber speziell am frühen Nachmittag und Sonnenschein sehr schweißtreibend. Glücklicherweise gibt es oben einen Kiosk mit kalten Getränken. Dieses Fort ist überaus gut erhalten und renoviert und daher ist für mich der Eintritt von 500 Escudos durchaus in Ordnung. Wenn man sich genügend Zeit nimmt kann man direkt noch das Trampeln der Soldaten bei Alarm auf der Rampe zu den Schießscharten hören. Unbedingt auch die Geschichte ansehen.

title: Touched story well told
text: 2019 is the year of home coming of African Americans in the diaspora. To those who believe they come from Ghana and others who are interested in the history of the trans - Atlantic Slave trade, the UNESCO world heritage site the cape coast castle is a must tour. Any day I visited the cape coast castle I connect with history and reflect on it. Obuoba Tours will recommend the castle to all those who will travel to Ghana this year. Make sure you ask of Sebastian a site guide who is so knowledgeable with the history.

title: A sad history lesson
text: Very educational tour. A place that you should visit if you go to Ghana. The building is not special, but the atrocities should not be forgotten.

title: to trzeba zobaczyć
text: to był moj pierwszy raz i chętnie powrócę! lekcja historii i pokory. Niesamowita lokalizacja, dobrze utrzymany obiekt, piękne widoki, trzeba zobaczyć i poznać!

title: Beeindruckendes Relikt aus dunkler Zeit
text:
Cape Coast Castle sollte unbedingt mit Führung besichtigt werden. Dann bekommt einen besonderen Eindruck, unter welchen Umständen seinerzeit der Sklaven-Transfer hier abgewickelt wurde. 
Humanitäter Umgang mit der "Ware Mensch" war eher sehr klein geschrieben. Hat man aber schon häufiger auf der Welt erlebt. In vielen Ländern, auch in der Neuzeit. 
Also, wer will da den Finger heben?

title: Very Good History Lesson
text:
My eyes were open to so much. There is so much to learn and to literally weep over. The things these poor slaves experienced is painful to hear and just to try to imagine. Reaching the point of no return is a sobering moment.  

Personally, my preference is Elmina Castle if you only have time to visit one.  But if you experience both, please do. It will change you forever, regardless of your race, nationality or age.

title: A faire absolument
text:
Château rempli d'histoire. Beau bâtiment avec vue sur la baie.
A 3h d'accra, facile d'accès en voiture.

title: WE RETURNED SO WE WON
text:
The most tragic experience of our life. The emotional turmoil over the kidnapping, forced incarceration and brutality rained down upon my ancestors sent of to the Caribbean and the Americas. Through the door of NO RETURN.

YET BITTERLY AND PROUDLY there we stood. Empowered that our ancestors survived the brutality and we will continue to make them proud!

A PLACE FOR DIASPORA TO SEE 10000% NEVER FORGET!

Pay to go alone with your guide so you can grieve privately.

title: Interesting, moving, great scenery, a must!
text: We visited this castle after Elmina, which I believe is even more impressive. The interesting museum here, the scenery, the dungeons, the fact that all the area surrounding it is still so active - gives you a feeling that this all happened not so long ago. I would strongly recommend to visit both castles. They are different and each one compliments the other. Ask the guides hard questions - I was not impressed with their knowledge and intrigued with their bias

title: History Not To Be Repeated
text: It was with much reverence for those that suffered here that we visited this former slave holding castle and dungeons.   It's hard to imagine the suffering that people endured here and elsewhere during the slave trade.   We pray for freedom of all people.

title: The scale of human enslavement.
text: This is the most preserved of the extant enslavement structures in West Africa. The tour guides give a riveting account of the warehousing of humans before transporting them to the Americas and the Caribbean. The guides explain the purpose of the holding cells for men, women and children. Also how rebellious men and women were punished and allowed to die without food and water. The tour also includes how women were raped and abused by the captors. The tour concluded with a walk to the infamous "Door of No Return".

title: Really Pulled At My Heart
text: To step into the slave dungeons that held so many before being transported through the middle passage to the Americas and other places, pulled at my heart. As I closed my eyes and listened to the tour guide tell what it was like, you could feel the presence of a people who went through here. This was an eye opening tour and the tour guide did a stellar job in communicating the history lessons.

title: Sobering history tour
text:
This is a very good tour, reasonably priced, and interesting. You learn a lot about the history of the castle, when it was built, what nations occupied it and when, and the slave trade of which the castle played a large part. The tour is guided and  very interesting! It is quite sobering to think of all the people that went through the "door of no return" on their way to serve as slaves in the new world. 
The location is awesome as well, right on the shore of the gulf, with local fishermen's boats pulled up on the beach in front of the castle and many other boats docked or beached in the lagoon behind the castle. It is a feast for the senses! So much color, and the hustle bustle of the townspeople going about their daily routines. The smell of the lagoon and open sewer system can be a challenge to ignore, but if you can, visiting the castle is an enriching experience. I've visited twice since 2012, bringing groups both times, and I would certainly visit again. Been to Cape Coast Castle as well, but I must say, I like Elmina a little better.

title: Well Worth A Visit
text: It’s a must visit to pay respects to those millions of Africans who suffered at the castle and were shipped off against their will to serve the empire building of the Europeans. Steeped in history, with great views of the coast, it’s a great place to remember that every soul on the planet is important and we should do to others as we would like done to ourselves....whatever our perceived differences....

title: Very emotional visit
text: As one of the smaller castles it packed a big punch. It was hard being in the slave cells it was so hot and then I realized this was my ancestors reality shacked and with 100’s or more people! Then I humbled myself. I want to visit the larger castles as well! Great place to visit!

title: Must see!
text:
Als je in Cape Coast bent dan moet je hier naar toe. Geen plaats om trots op je voorouders te zijn.
Heb een rondleiding met een gids gedaan. Op deze manier hoor je zaken die anders aan je voorbij gaan.

title: Home at last
text: This was a really emotional visit, great story telling and presentation of historical facts. The visit was inexpensive and educational. The gift shop was also a nice touch. If you are ever in Ghana, this place is a must.

title: Heartfelt tour
text:
I enjoyed the castle tour. The guide was very good. He actually made us cry when he was telling us the history of the slave castle. It was an emotional tour that left us uneasy. That aside the guide pulled some jokes to make us relax.

If u visit the cape coast u must definitely visit the castle.

**********loved it *********

title: Must see
text: Been twice and I still get chills walking the same halls many walked in shackles. Great place to see a little bit of what it might have been like so many years ago. Tony was our tour guide and he was great!!!

title: the place were my ancectors were before me.
text: This place is a amazing and a emotional piece of history that is a must see if you are in Ghana. you can feel the sprit of the people and were here before. You can feel the pain that they had to go through while they were here. You can feel the lack of air in the dungeon that they stayed in, until they had to leave alive or dead.

title: Национальный музей
text: Музей очень бедненький.. Но что еще там может быть?!) Культура, на мой взгляд, совсем бедная, без особых традиций, историй.. Если не посетите, то ничего и не потеряете. Сама территория - чисто, охрана, безопасно)

title: Undergoing Renovation
text: The National museum of Ghana is an important tourist attraction. We recommend it especially for those embarking on educational tour. But it is quite unfortunate that the museum is currently closed indefinitely due to an ongoing renovation.

title: Highly recommend that you pay for the guided tour
text:
I was lucky to get the services of a tour guide who is on site. Listening to her give the background to the pictures and artifacts definitely made this an interesting and enjoyable visit. Had I just gone around on my own, I think I would have been very disappointed and got little to nothing out of the visit.  
There's a small book shop on site for those who'd like to know more about Ghana's history and fight for independence.

title: Unfortunately Still Closed Due To Renovations
text: During my half day tour around Accra on Monday 27/11/17 we called into the National Museum Of Ghana for the first stop with my driver / tour guide &, unfortunately on arrival we were informed from staff the Museum is still closed due to renovations & could be another six months before completion. Very Disappointing especially being the National Museum

title: A worth while stop
text: We stumbled upon this museum as we were on another outing. Though things are not yet perfect here it was a delightful experience. I think we will take friends when they visit next month

title: 2017年7月まだ閉鎖中
text: まだ閉鎖中でした。職員に聞いたらいつ開くかわからないとのこと。外観は古びた感じです。近くにテクノロジー、サイエンスの博物館がありました、つまらなかったです。

title: CLOSED!
text: Went to the National Museum with an old friend from Abu Dhabi as our first point of call on our Accra tour.  It was an embarrassing site.  The building is supposed to have been locked up for renovation about three years ago.  There was absolutely no sign of construction work going on and all you could see were what seemed to be a few statutes dumped outside. It is a complete waste of time going to this hollow place.

title: Continues to improve
text: When I first visited the Museum in 2002 Nkrumah's statue was broken up and laying in a side yard. Now it is restored. The displays are still be bit dusty, but the variety of cultural artifacts is the best I've seen. If I remember correctly, photography is not permitted.

title: Quaint
text: To be honest, my experience here was disappointing. I have visited many museums globally, but it was hard for me to tell exactly what was being showcased in this one.

title: A must- see for all, especially for the youth.
text: Aside the old relics found in this national museum there is so much history to dig out. For those still in their youthful years my piece of advice is for them to pay a visit to this place. There is a narator/tour guide to send one round and explain issues. Going round alone you just see pieces of relics and seemingly unimportant images but upon narration and explanations you leave the place more knowledgeable.

title: Disgraceful
text: I know you have to adjust expectation to where you visit but this is very poor. Don't bother visiting. The gallery was closed when I visited but you can tell from other exhibits it is a national embarrassment

title: Not a proper museum
text: The museum was closed for renovations when we got there, but someone still allowed us in to look around.  There was no work going on.  There was barely any artefacts on display. The building is extremely small.  Hardly museum quality.  They said they would be acquiring more artefacts, but I would not waste my time again.

title: It's worth a visit
text: It's worth a visit to learn about Ghanas history, even though it's not splendid in any way. A museum like many others. The museum is closed for renovation, hopefully it will be open soon and more developed.

title: Enjoyable experience love museums
text: Anyone going to Accra should try and visit this museum I enjoyed it the exhibits are splendid. I am a museum lover so there were no drawbacks for me.

title: It was closed for business!
text:
Sadly I can't rate this beautiful place... I read reviews from others and was really looking forward to experience it myself but sadly it was closed down for renovations.

When next I am in Accra? It will my first port of call.

title: National museum

title: Historical

text: The Artists Alliance includes a vast and varied collection of art, crafts,  furniture, and clothing make by Ghanian artisans.  There is a nice mix of very fine paintings by well-known artists. Whether you are buying or not, the gallery offers a worthwhile tour of Ghana rich artistic talents.

title: Wonderful art
text: Established over 20 years ago this gallery in a grand old mansion or hotel building allows Ghanaian artists to seel their work directly to the public. Here you will find unique work that doesn't feature in the craft markets, and mostly at very reasonable prices. Go home with a crab shaped coffin, an intricate wire sculpture or a painting worthy of an international gallery. There are some more standar pieces for sale such as tin-can sculptures, printed fabrics and beads, but most things here are a bit different and special. It's a bit out of town, and well worth the visit.

title: Bustling
text: Elmina’s a bustling fishing town and the castle is at the far end of town. Not a lot going on but an interesting half a day wandering around. The castle is less busy than Cape Coast and fewer tourists. Still impressive and tells a horrific history. Lots of hassle outside but just smile and walk on and all is fine.

title: Very impressive
text: Going there you will be transported in what was the hell for thousands of slaves: you may feel their cries and desperation, really impressive. Guided tour perfectly organised.

title: Excellent tour guides
text:
Very well preserved castle. The tour guides give an excellent potted history of the castle and its role in the slave trade.  
Avoid speaking or even making eye contact with the aggressive even menacing young men hanging around the entrance. They have a number of scams going including forcing you to buy overpriced bracelets.

title: Encore beaucoup de progrès à faire

title: Absolutely fascinating
text: Beautiful scenery from the fort, great tour guide, and the fort itself is in very good condition. It gives the visitor a clear glimpse of the living conditions of the slaves at the fort prior to being shipped around the world. If they survived the fort,  70% of them would perish during their sea voyage. The fort is a must see.

title: Als weißer Europäer übt man sich in Demut
text:
Nach Durchquerung des Ortes Elmina erreichen Sie den Parkplatz vor der Festung. Trauen Sie sich, den Hügel hinauf bis unmittelbar vor den Eingang über Plastersteine zu fahren. Dort parken Sie sicher und unbehelligt. Parken Sie weiter unten, zahlen Sie an die omnipräsenten, selbsternannten Parkwächter einen kleinen Obulus (5,00 Cedi).
Der Besuch der Festung führt Sie in die Zellen der dort in Gewahrsam gehaltenen Sklaven, die Empfangsräume des Gouverneurs, die Schlafräume, die Kapelle. Man mag sich nicht ausmalen, wie es damals hier zuging. Allein die Vorstellung der olfaktorischen und sanitären Sensation ist grauenerregend.
Der Besuch der Festung kann nur jedem Reisenden auf das Wärmste empfohlen werden!

title: Very powerful and moving
text: Wonderful tour with great guide, but you have to be careful, as they can be very pushy.  Ask for recommendations from people who have been before.  The fort itself is in pretty good shape and it is amazing to think that it has been in continuous use (by several different gov'ts) over the past 500 years--truly a "living" castle.

title: Sobering but a must see
text: One of the saddest places you will visit. But well worth the visit. Tour guide spoke English well and was very knowledgeable. Important to learn this very sad part of Ghana history

title: Rondleiding door geschiedenis Elmina Castle

title: Geschichte verbunden mit schöner Aussicht
text:
Wirklich gut wieder hergerichtete Festung, die durch Piraten fast vollständig zerstört wurde.  
Von hier hat man eine wunderschöne Aussicht auf die Cidade Velha, die Bucht und das grüne Tal, das sich ins Landesinnere schlängelt. 
Der Infofilm am Anfang zieht sich ein bisschen und sollte nochmal überarbeitet werden.  
In der Festung selbst ist außer einigen alten Kanonen und der Zisterne nicht viel zu sehen, trotzdem ist das Bauwerk recht beeindruckend und für die Aussicht lohnt der Eintritt allemal.

title: Centuries of history and sweeping views
text:
While more of a site than a sight today, with just the one information board outside, this is a good place to come to with a guide or having read up on the place. It's a very impressive structure with an intriguing history and offers excellent views over Cidade Velha and the ocean below.

To gain admission (if the gate is locked, which it probably will be), try the smaller building opposite, where a film about the place can be watched. Tickets cost 500$/€5, which is on the more expensive side by Cabo Verde standards, but is about the only source of income there is to help with the fort's upkeep.

Be careful while moving round the fort and over its cobblestones: the surfaces are very uneven and there's not much to hang on to.

title: worth visiting; interesting history, etc. but don't expect too much
text:
it was quite along drive to the Fort from Praia. Been to tons of Forts all over the world and thus this one isn't an outstanding one from that point of view. But don't let that deter you. There are nice views of the valley and ocean from here one can enjoy.
It was built by Spaniards in 1590 and is a UNESCO world heritage sight.
The fort was built in the context of the Philippine dynasty , after the attacks of the English corsair Francis Drake in 1578 and on November 17 , 1585, with the mission of defending the city and its anchorage.
In 1712 he was assaulted by French pirates and rebuilt in the second half of the 18th century .
On sight you can see old cannons, 'holes' were prisoners were kept and an interesting cupula water storage building.

Fortaleza Real de São Filipe sto ferdig i 1593 og er i dag på UNESCOs liste over verneverdige  historiske byggverk. Det koster 500 escudos (5 euro) for å besøke festningen som er flott restaurert. title: Le lieu pour se faire arnaquer et harceler
text: Je marchais seule en direction du marché quand un homme sympa m'a abordée. Il disait être instituteur et sortait de donner un cours privé de français. Il m'a demandé si j'appréciais le Sénégal et si les vendeurs à la sauvette ne m'embétaient pas trop; J'ai répondu oui et il a proposé gentiment de me faire découvrir le marché de sandaga. Très vite je me suis retrouvée dans une filature ou j'ai dépensé tout l'argent que j'avais sur moi c'est à dire 150 €; Je me suis retrouvée dans un engrenage et j'ai honte de l'écrire mais je me suis faite avoir comme une bleue. Dans cette filature j'avais plusieurs personnes après moi dont ce soi disant instit qui sous ses airs bienveillant n'a jamais été instit de sa vie mais plutôt un rabatteur car je me suis aperçue qu'il connaissait les vendeurs mais c'était trop tard, je n'avais qu'une seule envie c'était sortir de ce guépier. J'ai dépensé 150 € pour 3 robes que jamais je n'aurais payé ce prix là en France. Pour sortir du marché j'ai été harcelée. Une horreur !!! Les sénégalais prennent les européens pour des pompes à fric dans ce marché.

title: Very Fun!

title: Marchandages

title: in the very center of Dakar
text:
Open air market formed by a couple of streets ! Here you find a lot of rubbish , and not much more : only rubbish !!
Hasslefree walking around is impossible if you are white !
From the first minute you will have a couple of guys hanging literally on your shoes trying to get you into 'their' shop and trying to convince you to buy anything that you do not need and that you definetely do not want ! As soon as you get rid of those guys some other guys take over , and so on...
That's really annoying ...
