title: Neat market with lots to offer
text: Went here on a public holiday, so although open not so many people around. Certainly found it worthwhile in terms of seeing what produce was available and at what prices. Haggling allowed.

title: A vibrant market
text: Be ready to haggle! I loved every part of it! It is hard if you are not used to it, but just be prepared. Not sure that this should be a tourist destination, but it is good to get a feel for Senegalese day-to-day living.

title: Not for beginners
text: This is probably the worst beginner tourist destination ever.  You can find pretty much anything you want to in here, but you have to haggle for it.  The prices they start out with are more than what you would've paid for it in U.S.  You need to do your homework and know what something is really worth before you even think about going here.  i've had them start out at $30 and walked away paying $3.  Other times they won't sell because they're waiting for some other chump.  Always be prepared to walk away.  You need to be assertive bordering on aggressive with them if you don't want to get straight up robbed.  Never hand them any money until absolutely finished with the deal. Once you hand it to them, you're not getting it back.  I never had any change made.  If you buy something for 5 CFA and hand them a 10,  they will try and fail to get you your change and now you're stuck having to haggle for something else "worth" 5 CFA.  I'm not saying don't go, just bring your A game.

title: Big dirty market
text: Типичный городской рынок для туристов.В отличие от марокканского здесь смотреть особо не на что.Обычный набор масок,дерева,китайских тряпок  и местного текстиля.От приставания типа гидов устаешь через пять минут.Очень неуютное место,не рекомендую.Лучше в деревню артистов за сувенирами поехать.

title: 散策程度（あくまで見るだけ）でよい
text:
このエリア、露店やら建物内にもマーケットがあり。地元の方のお店はじめ中国人資本の個人商店群、インド人資本の個人商店群などさまざまです。散策して見るだけで（あくまで見るだけで）十分です。食事処もあり。

土産物屋さんは値切っても高かったので、値段交渉力に自信がない限りあまりお土産を買うにはおすすめしません（空港の定価価格のほうが安かったです）。

title: Mauvaises sensations.
text: On est collé en permanence par des enfants qui ne vous lachent pas. Jusque là rien de surprenant. Mais ils sont accompagnés d'adultes qui font pareils et deviennent agressifs. Quand aux vendeurs c'est la meme chose voir pire. On se sent physiquement tres mal à l'aise. A force de vous toucher on est à la limite que ça dégénère vite.

title: Quel horreur, fuyez
text:
Première fois à Dakar et plus jamais dans ce marché. Nous y étions en famille (avec notre fils et sa femme -sénégalaise). A peine descendu de la voiture on se fait déjà agressé par "2 rabatteurs" , impossible d'avancer sans les avoir sur le dos. Ils n'hésite pas à insulter notre belle fille parce que nous n'achetons rien la pauvre elle n'y est pour rien. Nous ne savons même pas approcher un marchand, ils sont toujours là. Quelle épreuve fatigante, nous décidons  alors à regret de quitter ce marché. 
Un conseil si malgré les avis négatifs vous vous y aventurez, tenez votre sac à deux mains et croyez bien que vous n'y faites pas de bonnes affaires.

title: 靴がいっぱい

title: Call the bluff.....
text:
I read up Sandaga market on Trip Advisor from others who had visited the market. For someone who hates bargaining, thinking of going to Sandaga was a real nightmare. I was in Dakar on day 3 of a 5 day workshop, so I had the advantage of talking to other workshop participants about their experiences. The strategy that got me through a 2 hours fruitful shopping experience was : 
 - Getting one of the eager guides to the market from outside our hotel. 
 - Confessing to him that I had not changed my $ to CFA so ensuring that he takes me to a market trader who does foreign exchange at a good rate : This ensure he knows how much money I have for shopping. 
 - Telling him what I want to but and innocently telling him I depend on him for his help.  
Note : all guides have shops they get commissions for for bringing clientele. So if the guide knows how much money you have to shop you are abel to keep him in check through out the shopping expedition. 
Lets just say I got quiet a bit for the 200$ I changed.

title: Un musée d’art contemporain africain
text: La Villa Ajavon, belle bâtisse de type afro- brésilien construite en 1922 et cédée en baille par les héritiers à la fondation Zinsou, abrîte le premier musée d’art contemporain africain. Le musée Zinsou de Ouidah est d’abord la rénovation d’une œuvre architecturale unique. Visitez le musée de la fondation Zinsou, j'y ai vécu une belle expérience.

title: A voir absolument !
text:
Ouidah , fief du Vaudou béninois est une étape indispensable sur la route de Lome Ou dans l'autre sens sur la route de Cotonou .
Il faut s'arrêter en ville pour au moins 2 raisons :
La magnifique cathédrale de Ouidah , 1er cathédrale d'afrique construite au début du 20 eme siècle , et la fondation Zinsou ,fondation d'art contemporain , unique en Afrique .
Située derriere la cathédrale , la fondation est installée dans une vieille maison coloniale de 1929, cette fondation fait la part belle , aux jeunes et moins  jeunes artistes contemporains africains , venant d'afrique du sud , du togo , du benin bien sur mais aussi de Tanzanie et même d'Ethiopie .
En tous cas à ne pas rater , d'autant que les guides sont excellents et competents .

Suurehko linnoitus, jonka sisäänpääsymaksuun sisältyy noin tunnin pituinen opastus. Ennen opastusta vierailija ohjataan museorakennukseen, jossa kävijälle paljastuu linnan synkkä menneisyys.

Myös ruotsalaisten (Suomi oli Ruotsin vallan alla tuolloin) osuus orjakaupassa tulee hyvin selväksi. 

Oppaan opastus hyvä. Kierroksen jälkeen (tai vaikka ennen) mahdollisuus itsenäisesti kierrellä linnoituksessa. 

Käynnin aikana sisäänpääsyn täytyi tapahtua ennen kello 17. (Viimeinen opaskierros) Ulos linnasta pääsi omaa tahtia. Itse poistuimme vasta hämärän saapuessa. 

Linnan vieressä parisen ravintolaa ja normaalit turistirysät. 

Hyvä käyntikohde. Myös lapsiperheelle menneisyydestään huolimatta.

title: Door of no return
text: Despite the horror history of the Castles that line the coast of Ghana, this is a must see in Cape Coast. The castle history is detailed in a respectful and honest manner. There are many guides around the place who want to help, but there is a museum inside which outlines the history of the slave trading routes from Africa to the Americas and Caribbean through to the Independence of Ghana. We spent an hour or so walking around the castle, which was well worth the visit.

title: Amazing place!

It has a very sad history and it is strongly recommended to take a guided tour around the Castle and you will hear the history of the case that built by Swedes but in different time periods belong to Danmark, Netherlands and Great Britain. title: Slave fort
text: The whole world should visit this place. It is like auschwitz- a reminder of just how bad humanity can be. Just let it speak. Very challenging to black as well as white . The local black tribal leaders were as much involved as white traders. Won’t say anymore. The place speaks for itself. May it stand for a long tome as a warning as to what happens when we forget our humanity.

title: Lohnenswert

title: A reminder that the Empire was built on blood
text:
Cape Coast castle is an impressively situated fort in the old capital of Ghana. The tour, by a very knowledgeable and thoughtful guide contrasted the claustrophobic, dark slave dungeons with the British governor's airy quarters.

Rows of cannon can be seen on the walls and the views of the coast, fishing boats and the town is worth seeing. 

The slaves brought from what was then called the Gold Coast were transported to the Americas and British colonies in the west Indies.

title: Should visit
text: There are a number of Forts/castles on the West African coast and some in Ghana, including Elmina, there is a Fort at Cape Coast half an hour away. This was built by the Dutch/British and is a larger fort. In 2009 Barack and Michelle Obama visited this fort and there is a commemorating plaque adjoining the entrance to the 'male slave dungeon'.

title: Life-changing visit
text: Cape Coast Castle has a shameful place in history. Touring the grounds was emotional and draining, but a must-do for anyone visiting Ghana. We took a day trip from the African Regent Hotel in Accra. We had a guided tour and the tour guide was FANTASTIC. He took us through the castle and into the rooms where the slaves were kept and tortured before being taken to America or the Islands. You cannot visit here and not be touched and saddened over this horrible time in history.

title: Chilling History Of Rape, Murder & Slavery
text: So much to say about this place... everyone needs to go here to hear  the stories firsthand. To hear about how African were taken from there homeland using this "dungeon" (not a castle) to aid in the process. Get yourself a guided tour here. Bring comfy shoes to walk in. And bring tissue...

title: Very Interesting

It is very moving when you hear about how the slaves were treated and the conditions they lived in before they were sent through the door of no return.  It was very hot when we were here so take a bottle of water with you.

title: Never to be forgotten
text:
Africa will show us many harrowing areas of the trans Atlantic slave trade. Cape Coast is such a place. It was so harrowing to hear the stories and see that the Door of no Return would separate families for ever....it touched me so much 
This horrific period in history must not be forgotten.

 P!ease visit Cape coast.

title: Worth a visit
text: Cape Coast Castle is well worth a visit, though be prepared for a stark reminder of the horrors of the trans-Atlantic slave trade - thousands of black Africans forcible removed from their homeland to serve as slaves in the Americas. The Castle is a firm reminder that such things should never happen again...

title: Cape Coast Castle
text:
Ghana is the land of the European forts and castles, as there are more of these trans-atlantic chattel slavery and colonial edifices in Ghana than any other African country by a country mile. 

There are several forts built to protect Europeans and their wares all over the coast of Ghana, but there are only three castles that remain till date: Elmina, Cape Coast and Chrisitianborg or Osu. 

The Elmina and Cape Coast Castles played significant roles during the slave trade. The Portuguese, especially, traded over eleven Africans from across the Westerh Africa region, while the British traded over four million Africans from all over West Africa respectively to the Americas  during the duration of the slave trade.

It is therefore always a form of soul cleansing to visit these two castles and as said by someone, "no African should live through life without visiting the slave castles in Ghana". The Cape Coast Castle for example shows how the Europeans lived and did business with the locals and their ilk and sometimes how wicked they were towards their fellow human beings. 

I implore all who can to visit the Cape Coast or Elmina Castles to learn some of the sordid things done to the black race by  a race that thought it was superior.

title: Beeindruckende Geschichte Ghanas
text:
Das Cape Coast Castle ist ein beeindruckend Ort, an dem man einen sehr guten Einblick in die Geschichte des Sklavenhandels in Ghana erhalten kann. 
Die Tour durch die Burg (Student - 30 GHC) dauert ca 1 Stunde und ist super informativ. 
Definitiv ein Muss während der Ghana Reise.

title: Cape Coast Castle
text: Never have a quoted another reviewer.  However, I could not find better words..."One can actually feel the anguish, fear and humiliation slave men and women must have felt in the dark slave dungeons. The slaves did not know any crime they must have committed to deserve such dehumanisation. Families were ripped apart, family history was lost, centuries old culture was lost and all sense of humanity was sacrificed for filthy lucre"  NOT TO BE MISSED

title: Impressive Monument full of symbolism
text:
Saturday 27th May and this was the final stop, before lunch, on our Art and Culture Tour of Dakar.

The monument could not easily be overlooked as the bronze statue stands 52 metres (171 feet) high and overlooks the Atlantic Ocean.

It stands on the second of the Deux Mamelles hills, the smaller one of the two hills. The other taller hill is home to Phare des Mamelles, the Lighthouse.

There are 198 steps which lead visitors from the pavement upto the base of the monument and yes we did climb up to base of the Monument. Thankfully there was some seating areas along the steps. For those visitors unable or unwilling to climb the steps there is a roadway to the top, a more gentler way up.

The monument depicts a family rising from the bowels of earth, the rock base, heading towards the light. It comprises of a man holding his child skyward whilst holding his wife by the waist as he leads them from the darkness. It symbolises Africa leaving obscurity and rising up. It is rather poignant that the child is the highest point with it's finger pointing upwards. It acknowledges the the youth of Africa will the way forward.

There is a restaurant situated at the top of monument, it is in the man's hat, from the ground, the restaurant windows could be seen. At the time of our visit the restaurant was closed, it only opens in the evening.

There are a number of plaques, around the base of the Monument, bearing quotes from Abdoulaye Wade, the President of Senegal when the Monument opened. The quotes address the youth of Africa. It was inaugurated on the 3rd April 2010. The flags of the Nations, who attended the inauguration, were raised along the hill as we approached the monument.

When we visited the Ousmane Sow Museum we did see a version of the famous Sculptor's interpretation of the Monument, which obviously was not used.

Around the bottom of the steps, leading to the monument, there are a number of small stalls selling tourist souvenirs and coconuts. There is also Tourist Information Centre, Agence Sénégalaise de Promotion Touristique, nearby.

title: Bon si vraiment on est obligé!?
text: Alors comment le dire sans en faire trop non plus? Ce musée était en fait divertissant mais malheureusement pour de mauvaises raisons. Art et culture très peu mise en valeur, quasiment pas d'explication et par dessus le marché, un accueil qui fait surtout envie de repartir! J'imagine qu'il faille le faire vu que l'offre culturelle à Accra est de toute façon assez restreinte mais si vous repartez du Ghana sans avoir fait ce musée, ce ne sera pas trop grave... mais bien sûr tout cela: selon moi.

title: Closed for reconstruction
text: We just came back from the museum. The place is currently under reconstruction. Guard told us it may open in 2017 but it's advisable to check it before going.

title: Is alright
text: The artefacts on display are OK, but what really brings it alive are the tour guides who are well informed on Ghanaian history. Been there a few times and the two different tour guides I had both did a good job.

title: I Guess It Helps To Visit
text: This is an OK museum.....typical African displays....they would be poor in the west, but are adequate for Africa.....low level lighting....hard to see things....lots of well behaved children during our visit.....replica of Lucy is pretty poor when compared to the replicas in Narobi.....however, they did have a good series of human skulls demonstrating the development of cranial and facial features.....also a few good sculptures.....don't miss the things in the courtyard outside.....the Olmec head is nice....avoid the moth eaten stuffed baby elephant who is missing part of his trunk and part of one leg.....overall worth the hr we gave it.....the Lucy restaurant at the gate was also just OK....nothing worth returning for.....

title: A Great Start
text: This museum is having a makeover and is beautifully done.  However when we visited there was only one small room open to visitors.  The guide was very enthusiastic, conveying a lot of his knowledge inspite of the language barrier.  A great visit but a short one.

title: Muzeum warte odwiedzenia.
text: Napewno oczekiwalem wiecej po Narodowym Muzeum Ghany. Stosunkowo maly budynek, zaniedbany z mala iloscia eksponatow. Jednak nie ma co wybrzydzac, bo w Accrze jest tylko kilka muzeow, a to jest najlepsze.

title: Visit to the National Museum and use of their Conference Room
text: visited the museum and decided to have lunch there and it was really very nice.  It is mostly local cuisine well prepared.  The breakfast was nothing grand but simple and nice.

title: Good place to visit for history
text: I enjoyed going to the coast castles the most while in Ghana but the museum was something to do while I was in Accra. I do recommend it if you like to get a snapshot of history.

title: Momentan nicht vorhanden
text: Wollte mit Freunden hinfahren und ihnene dann das tolle Museum zeigen aber leider renovieren sie momentan die Ausstellungshalle. Wir wurden dann zu einen anderen Museum geschickt , wo die Ausstellung ausgestellt werden soll. Dies war nicht der Fall. Die Ausstellung ist momentan irgendwo gelagert und mann kann sich diese leider nicht anschauen.

title: Интересный музей
text: Небольшой, но очень интересный музей, раскрывающий историю Ганы. Много специфических экспонатов. Рекомендую!

title: Wird renoviert.
text: Das Museum wird zurzeit renoviert, wurde gesagt. Es sieht nicht so aus ob was gemacht wird. Gebäude und Gelände sind total heruntergekommen. Uns wurde empfohlen das Museum of  Science and Technology fast nebenan zu besuchen. Die Kollektion dieses Museums sollte jetzt da sein. Es gab nur ein Paar uninteressante Gegenstände zu sehen. Auch dieses Gebäude war ganz heruntergekommen. Schade.

title: there was nothing to see.
text: i was so ashamed of my country when i entered the national museum. there was actually nothing to see and the few monuments were not well kept

title: Very interesting and not too big.
text: Everything in one place to find out about the fascinating history of Ghana.  There are many artefacts that belonged to President Nkrumah in the small museum.

title: Non visit
text: Mid tourist season and that day the museum was being closed for refurbishment. How much bad timing is that! From the outside the museum looked tired and dilapidated so maybe this refurb is somewhat overdue. No idea when it will reopen.

title: interesante
text: Poco cuidado pero con piezas muy interesantes. Es la mejor opcion para conocer el arte antiguo de Ghana. Tambien tiene exposicion antropologica.

title: so much information
text: Loved my time visiting the Museum of Ghana, So much to see and read it was very interesting and to see the school kids learning as well was awesome. The kids also learnt things about the white lady with Tattoos... lol

title: a taste of the culture
text: Visiting the National Museum will give you a look at the multi-layered rich cultures the underlie the various tribes that make up Ghana. Worth a visit.

title: It could be more
text:
The first time i visited the National museum of Ghana a few years ago, it was a great experience. Well kept exhibits, air conditioned hall and fairly friendly staff. 
I decided to replicate this experience again recently but sadly met a run down facility, some exhibits falling apart (like the Egyptian mummy) and a very hot, poorly ventilated place. While i still experienced a natural thrill from exploring history, it was dampened by the reality of what i met on ground. It could be so much better. My recommendation is to visit at least once to learn about the history of the country and other parts of the world.

title: Don't Worry If you Miss It
text: I went on a Sunday morning. The staff were already asleep at the counter. As others have noted it is small, incomplete and poorly curated. Slave trade is poorly covered (you can do better in the castle at Keta) and the quite rich history of Ghana is virtually ignored. I have seen better museums in several developing world countries. And as for the odd "replicas" of a couple Egyptian artefacts! Even the Moorish connection does not make a link. Just makes it as a rainy day job.

title: I tried to get out put it kept pulling me back in
text: The National Museum of Ghana was uncomfortable hot with no AC or fan butt as much as I wanted to leave the exhibits kept pulling me along. I don't know about the authenticity of every object and when I first inquired about the ages of different exhibits the staff available did not know when the items where from either. That aside go in the earliest morning possible to beat the heat.

title: Just WILD!
text: One the wildest and most overwhelming markets I've ever been to anywhere in the world! There's just soooooo many people, food, clothes, motorcycles, cars,  and the smells! A must do while in Cotonou!

title: Sehenswert
text: Der Markt ist sehr voll und man wird als weißer sehr viel angequatscht. Im Großen und ganzen haben viele Händler die gleichen Produkte. Trotzdem als Europäer sehr sehenswert.

title: Nichts für mich

title: MARCHÉ DANTOKPA
text: Le marché dantokpa est situé au centre de la ville de Cotonou en République du Bénin.Le marché dantokpa l'un des plus grands marchés de l'Afrique

title: Shopping and chaos all around you!
text: We all love a crazy bazaar… Just be ready for people everywhere inside and out - and of course selling every type of imaginable item whether you can imagine using it or not!

title: Big city market
text: Fortunately I visited Dantokpa with a friend and he knew where to park and how to navigate the market. Great place to find West African cloth of any quality and pattern. Looks like you can find anything here and it's got a busy crowded energy.

title: Grand Marché de Dantokpa de Cotonou , Un Immense Grand Bazar , très animé !!
text:
Le grand marché de Cotonou de Dantokpa, se situe au bord de la lagune , qui relie le lac Nokoué à l'Océan et juste à coté de la RNIE1 qui traverse Cotonou . Le nom de Dantokpa en langue Fon signifie " Sur les bords de la lagune de Dan " , Dan ( personnage à trois têtes , portant un python sacré) étant le dieu Vaudou de l'abondance et de la prospérité . 

Ce marché , comporte un grand bâtiment de 3 niveaux avec des boxes pour la vente et, de plus tout autour , les étals constituent un marché en plein air de plus de 15.000 stands sur 18 ha . Ce qui constitue le marché le plus grand de l'Afrique de l'Ouest . 
On trouve tout dans ce marché en gros ou au détail , comme les matériaux  et produits de construction , la quincaillerie ,  jusqu'aux tissus , pagnes , objets de la maison , produits d'entretien . Les fruits et les légumes et agrumes ainsi que les volailles et la viande , sont regroupés , ce qui facilite les achats . Lorsqu'on entre dans cet espace , il faut observer les femmes vendeuses de rue , qui portent leur chargement en équilibre sur la tête ce qui s'avère assez spectaculaire . Les porteurs font aussi sensation avec leur rapidité de déplacement dans parfois une foule compacte . 
Les prix se négocient  âprement mais si , vous touriste , voulez acheter , attendez vous à voir les prix grimper . Tout se passe dans une bonne décontraction sans énervement , même si parfois des palabres enflammés vous font détourner le regard comme s'il s'agissait d'une comédie bien organisée  . Car , les béninois sont taquins et joueurs entre eux , quand ils s'expriment en langue Fon , majoritaire à Cotonou .

title: One of the biggest African markets
text: It could be a frustrating and chaotic experience for non-Africans, but I believe that every traveler should visit this market. You can find many thinks from food, fabrics, handicrafts, etc (it doesn't mean that you will find at a better price. There are smaller markets for that). But still, it is a market that you will have a very good feeling about the daily life of the locals. I also recommend crossing the river with the " pirogue", the wooden boat that the locals use for their transportation

title: SPECTACULAIRE
text: Gigantesque et vibrant, le marché à ne manquer sous aucun prétexte à Cotonou. On s'y perd aisément mais il y a toujours une bonne âme pour vous aider à retrouver votre chemin. Conseil : toujours solliciter l'accord des commerçants avant de prendre une photo sous peine de se faire véhémentement houspillé. Pittoresque et unique

title: Wonderful market!
text: I love visiting out door markets when I travel, and this being Africas largest made it to tempting not to visit! I went early, about 8-9 AM because it is cooler. It is busy, sure, but no where have I been able to walk this undisturbed! People greeted me, and when they understood that I do mot speak French, they did their best in English! I just love this people! Oh, did I say that I  was alone, female 50 + and speak no French? It went just fine! But do not be naive, wear your bag in front of you!

title: Transfer by bus Lagos Accra
text: To reach Accra from Lagos I took a bus and travelled across Benin and Togo. I remember Blvd St Michel, much traffic under a hot and bright Sun. Unfortunately I could not stop and take a walk there.

title: Mercado con productos de todo tipo.
text: A pesar de que había mucha gente, lo disfruté. Aunque la gente local no quiere que tomes fotografías.

title: Awesome
text:
DanTokpa is the only international market in Benin Republic, Cotonou. 
But while visiting dantokpa for the first time, you have to be very careful of démarché.
They will be pretend of helping you asin taking you to places where they are selling  what you want but all the places they show you and you bought from there, they has their (comition)  also be careful on agboro.  Tokpa is very beautiful in dry season but in rain season it's not. 
You can buy anything at Dantokpa

title: Belle expérience
text: Très grand marché avec une diversité de produits tant alimentaire, cosmétique et vestimentaire. J'ai trouvé mon compte. Très grand marché avec une forte affluence. Bon accueil des commerçants. Je compte y retourner.

title: Un marché incroyable
text:
Quelque soit le produit recherché, il se trouve à Dantokpa ! Quel plaisir de se perdre dans les allées de ce marché ville. Il est cependant conseillé de se faire accompagner pour s'y retrouver et surtout pour bien négocier les tarifs.
Superbes tissus permettant de se faire fabriquer des vêtements uniques à prix raisonnables...
Une visite incontournable pour tous voyageurs passant à Cotonou

title: Une aventure à part entière
text: À éviter sans boussole ou sans guide dans un dédale d'allées et de coursives plus ou moins spécialisées.attention aux portefaix qui déboulent avec deux poignées qui peuvent blesser si vous ne vous garez pas suffisamment vite. Un monde à part ou la vie pulse et donne l'impression que l'argent circule. L'Afrique au cœur.

title: Mostly for locals
text: Dantokpa is the largest open air market in West Africa. It covers more than 20 hectares, has 5.000 selling points and "employs" 25.000 people! Merchants mainly ell multicolored fabrics, foodstuff, alcoholic beverages, clothes and shoes, household electrical appliances, mobile phones, spare parts for cars, motorcycles and bicycles, cosmetics, household chemicals, jewelry, bijoux, as well as religious items and handicrafts. It is mostly oriented for locals. If you need souvenirs, it is better to visit Artesian village (centre Artisanal) close to Hall des Arts, Loisirs et Sports.

title: Très grand marché
text:
Ce marché est vraiment très grand / enorme. 
On y trouve beaucoup de produits différents ; et cela est aménager par zone. Zone pour les poissons, pour les habits, pour les chaussures, fruits, ... 
De nombreux dédales / allées ou on peut se perdre ; ou devoir marcher pour trouver une sortie pour tenter de se répérer. 
Activité qui mérite d'y aller, pour flaner, découvrir des produits, ramener des produits, trouver de quoi manger, ...

title: Not for the fainthearted
text: The market is large and there is also a building with 2 stories of kiosks mainly selling material and jewellery. If it has just been raining, the sellers take longer to open their kiosks and the outside area becomes muddy and messy with lots of muck and puddles. Beware of guys claiming to be security and offering to show you around free of charge. They insist on accompanying you and get very grumpy if you don't give them at the end. We visited the fetishes market as well. It is part of the larger market. It may well shock you to see live rats, cats, tortoises and egrets in cages. There were also heads of horses, dogs, baboons and monkeys for sale. Dead parrots, snakes and barn owls abounded.I am not sure if any of this decimation of wildlife is respectful of CITES. I rather think not. They even had a leopard's head. If you care for nature don't go there, because even a casual walk-through can be interpreted as interest in the animal products on sale.

title: Gesloten en verplaatst
text: Deze oorspronkelijke markt is gesloten en een alternatief is vlakbij. Nieuw gebouwd langs de oude spoorlijn. Heel netjes, alleen commerciële producten.

title: Marché des Arts (Former The Artisanal center)
text:
The Art Centre has been renamed Marché des Arts and opens from 0700-1900hrs. 
The location has been relocated to the other side of the road. 
There are lots of art works and souvenirs at the market. Make sure you can haggle the price too. 
It is very clean too.
There are chairs available if you need to rest and also a restaurant. 
There are about four-five entrances .

title: Good place to purchase gifts and sourvenirs
text: Good shopping and haggling for west African and beninois crafts and souvenirs. Went early on a Saturday morning and I was the only customer. Vendors were polite and good natured. Didn't feel hassled.

title: Overwhelming structure. Not very original finds.
text:
Although a good place to go for a souvenir -negotiate well! 
It isceasy to get overwhelmed as the lack of structure of the center.
Very few original finds.

Attention: they are in the process of moving location! (Date unclear)

title: Impresionada con la talla de Madera.
text: Me impresiono de verdad la forma como trabajan la madera,hacen cosas bellisimas,de verdad un verdadero arte. La atenciôn y la Risa simpatica de los artesanos hacen que les quieras comprar todo. Las mujeres son solidarias con nosotras las clientes. Me lleve un hermoso mantel de algodon con dibujos en pintura.   De verdad vale la.pena visitar este lugar.

title: Craft items of every ilk to remember your trip by!
text: Craft items of every sort and nice quality to remember your trip by. Necklaces, wooden stuff, paint, whatever you might like to bring home to hang or sit out can be found here… Virtually no crowd and you will have everyone’s attention when you walk in!

title: Même capharnaum que dans tous les autres marchés de souvenirs d'Afrique
text: Attrape touriste, très bas de gamme, peu de belles pièces et des prix inflatés. Mieux vaut aller flâner dans d'autres marchés.

title: INCONTOURNABLE
text: Le lieu incontournable pour remplir vos valises de souvenirs béninois, c'est ici. Commerçants agréables et souriants vous feront visiter leurs boutiques à tour de rôle. Bénéficie en plus de la présence d'un bon restaurant (le Babel) et d'un café très sympa (l'Atinssa).  En résumé, le manquer serait bien dommage !

title: Good place to go if looking for gifts.
text: Huge but not chaotic crafts market.  Tons of vendors.  Went first on a Sunday and it was pretty dead with few stalls open.  Returned on a week day and found dozens of vendors in huts and small shops.  You will have to deal with lots of vendors entreating you to see their wares but will take no for an answer.  They do offer a large variety of crafts.

title: Artesanía de toda la región.
text: Cotonú no es una ciudad para hacer muchas visitas turísticas...acercarse al mercado y callejear por sus puestos es casi lo que más me gustó de esta ciudad. Artesanía de toda la región...incluyendo cosas de Malí y Burkina.

title: Endroit a visiter absolument
text: Bonjour , c'est un endroit très intéressant a visiter absolument. Si vous voulez faire partir de notre groupe de touristes internationaux pour visiter cet endroit et pleins d'autres au Bénin a l'occasion de la fête annuelle du vodoun en Janvier 2020  , contactez moi: +447554783736 .

title: Tourist trap but would recommend!
text: It was difficult to find what I wanted but I actually bought some lovely items here..I bargained hard!  But some wouldn't budge and I sometimes worry I'm the only one buying so give in. Yes it's a tourist trap but I assume it's not frequented as much and I feel I've supported these locals but also got some lovely items!

title: Un peu agaçant
text: Un jour quelqu'un expliquera peut-être aux commerçants qu'insister lourdement n'invite pas à rester, même pour le "plaisir des yeux" (vous l'entendrez deux cents fois au moins 🙄). Certes il y a quelques belles choses mais c'est pour l'essentiel de trucs à touristes. Il y a mieux dans les commerces du centre ville ou les marchés.

title: village artisanal
text: Endroit parfait pour y acheter vos souvenirs du Bénin. Vous y trouverez tout et si vous négociez bien vous pourrez même faire des économies.

title: A visiter !
text:
Vu en février 2019.
L'artisanat ici est roi !
Il faut absolument visiter cet endroit. 
Nombre d'artisans important !
Je conseille de le faire sur 2 jours.(Si c'est possible)
Le premier pour visiter; le second pour acheter. Ça vous permettra de négocier les prix.
Un des lieux les plus touristiques de Cotonou. Il n'y en a pas beaucoup, alors ne le louper pas.
Les artisans veulent tous que vous visitiez leurs échoppes. Le tout dans une bonne ambiance.
Très bon souvenir.
Fred de Rouen

title: faute d autre chose
text: si vous n avez vraiment rien trouvé lors de votre voyage !!ou si vous ne faites que passer a au Benin .Les prix sont corrects pour nous ...mais au moins 2 fois plus cher que dans les petites villes !

title: interesting but not my cup of tea

After such a tour, you're now ready to see his mausoleum, which is within an imposing monument that can be seen from miles away. Take a walk around the park and admire the statue of Dr. Nkrumah and the various other sculptures around it.

Don't forget your hat and sunscreen. Watch out for the vendors who will try their best to get your attention as you enter and leave the premises.

title: 要了解民主和獨立歷史！不要只自拍，走馬看花！
text: 紀念公園內，池塘環繞著加納國父的陵墓。從遠處，我看到陵墓像一把顛倒的劍。導遊說當地文化中，這把劍是和平的象徵。陵墓被大理石覆蓋（有磨損的跡象），頂部有一顆黑色的星（不是紅色的星哦！），是團結的象徵。在陵墓的中心，我可以看到頂部的天窗。雖然陵墓不是很大，但它設計得很好。周圍維護得還可以。總體：要到加納旅遊，要了解民主和獨立歷史！不要只自拍，走馬看花！

title: 更多了解國家的歷史
text: 今天，加納是非洲國家當中經濟發展最快的。因此，我不得不來這個公園看看，更多了解這個國家的歷史。這裡是一個致力於加納國父的公園。他帶領該國獨立於英國。根據導遊（在入口處可以看到他們），他幾乎領導國家走向共產主義（仿效毛思想和共產主義）。如果加納政府沒有及時更換，經濟可能會毀，老百姓生活也可能會苦了。在公園內，有一座陵墓，葬了國父和他妻子的遺體。陵墓周圍是池塘和花園。 （注意：有幾個導遊是大學生，有著豐富的加納歷史。請僱傭它們，並給他們合理的費用）。

text:

A really good variety of art work, fabric and souvenirs. A very large range of paintings in different media and for all tastes, from the basic ( something to cover your walls)  to beautiful detailed paintings.
Prices as in all markets in Africa are variable from expensive to pretty cheap . if you aren't good at haggling I strongly recommend going with someone who knows how to haggle.
It is also a good place to buy fresh fruit and vegetables !

title: Final Resting Place
text:
Dr Kwame Nkrumah was on an official visit to Canada. He stopped over in Beijing along the way and visited as an official guest of Chairman Mao. There was a coup in Ghana and as a consequence the deposed leader found refuge in Guinea, then French Guinea. Following his death in Romania in 1972, his remains were returned to Guinea. His mother's plea was answered, and his second resting place was in his home village. Subsequently his remains were placed in this, his third and final resting place. He was survived by  his wife, Fathia Rizk whose remains are also interred in the mausoleum.
A suitable resting place for this great man.

title: Celebrating the Birth of a Nation
text:
In 1957, the Prime Minister of Gold Coast, Kwame Nkrumah negotiated the independence of the then British colony and became the first President of Ghana.
The park is dominated by the mausoleum containing his remains. The design of the building reflects the trunk of a tree. The museum contained in the park has an interesting collection of personal articles as well as an array of historic photographs. Visitors are given an interesting tour and a brief history before viewing the articles and reflecting on the life of this extraordinary man.
His education in the USA and in United Kingdom, combined with his political career, is an inspiration. Some of the photographs show this great statesman in the company of other national leaders, as diverse as USA President John F. Kennedy and Chairman Mao Tse Tung.
The mausoleum stands at the sight of his announcement of the Declaration of Independence. The park is a former Polo ground, and had been for British residents and their guests, an area previously denied to native Ghanaian.
My favorite quote is "We face neither East nor West: we face forward."

title: Great history and monument; museum left you wanting more

The park with trees gifted from political leaders and countries is peaceful and inspiring. You should not visit Accra without visiting. Unfortunately, the museum came off poorly, with dusty photos, little explanation of what you were seeing, and disorganized exhibits. A fuller narrative about his life and intellectual and political legacy would have done more to advance the impressive and important pan-African sense that he championed. I hope they revamp the museum soon - I'm sure they would find support for such a venture across the globe.

Vivement recommandé si vous passez au Bénin.

Beaucoup de monde donc il faut savoir prendre son mal en patience.

La négociation est de rigueur !

title: marché international
text: vous trouverez tout ce dont vous pouvez avoir besoin divers, cosmétiques, pièces détachés pour voitures etc

title: Une fois dans la vie ... juste pour savoir
text: Déjà la première fois je me suis juré de ne plus jamais mettre pied dans Dantokpa. Malheureusement, on m'a convaincu que j'exagérais et que ce serait bien de tenter encore une fois. Hélas, le marché est impossible à visiter pour un blanc car on est constamment harcelé par des démarcheurs, on n'ose même pas à s'arrêter pour jeter un coup d'oeuil. Et même si on cherche un article particulier, soyez certain, que vous en déhors de toute négociation qui se fait entre des personnes parfaitement inconnu et qui vous imposent un prix. par la Suite, vous ne pouvez pas partir sans qu'on vous soutire des Sous pour des "Services rendus". l'nsemble dans un vacarme assourdissant et une chaleur étouffante sans cesse obligé d'éviter des autres visiteurs ou des charriots ou autres transporteurs et ambulants. Si un jour vous voulez y aller, juste pour faire l'expérience, assurez vous d'être accompagné d'une personne de confiance qui maitrise la langue et les coutumes.

title: グランマルシェ
text: ベナンの最大都市、コトヌーにあるマーケットで、グランマルシェとも呼ばれる市場。 グランマルシェはロメのグランマルシェと同様に食料品から衣類まであらゆるものが売られ、女性の方が多い。奥にいくと、フェティッシュマーケットもあり、ブードゥー教の市場も連なっている。

title: un lieu haut en couleurs
text: incontournable pour faire des bonnes affaires, attention: munissez vous de votre répartie et votre bonne humeur car le marchandage est de rigueur. Bonne ambiance garantie!

title: Typische markt van Afrika!
text: Het echte leven zoals het in Afrika is. Je vind er alles; eten , stoffen, vodoo medicijnen , kruiden,

title: Rather rowdy and stressful
text: I was unable to buy anything because the market was too stressful and extremely rowdy. I left with nothing.

title: Incontournable
text:
Même si on n'y achète rien il faut y aller pour les couleurs, les odeurs, l'ambiance. 
Et un guide s'impose ou on s'y perd vite !

title: El mercado más grande de Africa del Oeste
text: Un lugar donde consigues de todo a precios razonables, aunque es obligatorio el negociar los precios! Un buen lugar si deseas descubrir en verdad,como yo le digo, la otra cara de Africa... Los niños de la calle abundan en este mercado, donde vienen a trabajar para ganar el pan de cada dia. Es una experiencia que te hace abrir los ojos a la realidad y ver lo afortunados que somos...

title: Love
text: C'est  un marché rempli d'amour, et si tu n'as  pas la maîtrise  tu peux  te perdre. Je l'aime beaucoup car il y a tout dedans  .

title: Stressful but rewarding
text:
Dantokpa boasts of a variety of goods and if you are not careful, you are sure to go above your budget. 

Loads of colourful and lovely ankara (African prints) to be purchased from here. Be sure to always bargain cos prices quoted are way higher than the sale price.

title: Everything
text:
Marche Dantokpa has everything. Fast moving, feels safe, lots of fabrics. Baguettes & mini doughnuts for sale as you walk around.
Prices are quoted higher for Yovo's, so go about ⅓ of what is quoted.

title: Le plus grand marché d'Afrique de l'Oeust
text: Fruits et légumes, condiments et épices, tissus et bijoux, produits aquatiques ... Tout s'y trouve et tout s'y négocie. Se requinquer avant de sillonner les allées du marché pour faire fasse au dynamisme et à l'énergie des marchandes.

title: African Market
text:
We go as often as our budget allows. The Lekki Market is a must if you want to buy gifts or any other household items, fresh food, furniture, art, jewellery, etc, etc.
Wear flip-flops or gumboots and leave flashy jewellery and expensive items at home....then be prepared to negotiate!!!

title: Good Exploration and Bargain Place
text: Market provides lots of local/nearby African countries art works. Ranging from semi precious stones, wood carvings, brass antiques, paintings, ornaments, leather goods,  elephant tusk etc etc. However one need to be cautious about the ingenuity of products as well local rules for animal goods trade. Bargain depends upon individual ranging from 1/2 to 1/4 of original price.

title: Unique shopping experience
text: The market is not easy to find because it's located at the back of main parking area but once you find it, it presents a variety of art pieces. To get value for money, you have to be very good at bargaining! We got some nice jewellery at fair prices. Because of the weak Naira, if you change your dollars you can get really nice art pieces and souvenirs.

title: Once a Treasure Trove
text:
Lekki market I believe also know as lekki craft market was a place I enjoyed and looked forward to visiting. It had various merchants with an array of items, from paintings, carvings, jewellery, books etc. I was fortunate to have acquired some beautiful pieces in the past. That was about 5 years ago.
I visited the market last month and was a bit disappointed. It seemed to have been improved but not sure it adds credit to it. You have somewhat more solid concrete stalls, but no order to the arrangements of the stalls. Also it seems more of a general market than for arts and crafts. It is quite difficult to navigate. 
Access road and parking is an issue as road is bad and parking inadequate. 
Overall still worth the visit and you might be lucky to find odd interesting pieces.

title: Local craft and textile market..a tourist hotspot in a very unaccesible place
text: This is a definite must- visit market for tourists to pick up arts, crafts, local fabrics already sewn, beautiful bags made with local fabrics etc etc. I am a local but I visit often to buy pearls and ready made ankara loose kaftans. I went there for some nice loose ankara blouses over Christmas which I wear on leggings... The market is quiet but the road is very bad and untarred!!! In the rainy season, it is terrible and not motor able!! Be prepared to pay a levy of 200 NAIRA for packing!!! Enjoy your visit if you can get there

title: Lots to see at the market!
text: A very busy, easy to get lost in, market. Most important tidbit is to not show up until about 11-1130 am. Various shops will all kinds of local crafts. My personal favorite was the hand woven baskets. Many of them come from Ghana, and you can bargain a bit on the price. As always in these kind of markets, keep your pocketbook close to you and stay alert. Never had a problem, but you never can tell. I visited this market a few times with friends while I lived in Lagos 2013 to 2015.

title: Crazy, Fun Place
text: I went on a Sunday and only a fraction of the shops were open.  But it was even better.  Great crafts, art and jewelry.  Be prepared to bargain and push the vendors away.  It's a must see while in Lagos.

title: Difficult to Navigate
text:
Many sellers all willing to do a quick trade, it can be a bit overwhelming when so many are trying to see to you.  It is useful to have someone who knows the area and can fend off the crowds.

Be careful off the prices, there is a lot of flexibility, paying too early will cause you to pay too much.

title: Difficult to find
text: This is well worth a visit but it is very difficult to find as Lekki is the name of the area so there are a couple of markets but you'll know when you're going there because the road is difficult to negotiate in a car or motorbike. You walk through a food market first and then in a compound is where the real market is selling all local hand made items such as wood carvings, jewellery, cloths, paintings, artwork and many other items. You will have to haggle of course but i paid 6500n for a wood carving that was 15000n at the hotel. Bargain.

title: Crowded, Everything Under the Sun
text: The Lekki market is a fun place to visit & shop around. Be prepared for some vendors that pitch aggressive attempts to get you to buy their wares. If you see something you really like, ask the price, then shake your head a walk away. The vendors will immediately cut their offer 25-50%, then you can start bargaining. Many stalls claim to be selling "African Ivory" but it's really some other wood darkened with shoe polish.

title: Hard to find but worth it
text: this is really called jakande market and it is tucked down a back street, went on a sunday when not all stalls open, and just as well as huge, with loads of stalls selling every sort of souvenir you could ever want, prices half of that charged at Silverbird culture village in Abuja and good quality. friendly non-pushy stall owners make it nice to visit.

title: Loved it!
text: So much amazing art. I went in search of some leather and got carried away by all the art, jewelry, color, and textures. You would find pretty much anything here but prepare to drive a hard bargain so you get a fair deal.

title: Arts, crafts, furniture, souvenirs, antiques....nice!
text:
If you haven't been before take a guide. Even for me as a local there's plenty going on and lots to see. You can order hand carved furniture, get a dress blinged with beads an buy ingredients for your dinner all in minutes.

It you need a relatively decent market setting at which to purchase you African souvenirs, this would be the place, so long as you're coming from Ikoyi or Victoria Island. I would think it would be quite out of the way for anyone coming from other locations. Its a must see place though. Parking is typical Lagos, always a crush when you find a space. What amazed me was finding fabric with designs from way back when I was a young 'un. :)

Expats come to frequent this market to find those 'one-off' pieces for their homes.

Nice place to visit

title: muy bueno
text: Si quieres llevar de recuerdo algo africano, éste es el lugar. El lugar es ideal para conocer la cultura de un país. No puede faltar en tu lista de sitios por visitar.

title: Art Market
text: If you're looking for a market that has African fabric, locally made African print clothing, jewellery and art work, look no further. This market has it all. The market can be a little overwhelming and confusing with the amount things happening at the same time. Be patient and take your time.

title: Hard to Rate
text: Lekki market is a place to find all sorts of items from staple foods to artisan crafts. Some merchants are a bit pushy. If you find something that you like, ask the price, shake your head and walk away. The original offer will drop, then start negotiations. You'll find the least expensive souvenirs here with the most variety.

title: Lekki Market
text: If your looking for where to buy anything or trading of all kinds like beads,native wears, art and crafts and many more think of Lekki Market

title: Lagos Market for Art
text:
Love paintings, tradition beads, native attire, art and crafts of ivory, wood, etc then this is where to be.
This is where I bring my foreign friends to shop for something African they would love to take back with them. Look no further for such souvenirs.
There's something for everyone in terms of price. You could also have some customization done. Please only go with money you want to spend as you're likely to spend every cash as there's always something extra you would like to have.
The roads that lead to the market can be tricky in the raining season but once you arrive at the market you're fine.
Also make sure there is always an attend on ground and close by when you enter any shop or inspect any wares. There was one nasty but the other time with a foreigner (I won't mention country) and a trader who claimed some of his stones were missing. Same shop I was buying something from so I tried to intervene, thought I could settle the cost but alas one stone cost half of all the money I brought to the market. Very likely an isolated event but something to learn from.
So if you're in Lagos and want to purchase art or native memorabilia, etc, you know where to be.

title: Great place for fun, art, souvenirs, etc.
text:
There are two Kekki markets right next to each other, one is more general and one is more arts and crafts. The market is a bit overwhelming at first and through it looks a little rough, I never felt unsafe. Had loads of fun looking around. I'm told the market does start closing up by 6 or so on week days (and the traffic is crazy by then anyway) so either go during the day or on the weekends. 

LOCATION NOTE: When I visited the TripAdvisor site (October 1, 2016) it displayed  a correct description of the market location but their map (and therefore navigation in the app if you use it) was completely wrong. Make sure to check Google maps for the correct location. 

Have fun

title: Cultural goods
text: I enjoyed the market and the traders were keen to sell but friendly and not intrusive or rude. My group purchased local crafts like painting, engraved cattle horn, bead jewellery, animal bookends and a traditional knife. Very colourful and enjoyable walking through the narrow stalls.

title: Interesting
text: The place itself does not really look like a palace, but with a good guide you do get the story and the right impression. We like especially the strange clay figurines on the walls and the stories behind them,

title: Amazing history
text: We really enjoyed our visit here. I would recommend getting an English speaking guide. This is very well preserved on African standards and some fascinating history comes from here. Would definitely recommend!

title: interessante
text:
Sito Unesco da oltre 30 anni e forse per questo è riuscito a conservarsi in buono stato. Anche se al posto dei tetti in lamiera potrebbero essere ripristinate le coperture tradizionali.
Interessanti le descrizioni della guida, che spiega nel dettaglio tradizioni e riti.

title: Interestinf
text: Informative and interesting. Recommend to those wanting to know more than just a beach . It’s about learning that Benin is an amazing place of history

title: Interessante
text: Visita interessante peccato sia vietato fare le foto! Consiglio la visita, perchè le storie raccontate dalla guida sono impensabili

title: Interesting history
text: I was the only person visiting when I came and I found this trip interesting. They had an English speaking guide who led me around the large complex and explained everything. The buildings have lots of bas reliefs and there are some artefacts inside including many ancient thrones and decorative staffs and some gifts from Europeans during the slave trade. Not a huge amount of things but enough to keep interested and imaging how it would have been in its glory. The history was interesting. Took around an hour all in and the tour is mandatory, you can’t visit alone. Photos weren’t allowed inside the complex at all which was a pity, even the outside of building with the bas reliefs.

title: L'histoire des rois
text:
Le musée ouvre à 9H et sa visite est conditionnée par la présence d'un guide officiel sur place ; sauf qu'elle est arrivée à près de 9H30. 

Le lieu n'est pas très bien entretenu malgré le prix d'entrée de 2500CFA. 

Les photos ne sont pas autorisés. 

Il y a certes quelques objets historique, mais rien de transcendant / exceptionnel / rare. 
La guide parlait doucement et me donnait envie de dormir ; cependant ce qui est raconté sur l'époque des rois reste intéressant.

title: A Slice of Dahomean History
text:
Interesting site that focuses on the once great Dahomey empire. These are the palaces of King Ghézo and King Glélé that has been turned into a museum.

The palaces showcase interesting bas reliefs, artifacts and collections. I had an English speaking guide who is very knowledgeable about the history and gave me a thorough explanation of the different sites within the palace. 

Only downside is you can’t take pictures inside the palace.

title: Fascinating place
text:
Located right in the heart of Abomey this is a great place to learn about the Benin Kingdom - a part of history completely neglected in my UK schooling. There are some very interesting artefacts and you can easily spend a couple of hours wandering around. Although some of the buildings are slightly falling into disrepair you do get the sense of what it must have been like at the height of the kingdom (surely the main aim of every museum right?) The English speaking guide was informative and very knowledgeable about this time period, which was good.

Only disappointing thing was we weren't allowed to take photos anywhere on the tour. Other than that, it's a highly educational morning out.

title: a place of history
text: a great place to learn abt History. the guide was totally great explain to us about the great Abomey Empire. he brought us room to room  and show us the abomey stuff ,the history of the kings,the warriors ,the wars ,how the abomey people lived during that time. after the guided tours, there were stalls of souvenir shops where u can buy stuff if you are interesed

title: Quick Visit
text: I was staying in Bohicon and went for to see the Royal Palace of Abomey, its not too far. I paid 500 CFA for a Zem to take me there. The entrance fee was 2500 CFA and that comes with a guided tour. Afterwards you can hire the guide again to take you around Abomey on a Moto if you'd like.

title: Full of history, the other edge of the brazilian slavery sistem
text: A great place to see that there was history outside europe. They never teach us this in the school in Brazil.

title: Visite
text: Dommage que nous ne puissions pas faire de photo, visite intéressante, un guide très compétent connaissant sin sujet

title: Belle visite du Palais des Rois d’Abomey .
text:
Visite incontournable du Palais des Rois d’ Abomey . Pour s’imprégner de la culture de cette région du Bénin et comprendre son histoire .
Et puis à la sortie l’ artisanat proposé est intéressant surtout pour les tissus.

title: Belle découverte.
text: Visite à faire avec un guide local, nous avions  "Mathieu" qui nous a fait découvrir l histoire des rois avec beaucoup de passion. Nous n avons pas vu le temps passé 1h30. Ce fut une belle découverte.

title: Un viaggio nel tempo....
text: Luogo interessante da visitare anche se non è tenuto in buone condizioni. Merita comunque la visita se non altro per rendersi conto di come era strutturata la vita di corte in questa nazione africana. Nel cortile principale ci sono venditori di suvenir, c'è anche un telaio per la tessitura con cui vengono prodette le stoffe che sono messe in vendita.

title: schreckliche präsentation
text: Der königliche Palast gibt wirklich nicht viel her , die wenigen Ausstellungsstücke sind nicht beleuchtet, da ständig der Strom gekappt wird . auf die Frage warum die Führerin keine Taschenlampe hat - nur Schulter zucken . alles verstaubt . Der letzte Raum mit Königsstühlen und einigen Reliquien ist ok . Man muss ihn aber extra aufsperren .

title: Eher enttäuschend
text: Ist die gleiche Sehenswürdigkeit wie die Royal Palaces, also siehe die Bewertung dort. Zusammengefasst: trotz Weltkulturerbestatus kein wirkliches Highlight.

title: Eher enttäuschend
text: Ein Weltkulturerbe, dass von außen noch halbwegs interessant aussieht, aber von innen leider nur wenig zu bieten hat. Einige der Räume zeigen Gegenstände der alten Könige und der Führer gibt sicher sein Bestes. Allerdings ist ein Fotografierverbot im Inneren der Paläste und die Baustellenatmosphäre eigentlich ein "No-Go" für ein Weltkulturerbe, zumal Fotos keine Schäden verursachen würden. OK, es ist eine Sehenswürdigkeit, aber kein wirkliches Highlight.

title: Vietato fotografare.
text: Appena entrati, presso la biglietteria iniziano i cartelli che intimano di non fotografare né all'interno del palazzo né nei cortili interni ma soltanto nel cortile principale (dove ci sono i negozi di souvenir). Ci sono degli armadietti dove depositare le macchine fotografiche. Non si capisce bene la logica di tale divieto, che è comunque sgradevole perché alcuni punti del palazzo sono molto fotogenici, in particolare le facciate con le nicchie con gli inserti scultorei e le porte di legno finemente intagliate. Il sito è protetto dall'Unesco, ma la manutenzione lascia molto a desiderare. Le nicchie con le sculture sono piene di ragnatele e i prati incolti. Bruttissimi i tetti di lamiera, che hanno l'unico pregio di riprendere vagamente il color rosso terracotta dei palazzi e delle mura. Alcuni palazzi ospitano il museo, i cui pezzi salienti sono, a mio avviso, gli scettri reali (ce n'è uno per ognuno dei re) e i troni. Il regno del Dahomey termina nell'anno 1900 con l'invasione francese.

title: Une ile à visiter
text:
Une belle découverte déjà le bateau que nous prenons pour rejoindre cette ile on s'y trouve un peu dépaysé nous avons fait toute l'ile assez petite de long en large en passant par l'incontournable maison des esclaves à visiter où l'on apprend toute l'histoire des esclaves et par où sont passer ces humains et par ses petites ruelles aux maisons colorées. 
Cette ile n'est pas petite on dit d'elle "quelle est le continent de l'esprit"

title: Ile de Gorée
text: Très bonne expérience avec notre guide Bekaye. Tout s'est très bien déroulé nous sommes satisfaits merci Bekaye et Secretoo n'hésitez pas !

title: Bouleversant
text: Excursion effectué avec Secretto et notre guide Olivier qui fut vraiment un guide d’une gentillesse et d’une efficacité exceptionnelle. La visite de l’île de Gorée fut très intéressante et bouleversante.

title: Riche expérience
text:
C’est un incontournable au Sénégal. Nous avons visité  Gorée et la maison des esclaves en famille. 
Avec notre guide Casimir, un passionné d’histoires et d’une gentillesse, la visite est encore plus poignante. À contacter au 221 77 237 34 67.

title: Visite de l'Ile de Gorée avec Casimir
text:
Nous avons eu la chance de visiter l’île de Gorée accompagnés par Casimir, un guide passionné, extrêmement bien informé et d’une grande gentillesse. L’expérience a été tout simplement formidable. Il a su nous transmettre l’histoire poignante de l’île avec beaucoup de respect, d’émotion et de clarté. Grâce à lui, la visite a pris une toute autre dimension. Nous avons appris énormément de choses tout en nous sentant accompagnés et écoutés à chaque étape.

Si vous prévoyez de découvrir Gorée, nous vous recommandons vivement de le faire avec Casimir. C’est une expérience enrichissante que nous n’oublierons jamais.

Ibrahima

title: Gorée magnifique
text: Visiter l’île de Gorée c’est faire un voyage dans le passé. Cette île a vécu la tragédie de l’esclavage.Cependant ,  les maisons coloniales colorées, les bougainvilliers, et surtout l’accueil des goréen tout cela est splendide. Merci au guide de sécrétion Becaye, qui nous a relaté avec passion l’histoire de l’île.

title: À voir
text:
À voir avec un guide francophone qui habite sur l île et qui aime son île 
Une histoire qui devrait nous faire réfléchir et en plus encore naturel

title: Super visite de l’île avec notre guide Casimir
text: Abordées à l’embarcadère, Bénédicte et moi nous sommes laissées guider par Casimir toute la journée. Nous avons adoré découvrir cette île; la beauté de ses paysages, la force de son histoire, c’est un devoir d’y passer. Et ce grâce à Casimir qui a exceptionnellement allongé sa visite (12h-17h) car nous prenions le temps (trop haha) de tout voir. Normalement chaque guide fait au moins 2 aller-retour Dakar-Gorée par jour. Je le remercie donc chaleureusement pour le temps qu’il nous a accordées et les riches informations qu’il nous a données. (son numéro : 77 237 34 67)

title: Marquant et incroyable
text: Historique ! Lieu chargé d'histoire africaine  et visite guidée excellente réalisée par Casimir: +221 77 237 34 67. La maison des esclaves est à ne pas rater.

title: île de gore
text:
Visite émouvante,
nous recommandons le guide Casimir, qui a une maitrise parfaite de l'histoire de l'ile et aussi qui s'est montré très disponible. 
il est au 00221 772373467

title: Remerciement à Bekaye et Spartoo pour leur expérience
text: Lieu chargé d'histoire le paroxysme de cette visite la maison des esclaves . Guide au top son expérience parle pour lui.

title: Nice day out but very long!
text:
What a day out! 

My husband was super excited to visit here we had a private tour guide who we met at the hotel we stayed at the Rui Baobab which was 2 hours drive to get to Dakar. 

was very very busy in Dakar, queue was long the order is kinda messy and waiting around is long. once on the island its beautiful can really sense the history. Remember you are in Africa so be mindful of your expectations. I needed to take my 6 year old to the toilet she was desperate and when we were shown a toilet she wouldn't use it we ended up waiting. food from one of the restaurants was nice, basic!  Flys everywhere so be mindful. learning about history was great and seeing so many REAL buildings was emotional. Ensure you leave out early to catch the early ferry otherwise its a rush.

title: Visite île de Gorée avec Casimir
text:
Je recommande de faire la visite de l'île avec Casimir qui explique bien l'histoire de Goree, avec une touche d'humour appréciable et une expertise passionnée !
Son numéro: +221 77 237 34 67

title: Visite de l'île de Gorée, avec Casimir
text:
Nous avons été accompagnés tout le long de la visite de l'île par Casimir, un guide rempli de savoir et passionné par l'histoire. Nous avons passés un excellent moment, nous le recommandons les yeux fermés, il est joignable au +221 77 237 34 67. 
Merci encore pour cette journée qu'on oubliera jamais Casimir, on espère te revoir. 
Emma et Louanna.

title: Excursion île de Gorée avec Secretoo
text: On a passé une excellente journée avec Olivier guide local pour Secretoo. Il est arrivé en avance et nous avons pu profiter de l'île de Gorée sans trop de touristes. On est ensuite allé au lac rose qui était bien rose et on a fait du 4x4 dans les dunes. Les enfants ont adoré...

title: Visite solo très sympa
text: Île magnifique au passé chargé. Super guide Casimir - très honnête et très pro +221 772373467. Évite les mauvaises expériences !

title: Guide touristique
text: Je vous recommande un excellent guide Casimir ! Il vous explique dans les moindres détails l’histoire de l’Ile. Contact : +221772373467.  3h de visite pour 8 000 fac.

title: Les fameux guide et les vendeurs !!!!
text:
Quel deception, les vendeurs et les guides qui harcèle, limite t’agresse.
Pour un tel lieu de receuillement ces dommage de ne pas se sentir a l’aise, il faut être sur ces gardes a chaque instants et ne jamais être naïfs.

title: Une honte !
text:
Une honte ! 
L'île de Gorée qui est classée au patrimoine de l'UNESCO est une déchetterie à ciel ouvert. Les bâtiments sont squattés et dans des états pitoyables. J'ai été profondément choqué et ai même contacté l'UNESCO sans réponse pour le moment. 
De plus, les informations transmises ici sont fausses. Ce n'est pas un ferry mais des chaloupes. Le tarif pour les non résidents est de 5200 CFA + taxe de 500 CFA. Sur l'île, les tarifs sont exorbitants et vous êtes harcelés de tout part par des petits vendeurs. Quelle profonde tristesse de voir ce lieu de mémoire totalement ravagé

title: Dommage
text:
Dommage que nous soyons assaillis par les marchandes, guides et colporteurs dès le ferry. Et encore pendant plus d'une heure à faire la queue pour le ferry du retour. Et faire la queue pour rien puisque sans explication les officiels en charge du ferry font passer des dizaines de personnes devant celles qui font déjà la queue. 
On vient en pèlerinage à Goree, retrouver des racines et célébrer des ancêtres. Et tout est gâché. Dommage.

title: c'est un marché international on y trouve de tout .
text: il y a des guides ou des démarcheurs qui vous aident facilement à vous orienter pour vos achats.il faut prévoir un appareil photo pour capturer les paysages les plus insolites car au marché Dantokpa on y voir de toutes les couleurs des vendeuses ambulantes déambulant avec leur étate sur la tête.

title: Interesting.  Very big but not stressful.  Good for African prints and jewellery

title: Un autre monde
text:
Ce marché est immense. Ce marché est dépaysant. Ce marché est d'odeurs, de couleurs, de langues diverses, d'éclats de rires, de disputes, de marchandages, de tout un monde totalement éloigné de ce que l'Européen peut connaître, voire imaginer.

Si vous passez par Cotonou, il faut le découvrir. 

Accompagné d'un ou d'une autochtone de préférence. Pour le marchandage (une nécessité absolue et coutumière), pour la tranquillité aussi éventuellement.

Sous cette double condition, vos yeux, vos narines, vos oreilles, voire votre toucher seront dépaysés et, si vous êtes ouvert à la différence, comblés.

title: Auf jeden Fall einen Besuch wert; aber Vorsicht !
text: Es ist nicht übertrieben, dass der Dantopka- Markt als einer der größten Westafrikas gepriesen wird. Aber das Größte muss nicht immer auch das Beste sein. Wer schon mehrere dieser Märkte in den Nachbarländern gesehen hat, der wird hier nicht in übermäßige Begeisterun g ausbrechen. Nur wer sich in Cotonou aufhält, für den ist der Marktbesuch ( nicht unter 2 Stunde ) schon ein Muss., Leider gibt es immer Ärger, wenn man Pewrsonen fotografieren will. Das reicht von Abwinken bis zum enrgioschen No. Auf jeden fall immer vorher fragen oder noch besser ist es, mit dem tele sich die Motive suchen. Achtung am Fetischmarkt: Hier kommt es zu Agressionen, wenn der  daher kommende  Tourist meint, er könne die Kadaver und Fetische einfach ablichten. So manch einer hat deswegen schon fluchtartig die Stände verlassen. Daher keine ostentive Fotos ohne das o.K. oder Besuch des Marktes mit einem der sich zahlreich anbietenden Führer !

title: dépaysement total
text:
En s'immergeant dans le marché Dantkpa, on se croirait presque dans un autre monde, ou plutôt dans un autre temps...
Tout vous saisit: le bruit, la foule , les odeurs, les senteurs, les "pétarades" et la fumée des zems et des mobylettes  qui tentent ( et qui y parviennent...) de se frayer un passage aux abords immédiats du marché, au milieu parfois de la foule.
On y trouve de tout, on se demande comment de si petites boutiques (pour certaines) peuvent abriter tant de choses.
Mais mieux vaut être accompagné en ces lieux ou sévissent les pick pockets.
Il faut savoir que des commerçants vivent là, vendent la journée et y dorment la nuit, font leur popote et sans doute...Le reste...
Bref, un endroit très animé et très typique, c'est à voir.

Par contre, j'émettrais tout de même une critique très sévère... En effet, j'ai vécu à Cotonou il y a bien des années, une cinquantaine pour être plus exact et, le long du marché se trouvait une lagune dont les eaux étaient alors d'une clarté éblouissante, un lieu privilégié où il faisit bon se baigner, loin des vagues et des courants de la côte.
C'était un endroit paradisiaque ! Quand j'ai vu ce que cette lagune était devenue ( on y jette tous les déchets du marché, et ceux des humains également...) ...Cette magnifique lagune n'est plus qu'un immense dépotoir dans lequel les poissons eux même doivent avoir peur de se baigner.

Dommage donc que cet immense marché ait détruit l'environnement.
C'est désolant !

J'éprouve un immense regret en pensant à "ma" lagune et des béninois auxquels j'ai pu montrer des photos de ce site merveilleux se sont eux même écriés: " Mon Dieu ! Qu'est ce qu'on a fait ? !!! "

title: Marché-Découverte!
text:
Le marché Dantokpa est le plus grand de l'Afrique de l'Ouest. Il est très animé et on y rencontre toutes les nationalités africaines et même au-delà. On trouve tout à l'intérieur de ce marché quelque soit l'article recherché. C'est un grand centre d'affaire brillamment tenu par de braves femmes pour la plupart. Pour bien visiter ce marché et faire de bonnes affaires, il faut y passer plusieurs heures. Mais attention aux pick-pockets qui y sont nombreux. Je vous conseille de faire la visite à plusieurs et d'être très vigilants.
Malheureusement, ledit marché est très encombré et on s'y déplace difficilement surtout les jours de marché ( tous les cinq jours) où ce lieu est gorgé de monde.

title: Outdoor shopping marvel
text: Marche Dantokpa is huge.  Anything you want, you can find here, but be prepared to walk around.  The only way to really appreciate the market is to walk around and see the different vendors and bargain.  The best time to go is at the end of the day when vendors really want to sell you can get your best deals.  Aside from shoppoing for goods you can also by local food here.  Make sure you have a strong stomach and a healthy appetite.

title: Difficult to Miss!!
text:
My wife and myself are currently holidaying in Senegal for the first time since we had lived in Dakar in the early/mid 80s.

Certainly one thing that didn’t dominate Dakar’s skyline during our time there was Le Monument de La Renaissance Africaine - difficult to miss positioned on the top of a hill and - at 52 metres - the tallest  in Africa!

It is accessible by walking up some 200 (steep) steps so not for the feint hearted but well worth it as on reaching the top one is rewarded by panoramic views. The Monument itself is impressive up close but some of the surrounding infrastructure (notably the toilets) is not well maintained. Hopefully, a temporary situation as it does take the gloss off an otherwise quality attraction.

title: Occasion raté de mettre une endroit classé par Unesco en valeur
text:
L’ enceinte des palais devrait être assez impressionant, mais l’ indifference pour la patrimoine de Bénin par les autorités de ce pays devraient drolement s’ améliorer avant que la visite sois satisfaisant au lieu d’ être une grosse déception.
La toiture traditionnele en paille de TOUT les palais est remplacée avec de l’ ondulé. on ne peut prendre AUCUNE photo, et ils ne disposent même pas d’ une brochure, et encore moins d’ un catalogue.
Pourtant il y plein de bas reliefs de toute beauté sur les murs, et une collection d’ objets assez impressionante.

title: Lieu impressionnant à découvrir
text:
un lieu classé à l'unesco pour de très bonnes raisons. J'ai découvert les raffinements d'une culture que je connaissais peu. Les palais forment tout simplement un ensemble magnifique. Le guide est efficace et répond à vos questions.
Cependant, une petite déception, j'aurais aimé passer plus de temps sur les différents blasons et mieux observer l'architecture des palais. Il y a un art visuellement très riche qui s'étale sur les murs des palais et que l'on voit un peu défiler au pas de course... pour se concentrer sur les objets vaudous qui au final m'intéresser peu. 
Par ailleurs, il est urgent d'agir pour la conservation des objets !

title: Enrichissant
text:
Une visite à faire qui explique bien la dynastie du Dahomey qui s'étale sur 3 siècles avec ses 12 rois.
Il ne faut pas s'attendre à trouver une architecture phénoménale, ce sont des constructions en terre, mais il y a quelques expositions avec les sièges des rois, les autels portatifs, des manequins, photos, ... l'essentiel donc, qui se visite en 1h / 1h30.
Le guide (essentiel !) a su mettre en valeur et à faire vivre le site.
Tarifs doux (2000 CFA pour de mémoire pour les étrangers), petit village artisanal.
Bémol : photos interdites dans le site même, toilettes pitoyables, pas d'eau pour laver mains, pas d'indication pour trouver le site (faut demander sur la route ;)

title: Un patrimoine à protéger
text: Le musée est intéressant, on se laisse guider par un guide local qui connait bien l'histoire du pays et les petites anecdotes. Malheureusement, le musée commence à vieillir, les expositions sont peu protégées et prennent l'humidité. Il reste peu de musée de ce type au Bénin, je trouve cela triste que leur patrimoine ne soit pas mieux préservé.

title: Excellente visite
