title: You really need a guide to understand the stories behind the palaces
text: We had an excellent guide.  You can visit two of the 12 palaces (the only ones that survived when the then-king burned them down in 1892 as he fled the French invasion).  The buildings contain traditional thrones, weapons, etc.  On your way out, you can take a look at the handicrafts: some fairly good stuff actually made locally.

title: For history buffs!
text:
If you are interested in the history of Benin then this is a must-see UNESCO site. There are no pictures allowed inside and you can only visit two of the palaces as the rest are in ruins. Our English speaking guide was exemplary and by asking lots of questions we learnt a lot which brought together our knowledge from visiting other sites across Benin.

At the time of visiting we were made to pay an additional tourist tax of 1000 CFA which was advertised on the wall in French. We were given a receipt for this but it is worth bearing in mind for budgeting.

title: Great tour
text: The Palaces are very interesting as is the tour. If you do not speak French you may not understand all the information as the tour is very detailed.  Pictures are not allowed which is too bad, as it would be nice to revisit memories.

title: Abomey Palaces - A Royal Letdown
text:
The royal palaces of the Dahomey kingdom are spread all around the town of Abomey.

We are traveling around West Africa with a Togolese English-speaking guide. He suggested we begin our tour of the kings palaces with a visit to one palace that also houses the main museum. 

We didn't visit a second palace. 

Our visit to the palace was underwhelming. Yes it was interesting to see the architecture and a few of the items showcased in the museum, however the museum collection is spread all over the complex in small, dark rooms in locked buildings. 

A map of the complex is not available aside from a heavily weathered, to the point of being unreadable, plaque when you first enter. 

We were provided with a museum staff member who was supposed to be our guide, but he did essentially no guiding and just followed us around. I refuse to call him a guide. 

We wandered around the complex with our Togolese guide doing his best to recall what he'd learned on previous visits to the museum. 

We had to wait for our museum staff member to unlock every building before we could enter. 

You aren't allowed to take pictures for some reason and our unlocking staff member did double duty as our photo policeman. 

In my opinion, tourism works as follows: a tourist visits somewhere, takes photos, shares photos and the experience with others and inspires them visit as well....

Don't waste your time travelling all the way to Abomey to visit here.

title: Un musée qui s'appauvrit
text:
Le musée perd en qualité et s'appauvrit en objets d'année en année. Sans compter le fait que le prix vous sera demandé avec un facteur 3 ou 4 par rapport aux locaux. 
Il reste tout de même une part de l'histoire du Bénin et mérite qu'on s'y attarde si on a un peu de temps

title: Interesting if you are into cultural history
text: Yes it is true, some of the palaces are not well preserved and not being taken care of. UNESCO efforts to restore and protect have been burned down several times "accidentally" by children igniting the grass around the structures to catch bushmeat. But a lot of archeological sites in the world have not a lot to see any more. The history behind those palaces is really fascinating and you can get a very good feel of the sites if you take some time and walk around the premises of the ruins. Locked front gates should not prevent you from it, everybody walks around them. The guide we hired from the tourist office was very helpful though not knowledgeable to an academical level naturally. We liked him anyhow and hired him next day to show us markets, places to eat and the museum. Official rate is CFA 4.000 for two hours plus 2.000 for the tourist office. Later one you can save if you hire him directly. We strongly recommend a guide, they are helpful, not expensive and you do a good job in directly supporting the young people there. Our official guide from the tourist center was the only English speaking one, we where his second customers this year in October.

title: Pas très bien mise en valeur mais des nouveautés en perspectives
text:
Guides très bien parlant 3 langues : Français, anglais, espagnol
Par contre le site n'est pas très bien mis en valeur et il faut pas hésiter à poser pleins de questions pour bien comprendre.
Le site est immense (45ha) mais tout ne se visite pas et surtout les photos sont interdites.
Ne pas hésiter (si vous avez un véhicule) à demander en fin de visite d'aller voir le fossé périphérique de protection pour bien comprendre comment était organisée cette place forte.
Un pan d'histoire de toute la dynastie des rois de Dahomey, des guerres, du business de l'époque avec portugais puis français ...

title: Une visite à enrichir de lectures
text:
Si vous ne savez rien de l'histoire du royaume, vous aurez bien du mal à comprendre. 
Abomey et son histoire se vivent au quotidien. Les guides ne sont pas toujours à niveau, mais les efforts sont tout à fait perceptibles pour rendre ce moment abordable au visiteur non initie et chaque béninois  vous en contera... Un morceau... Avec sa vision... 
À voir : les collections d'assens et trônes dans le musée, les nombreuses cours et le village des artisans avec la boutique où vous trouverez de la documentation sur le site et des cartes postales. 
Complétez la visite par un tour de ces 44 ha en Zem ou à pied pour vous imprégner de ce haut lieu du patrimoine mondial : palais du roi Behanzin, palais d'Akaba,honnouwa d'Agadja, marche des amazones... 
Ce site est magique comme la ville, comme ce royaume encore tellement vivant, patrimoine de l'humanité.

title: Royal Palace and Museum
text: Well worth a visit. Unfortunately they wouldn’t let anyone take any pictures inside the palaces. The temple walls in the palaces are built from clay mixed with the blood of prisoners of war combined with gold dust, pearls and gunpowder. There is a royal throne inside which rests on the skulls of enemies.When a king died all of his wives were buried alive so that they could serve him in the after life. And most of the kings had more than 200 wives.Get a guide who can speak English, otherwise you cannot make head or tail of what you see.

title: interessanter Ort
text: Die königlichen Paläste sind weitgehend einstöckig, rituelle Rundgebäude sogar eher unterirdisch und nicht so spektakulär, weil sie sich über eine riesige Fläche erstrecken. Die mit Wellblechdach beschützen Gebäude wirken sehr wenig original, sondern stark nachträglich rekonstruiert. Innen die Museumsräume bergen einige wahrhaft sehenswerten Schätze, von außen sehen sie weniger spektakulär aus.

title: Could do with some improvements!
text: Went to the places and museum. Signage is awful (and all in French which would be fine if it was readable), so it is hard to know what it being conveyed. The museum was good, however no English guides and again all the signage was in French. All 6 of our group were English speaking as well as 2 lots of other visiting groups. Perhaps this could be an improvement. The artefacts were interesting, and the museum itself was interesting just a shame it got lost in translation along the way!

title: Mauern und sonst nichts
text:
Wie beim Palace nichts interessantes zu entdecken. Man schaut sich eine große überwucherte Fläche, mit ein paar Mauern drumherum an. Der Rest ist für Touristen gespeert.
In der Nähe ist ein Vodoo-Markt den man noch besuchen kann.

title: Mauerreste und rostiges Blech
text: Außer ein paar Lehmbauten mit verrosteten Blechdächern und div. Mauerresten gibt es nicht viel zu sehen. Einzig um einen Eindruck über den Sklavenhandel zu erhalten geignet. Am Besten man besucht das Museum und schaut sich die Königsschätze an.

title: And this is a UNESCO World Heritage Centre
text:
The signage is awful or non existent, the locations spread across the town and no map available so you absolutely must have a guide to make sense of the place. We found a good guide at the Tourist Office, we paid about €30 for 2 of us for about 4 hours including the use of motorcycle taxis to travel between the various locations. The guide was knowledgeable and helped make sense of the restored monuments. There is essentially nothing original, the walls and buildings were rebuilt around 2007 and since then nothing has been done. The buildings are decaying, the signs are rusting and becoming illegible. 
The museum is worth visiting separately, it gives some more information on the Abomey Kingdom. Entry is 3 euro. Our guide was OK but more interested in completing the tour than imparting understanding of the Kindgoms.
One day is enough for Abomey.

title: Malheureusement très mal maintenues
text: Les guides essayent de leurs mieux de rendre l'experience excellente. Pourtant les structures ne le permettent presque pas. Quel dommage!

title: Why...
text: This is a Unesco world heritage and really poorly maintained. Despite that the guides are really striving at making it a superb experience. The palaces are barely recognizable - really a pitty. Sorry to be so frank about it.

title: storia
text:
Il Benin è un paese bellissimo, dove le persone sono pacifiche e gentili. 
Ti senti subito a tuo agio. La strada per questo sito ci è stata indicata da un signore incontrato nell'ufficio postale.
La guida ti spiega tutto alla perfezione, ma non vuole essere fotografato.
Entri nella storia di questo paese prima che arrivassero i conqustatori a tentare di rovinare tutto.

title: Interessant
text:

Les filles apprécieront les vendeurs de bijoux à la sortie du musée

title: Royal palaces
text: Really interesting to visit. The palaces have many features realting to the Ancient Voodoo Culture and also the warring Kingdoms of Dahomey. The buildings are partially preseved and extensive as each generation established their own palace.

title: Belle visite

title: Worth Visiting
text: It's all depend on the individual and your perception about African culture and tradition, about how  kings were venerated and the cruelity by which our forefathers were governed. There is an entrance fee though but pictures are not allowed inside the once palace because things there are sacred.

title: Incontournable, centre historique du Benin
text:
Pour qui veut comprendre l'histoire de ce beau pays, la passage à Abomey est incontournable. Il est rare dans les musées des ex colonie de retrouver une collection d'objet digne de ce nom, ici, par chance beaucoup de trace de l'histoire sont restées (même si le guide fait remarquer avec un sourir en coin que "Chirac nous a volé cet exemplaire pour le mettre au musée d'Orsay").
La visite dure environ 1h30 ce qui est tout a fait compatible du temps de concentration des enfants.

title: Iconic
text: If ever in Dakar, you have to visit this place.The African Renaissance Monument (French: Monument de la Renaissance Africaine) is a 52 m (171 ft) tall copper statue located on top of one of the twin hills known as Collines des Mamelles, outside Dakar, Senegal. Built overlooking the Atlantic Ocean in the Ouakam suburb, the statue was designed by the Senegalese architect Pierre Goudiaby after an idea presented by president Abdoulaye Wade and built by Mansudae Overseas Projects, a company from North Korea.[1]

title: Une île riche en émotions
text:
L'île de Goree est accessible par ferry, il vous en coûtera 1500 Cfa pour un aller retour.
En semaine vous avez des départs toute les heures, un peu moins le Week-end. 
L'île de Goree est sympa à visiter avec des lieux typiques et historiques comme la maison des esclaves,  les canons de Navaronnesxqui ont été installés par les Français en 1904.

title: ''Πολύ καλό''
text: Αξίζει επίσκεψη το νησί.Ωραίο νησί με όμορφα σοκάκια για περπάτημα και φυσικά αξίζει και η ιστορία του.Εκεί συναντήσαμε τον Fallou που μας ξενάγησε.Το κόστος μεταφοράς είναι περίπου 9€ με επιστροφή.Η διαδρομή είναι 25 λεπτά.Στο λιμάνι που βγάζουμε τα εισιτήρια πρέπει να έχετε και το διαβατήριο γιατί θα σας ζητηθεί στην πύλη.Υπάρχουν δύο ταμεία,στο ένα είναι η έκδοση εισιτηρίου και στο άλλο πληρώνεται τον φόρο.Επίσης στο λιμάνι θα σας ρωτήσουν αν θέλετε ξεναγό για το νησί.

title: Most recommended
text:
Amazing place to see and learn about the dark days of slavering.
The island is very safe, clean and clear air. 
It is authentic and impressive.
We did a 2 hours tour with an English talking guide- Fallo, very recommended.
A must see site.

title: Tasteful Review of Slavery with Hope for the Future.
text:
Goree Island is the place where blacke people were sent from all over West Africa to be sent to the Americas and Caribbean for slavery.  The slavery area shows the holding areas (really, cells) with one barred window where people were crowded in. We saw the men's area, women's area, women with babies area, and the children's area. This is a tasteful presentation of the horrible slavery that took place.  The museum shows more pictures and gives details on the life of the slaves and teh development of Goree Island. 
Today Goree offers several good restaurants, shops for souvenirs, a tribute monument, and an area of paintings and hand crafted quilts.  The Island also houese the best girls boarding school in Senegal and a Catholic Church.

Be sure to begin passport for ferry tickets!

title: Historical
text:
We spent the best part of a day here recently

It's a 20 minute ferry ride from the port in Dakar (if you can avoid the toilets at the port, they are disgusting)

We had a good tour guide who explained the history of the slave trade on the island. A lot of it was very difficult to hear and the conditions in which children, women and men were kept were appalling. 

The were plenty of restaurants on the island as well as a variety of, touristy, shops

It was well worth a visit

title: J'adore
text: Magnifique et reposante ile de Gorée. Petit havre de paix après la visite  de Dakar, très polluée ,moderne et plutot inhospitalière. Avons passé la nuit sur place . Quel calme  et quelle relative douceur de vivre ici. La visite de la maison des Esclaves est bien sur le moment le plus émouvant . A voir absolument .Grand moment d'émotion.

title: Sehr empfehlenswert
text:
Ile de Gorée 
Palmen und große Baobab Bäume säumen die Wege, bunte Kolonialhäuser, einige Einheimische schwammen  im Wasser des Hafenbeckens. 
Die Insel ist  ruhig. Keinerlei Verkehrslärm, denn sie ist komplett autofrei. 

Die Insel ist circa einen Kilometer lang und 300 Meter breit. Sie liegt in einer Bucht hinter dem Cap Manuel. Es wohnen  ca 1700 Einwohner auf der Insel. 
Man kommt problemlos und günstig  mit der Fähre zur Insel. Wir fanden den Ausflug sehr gelungen und überaus interessant

title: Worth going to Senegal just to visit Goree Island
text: The ferry from Dakar is busy when travelling at peak times but it is easy to figure out, to queue and comfortable to wait for the next available ferry.  Of course, Maison des Esclaves with the Door of No Return is the reason to visit Goree Island and an important place for reflection and education.  Surprised how busy it was but if you hang around and are patient, you can find space between the jostling to look through the door to appreciate and connect.  The island is very small so it is easy to walk around and enjoy.  Unique buildings and streets made all the more enjoyable with no cars.  Towards the right of the ferry are two crepe restaurants, which are very good.  And away from the flies.  Unfortunately sewage is dumped straight into the ocean so many of the restaurants are bombarded with flies.  In the market area, sometimes challenging to navigate the women selling the usual Senegalese items as many women are kind but we found some to be out of their way rude to us when we wouldn't purchase.  Didn't affect us in any way, just a heads up and too bad they behave like this on an otherwise peaceful island.  Stayed at NAFI'0, which I highly recommend.  Away from the flies.  The owner is an inspirational entrepreneur and hostess and her place is alongside the old colonial walls and near basalt on the ocean, making it truly unique.

title: ⚠️Une expérience désastreuse et inadmissible
text:
Je n'ai jamais vécu une expérience aussi décevante et désorganisée que ma visite à l'île de Gorée.

1. Attente interminable : Nous avons attendu de 16h à 21h pour rentrer sur le ferry. Une attente interminable et incompréhensible pour un lieu aussi touristique.

2. Entassés comme des sardines : Aucune gestion des flux. Les femmes, enfants, et personnes âgées étaient littéralement écrasés par la foule, dans des conditions indignes et dangereuses.

3. Organisation inexistante : Que ce soit à l’aller ou au retour, il n’y avait absolument aucune organisation.

Les gardes faisaient passer leurs amis ou connaissances devant tout le monde, au mépris des autres.

Aucune information claire n’était donnée aux visiteurs. Nous étions livrés à nous-mêmes dans le chaos.

4. Retards constants : Les bateaux ne respectent jamais leurs horaires, ce qui aggrave encore l’attente.

5. Climat de tension : L’attente interminable a conduit à des bagarres et à un sentiment d’insécurité pour tous.

Ce lieu, malgré son potentiel touristique, est totalement gâché par une incompétence flagrante. Je ne recommande à personne de visiter l’île dans ces conditions actuelles.

Message aux gestionnaires : Il est urgent de revoir votre organisation pour respecter vos visiteurs et assurer leur sécurité. Ce genre de service est inacceptable, surtout pour un lieu aussi emblématique.

title: slechte ferry organisatie
text: twee verschillende dagen proberen de ferry te nemen rond 11u. meerdere uren wachten tussen ongeduldige mensen en twee keer niet op boot geraakt wegens te druk. zeer chaotische en slechte organisatie.

title: Au petit bonheur la chance, prévoyez 4 h de marge
text:
La rareté des transports gâche la magie car c'est un grand stress.

Arrivée à 11h, bateau de midi plein et attente jusqu'à 14h

Sur place nous prenons un guide qui visiblement ne connaissent pas bien le système car nous avons raté le bateau de 16h qui était déjà plein 30 min avant son départ. J'ai attendu celui de 17h30 et suis arrivée au mariage ou j etais invité une fois fini.  En tous 3h de perte de temps pour les bateaux. Faut le vouloir pour y aller et ne rien prevoir ou avec 4h de battements 

Seule avec mon fils de 4 ans sur le ponton et mon amie dans le bateau de 16h (nous avions convenu de s'y rejoindre)....plus de batterie et étrangère ne connaissant pas l'adresse de mon amie, j ai expliqué au chef que mon amie était dedans. Il m a parlé avec haine et maipris... raciste clairement....limite je suis une colon et je demande un privilège... il m'a insulté...traiter de con**sse et demander de fermer ma g***le. Qu'il allait me mettre en prison .... vraiment  quel stupide homme. Tout ça devant mon petit de 4 ans.
Première et dernière fois que cela m est Arrivée au Senegal.. mais je m en rappellerai... heureusement mon amie arrivée de l autre côté m'a attendu

Quant à l'île, elle est incroyable, sans déchets et bien préservée. Magnifique! J'y est rencontrer des personnes formidables

title: Amazing so happy that I had a chance to visit this island so much history.. a must see…
text: Amazing! A piece of history .. finally got a chance to visit GOREE Island.. Most important trip of my Life!. only a 20 minute ferry ride

title: Una visita para olvidar ....
text:
Gastos: para ir debes pagar una tasa + el billete del barco. Luego allí si quieres entrar a la única casa visitable, tienes que pagar otra vez. Además tienes que pagar el guía turístico. 

Positivo: Está relativamente bien cuidado.

Negativo: la isla en si no tiene mucho que ver, la casa visitable, se compone de unas pocas estancias. Si tu guía no se expresa bien en tu idioma, como fue mi caso, no será demasiado interesante... Hay poca cartelería con datos históricos, no esperes mucha información, como en los museos europeos. El resto tampoco es demasiado interesante, una batería en la zona alta, como la que puedes ver en muchas ciudades.

Lo peor: para llegar a la isla todo son sonrisas, pero para la vuelta, dieron preferencia a los residentes, y tuvimos que esperar una hora y media para el siguiente ferry, y en las explicaciones ( escasas) ya no había sonrisas. Comimos algo en la misma playa, y la comida era cara, y bastante mala. El aseo, que estaba en otro local, era "poco higiénico". El guía, cuando avistó el puerto, comenzó a acelerar el paso, no sabíamos la razón. Pero luego ya entendimos que quería pasar como residente. Seguramente sabía ya que nos quedábamos para el siguiente....no nos dijo ni adiós.

Lo muchísimo peor: el acoso de los vendedores ambulantes. Fue agotador psicológicamente....

title: Spectacular
text: If you're not afraid of crowds and if you like lively colors and people, you really should visit Dantokpa. For a first time it helps to be accompanied by a guide, because not knowing some landmarks, makes it easy to get lost. It really is a pleasure to walk and look around. People are not bothering you to much,  be a bit discrete though about taking pictures, because not everybody likes that. A must for somebody who likes African markets.

title: What a sight! Worth a visit!
text: This is the largest market we have ever seen!  We didn't have enough time to walk around. So we saw the market from the comfort of our car.  We drove from street to street seeing different sections where different types of merchandise are sold.  You can probably find ANYTHING that you need there.  So it's organized in the sense that there are different sections for different things, but not organize within each section...or it's organized in the west-african logic.  We didn't buy anything but we were told that prices are good, especially if you are a good bargainer.

title: Le plus Grand Marché de L'Afrique de l'ouest
text: J'ai travaillé dans le marché Dantokpa et je crois que le marché est très bien organiser. Les rues sont divisés par sujet (ex. électronique, pièces de voitures, vêtements etc.) Il suffit de passer un peu de temps et découvrir toute les facettes de ce marché. C'est en fait le plus grand marché de l'Afrique de l'Ouest au niveau des échanges commerciales et je crois en superficie aussi mais cette information reste a vérifier. SI vous avez quelques heures et bien je vous recommande cette visite, un incontournable de la ville.

title: marché artisanal
text:
Ici on trouve plusieurs boutiques qui proposent des produits artisanaux. 
Les vendeurs ne vendent pas tous la même chose, mais si il y a des similitudes ; et parfois il y a des différences (taille, couleur, matière)
Les produits sont de qualités et sont globalement bien représentatif de ce qu'on peut trouver dans le pays. 
Les prix sont clairement négociable.
Idéal pour trouver des cadeaux à ramener.

title: All shops look the same
text: All shops look the same, all prices are high but it's their joy to negociate a new one. There is a lot of nice and beautifull items.

title: A ne pas rater quand vous visitez COTONOU
text: Le centre artisanal de Cotonou regorge une panoplie d'articles originaux vous permettant de garder un souvenir inoubliable du Bénin: vêtements, sculptures, articles de décoration etc.

title: Bien négocier les prix.
text: C'est le lieu où trouver tous les souvenirs que l'on veut ramener du Bénin. De là à dire que tout est fait local j'ai de gros doutes. On trouve quasiment les mêmes choses dans chaque boutiques. N'hésitez pas à négocier (On peut descendre à 50% du prix de depart). Il faut prendre son temps et beaucoup parler.

title: Principal lieu pour les souvenirs, bijoux et autres cadeaux
text:
Principal lieu de Cotonou pour les achats de cadeaux. Vous y trouverez bijoux, jolis boites, éventails, hamacs, masques et autres statuettes. Impossible de trouver ces produits autre part à Cotonou, à Dantokpa vous trouverez plutôt les tissus et les bijoux en plastique, brillants, de pacotille.
Par contre vous allez vous faire assaillir par les vendeurs, ne vous laissez pas marcher sur les pieds. Les vendeurs vont vous proposer des prix indécents, il faut marchander, marchander et marchander. Par exemple un collier : entre 2000 et 5000 Fr CFA, pas plus (sauf matériaux précieux).

title: Idéal pour les souvenirs
text: Sans grande surprise, le centre artisanal regroupe les artisans locaux produisant le meilleur de l'art béninois et d'ailleurs, notamment ouest africain. Vendeurs pas trop insistants, prix négociables 'évidemment'!! Bref idéal pour faire des bonnes affaires si vous souhaitez repartir avec des souvenirs.

title: Super
text:
Agréable les vendeurs sont sympas et prix correct
Pas de problème de sécurité. On trouve statue, vêtements, cuirs, et même des ateliers ou on assiste à la fabrication de diverses choses.

title: Many options
text: This is the most popular spot to find local arts and crafts.  You need a local with you to negotiate prices.  Never accept the opening price.

title: Boutiques souvenirs
text: Si vous souhaitez ramener des souvenirs, passage incontournable. Vous étés accostés et interpellés de toute part. Bois, métal, tissus, il y en a pour tous les prix et tout se négocie.

title: Déçu
text:
J ai connu ce centre artisanal il y a 20. Il a perdu en authenticité et en charme. Les objets sont  tous les mêmes 
Beaucoup vient de Chine. Dommage

title: Il n'y a pas grand chose d'autre
text:
Si vous fonctionnez à l'européenne allez-y plusieurs fois pour comprendre le jeux. Ayez du temps et de la patience. 
Ce n'est pas pour faire des super affaires mais les vendeurs quand vous êtes blanc commencent  l'enchère plus haute. 
En général vous pouvez divisez par 2 ou 3.
Prenez le temps soyez inventif amusez vous amusez les, la considération sera mutuelle.ce n'est pas un combat. C'est un jeux, les yeux restent rieurs et vifs.
 Si vous arrêtez ils continueront encore longtemps. 
Si vous partez ils vous rattrapent .
Si vous êtes OK et eux aussi c'est une minute festive ! 
Si la proposition n'est pas la bonne la négociation s'arrête, il faut recommencer avec un autre. ....
Quelques exemples :
Personnage "colon" en bois hauteur 1metres "départ 25000fcfa arrivée 10000.
Masque départ 45000 arrivée 12000.
Cela dépend aussi des périodes. Avant les fêtes c'est plus facilement négociable. 
Bon séjour !

title: Best concentration of art, artefacts and touristy gifts
text:
The stall holders are predictably and pleasantly persistent in welcoming you and trying to tempt you into their shop.

The artisanal works on offer range from paintings to masks to trinkets.

The quality varies but it is a relatively calm and spacious environment in which to wander, perusing unhurried.

title: nix brsonderes
text: klein , in 5 minuten erledigt , lauter neue relativ uninteressante sachen , vieles aus holz , taschen ...

title: De l'artisanat pour touristes
text: J'ai fréquenté le centre artisanal durant 15 ans et y ai fait de nombreux achats. Ce centre répond au besoin de souvenirs des touristes à des prix plus élevés que dans le reste du pays. On y trouve cependant 2 produits intéressants : les  animaux (hippo, éléphants, rhino de toutes tailles) laqués en couleur vive et les sculptures /soudures métalliques comme des motos ou des voitures de grande taille qui sont du plus bel effet dans un salon. Les objets en bois et les tissus sont par contre assez moyens.

title: Chouette endroit
text: Bien entendu, vous vous faites alpaguer par les marchands... Mais bon, c'est de bonne guerre. Il y a de très belles pièces, parfois anciennes. Y compris en bronze (si je suis bien renseigné, il semblerait que le Bénin soit le premier pays africain à avoir utilisé ce matériau). Allez y sans craintes, soyez sympa, négociez (en général la moitié du prix doit pouvoir être obtenue). Si vous avez un gros budget, vous pourrez y trouver de véritables pièces rares et anciennes (même si les plus intéressantes se trouvent parfois dans les "greniers" de villages reculés).

title: Beaucoup de choix
text:
L'endrit est sécuritaire on peit y aller seul. Les artiszns et vendeurs sont plutôt gentils et on s'amuse a blaguer et à négocier. 
 Il ya beaucoup de choix et on peit facilement marcher une journée pour le plaisir des yeux.

title: Marché artisanal de Cotonou
text: En ce qui me concerne, j'y suis allée plusieurs fois et j'ai beaucoup marchandé à chaque fois. Par contre là ou j'ai un peu honte c'est d'avoir obtenu une peinture, encore humide, marchandée 5 € mais absolument magnifique! Je ne parviens pas à lire la signature mais il me semble que ça commence par Fouzy...Si  quelqu'un y passe et peut me donner le nom et les coordonnées de l'artiste... Merci d'avance!

title: Objets locaux
text:
C est un endroit incontournable pour celui qui cherche des souvenirs à emporter. 
Il faut négocier les prix absolument et ne pas hésiter à refuser d entrer dans les petites boutiques. Car évidemment chaque commerçant appate le touriste plus ou moins délicatement
Endroit sécurisé

title: Charming Marche
text: Charming collection of stalls and small shops selling souvenirs, clothing and art. The shop owners are easy-going and willing to bargain over a price. Most of the owners are multi-lingual and eager to make a sale. As a veteran of much larger souvenir markets such as Dakar, Ghana or Kumasi. This one hit the mark for it's relaxed atmosphere.

title: Good Collection
text: A place where all the traditional african collections are available. From leather to wooden to pearls. Great place for Interior decorative items, portraits.

title: Art Shoppers Haven
text:
If you follow my reviews,  you'd know I'm a serious art lover.
With the Lekki Art Market, I literally stroll through the stalls for hours! I go from stall to stall looking through the different art pieces. And when I find a special piece, I find another slice of heaven!
If you've never been,  you should! And if you're planning a visit to Lagos, you should add a visit.

Preferably go with the local currency: Naira. Go with cash, not your card.

title: So many shops!
text:
I wanted souvenirs to take back with me and found the Lekki Market on Trip Advisor. 

If I had spent 8 hours there it would not be enough time! Each little Shop contains so many beautifully created object from carvings, clothing, cloth, jewerly, and so many different and well displayed wares.

You need to go several times to fully appreciate the vast volume. 

Do not be afraid to negotiate, a great place to learn if you have never haggled before.

title: Bits and Pieces of Nigerian Artwork
text: Though the road to this market is not exactly smooth, but like the proverbial "narrow gate' it leads you to a market that has a lot of local Adire fabrics for table cloth and mats, traditional  Yoruba fabric Aso - Oke , unimaginable wealth of Nigerian as well as African artwork and painting collection. I went there at the beginning of the year when I needed a gift for an out -going British colleague. Got a painting that depicted the Lagos you must see from the main bridge that connects the mainland to the Island- Little huts built in the Lagoon. It is a must visit when you come to lagos. Better to arrange with your hotel for a tour guide.

title: LOCAL ARTS & CRAFT TYPE OF MARKET
text:
The market is surrounded by slum / shanty town and the unpaved road has huge pot holes with large boulders hidden under the mud and water.....
I personally do not find it worthwhile to make this trip to Lekki Market to see local handicrafts unless one has a serious SUV to navigate the mud track.

title: Good place for ethnic handicrafts and paintings
text: Good place to shop for ethnic handicrafts and paintings at reasonable prices. Lots of tiny shops with variety of wooden artifacts, paintings and artificial jewelry. Only buy precious stones if you are an expert and can differentiate real from fake. Feel free to negotiate hard and strike a reasonable bargain, sometimes 50% or more. Avoid going there on a rainy day. Best time is after and before office rush hours. Sunday the market is closed though some shops are still open. Good for couples or grown ups for young kids nothing much interesting. A must visit even if you don't want to shop!

title: Pamiątki ok ale miejsce słabe
text: Ten rynek jest w innym miejscu niż pokazuje Tripadvisor, szukajcie na Google prawidłowego położenia.Biali lepiej niech sami się tam nie wybierają tylko z przewodnikiem i nie chodzić wieczorową porą bo okolica jest niebezpieczna. 2 duże obrazy za 50$ cena do zaakceptowania.

title: It's a market
text:
I don't know what to tell you, it's a market. If you are a foreigner it's advisable to go with a trusted local, be prepared to "price" (haggle) everything.

A good tip is to divide whatever price they give you by four or five and work your way to a happy medium and be prepared to walk away if the amount is still too high.

title: Foreigner Rip off
text: You get much better value visiting markets in other Nigerian states to purchase the local handicraft, some at one fifth of the costs in this market and without even much bargaining. While i understand there are transport costs involved to bring items to Lagos to sell, but the prices quoted were ridiculously high. Surprisingly even though we walked off after some negotiations, they did not call us back.  Secondly, the layout was confusing and there was poor ventilation.

title: Heaven for shoppers
text:
Availability of the beautiful Nigerian cultural artifacts at affordable prices.
Pearl jewellery awesome and most importantly original.

title: BEAUTIFUL AND COLORFUL MARKET!
text: The Lekki Craft Market is an open air African market, In which almost everything you need is available for sale; from furniture to food, from paintings to table cloths and CD’s; the list goes on. This market will engage all of your senses and emotions; as such one should come prepared to buy several items from this market. The walkways are flanked on either side by stalls laden with beautiful jewelry made from glass countries such as Ghana and Senegal, there are intricate wood and stone carvings with exquisite detail, some carry rare and old bottles used for oil and alcohol, some which date as far back as the 1930’s and 40’s you will find antique telephones, record players and typewriters, there are traditional Nigerian woven fabrics (aso oke) and batik pieces for sale, leather goods abound, with some goods made from alligator or snake skin, there are Benin bronze works, wood carvings, drums and masks and still, the list goes on. There are great bargains to be had and take time to engage your vendor about the origin of his pieces.

title: cool market
text: you will get the exact thing you want in good quality, great way of appreciating customers who patronize, its such a wonderful market you will like to go there all the time

title: Myriad of traditional treasures
text: Great to go and experience a well established local Lekki market. Shop for leather sandals, jewelry, artworks, iron and wood sculptures and even large pieces of furniture. The traditional glass beadworks are exceptional and well worth investing in. Haggle hard, but with good humour and you'll come away with great bargains. Good for good quality herbs and vegetables that may not be in the main food shops, and popular with many expatriate communities. Watch out for flooding in rainy season or take your wellies.

title: Good place for African curios
text: Went here with some work colleagues. Great little place for African souvenirs and seems safe to walk around. All the usual stuff and some decent art. Very cheap prices by European standards though you will need to bargain, even if the starting prices are still cheap! Be warned though, the roads leading up to it are awful.

title: Great Nigerian mementos
text: Lekki market is great for buying Nigerian arts & crafts and jewelry. The road leading to it (off the highway) is rough though. I understand it's currently being fixed. Feel free to haggle and never accept the first price given to you.

title: Only place to buy arts and crafts in Lagos
text: I have been coming to this market for years. It has a huge selection of arts and crafts, as well as other small shops and services.  Its hidden away from the road and you need to find a driver who knows how to find it.  If you bargain well, the prices can be very reasonable.

title: Great value for money
text:
This is an arts and crafts market. Good for shopping for souvenirs, great and small.

There is a huge variety of African (not necessarily Nigerian) articles that you can buy. From as little as 25cents (0.25USD) for key rings, upwards.

I always get a receipt/invoice for payments, and I suggest you do same if you are taking your purchase out of Nigeria.

For some articles that are copies of artefacts, you may need to process them with the National Museum, to get a certificate for customs purposes. Normally for small items or common, there will be no issues.

title: Alladin's cave
text: Tucked away off the expressway is a maze of shops selling everything you could possibly want from some really impressive original art work through 'pirate' DVDs to hand woven rush table mats, pottery, bangles and beads as well as wooden figures and some really old artefacts - better than you can find in the museum! If you enjoy bartering then this is the place for you. Beware of opportunists but most of the traders are friendly and very entertaining.

title: Hidden Treasures
text:
We have been going to the market for the last 10 years and it has always been a pleasure.
Suggest you spend time in the shops selling masks and curios. ...
Ask the shopkeepers about the history and you will be surprised ... 
Once done head to the beach....

title: African Art, Coral & Pearls
text: Place is 9 KM from Victoria Island. Local market with amazing artworks, souvenirs, paintings, wood carvings, masks, pearls, Corals, wall hangings, and many more. Park inside the allocated parking space and pay N200. Always go with a driver and frined who knows Lekki market. You have to bargain a lot...

title: Comprendre...
text:
Monument localement critiqué, pour sa construction, son sens et son coût, mais qui apporte une certaine vision des ambitions du pays.
Et Dakar manquant cruellement de monuments, le site en devient incontournable.
Mérite donc largement la visite complète jusqu'au sommet.

placeInfo.name: Le Monument de la Renaissance Africaine
placeInfo.address: Rte de la Corniche Ouest, Dakar Senegal

title: Découverte
text: Après avoir été sur l'île de Goree nous avons fait le tour de Dakar par la corniche et nous nous sommes arrêtés à la statue. C'est impressionnant. Belle réalisation. Des escaliers nous conduisent au pied de cette gigantesque statue. On peut même monter à l'intérieur mais il y avait la queue nous ne l'avons pas faite.

placeInfo.name: Le Monument de la Renaissance Africaine
placeInfo.address: Rte de la Corniche Ouest, Dakar Senegal

title: Molto imponente
text: Premetto che Dakar come città non offre niente di interessante a parte questo grande monumento che é un pò il loro simbolo. Per via del volo siamo riusciti a vederlo sia di notte per cui illuminato che di giorno ma, dall'alto ti accorgi che il panorama di interessante non offre nulla.

placeInfo.name: Le Monument de la Renaissance Africaine
placeInfo.address: Rte de la Corniche Ouest, Dakar Senegal

title: Schöner Blick von oben
text: Das monumentale Denkmal erdrückt die Zuschauer, ein Nachdenken über Afrikas Renaissance wird dadurch gerade nicht ermöglicht. Die vielen Stufen aufwärts sind nur für körperlich fitte Personen

placeInfo.name: Le Monument de la Renaissance Africaine
placeInfo.address: Rte de la Corniche Ouest, Dakar Senegal

title: Imposing Statue
text: We drove here with our guide as part of our city tour.  It’s quite an impressive statue, set on an extinct volcano overlooking the city.

placeInfo.name: Le Monument de la Renaissance Africaine
placeInfo.address: Rte de la Corniche Ouest, Dakar Senegal

title: Spectacular
text: It's a spectacular sight that dominates the area around Les Almedies. The admission price includes the guided tour. The views from the statues of Dakar are truly amazing. It was wonderful to see a recognition of both Rosa Parks and the Reverend Jesse Jackson.

placeInfo.name: Le Monument de la Renaissance Africaine
placeInfo.address: Rte de la Corniche Ouest, Dakar Senegal

title: Worth a stop
text: Within walking distance from mosque of the Divinity , it is worth stopping by to enjoy a good view of the city and to take some photos/selfies.

placeInfo.name: Le Monument de la Renaissance Africaine
placeInfo.address: Rte de la Corniche Ouest, Dakar Senegal

title: Gigantesque
text: Très imposante statue, nombreuses marches à gravir pour avoir une magnifique vue de Dakar. À faire un dimanche matin pour être tranquille

placeInfo.name: Le Monument de la Renaissance Africaine
placeInfo.address: Rte de la Corniche Ouest, Dakar Senegal

title: The monument symbolizes the rebirth of Africa.
text:
Africa's highest statue, it was unveiled in 2010 to commemorate Senegal's 50 years of independence from France. At 49m in height, it is taller than New York City's Statue of Liberty and Rio de Janeiro's Christ the Redeemer.
The monument symbolizes the rebirth of Africa.

placeInfo.name: Le Monument de la Renaissance Africaine
placeInfo.address: Rte de la Corniche Ouest, Dakar Senegal

title: Great View
text: Great experience, nice visit quite cultural and the sight seeing from the top floor is something ! If there is a good weather, you can see all of the Cape Verde peninsula @360° !

placeInfo.name: Le Monument de la Renaissance Africaine
placeInfo.address: Rte de la Corniche Ouest, Dakar Senegal

title: Travel guru
text: Fun place to take pictures of the city and ocean, good exercise to walk up the steps, some shops and also a restaurant at top, statue isbopen to acees the top for a fee nut not worth it. Some vehicles allowed to the top . Nothing else to do here. Sometimes the place has events in the evenings. Check local schedule. Best to reach by walking or taxi.

placeInfo.name: Le Monument de la Renaissance Africaine
placeInfo.address: Rte de la Corniche Ouest, Dakar Senegal

title: Meh
text: You can see it from driving past it. Not worth the time. It’s crowded and you can’t see much up close.

placeInfo.name: Le Monument de la Renaissance Africaine
placeInfo.address: Rte de la Corniche Ouest, Dakar Senegal

title: Very impressive size and design!
text: It was nice and quiet for a Saturday. From the top you get different view of the ocean , part of the city and the big military airport. Just watch out on the taxis. If you are going from your hotel with taxi make a deal with him to wait for you and take you back or anywhere else. If you are a tourist taxis will give you a price and then will change it at the destination. It happened to us.  Enjoy the visit and climbing up the stairs that are 99 of them.

placeInfo.name: Le Monument de la Renaissance Africaine
placeInfo.address: Rte de la Corniche Ouest, Dakar Senegal

title: you can see it from everywhere
text:
Even if you don't go up the hill, you can see it from far away, due to its position and the fact that Dakar is almost everywhere flat.

A must-see, not for its beauty, more as a symbol and for the history and the debate  about its construcion.

Not worth visiting inside.

placeInfo.name: Le Monument de la Renaissance Africaine
placeInfo.address: Rte de la Corniche Ouest, Dakar Senegal

title: Colossale
text: Questo monumento bronzeo è colossale, misura 49 metri ed è posto su una collina che ne misura altri 100, pertanto è visibile anche da lontano. Con un ascensore a pagamento si sale fino al cappello della figura maschile della statua, dove c'è una sala con delle finestre panoramiche. La sera questa sala è illuminata e da lontanto fa un effetto carino.

placeInfo.name: Le Monument de la Renaissance Africaine
placeInfo.address: Rte de la Corniche Ouest, Dakar Senegal

title: A voir de l’extérieur
text:
Après avoir monté les 198 marches, il n’est pas indispensable de visiter l’intérieur du monument. Il est dommage que la visite intérieure des 3 étages ne soit pas libre, ce qui gâche un peu le plaisir.
Prix de la visite complète (3 étages + le 15ème qui correspond à la tête): 6 500F CFA pour les non résidents.

placeInfo.name: Le Monument de la Renaissance Africaine
placeInfo.address: Rte de la Corniche Ouest, Dakar Senegal

title: Pour la vue...
text: Point positif : la vue sur Dakar. Après, ce monument construit par des nord-coréens est sans grand intérêt. Inauguré en 2010, il commence déjà à se dégrader faute d'entretien. Allez-y, montez les marches, restez 10 minutes, et ça suffira.

placeInfo.name: Le Monument de la Renaissance Africaine
placeInfo.address: Rte de la Corniche Ouest, Dakar Senegal

title: Gigantesque !!!!
text:
Quel monument gigantesque dédié à la renaissance africaine !!!!
Lieu de passage obligatoire à Dakar !!!

placeInfo.name: Le Monument de la Renaissance Africaine
placeInfo.address: Rte de la Corniche Ouest, Dakar Senegal

title: Very impressive
text: Great attraction to see. If short on time, viewing from the car is fine. I didn't go to the top in the escalator - seemed a bit costly at 10 euros.

placeInfo.name: Le Monument de la Renaissance Africaine
placeInfo.address: Rte de la Corniche Ouest, Dakar Senegal

title: Impressive Monument
text:
We visited this monument as part of day tour by Nouvelles Frontieres.  This bronze monument is 49 meters tall and cost $27 million USD.  It was constructed by a North Korea.  It commemorates the 50th anniversary of Senegal's Independence from France.

This monument has been criticised by the locals for the amount of money that was spent on it as well as the immodesty of the family as Senegal is a Muslim state.

I found the monument is very impressive when seen in it's place.

placeInfo.name: Le Monument de la Renaissance Africaine
placeInfo.address: Rte de la Corniche Ouest, Dakar Senegal

title: Ville de Porto-Novo
text:
Très bon ville pour avoir négliger pendant tant d'année (capitale du Bénin).
Sans l'union des filles et fils cette ville ne changera pas.

title: One hour is enough!
text:
A poorly maintained collections of dubious quality. The guide did her best to make it sound interesting. There are old Voodou masks, some relics from the Dan-Abomey kingdom. But pretty disappointing for the national museum in the capital city. In the basement there is an exhibition of callabash (excuse the yawn).
And photos inside the museum are not allowed!!!

title: Gèlèdè masques and dance
text: A rather unknown museum, but worth visiting, if you like to know more about the culture and history of Benin. The museum has different Gèlèdè masques, which was for me interesting to see and to hear the story about it, because we visited that before. The guide can tell you a lot. Also look at the other items the museum has.

title: Een stukje historie Benin
text: In Porto Novo bevindt zich het museum waar je meer te weten kan komen over het land en historie van Benin, de vele koninkrijkjes die officieel niet meer bestaan maar soms kom je nog een koning met kroon tegen die in de loby van het hotel ligt te slapen, en de slaven historie met de trieste verhalen van transport naar verre landen en verhalen van slaven die teruggekomen zijn met hun "rijkdom".  Het museum ligt in het centrum echter wat lastig te vinden vraag het aan een lokaal of aan je chauffeur. Een bezoekje aan de markt levert ook mooie plaatjes op "een andere wereld" en zeker de moeite waard!!

title: À ne pas manquer !
text: Musée vraiment intéressant et incontournable pour qui veut toucher un peu à la diversité ethnique et culturelle du Bénin. Un collection remarquable de masques mais aussi des objets caractéristiques liés aux croyances des diverses population du pays. Comme souvent en Afrique le manque de moyens ne garantit pas une préservation et une présentation optimales des objets exposés. Le guide est intéressant. Un artisanat de tissage notamment est présenté en parallèle.

title: Ne pas manquer
text: Vaut surtout pour la collection de masques Gélélé et les commentaires qui sont une bonne introduction à ce que l'on voit tout au long du voyage. J'espère que vous aurez comme nous la chance de faire la visite guidés par Emilienne.

title: Manque de moyens
text: Les musées manquent malheureusement de moyens en Afrique... et je suis toujours un peu déçue ... les pièces ne sont pas très bien entretenues. En revanche, le guide était très bien.

title: It's ok
text: The most interesting part was looking at the map with the different ethnic/tribal groups and having some Q & A with the guide.  For the rest of the museum, we would have preferred to walk around ourselves, see the exhibits and read the signs.  What the museum guide was saying seems to differ from the signs.

title: de moeite waard
text: Een interessant museum om iets over de etnische groeperingen van Benin te weten te komen.

title: A must  go
text: see how a  society lived  and worshipped  just  a  bit over a  century  ago. Grandchildren  who  rememebred  gradndparents who  knew these rulers -  marvel  of  fetishes,  gods   ,  ancestor  worship  and  abject  cruelty  to enemies

title: A  Go See if  in Benin
text: If in the area  one must  go visit this   famous  palace.  Read up on this,  ( I arranged  to  go with an anthropoligst  who  explained    quite  a  bit  about a  society  that  was around  relatively  recently. See the  mediation room  built  with blood  of  41  slaves. It  would be great if  it vwas  maintained   decently and explained  in much  more  detail.There wasnta  soul  there when I visited, went  away marveling .

title: Must visit
text: We visited the Royal Palaces of Abomey as part of a study abroad program in college.  I believe you experience more if you are with a professor or guide as we were.  Very interesting history and cultural experience.  The red sand was amazing.

title: Throne atop Skulls
text: All reviews here are very good. Its a few hours drive up from the coast. A MUST SEE if you are in country.  The Palace has one very unique item.  The Throne. it sits on each leg upon 4 human skulls.  Also visit voodoo Dr. In town.

title: Royal palace and historical atrocitoes
text:
Worthwhile to visit. Do hire a personalia guide. Interesting items referring to voodoo. Benin is the birthplace of voodoo.
The palace had many symbols from formeren Kings. After the death of the old one, a new king extended the palace.
Every king had many wives. After his death, 10-15 wives wereld selected, drugged and forever locked up in a death chamber....

title: Terrific, evocative tour!
text: Great tour of the palaces of two of the kings of the former Kingdom of Dahomey. Lots of artifacts (some original, some copies of originals housed in the Musee de quai Branly in Paris) to help created a sense of life and society during the 300 year expanse of the Kingdom. A must-see if you are touring Benin!

title: Interessante para conhecer a historia do Benin
text: Fizemos a visita com uma guia do museu, que nos deu varias informações interessantes sobre a historia do reino do Dahome e dos reis aos quais os palácios pertenciam. Infelizmente o museu não foi organizado pra visitas sem guia, as explicações escritas não são muito completas.

title: old memory
text: it's all my personal opinion. this old palace that reminds you of a past splendour now it's only an empty space with nothing to show. not worth a visit

title: nothing special
text: it's all my personal opinion but this oldpalace that reminds you of a past splendour now it's only an empty space with nothing to show. not worth a visit

title: Great palace.. but is it worth the trip?
text: Dahomey empire has very interesting characteristics and history, which even made someone who doesn't like museums like me to pay attention to its artefacts and surroundings. But the fact that you're not allowed to take pictures inside is little bit too harsh, and since this is about only attraction you will see in Abomey, and considering it takes such long time to get to Abomey from usual big cities down south, I don't know if it's worth the trip. If you're inevitably passing by the region, or if you're really interested in histories, then sure it's good to go. But I wouldn't say it's a must visit site if you have limited time in Benin. The town itself is interesting in many ways, it's just not that photogenic except for the old symbols on the palaces of Dahomey.

title: Pas d'un grand intérêt et accueil détestable
text:
Nous avons visité le palais royal d'Abomey en janvier 2014. Bon d'abord il faut savoir, mais on s'en doutait, que ces batiment n'ont de "palais royaux" que le nom. Vous n'y verrez que des batiment de terre, quelques "tombes royales" et quelques objets de la vie quotidienne que vous aurez déjà vus dans d'autres musées, voir encore mieux dans les villages locaux.

L'accueil dans ce lieu a été en ce qui nous concerne vraiment détestable : il nous a fallu attendre un bout de temps que quelqu'un vienne, qui n'avait visiblement pas envie de faire de visite. Ma visite a été expédiée en quelques 30 minutes (remarquez plus, pourquoi faire ?) et à noter pour nos amis photographes : il est rigoureusement interdit de prendre des photos à l'intérieur comme à l'extérieur !!! Pour des raisons de respect bien entendu sachant que des cartes postales sont en vente à la sortie....

Bref, visite sans grand intérêt, pas très agréable. Il y a beaucoup d'autres endroits à voir au Bénin, bien plus agréables. C'est en ce qui nous concerne le seul endroit où nous n'avons pas eu le sentiment d'être bienvenus dans ce magnifique pays qu'est le Bénin. passez votre chemin !

title: Visita senza foto
text:
Il sito è patrimonio dell'umanità e non capisco perché non si possano fotografare neppure gli esterni degli edifici. Per il resto un ampio palazzo ricco di storia. La guida illustra in francese la storia e i singoli reperti, secondo me messi un po' a caso, in stanze buie illuminate solo dalla luce delle finestre.
Vale comunque una visita

title: Great grounds, excellent tour
text: Great grounds and museum! Guide w/very good English.  Easy to imagine life as it must have been.  Not many artifacts left; mostly copies of originals now elsewhere.

title: Étape incoutournable d'un voyage au Bénin !
text: L'histoire du Sud du Bénin tourne autour du roi Béhanzin, héros national qui a tenu tête aux colons français. Abomey est le siège de la lignée de ce roi glorieux et de tous ses prédécesseurs. L'ensemble des palais royaux d'Abomey et son musée, sont inscrits au patrimoine mondial de l'Unesco depuis 1985. Plusieurs palais dans un même ensemble permettent de connaître les coutumes des sujets du royaume du Dahomey, de découvrir de nombreuses salles, cours et tombeaux, avec des collections de trônes royaux et de récades (sceptres royaux) en bois sculpté. La visite sous la conduite d'un guide -indispensable- est vraiment passionnante pour comprendre l'histoire longue du pays avant qu'il ne devienne à la fin du XIXème siècle une colonie française. Autour du palais une cité des artisans présente également un grand intérêt avec en particulier des tisserands.

title: Interesting History to Learn
text: The palaces (and other historical sites and museums) were a fascinating insight into the history of the area and of the slave trade.  And if you visit enough different sites around the country, you start piecing things together and understanding better at each stop.

title: Palais à la mode béninoise
text: Plongez-vous dans l'histoire du royaume d'Abomey. Les bâtiments sont de construction traditionnelle : salles de réception, tombeaux, lieux de culte, les collections sont intéressantes, mais ne vous attendez pas à un palais des mille et une nuits. Village artisanal avec des tissus et objets intéressants.

title: kinda interesting...
text:
We are not too much into museums and historical stuff but with Benin having not too many "proper" sightseeings we visited the palaces.
you need a bit of the imagination to get the right impression of the scale of the things that used to happen over there because the only thing you really is a bunch of clay huts - and that is mostly is. the rest your imagination should work out - then why not to watch National Geographic? :)

title: Site historique
text: Très bien documenté ; visite guidée passionnante. Belle collection d'objets, certains étant hélas au Musée du Quai Branly de Paris.

title: Not worth the road trip to get there
text:
The palace tour takes about an hour and is quite interesting. The history of the kings from past to present is included and the exhibits are good and fully show the cruel history of slavery and human sacrifice.   The sight is a Unesco Heritage site but you are not allowed to take photos inside which really annoys me personally. The craft market inside the gate is the best I have seen in Togo and Benin combined.  That said, the road to get here is a disgrace and we have been on some awful roads in this part of world.  It took 5.5 hours to get from Cotonou and the distance is approx 85 miles.

Also the hotels in this area are very low quality.   It is impossible to just go for the day and visit the site so my advice is to wait until Unesco can get the road fixed before you consider going.

title: Brutal!
text:
So if you are lucky enough to have found yourself in Benin, The Royal Palace of Abomey is definitely worth the visit.  This complex of historical palaces traces the history of the Dahomey empire, ancient ancestors of Danzig (little known fact).  The walls of this place are painted in blood and lined with animal bones. There is a mural depicting a wide variety of punishments and tortures, my personal favorite being the clay flute which was shoved up "somebody's bum", as it was translated to us.  Oh, and yeah, there is a THRONE OF SKULLS.  An actual throne, resting on a bed of skulls. Metal.
Also, FYI, it is a very short distance from the taxi park to the museum, probably even walkable, so don't let zemijohns overcharge for the trip.

title: Glad I went, but not much to see
text: Since I live in Accra, this was a good visit to learn more about recent history, but if you’re here for a short time, this place is probably not worth the effort and time.

title: ンクルマ霊廟訪問
text:
出張先で1日空いたオフ日に同僚と訪問、併設のとても小さな展示室にはンクルマ元大統領の所縁の品々が置いてあり、アフリカファンや、第三世界の言葉が流行ったのを知っている世代にはとても魅力的な内容です。
特に、ンクルマさんが2度目に埋葬された時に使われた金属製の棺や、スタインウェイのピアノ2台、学生時代に大学寮で使用したベッド、中国指導者(毛沢東や周恩来)やエジプトから迎えた夫人&家族との写真、40冊に及ぶと言われる著作(和訳本も数冊)が並んでおり、とても興味深いアイテムが数点置いてありました。
若い館員は何でもンクルマに関する質問に即座に答えてくれる等、外観では判断出来��いような価値を感じました。
霊廟敷地にある、旧式のベンツがポツンとショーケース内に別展示されており、説明が全く無いのが不思議でした。

title: A great sense of history
text: This is easy to reach in the centre of Accra and there is plenty of parking in the carpark next door. Like much of Accra and Ghana the gardens that surround the Mausoleum need some attention. Unfortunately when we visited the large fountain in front of the Mausoleum was not working. The small museum behind the Mausoleum is worth visiting and gives you an overview of Ghana's short history post Independence. It is a real shame that the locals have constructed a cheap stand in front of the great man's statue so you can take cheesy photographs in front of the main statue. Shame on the powers that control the Mausoleum.

title: Must see in Accra
text:
Beautiful and historical place. Makes you connect with the legendary Kwame Nkrumah.
Also conveniently located in the heart of Accra.

title: Drive round Ghana
text: It was really nice seeing this memorial park. I felt really proud being an African. I loved the pictures on the wall, where I got to see him with all those famous people. He made Africa proud. Lovely experience.

title: Sehenswürdigkeiten in Accra
text: Kann man sich anschauen!!! Letztlich von der Architektur her lieblos und klotzig hingebaut. Eintritt wird hier nicht fällig und in kürzester Zeit ist es erledigt!!!

title: Gorashers
text: Great monument Not too expensive to enter But around you What's your round you for robbers  And beggars and people trying to sell you things

title: A must in Accra - the memorial of the father of independent Ghana
text:
This is a relatively peaceful and impressive site to visit.  We went on a Sunday and it was very quiet indeed.  Very nice small gardens with a very impressive memorial structure under which is the tomb of Kwame Nkrumah, surrounded by lovely small bridges over a most style water feature.  The fountains and statues with fountain horns in the other moat style ponds were not working as it is under repair we were told.

The very nice air conditioned museum is interesting too, if somewhat understated.  Lots of pictures telling the story as well as some clothing and furniture but not made as much of as any of it could have been. It doesn't take a long while to walk around and reading the descriptions is worth it.

title: Parte del tour de Accra
text: Deja mucho que desear. Poca información de lo que logró o no logró este primer jefe de estado. Mucho concreto para mi gusto. Las fuentes estaban en mantenimiento

title: Parc riche en histoire
text: Le ghana pays incoutournable de l'histoire de la traite négrière possède plusieurs espaces tel que celui ci riche en histoire.

title: Great History
text: Great history and the tour is definitely worth it. Kwame Nkrumah was a great man indeed!m Excellent photo opportunities!

title: Excellent
text:
A very informative tour. Make sure you hook a guide when you arrive so you can learn all there is to know.

A good educational, fun day out.

title: Inspiring site giving much food for thought
text: The mausoleum includes pictures, books and documents of Nkruma and our group was able to receive a guide who was knowledgeable. His talk was so inspiring, I purchased a book on Nkruma in the bookshop and have been reading it since.

title: Good place of history
text:
The mortal remains of Ghana's first President, Osagyefo Dr. Kwame Nkrumah lies by his wife Fathia in a mausoleum at this park in Accra. It is the final resting place for Nkrumah who died and was buried in Konakry, Guinea and then in his hometown at Nkroful in western Ghana before being exhumed and laid at the park in Accra dedicated to him. 

The Kwame Nkrumah Memorial when in good shape is a very beautiful place to visit with the family. The lush green park and the fountains create a beautiful ambiance to hangout. It is also a place to learn a lot about the history of Ghana through Nkrumah at the museum that adjoins the park. 

A good place to visit when you are in Ghana.

title: Vale a pena para conhecer um pouco da história do país
text:
O memorial é interessante, e a visita vale a pena para conhecer um pouco da vida do ex-presidente, importante lider para o país e para a África. O museu tem potencial, mas infelizmente está mal cuidado, e a 'exposição' acaba parecendo um depósito. Os jardins trazem um grupo de estátuas/fontes muito bacana, representado diferentes tipos de homens africanos, e no dia em que fomos havia um pavão tranquilamente passeando pelos arredores.
Minha visita ocorreu a um ano, em janeiro/2018.

title: Interessante Gedenkstätte für eine großen Ghanaer
text:
Gleich am ersten Tag unserer Ghana-Rundreise haben wir die Gedenkstätte des für Ghana wichtigsten Politikers der Neuzeit besucht.
Sehr schön gestaltete Anlage mit informativem Museum.
Sollte man sich als aufgeschlossener Landesbesucher unbedingt ansehen.
