Sollte man sich als aufgeschlossener Landesbesucher unbedingt ansehen.

title: Pleasant enough
text: Nice gardens to walk through with an impressive monument to Ghana's first prime minister and president. It was rather busy on the day we arrived with lots of school children. If you're in the area, a visit is recommended. It's something different.

title: Great to see OUR greats resting place
text: Went to see the Big man and learn more about his life! My daughter and I loved the memorial park and would return to soak up the rays and meditate on the fight some of our ancestors encountered to ensure we have better lives today. GREAT FOR ALL THE FAMILY TO VISIT. beautiful architecture and grounds. OUR TRIP WAS DECEMBER 2017

title: History lesson
text: A well spent afternoon delving into history. Our guide was able to answer most of our questions. Because of what Dr.Nkrumah means to Ghana I expected to see more and expected the items to be in better display. Many of the items were on loan from his first child, Dr. Francis Nkrumah. I am assuming that I would see more at the National Museum, however, that was closed during he time I was in Accra. There were not many visitors so we were able to peruse inside for as long as we wished, then the guide gave us a tour of the grounds.

title: Imperdible
text: Una visita obligada par toda persona que desee conocer más de la artesanía del país.  Como es costumbre,  se debe negociar para poder llevar presentes a toda la familia.

title: shopping touristique
text: Un endroit clef de cotonou pour tous voyageurs voulant repartir chez eux avec un souvenir du Bénin, vous trouverez de tout en partant d'objet de déco jusqu'au bijou

title: Correct sans plus
text: Plusieurs articles ne sont pas originaux , car fait de la même façon. Cependant, il y a aussi de bons artisans.  Il faut négocier tres fort , car il n'y a que les touristes qui vont la-bas.

title: Typical artists market
text: The same 'tipical' artisanal objets d'art as found in other westafrican towns and cities. Everyone wants to get you into your shop and you keep trying to walk away. Of course we ended up buying stuff anyway, so if you still need a souvenir and have some spare time on your hands...

title: pezzi interessanti
text:
la maggior parte dei "negozi" è per "turisti" ma ci sono alcuni che hanno dei pezzi pregevoli, quello che conosco da anni è il negozio di valentine dove ho acquistato sia dei bronzi,  notevoli ed originali a detta di amico esperto, e delle belle "porte di granaio".
certamente si trovano gli stessi articoli in altre parti del benin ma se si ha occhio e capacità di trattare si possona fare buoni affari anche qui.

title: Good for presents
text: Very good place to buy souvenirs from Benin...just be careful, if you are white, they will charge you double...its better to visit with somebody local !!! I bought a lot of stuff for my family and friends!!!

title: Un aperçu de l'artisanat du Bénin
text: De beaux articles ; des vendeurs sympas ; apprêtez vous à négocier serré si vous souhaitez faire des affaires ; localisation très pratique, c'est en plein centre

title: viaje a benin
text: el ultimo dia en benin fuimos a este mercado "artesanal",la verdad que lo que yo vi es solo para turistas y los dependientes como en todos los mercados de este tipo un poco pesados,pero para algun regalo de iultima hora se puede ir.

title: coin sympa avec artisanat de qualité
text: Si vous cherchez des souvenirs de qualité, des tissus, des statues, des sacs en tissus coloré, des trousses de toilettes, des sacs à dos pour écolier, des colliers et toutes les babioles possibles et imaginables.

title: Artisanal souvenirs
text: I always visit artisanal centre when in Benin. They used to have a nice restaurant there, but it is closed now. Most of the sellers speak English - and can be little pushy at the time, but hey, that's their style of selling. You can feast your eyes on pretty much everything from paintings, statues, masks, bags, clothing, hammocks & table settings majority made here. You can watch the artists at work And have things specifically made for you - if you have time to wait. We brought a bunch of old silver has had some unique jewellery made. A must see place.

title: Loads of local crafts
text: An interesting variety of crafts and gifts. Mostly locally made. They can be really pushy, but appreciate you bargaining. There's a bar at the entrance with a lovely garden.

title: To much of the same crafts
text:
If just visiting Cotonou and have some free time this market is worthy of a hour or two of your time.  Many of the shops have the same merchandise, but there are a couple that have unique handcrafted items of good quality.  
This is definitely a dream of a place if one likes to barter, so start low and meet below the middle.
First time I visited was during the week and some of the shops weren't open, so I returned on Saturday.  The shops that weren't open the first time was where I found the items I was looking for.

title: Very Expensive
text: After leaving the rowdy Marché Dantokpa, I went to the Artisanal Centre. I collect fridge magnets and was hoping to find at reasonable prices, as these are like the cheapest souvenirs in the world. I found the magnets rather expensive, the paintings were also expensive. I ended up buying only Benin carved key holders for my colleagues and a very lovely sculpted-beaded lady with her child on her back.

title: A lot of variety, but not attactively displayed
text: Hot and dusty, with considerable hype from the sellers (although we have suffered worse hassle elsewhere).  If there are any hidden gems among all the merchandise offered, we didn't find any to our taste. We felt the items were mostly of mediocre quality.  Since we were going to do another 12 days in West Africa, we didn't bother to look for a better place in Cotonou for handicrafts/souvenirs.

title: A voir mais pas indispensable
text: Ce centre artisanal vous permettra de trouver des objets sympa mais que l'on trouve partout en Afrique lorsqu'on voyage un peu. Attention à bien négocier : ne pas payer plus de 50% du prix demandé.

title: Oppressant
text: La pression que vous mette les vendeurs dès votre arrivée est insupportable !! Nous avons fuit sans rien acheter tellement l'ambiance était oppressante. De plus je ne suis pas sure qu'il y ait vraiment un artiste digne de ce nom. Je déconseille vivement.

title: Bien sans plus
text: On y trouve toutes les africaneries habituelles, et on est un peu harcelés par les commerçants qui finalement ont quasiment tous la même chose. La négociation s'impose mais reste difficile.

title: Médiocre car plus centre commercial de l'artisanat que centre artisanal
text: Beaucoup de boutiques et de marchandises. Mais peu d'artisans en fait. C'est plus du commerce "d'artisanat" que de l'artisanat pur qui pourtant existe à Cotonou. Avec beaucoup de marchandises que l'on trouve partout ailleurs. Rares sont les boutiques qui proposent des produits originaux et originaux. Et puis, la pénibilité trop classique de ces endroits ainsi dédiés du fait de l'approche et du harcèlement stupides de certains commerçants d'origine nigérienne ou sénégalaise lesquels visent systématiquement à escroquer le client en abusant des prix. Oui, bien sûr "c'est l'Afrique" mais faut-il rester vraiment dans ces méthodes qui finissent par être lassantes et décourageantes.

title: Nice.
text: A collection of small shops with bargaining on objets d'art. I went on a Sunday morning, and therefore was not surrounded when I exited the taxi.

title: Agreable
text: Très beau centre. Certaines boutiques exagèrent sur le prix mais d'autres sont tout à fait corrects. Nous avons acheté des bracelets moins chers qu'au marché de notre quartier. Le tout est de regrouper ses achats dans une boutique et négocier au global. Mention spéciale aux 2 dames qui tiennent une boutique à l'entrée à droite. Les prix de dēpart sont corrects et au final on arrive à des prix où tout le monde est satisfait. Elles ont compris ce qu'est le commerce.

title: Sensational visit
text:
This is must be one of the most stunning places to visit in Africa. A 20 ferry ride from Dakar and you are in another world, transported to the Mediterranean.

Beautiful buildings with stunning narrow passageways and such an interesting history. The real history may not be the the official history but the sentiment is still correct.

Easy to spend most of the day here but you should arrive early.

title: Île de Gorée : à ne pas rater
text: Superbe journée sur l’île de Gorée avec Adama qui nous fait découvrir avec un guide expérimenté l’histoire des esclaves. Cela restera un moment fort de notre séjour. Adama a été très professionnel et nous le recommandons pour vos visites. N’hésitez pas à le contacter par whatsapp au +221 77 364 99 65

title: Mélange fascinant de passé et de présent
text:
Explorer l'île de Gorée est bien plus qu'une simple visite touristique ; c'est une immersion profonde dans l'histoire et les émotions. Traverser ses ruelles pittoresques bordées de maisons colorées, chargées d'histoires des différentes occupations européennes, nous transporte dans un voyage à travers le temps.

La Maison des Esclaves, bien que controversée quant à son utilisation historique précise, reste un lieu de mémoire incontournable. Ses couloirs chargés d'histoire invitent à une réflexion profonde sur les horreurs du passé et sur la condition humaine. La visite atteint son point culminant avec la porte du non-retour, symbolisant le départ tragique des captifs vers les Amériques.

Gorée offre également des moments de quiétude sur ses plages de sable fin et dans ses ruelles colorées, où l'art et la culture s'entremêlent. Le plateau du Castel, garni de fortifications, offre une vue imprenable sur l'île et ses environs, ajoutant une dimension supplémentaire à cette expérience.

Le mémorial Al Mahdi témoigne de l'histoire douloureuse de la traite des esclaves, rappelant aux visiteurs les souffrances endurées par le peuple africain. Autour du mémorial, des boutiques artisanales ajoutent une atmosphère particulière à l'endroit.

En déambulant dans les rues étroites de Gorée, on croise d'autres bâtiments emblématiques, témoignant du passé éducatif et culturel de l'île, renforçant ainsi son caractère historique et authentique.

En résumé, explorer Gorée, c'est plonger dans un mélange fascinant de passé et de présent, où l'histoire se mêle à la beauté naturelle de l'île. C'est une expérience qui invite à la réflexion tout en permettant d'apprécier la magie intemporelle de cet endroit unique.
VOYAGEAVECNOUS.COM
FB ET INSTA AUTOURDUMONDE2023

title: À faire absolument
text:
Très belle île, chargée d histoire, plutôt bien entretenue et propre.
Navette à prendre prendre pour s y rendre, il vaut mieux prendre un guide pour faire la visite guidée. Une ancienne maison des esclavages à faire impérativement pour savoir l horreur que beaucoup ont vécus, c a fait froid dans le dos.
Petites ruelles sympas pour se balader.

title: Very interesting historical location
text:
Visited (and stayed one night) as part of a tour.
Short ferry ride (always fun on a ferry eh?) from Dakar port.
Small population reliant on tourism (mainly day trips) and fishing. One can see many reminders that this was one of the major embarkation points for the slave trade  run by numerous European countries .
The day we went (Monday) the museum was closed .
The are some interesting memorials.
As well as the history of slavery, one can see ,on the hilltop ,the gun emplacement that was the rangefinder for the Dakar batteries in WW2, when the Vichy  administration were in charge and the Allies and the Free French  attacked to try and take control of the port (but lost the battle and ships)

title: Excursion au top
text: L’équipe secretoo s’est tenu disponible pour tout renseignements avant de prendre une excursion nous avons opté pour la visite de l’île de Gorée et le lac rose , Olivier notre guide est gentil et à l’écoute des besoins de ses clients l’île de Gorée est une visite incontournable cette visite était très touchante , je recommande secretoo pour leur service et leur réactivité. Nous étions 4 2 adultes et deux enfants tout s’est très bien passé

title: Interesting.
text: The Island was very nice to walk around and the old buildings interesting especially the slave house. The art work with sand was amazing. There were a lot of items on sale too.

title: INTERESTING
text: The island was very nice to walk around and the old buildings interesting especially the slave house. The art work with sand was amazing. There were a lot of items on sale too.

title: Lohnenswert ....
text: Es lohnt sich, für einen Tag auf die Insel Gorée zu fahren. Mit der Fähre vollkommen unkompliziert. Schöne, kleine Insel mit vielen kleinen Handwerksläden und ein paar Museen.

title: Île de Goree 01 2024
text:
N'oubliez pas de vous munir de votre carte d'identité ou passeport!!!!
Choisissez un bon guide (pas obligatoire sauf si vous oubliez vos papiers il saura vous faire rentrer mais pour min. 16000cfa :( ) 5200cfa p.p pour la chaloupe + 500 cfa p.p pour taxe communale + 1500cfa p.p entrée maison des esclaves.
Chaloupe correcte et part à temps! Horaire à consulter pour départ et arrivé sur le site! Car il n'y qu'un bateau par heure ou voir toutes les deux heures!
Arrivée sur l'île pleins de vendeurs de tout (cadeau/souvenirs) négociez bien, voir enlever + que la moitié de la somme demandé! Acceptent souvent également les euros. Distributeur d'argent sur place. Différents resto sur place, prix corrects et bons mais énormément de mouches :(
Très belles rues pleins de couleurs.
Artisan tableau de sable à visiter, quel talent.

title: Pas op voor gevaarlijke loslopende hond
text: Schilderachtig eiland met beladen slavernijverleden. Voor mij overheerste echter het feit dat ik out of the blue werd aangevallen door een hond. Volgens inwoners had hij dit al vijf keer eerder gedaan, wat de arts bevestigde. Hij verwees meteen door voor rabiesvaccinatie (was in Nederland niet beschikbaar). Aangifte bij de dorpspolitie van Goree verliep keurig. De eigenaar werd opgetrommeld, heeft mijn medische kosten vergoed en de hond wordt (eindelijk) afgemaakt. Wees toch gewaarschuwd, want dat zou twee jaar geleden ook al gebeurd zijn. Het is boven op het fort bij het puntige monument.

title: Sehr zu empfehlen
text: Die Insel Gorée ist einzigartig. Nicht weit von Dakar, allerdings eine fast andere Welt. Der Besuch dieser Insel ist ein Muss für jeden Senegal Besucher

title: A faire
text:
Visite de l'île de Goree, visite de la maison des esclaves, visite chargée d histoire. On a des frisons....
Visite de l île agréable

title: À voir absolument
text: Île magnifique, de beaux décors, maison des esclaves très bien conservée, explication du guide très intéressante ! Nous avons très bien mangé, seul regret je pense qu'il faut faire une nuit sur place pour vraiment profiter !

title: La beauté de l’indicible
text:
Goree est une île chargée d’émotion. Une petite préparation par la lecture permet dès l’embarcadère à Dakar de se mettre dans l’ambiance. La possibilité de flâner sur l’île est très agréable. Les aménagements récents rendent les pauses sympathiques et conviviales. La restauration est variée . Les commerçants savent exercer une pression sans  harceler. 
C’est tout cela qui fait le charme d’une visite dont le clou demeure la maison des esclaves.

title: Entre histoire et déchets
text: A faire absolument pour la maison des esclaves, que j'ai trouvé bouleversante. J'ai été choqué par la saleté et les déchets... Que fait les autorités locales et les locaux.... CEST HONTEUX!  Voir en images.

title: Critical piece of Senegal's history
text:
It's so sad to think of the inhuman things people did to others, and a visit to this island makes it so real. 

You'll need a passport to get ferry tickets, and the ferries are packed before they ever depart. Definitely worthwhile to do a pre-arranged tour to help you navigate the ferry and to truly understand the history of the island.

Plenty of tourist shops and small cafes/restaurants. You can do this tour in as little or much time as you like. The ferries return frequently.

title: Endroit très riche en historique
text: Tour fait avec des clients. Endroit très riche en historique Pour plus d'infos n'hésitez pas de me contacter sur WhatsApp +221 77 364 99 65

user.name: Adama n Chauffeur et guide au Senegal

title: Not easy but important to do
text: I don’t know right words to describe feelings about island. For sure is important place from historical point of view to visit… for sure visit is not nice more touching and sad .. on the other point of view island is beautiful peaceful and colourful place is under unesco list so it is also a little tip is is worth of visit.. restaurants are fine people really friendly sellers a little bit tiring but on the other hand they are fighting about their families…

title: Une superbe demi journée à Gorée!
text: Cela vaut le détour! Endroit reconnu par l’UNESCO. Poste de traite des esclaves et une histoire sombre mais aujourd’hui une magnifique île avec habitants sympathiques. Des ruelles en fleurs, De belles découvertes et de la très bonne nourriture dans les petits restos sur la plage

title: Don’t Miss Osu Castle
text: Love. Love. Love the opportunity to visit Osu Castle. It is a lasting memory of the past. I was amazed at the longevity of such a horrible place, but glad to see that it remains as a reminder of past evils. The castle has so much history and the guide was incredibly helpful and knowledgeable about the history of the castle. Queen Elizabeth and Barack Obama both visited the Osu Castle. Really appreciated learning and walking through history. Amazing. Simply amazing.

title: The history comes alive.
text: Wow, visiting this castle made a great impression on me. We had a great guide who really made history come alive in the narrow cells of the slave trade times.

title: Osu Castle
text: Osu Castle is worth the visit when in Ghana. The history of slave trading and this castle which was once a trading centre for slaves is the focal point of the tour but also touches on how it became a government building for politicians. Even the Queen of England stayed in this Castle for a period of time. Seth the tour guide had extensive knowledge on the history of Ghana & the castle . He really did a great job. One of the best tour guides I’ve had.

title: Worth the visit
text: Not an especially developed tourist destination but the history was rich and detailed and the guide was excellent (and worked only on tips).

title: Enlighten
text: Osu Castle has Deep rich history. That’s all I will say. Go visit. It will be worth it! You will be enlightened by the historical events.

title: A Memorable Family Trip to Osu Castle
text: Osu Castle provided a perfect blend of history, culture, and beautiful scenery, making it a highlight of our trip to Ghana. We highly recommend this visit to anyone interested in exploring Ghana’s rich heritage.

title: Nice tour & history - once you find the way in!
text:
This castle is a must see if staying in Accra. It was both an old slave trading post, and a more recent seat of government. The tour guide was quite knowledgable and fun. You'll learn the slave trade history, see some rooms from more recent government stays and they room where the Queen of England stayed. 

The challenging part was finding your way in. As it still houses government workers, there are gates & checkpoints to pass through and it's not very obvious where to enter, park or go for visitor entry. We had a taxi driver who knew the way, but without that it would be tricky with little signage.

title: Einblick in die Geschichte Ghanas
text: Ich bin vom Hotel aus hingelaufen. Eintritt 100 Cedi. Allerdings war die Kasse noch gar nicht geöffnet und ein Mitarbeiter hat mich abgefangen. Mir wurde dann ein Guide zugeteilt. Im Vergleich zu den anderen Forts sieht man hier eher die Außenanlage. Der Guide hat mir viel zur Geschichte erklärt und u.a. auch welche Motive auf den Geldscheinen zu sehen sind - z.B. die Treppe auf dem 50 Cedi Schein. Gen Ende sieht man noch die Kerker. Die Tour dauerte 30 Minuten. Nach der Tour kann man noch durch den kleinen Garten gehen.

title: Mit Guide ein absolutes Highlight
text:
Osu Castle ist ein relevanter Teil der Ghanaischen Geschichte und für mich ein absolutes „Must See“

Wir haben an einer Tour mit dem Guide vor Ort teilgenommen für 40 Cedis. Die Tour dauerte etwas weniger als eine Stunde.

Große Teile der Festung sind nicht besonders gut Instand gehalten. Ohne den Guide wirkt es wenig spannend, aber mit den nötigen Infos versteht man die Anlage trotz des mäßigen Zustands. Es ist sehr beeindruckend, wie er über die Sklaven Vergangenheit referiert hat.

Neben dem Castle gibt es noch einen Garten bzw. kleine Parkanlage. Dort kann man nach der Führung noch einen Spaziergang machen.

Tipp: Direkt mit dem Uber/Bolt hinfahren. Wir sind vom Black Star Arch hingelaufen. Der Weg ist nicht weit, aber es lungern entlang der Straße überall Gruppen herum und man wird schnell etwas bedrängt.

title: Great insight into the Ghanaian slave trade
text: Really enjoyed visiting this castle.  The tour guide was really interesting and the history of the castle is grim but fascinating.

title: So glad I visited
text:
I’m so glad I visited Osu Castle. The guide was brilliant and gave such an impactful, informative tour of the castle spanning so much history. You can see the awful history of the trade of enslaved people as well as recent history such as where modern presidents of Ghana lived and worked. The guide was very knowledgeable and gave poignant descriptions of all the places we saw.  

If you go just make sure to walk past the government building still in use to get to the castle. Everyone was helpful in pointing me in the right direction but it was confusing and a little intimidating to walk up to a big closed gate with guards. 

I’m giving 4 stars because it was kind of hard to leave if you don’t have a car with no taxi rank or Uber drivers wanting to come that far. Took me about 45 minutes and walking further up to main roads before I could get an Uber back to the city centre.

title: definitely worth visiting
text:
Got here good and early, no one else around just us, so had the whole place to ourselves, the tour guide from the Castle brought us around the grounds and showed us the many rooms of the Castle, and also brought us down below where they used to keep slaves. 
He told us a lot about the history of the castle, of slavery, and the subsequent uses of the castle.....was very interesting and the guide was kind enough to go above and beyond in showing us things that perhaps on another day might be off to the public.   
Very informative. 
Spent over an hour here, and the castle is definitely worth visiting, if only to get an idea of the horrors of the slave trade.....

title: A fascinating place
text:
Also known as Christianborg Castle, Osu castle was a fascinating place to visit.  We learned so much about this place and its history from our tour guide.  We learned tat the Danes originally built it, but then it was occupied by many other entities after that.  The Portuguese, Dutch, British, and local rulers have occupied it over the years, all of which were active in the slave trade.  The dungeon where the slaves were held captive was absolutely horrifying.  I couldn’t get out of there fast enough.  The beautiful garden we strolled through after the dungeon was calming though...  
A must visit place in Accra.

title: Eye Opening: Visit for some Black History
text:
A castle with a mixed history of both African slave trade by the Europeans, as well as Ghanaians' leadership/government's seat of power.
A castle of dungeons for black slaves, a gate of 'no return' for slaves, a chapel for white slavers to worship, diplomatic rooms, and presidential offices all rolled into one. 
A nice place to visit for black history.

title: Informative and interesting
text:
An interesting trip lead by a friendly and knowledgeable guide. 
You have to walk through government run area and sign in and out. Just be careful not to take any pictures in that section.
I preferred my trip to ussher fort but this was still interesting and sad. 
It cost 40 cedi and the tour lasts approximately an hour. 
There's a nice park next door built by the British once they'd run out the locals :( nice park to relax in and good for bird spotting.

title: Worth a Visit
text: Really good tour.  Lots of history about the horrors of the Slave Trade and the history of the Castle up to present day.

title: A must see in Accra
text: Osu Castle - or Fort Christiansborg - is a must-see when in Accra. There seems to be some confusion on whether it is open to the public or not. It is, so go there when you can. It is a bit confusing when you arrive because the part before you come to the old castle is government territory and you are not allowed to take photos there. You register and pay 40 GHS per person and then you get a guide for app. 45 minutes. The castle was central to the slave trade for Denmark during 200 years. It was built in 1661 and was eventuelly sold to the British mid-1800. Like Elimna Castle at Cape Coast it is central to visit in order to get an understanding of the terrible conditions for the slaves kept here before the transport across the Atlantic to the sugar plantations at the Virgin Islands.

title: Pay your respects at Osu Castle
text: It's well worth a visit, so much history to this place.  If you don't have time to travel as far as Cape Coast and Elmina, it is very much worth a visit to go and pay your respects to the past.  There is still much to do in its restoration and different parts of it are open at different times, but still worth it

title: It is Slavery We Talking About!
text:
I cannot come to terms with the fact that we as a country agreed to use a place where our grandparents etc were treated like "animals" as a seat for our Government for so long and happily, until just recently that we could "think right"? I was and still is ashamed of myself when I visited the Osu Castle.
As I walked through the dungeons and the stairs listening to our host narrates to us the horrible history, shivers run down my spine as I reflect and imagine those days of abuse.
I will say "Never Again"

title: Cool castle in contrast to Elmina and Cape Coast
text:
Visited the castle on 12/30 morning. Very quite with nobody around. Our guide, Kobi, gave us a tour of the place for a pretty cheap costs. Tour lasted about 45 minutes and was very informative, showing us the history of the castle, it’s use as a presidential office until 2012, and of course the slave dungeons. Recommend going to Cape Coast and Elmina if you want to see the bigger slave castles. This one only transacted around 48,000 slaves during its history (as opposed to the millions at Cape and Elmina). 

Worth a visit!

title: Art Market & Souvenir shops
text: a lot of African souvenir, traditional shirt, handcraft, etc. also you can find ivory craft selling here, but please check is it original or may create by bone.

title: Art,  Pearls and handicraft.
text: If looking for semi precious stones,  Art and craft pearls.  This market has all.  Lots of Chinese tourists buying stuff around.  Shop keepers even speak the language.  Lots of bargaining can be done.  Stuff much cheaper than at hotels.

title: It was  splendid
text: I loved loved and loved every moment, stressful but worth it. Lekki Market is a beautiful place to be.

title: Amazing Handmade Crafts
text: If you are looking for some amazing African handmade statutes, figurines, paintings then this must be the place to visit. Parking may be a bit of an issue but if you go there with your driver, then that's sorted out. This is also the place to hone your haggling & bargaining abilities. The general rule of thumb is that you should get your selected item at 50% of the quoted price (if not less!!). This is the place to explore and look around. You'll find some amazing stuff here!!

title: Loads to choose from for self and presents.
text: Loads to choose from for self and presents. Arts, fabrics, brick a brace for all price ranges. A lovely covered market. Always with s visit whenever I go into Lekki.

title: Lekki Market: My View
text: I live in Lagos and I am Nigerian. This is a great market for getting some local art works from Nigeria especially those native to Lagos. However it is best visited with a local person. You must know how to bargain as prices tend to be highly over stated. Rule of thumb is to cut it down by 50% and maintain your stand know matter how much you want it. you can go lower too.never stop at a shop. go around the market to see other items you may just getter better stuffs. Do not try to visit this market whenever it rains.It will be like crossing the biblical red se.a. Try to get a little model of the old Lagos Danfo and other interesting artifacts. Just don't forget to ensure you head to the Lagos Museum to register the artifacts and get your export permit

title: Saturday exploring
text:
Stopped at the market for something to do. Nice range of produce, wooden carvings, bags and clothes. 
Was hard to get into as it had rained the night before. Hard to get there without a four wheel drive. 
All the people will try and pull you in their stalls so it can be a little overwhelming but worth a look

title: Great market for souvenirs
text: The Lekki market hosts several hundreds of souvenir stalls. Here you will find paintings, wood carvings, cloths and jewelry from Nigeria and neighbouring countries. The salesmen are not too pushy, but you have to bargain till you settle for about half the price initially asked for. All taxidrivers know the place so it shouldn't be difficult to be dropped there.

title: hard to find, bargain hard
text:
Road there goes through another local market - turn off Lekki Expressway between 4th and 5th roundabouts, just before the footbridge onto dirt road.  Take first left, go straight around 200m, then right.  Market is about 50m on the left - walk through the red buildings to get to the main market.

Negotiate hard - opening prices are 2-3 times high.

title: Interesting!
text: The Lekki Market is a bustling market where you can buy African arts & crafts as well as all sorts of curios. Nice place to visit

title: Hone your bargaining skills
text: The road in can be a challenge, particularly if it's been raining, but it's worth it when you get there.  A broad range of artworks and souvenirs including paintings, wood carvings (including masks), jewelery, wall hangings, and many more.  You'll definitely need to bargain hard, but if you're a practiced negotiator you can get some very good bargains.

title: Diversidade em artesanato
text:
Lá encontrei artesanato de vários países africanos além da Nigéria. Comprei toalhas de mesa lindas em Batik e vestidos também.
Há muita bijouteria e bolsas de couro de animais que morreram de doenças segundo eles dizem.

title: Conhecendo a Cultura local
text: O mercado de Lekki tem uma variedade de produtos locais, aconselho reservar dinheiro para comprar uma máscara de madeira, são magníficas. Mesmo se não for para fazer compras a visita vale muito!

title: Wonderful place for affordable indigenous art work
text:
Walking through the stalls was an interesting experience,thé various sculptures,oil & acrylic paintings,excellent wood work;you know the kind we had in our grandparents homes with intricately carved designs (some of which I had previously seen at named galleries with hefty price tags 😀).
An eye for quality artwork is necessary to avoid being hustled,and good bargaining skills too.All in all,it was a rewarding experience,I now visit often on the lookout for nice pieces to acquire for my home.

title: Authentic artisan market
text: This very authentic artisan market is a go-to place for anyone wanting some handcrafted souvenirs. There is a wide range of items. We went on a Sunday before noon so we were the first tourists there, but it picked up after an hour or so but it definitely was not crowded.

title: Lekki Tourist Market
text:
The Lekki Tourist Market is a must visit. Quality souvenirs at rock bottom price, if you can bargain well.  

It is located very close to the Elegushi Beach and tucked Off Oba Saheed Ademola Elegushi Road, Beach Market Road, Jakande Estate, Lekki-Epe Expressway, Lagos.

title: For Jewelry & Art Lovers
text:
I went to the market with N5,000 as my spend budget on accessories. My discovery was slowed down by the crazy heat (Sun), It was really crazy but I eventually got cool accessories.

These are the kind of things I found when I went to ghana. The market was filled with a lot of handmade accessories from beads, to fresh water pearls, leather skins, it was almost unbelievable. 

I said to my friend that Nigerians are so super creative with the artifacts in the market. 

The market is not your typical market but more modern like you will find in other countries, if you understand art and are looking for different unique craft items this is the market to go. 

They make a lot of the art and crafts there e.g butterfly skin paintings (I probably touched more animals in the market than I have ever done in my life). So, they use animal skins for some of the deco’s (Butterfly, Zebra, snake and more). 

I barely spent the 5,000 from the market but I only got 2 items for N2,500 (A vintage purse I adore for N1,900 and N600 for the necklace).

For accessories the market is really affordable. Advice for local's is don't be deceived by the prices they tell you, still go hard on negotiating and the sellers don't like that.

title: Un mercato caratteristico
text: Al Lekki market potete trovare veramente di tutto. Manufatti tipici dell'arte africana e, se sapete come muovervi potreste anche trovare pezzi "unici" e meno turistici. Non semplicissimo da trovare.

title: Excekente
text: Para llevar recuerdos de este país es muy buen mercado,  los precios son buenos y los vendedores no presionan y esta limpio

title: Lekki, a bazzar
text:
You can find anything you want. 
All the prices can be negociated as long as you do not insult the vendors.

A good practice is to buy in bulk and ask for a discount then fake that you are leaving (works everytime) and wait.

title: So much wasted potential
text:
This place has so much potential which is not being realised. The historical and educational significance of the park is evident in the atmosphere. I learned about Kwane Nkrumah in school as did many African children. The park is not presented as modern attraction. Kwame Nkrumah's car is gathering dust. The trees and lawn are not well  maintained. One isn't allowed to take pictures inside the museum, which is unfortunate. It could have served as a way to share information and publicise the park. The artefacts are not displayed in the best cases.
Despite all of these I would still recommend a visit.

title: So much potential wasted
text:
This place has so much potential which is not being realised. The historical and educational significance of the park is evident in the atmosphere. I learned about Kwane Nkrumah in school as did many African children. The park is not presented as modern attraction. Kwame Nkrumah's car is gathering dust. Despite all of these I would still recommend a visit.

title: Fascinating space
text: You really get a feeling of a time gone by era when visiting this place, it’s like a soviet arena in blazing sun. Totally safe with friendly local people. I would highly recommend a visit to soak up the atmosphere and imagine it full of people cheering their leaders.

title: Kwame Nkrumah Park
text: Touring Accra you can’t miss the famous Kwame Nkrumah park the first president of the republic of Ghana.

title: Breathtaking
text: Historical site.  I was amazed to have been such a part of history.  The weather was great and the staff was amazing.

title: Historical Site
text: Very inspirational and breathtaking.  We walked around and took a lot of pictures and absorbed the positive energy that this place exudes

title: Quick visit
text: A  good opportunity to know more about ghana history, the memorial is simple, don't expect to spend half day there (especially it is very hot)

title: History lesson for everyonr
text: A cruicial information about Ghanas first president. Of course the glory has been diminshed throughout the years, but yet very fascinating history. Worthwile a visit

title: Giant of Africa.
text: The guided tour for this memorial will leave a lasting impression and understanding of Nkrumah's legacy for all of Africa. His museum also documents his relationship with other leaders in Africa, the Caribbean and the United States. The memorabilia and documents in his museum will force you to read more about him. It was an honor to pause at his gravesite to pay respects to a personal hero.

title: Awesome place.
text: Take the guided tour and maximize to learn on Nkrumah's rich history. The view outside is beautiful and you see where he and his wife were laid to rest

title: Historisch hochinteressant
text: Mit dem Tagesausflug von Nouvelles Frontieres kann die Insel ausgiebig erkundet werden,vor allem die Sklavenhistorie wurde ausreichend dokumentiert,auch der Angriff 1940 durch England war aufschlussreich.

title: Isla cargada de historia
text: La isla de Gorée está muy cerca de Dakar y se accede en ferry desde el puerto en poco tiempo. Tiene un pasado colonial y fue el punto de salida de los esclavos que se enviaban a América. El entorno de la isla es bonito, se puede pasear hasta la parte más alta y la experiencia de visitar la casa de los esclavos y ver las terribles condiciones que padecieron no la olvidaré, En la isla hay muchas vendedoras de artesanía y a veces puden resultar agobiantes. Junto al puerto hay varios restaurantes donde comer a buen precio.

title: Devoir de mémoire, incontournable
text:
cette île au large de Dakar nous rappelle les heures sombres du passé. La maison des esclaves permet de se plonger au cœur de cette histoire et merci à l’orateur qui raconte les conditions de vie des esclaves avec beaucoup de cœur
L’île est vraiment jolie, pensez à monter au point culminant pour une vue panoramique. Il y a de nombreux resto au débarcadère, je vous conseille de prendre le premier bateau à 9h pour éviter la foule. C’est très fréquenté le we. La traversée en bateau dure 20 min environ

title: Isola con una triste storia
text: Già  da imbarco sono stato avvicinato da venditori che invitavano una visita presso il loro locale sull'isola. Ho trovato una guida che per 20000 franchi locali (15 euro) ci ha guidato in ogni angolo dell'isola. Consigliata ka guida. Isola molto caratteristica e pulita se confrontata con dakar. Presenza di tanti giovani. Da non perdere visita alla casa dello schiavo

title: Uma ilha colorida com uma história de escravatura arrepiante
text: Goreé é uma ilha colorida de estilo colonial. Fica a uns 20 minutos de ferry saindo do cais de Dakar. Com estreitas ruas cheias de flores e casas coloridas. Aqui fica a Casa dos escravos que agora é um museu. A população é muito acolhedora e vive do turismo. Existem vários restaurantes onde comi camarões salteados como entrada, espetada de tamboril como prato principal e manga como sobremesa. Gostei muito.

title: MAI PIU
text: 4 ore di fila senza il minimo supporto dal personale pazzia! Veramente la peggior esperienza della mia vita, non lo merita. PS i non africani pagano 5 volte il prezzo del biglietto

title: A historical gem
text: I was here for a day and it was nice. Full of history. Small island with a vibrant culture. Kind of like Zanzibar. Very nice to stay overnight.

title: Super belle endroit
text: Lieux historique j’ai étais surprise du très belle endroit  l’île de Gorée île paradisiaque dans laquelle certains homme on connu l’enfer

title: Chouette expérience
text:
Si vous pouvez, allez y seul! Il vous suffit de vous rendre au port maritime de Dakar, vous devrez avoir votre pièce d’identité ainsi que;
-500fcfa
-5200fcfa pour votre trajet si vous êtes non résident, c’est le prix du transport aller/retour en ferry cela dure 20min +-.
Vous avez des ferry toute les heures +- !
Sur place vous devrez acheter un ticket de visite de 8000fcfa peut importe le nombre de personne. Vous trouverez pleins de guides prêt à vous faire visiter l’île des votre arrivée, vous leurs donnez ce que vous voulez en fin de visite. 
L’entrée à la maison des esclaves est de 1500fcfa p.p
Au final, cela est vraiment très bien en terme de prix! 
Une visite comme celle nous a été proposé à pas moins de 60-70€ par personne….. 
nous avions loué un véhicule donc c’est déjà ça de gagné, mais du coup la visite pour 2 à l’île de gorée nous est revenue à Max 30€ pour 2!!! 
Merci à Abi qui a une petite boutique super chouette; ainsi qu’à son mari qui nous a fait visiter l’île (il connaît les moindres recoins) !!!

title: Un'esperienza forte
text:
Visita con guida che parla italiano.
Una visita completa, esaustiva, rispettosa.
Anche il pranzo vicino all'imbarcadero è stato ottimo.
La gente è cordiale , andate a visitare il laoratorio dove fammi i quadri con la sabbia. Il migliore che abbiamo visto nel nostro viaggio

title: A must see when in Senegal bring your passport!
text:
Despite the historical atrocities that took place in Goree, an island from which slaves would be shipped to the Americas, the place is incredibly beautiful and peaceful. It is a testament to the beauty and resilience of black people. Take a good guide to visit the slave house and the island and do not be bullied in tipping them more than you want (they will always ask for more). There are no cars on the island so be ready to walk. Also bring official ID (passport for foreigners, residence cards for resident) otherwise you won't be able to buy a ferry ticket. 
The ticket prices will vary if you are a national, an African or a non-african but the most you will pay for a return trip is about 10usd/person.
Wear comfortable shoes, have change with you (no ATMs), wear sun protection. Oh and you need patience with the street vendors who will most probably sit next to you on the boat to try and sell you something or convince you to come to their shop on the island.

title: Faut avoir le temps et être armé de patience
text: Inadmissible. 2h d’attente pour acheter un billet. Vendeur tout simplement pas présent au guichet. De plus, 1 bateau en panne ce qui ralentit également le flux

title: Un lieu chargé d’histoire
text: Cette île est très jolie malgré son histoire lourde à porter ! La visite de maison des esclaves est un incontournable. Traversée en 20 mn en ferry. Contrairement au continent,  les maisons sont terminées,  peintes...

title: Trés mauvaise organisation
text: Nous avons essayé d'aller à l'ile de gorée. une heure d'attente pour prendre les billets en plein soleil, puis quand on a pris les billets, on nous dit qu'un des 2 bateaux est en panne.. donc encore une attente d'une heure.. toujours pas de bateau, ça faisait 2 h qu'on attendait donc on a décidé de partir.. et là pas de remboursement !!! ils auraient du nous le dire qu'un des 2 bateaux était en panne, on était avec 2 jeunes enfants en plus.

title: Visita obligada
text:
Para llegar a la isla hay que coger un ferry. El trayecto es corto, unos 20-25 min. Si eres turista, es normal que se te acerquen mujeres senegalesas ofreciéndote que visites sus tiendas cuando llegues a la isla.
Goreé tiene un encanto especial desde el momento en que la divisas desde el ferry. Su aire colonial, su historia y sus habitantes hacen que sea un punto y a parte, si ya has visitado previamente la ciudad de Dakar, este te parecerá un lugar muy distinto.
Al desembarcar encontrarás guías que te mostrarán todos los rincones de la isla y la terrible historia que le da fama. Turistas y hogareños llenan de vida una isla que se aprecia muy tranquila. Los edificios están muy bien conservados, la vegetación, las flores en concreto, decoran muchas de sus calles. En la parte más alta se encuentra un impresionante cañón. 
Puedes comprar artesanías y cerca del muelle hay varios restaurantes donde poder comer gastronomía local a un precio correcto.

title: Passage obligatoire
text:
Passage obligé lorsque vous êtes à Dakar.
Magnifique île chargée en histoire.

title: Haut lieu de la mémoire esclavagiste
text:

La première est que c’est un haut lieu de la mémoire esclavagiste. Le fait de visiter ces lieux où l’on entassait et triait les esclaves par sexe et selon le poids nous prend aux tripes. On a du mal à imaginer que des hommes aient pu faire subir de tels châtiments à des êtres humains et cela nous révolte au plus haut point.

La deuxième raison est que Gorée est une très belle île avec des habitants, des maisons coloniales, un fort, de belles rues et magnifiques paysages sur la mer.

Si vous passez par Dakar, ne manquez pas cette visite car la ville même ne présente aucun intérêt avec ses embouteillages incommensurables.

text: If you are a visitor to Abuja and want some items to remember the city by, The Crafts Village is a good bet. title: En del av Danmark-Norge sin historie,
text:
Målet mitt med å besøke Ghana var å se selv et av fortene som var sentrale i den dansk-norske trekant-ruten fra København til Gullkysten for å kjøpe slaver som så ble fraktet over Atlanterhavet til den dansk-norske kolonien i Karibien som i dag utgjør de amerikanske Jomfruøyene. 

I stedet for å bestille omvisning hos et av byråene var det sjåføren tilknyttet La-Paradise Inn som kjørte meg dit. Vi fikk omvisning sammen med en skoleklasse samt noen andre turister. Guiden gikk gjennom Christiansborg sin historie som inkluderte flere europeiske land. Det som overrasket meg positivt var guidens poeng at det var afrikanske stammer som solgte slaver til oss, enten fordi de var krigsfanger eller ble "lurt" til fangenskap. Å se stranden utenfor fortet hvor slavene ble samlet før de ble ført gjennom døren for "no return" og de lave "rommene" i kjelleren de måtte oppholde seg i før de ble overført til det ventende skipet, var sterkt.

Å være på et slikt sted er i seg selv både tankevekkende og grusomt. Hadde det bare vært historie, men for både afrikanere og andre er en slik skjebne dessverre virkelighet i dag også. 

Enten du er voksen eller har med barn, er et slikt besøk en påminnelse om hva som er viktig i livet. 

Jeg anbefaler et besøk.

title: Bring camera!  A photographer paradise
text: The history of this slave castle is intense; the tour is good, but I find it best to wander. If you love photography, you will love the whitewashed walls, intensely colorful native flowers, and the patina and architectural details. There are several areas of photo restrictions, but just ask the staff. I found the amazing concrete block wall in the front entrance simply stunning, wow (that area was photo restricted, but trust in me - this block wall was amazing!). Step out of the Door of No Return and get fabulous photos of the castle walls from the sandy beach. The large empty pool - a fun fact - Muhammad Ali swam in this pool with Kwame Nkrumah many, many years ago.

title: Historical Visit
text: A insightful visit to the castle.  Our tour guide was very knowledgeable and provided a good overview of the castle and Ghanaian political history.  Please note that the castle is open only on certain days, so check before you head over.

title: A glimpse of Ghanaian history
text:
The different parts of the castle were built at different times and used by different colonisers and Presidents. To visit this castle is to get a snapshot of the country's history.

The most moving experience was going into the dungeon where slaves were kept and coming out through the gate of no return that looks out into the Atlantic Ocean. After visiting the dungeon, you are taken to a refreshing garden with a sad history.

A tour of the castle costs about USD8 and lasts about an hour (or longer if, like me, you ask a lot of questions).

Many parts of the castle are falling into disrepair and so I hope that they will have major renovation works soon.

title: Beach work out. Osu Castle Beach
text: Cool and unbothered location. Free to move about. Family can organize a picnic and have fun . Eyes should be on little kids as some tides are dangerous

title: Fairly good
text: The castle is reasonably interesting and usually fairly quiet. The tour guide we had was very friendly and answered any questions we had. However, unfortunately, there is not too much to see. It is fairly empty bar some old furniture. The views from it are quite nice and some of the history of the place is interesting. All in all, if you have time to spare in Accra I would recommend it. But it is certainly not an essential visit.

title: Absolute Must See, Great Experience
text: We walked to the castle from the Movenpick Hotel on a Friday afternoon and felt we learned more from that one experience than any thing else we did -- both the walk and the tour. There is minimal signage. Proceed right up to the front gate. There is a minimal fee. Our guide was an intern, a student, who was remarkably well informed. You see parts of the recently vacated presidential apartment. The original structure was built by the Danes. The chapel was built by the Portuguese. Seeing the "dungeon" was a remarkable experience. Overall, they need a lot of help in turning this into a museum and dealing with the decay you get in a coastal environment. But, we are very grateful we had the experience. It's a must do.

title: Great addition to any Accra city tour!
text:
For until recently access to the castle had not been possible for the public as it had still been in use as the presidential seat.

Now this is also history and the castle is undergoing severe restauration to become a 'museum'. In the meantime the public is invited to see all that's there in his current state.

I thoroughly enjoyed this tour!- The history this castle has seen over CENTURIES is simply impressive and this includes the actual more recent Ghanaian events. In this respect it strongly differs from other castles in Cape Coast and Elmina. 

Our castle guide was very well informed and I believe we've seen everything there was to see and we could ask absolutely everything! Of course it will be even nicer in some years time once renovation will have advanced. But in the meantime ... HIGHLY recommended. An absolute must if you don't have time to travel to places with other castles.

title: Very quaint
text:
We visited on a Sunday and the approach was very quiet, so quiet that we thought it was closed. 

We got down from our Uber just to confirm the right opening times, and lo and behold, we not only were able to visit the Castle, we got a very informative guided tour. 

A very historical castle, with dungeons below and state rooms above. A place for rulers and right there so seaside as to be seen as partially floating partly on the Atlantic Ocean. 

I would really love to go back there.

title: 推薦這個地方
text: 這是一座美麗的堡壘，從17世紀就建起來，然後經過好幾次翻修。它過去是用來扣押奴隸，但後來被用於加納總統的辦公室。我一早就詢問酒店和司機關於這個地方。但它們不曉得堡壘是否向公眾開放。無論如何，我叫司機嘗試一下。在入口處，我看到處有警察和軍隊。看來是有國家的外賓要到這裡訪問。經過一番討價還價後，警察讓我進去大門，但只在靠近正門的地方看看。從遠處，看到這個地方有一座漂亮的白色建築，很可能是舊建築。但它的周圍增加了許多新的結構。除了堡壘外，還有一個帶花植物的大型美麗花園。雖然，我沒成功進去堡壘，但我還是推薦這個地方。希望其它遊客比我幸運，能夠堡壘裡面和周圍逛逛。

title: The Fort!
text:
Osu Castle, Accra aka Fort Christiansborg or simply the castle, is located in Osu, Accra on the coast of the Atlantic Ocean; Gulf of Guinea. This castle was the official seat of the government of Ghana before it moved to The Jubilee House. The castle was built by the Danes as a fort to facilitate trade activities between the indigenes and the Europeans but later turned to the harbour of transferring captured indigenes who were transported out to be sold as slaves.
The Castle was later sold to the British after the abolition of the slave trade and is now open to #tourist as a museum for people to know the history of the Ghanaians. We got to see where Queen Elizabeth II slept when she visited the castle in 1962. This spot has a melancholy feeling to it after seeing and hearing how people were treated and kept during the slave trade days, after which you see the view of the ocean and you marvel at the wide spread of the deep blue ocean with ships sailing and the air so pure and tranquil.
In the Castle, you can take a walk through the well-kept gardens listening to beautiful melody by the birds with lots of flowers and trees clapping and singing along side, you also get to take a guided tour of the castle, listening to history, you get to see the fort and dungeons used for slave trade and also a place to shop at the shopping centre.
This spot is children, family and lovers friendly, you can take long walks to clear your head; get inspiration if you need one and it’s a spot to sit, reminisce and read books. The atmosphere is everything!
Don’t forget to follow @tourwithswagger and @gbogbo_swagger
Life is beautiful... Take a trip!!!

title: Historique

Worth watching series 2 episode 8 of The Crown, as this was where Nkrumah hosted Queen Elizabeth on her visit in 1961.  Tours take about 60-90 minutes.

title: Meet the artists
text: This place is a wonderful place if you want to see unique Senegalese art. This place supports the local artists give them a place to do their art work and sell them in the economy. I had the pleasure of meeting Soguy who paints really great pieces. He shared his vision behind his painting and his message is about peace and harmony among the Senegalese people.

title: Unusual artist colony with a great history
text:
This artist colony was a self-initiated effort some years ago by working artists who needed a place to do their work.  It is now has some government support. Not every artist can work here and from the quality we saw (including work from an artist we saw at the Venice Biennale) that strong curating shows -- of course your experience would depend on which studios were open.  
    During our visit not all the studios were open but the gallery was and had a representative sample of the fifty or so artist who work here.  In the ateliers we visited,  there was a nice combination of large and small works, painting and sculpture. The garden was fun as well and a peaceful respite from busy Dakar. 
       I think some of the other reviewers got their artists sites confused. We didn't see things that looked mass produced (like the artists on Goree who all seem to be doing the same thing). I would recommend this for people interested in contemporary, working African artists.

title: Most items too large for any traveller to contemplate buying

text: More like a sleepy Art & Crafts compound. A few places were creating their own arts while others seem like mass production. Prices seem ok.

title: Un Condense d'artistes
text: peinture sculpture vous trouverez les artistes dans ce lieux qui leur est réservé, mais attention n'arrivez pas avant 11h du matin voire 12H , ils ne seront pas réveillé!!!

title: Een goede bestemming om kunst te kopen
text: Een goede bestemming om kunst te kopen en in het museum te bekijken. Diverse kunstenaars mooie beelden, foto's, fijn houtwerk en schilders. net alsi n een restaurant vindt je hier kunstenaars als assanna Gassaama en isa djopp met mooie sculpturen.

title: Qualité trop inégale
text: Un de ces marchés à destination des touristes. Quelques artistes mais beaucoup de marchands. Des bibelots, peu d’œuvre véritables d’artistes.

title: zawrót głowy
text: Trzeba mieć bardzo silną wolę,żeby nie wydać wszystkich pieniędzy.Jeśli się zdecydujecie na zakupy , tzreba się bardzo, ale to bardzo targować- cena wyjściowa  wielokrotnie wyższa od tej ,za którą ostatecznie kupuje się jakąkolwiek rzecz- warto.

title: De belles trouvailles
text: Là-bas, rien à avoir avec les marchés où on trouve des articles génériques poussés par des marchands harcelants et féroces négociants. Là-bas, vous ne trouverez que des pièces uniques et des artistes généreux, désireux de vous parler de leur démarche artistique et de leur création. Aucune pression d'achat. Ce fut notre dernière activité à Dakar, un peu choisie au hasard, et nous ne retournerions plus dans cette ville sans une visite au Village des Arts.

title: inaspettato e generoso
text: Ci siamo capitati un pò per caso, in un pomeriggio in cui i piani originari erano saltati. Si è rivelato una delle più belle, intime e soddisfacenti esperienze di questo viaggio in Senegal. Il villaggio va esplorato con lentezza, fermandosi a parlare con gli artisti che hanno qui i loro ateliers e magari ammirarli all'opera. Non siate timidi, e se vi offrono un mango appena raccolto, accettate l'invito...

title: Attention
text: Attention à l'arnaque il faut bien négocier les prix et de préférence être accompagné d'un sénégalais. Rares sont les articles intéressants sinon un petit souvenir permettrait d'immortaliser le voyage.

title: Same art over and over again
text: I was expecting more original pieces at this place. I found only two places where artists were creating original pieces otherwise most of the artists were re-creating the same pieces over and over again. It is also a test of nerves to get through here as everyone wants you to come in their shop (even though most of it is the same). Everyone was nice so there was no worry that way but you have to be persistent that you are not interested. I really hope this place can attract new and upcoming artists as it would make for a very pleasant way to spend the day.

title: Peace and love
text: An island of peace in the heart of the burning Dakar. I go there every sunday when i am in town. Must see absolutely when you are in Dakar. You can eventually buy some nice paitings.

title: Typique, rencontre avec les artistes
text: En termes de qualité artistique on trouve un peu de tout....le point fort c'est le côté typique de l'endroit, une enfilade d'ateliers, et la possibilité de discuter avec les artistes. On y trouve de riches idées, des talents..inégaux...

title: If the vendors allow you to browse ...
text: The place is full of mass-produced items. But the quality is not bad and if the vendors actually let you browse in peace, you will find unique items (I did). It is just a hassle to look and explore without being harassed. Also, the initial price you get is at least 4-5 times higher than what you can actually end up paying for. But it's better than Sandaga market in every possible way. Worth a visit.

title: DA VEDERE
text: Non  vi prenderà molto tempo quindi un paio d'ore io cercherei di dedicarle a questa, tipo, galleria d'arte a cielo aperto

title: Un endroit pittoresque
text:
Nous avons eu la chance d'être accompagnés lors de notre passage mais il est facile de voir que ça peut devenir désagréables pour les touristes.

Mais un incontournable pour se procurer des produits des métiers d'arts locaux.

title: Better Than The Markets
text: A village of talented artists. Adjoined studios located in a village like setting.  Authentic originals that is a cut above the mass marketed "art" in the local tourist markets and side of the street sales.   You can visit the studio, see the artist at work, buy or commission pieces. A little pricey for some,but they are authentic and some genuinely beautiful pieces.  The village appears to be open at all hours, but not all artists are always there. There's a great variety of studios featuring many different works in 3D, stipple dots, paint, sculpture, pottery (they have a gigantic kiln), tapestry, glass, tile, unusual objetsd'art and some collectibles ---- just about any type of original artwork.  The village is a short drive from Dakar...close to the stadium so you get a good cultural exposure before you get to the village. There is a large exhibition space and flyers for upcoming art events at the village and at various places in Senegal. Visiting artists would like it.Tourists have a good exposure to some of the areas most talented trained professional artists.

title: Amazing Arts place full of surprise
text: The Village of Arts of Dakar is amazing. A local friend of mine took me there, and I was privy to Artists in the middle of their work. The quality is amazing, and the artists are very welcoming. As we were visiting, one of the artists was getting ready to go on a world tour to Germany, and Brazil, and gave us a tour of his work. At the end, we stumbled upon some musicians rehearsing, and they gave us a little concert. It was good and unforgettable. I recommend it to all.

title: Besuch der Festung
text: Sehr schön restaurierte Anlage leider war eine Videoinfo durch Stromausfall (normal auf den Kap-Verden) nicht möglich, insgesamt sehr beeindruckend, die Aussicht von der Anlage ist traumhaft - für kleinere Kinder nicht unbedingt geeignet (war mit meinen Enkeln dort 1 und 4 Jahre) aber ein Ausflug dorthin lohnt sich

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Interesting place to visit
text:
The fortress has been reconstructed to a good standard. There is a 15 minute video about the fortress and other places in the old capital which is good.
Look for the cannon made in tudor England which came from Drake's ship.
 An impressive place to visit.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Beetje duur
text: Ik weet niet hoor, jongens. Mooi uitzicht en het fort is nog in mooie staat en alles (en er is ook museum met een film die heel lang duurt en die je heel vaak kunt zien), maar de indruk die het meest bij me achterbleef was dat het zo duur was. Tsja.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Mächtige Festungsruine mit Panoramablick
text:
Die Festung wurde 1590 von den Portugiesen errichtet, um die ehemalige Hauptstadt Cidade da Riebeira Grande vor Piraten zu schützen. 1712 wurde die Stadt und die Festung trotzdem vom Piraten Jaques Cassart erobert und zerstört. Die Portugiesen bauten diese im Jahr 1960 wieder auf. Die mit historischen Kanonen bestückte Bastion bietet eine imposante Aussicht über die Bucht und Cidade Velha.
Für Besucher gibt es ein kleines Informationszentrum mit einem Film über die Entstehungsgeschichte.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Great history
text: When you go with a guide you will be told the whole historic background of this fortress. Interesting to know howthe old city was protected and rebuild

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Interesting History
text: Very nice visit and I recommend hiring the local tour guide to walk you through the fort and explain the history of the area.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Un coin d'histoire
text: Ce fort a été entièrement restauré sur un nid d'aigle qui permet de très belles vues sur la côte et le village. La petite vidéo est assez intéressante. Une jolie balade débute à côté de la billetterie, va longer la falaise de la Ribeira Grande avant de descendre dedans et revenir par la rua banana.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Guide impressionnant!
text: On commence par une vidéo... devrait être actualisée (qualifie le site comme candidat patrimoine de l’Unesco alors que c’est le cas depuis 2009) et n’est pas très bien faite. Par contre le guide est exceptionnel! Dans un très bon français, il a donné un tas d’explications, ce n’était pas récité, on voyait bien que c’était une personne cultivée qui pouvait parler de plein de choses et qui expliquait les raisons. Son récit nous a captivés, on a bu ses paroles et il avait une réponse pour toutes nos questions. C’est une personne passionnée et passionnante, on a adoré.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Belles vues et c'est déjà pas mal...
text: Les vies sont incroyables autour de forteresse, mais je ne sais pas s'il a autre chose à voir... l'intérieur paraissait pas si grand...

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Imponente
text: Conhecer esse lugar, foi histórico a fortaleza é imponente e faz parte da bela de Cabo Verde, sem dúvida um ponto turístico para ser visitado.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Historia Portuguesa com vista para o Mar!
text: A fortaleza Real de Sao Filipe e um testemunho da presença Portuguesa em Cabo Verde.Com vistas panoramicas unicas sobre o mar e cidade velha.Bem conservado e merece uma visita.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Em local priveligiado
text:
A Fortaleza Real de São Francisco ou da Cidade Velha, está bem conservada e localizada num local com vista fantástica.
è merecedora de uma visita e leva-nos a momentos históricos inolvidáveis.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: A voir, , belle vue sur le village
text: Si vous le pouvez, ne vous faites pas déposer sur le parking de la forteresse. En partant de la place, y monter à pied en traversant le village cela permet d'avoir un aperçu de la vie des gens. Nous y avons fait de belles rencontres.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Visite très intéressante
text: Pour nous c'était La visite de l'île. Le film projeté expliqué bien toute l'histoire de ce fort. Puis le guide, nous a donné tous les détails à l'histoire du fort. Vue magnifique sur le village en contrebas.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Forteresse de citade velha
text: Une belle forteresse reconstruite sur la base des ruines laissés par le temps. La vue est imprenable et avec un bon guide l'histoire de la piraterie et des premiers balbutiements du peuple capverdien se font sentir.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Interesting
text: Nice walk to the top of the hill. It offers great views of the area and the walls are still quite imposing.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Fortaleza reconstruida
text: Es una fortaleza reconstruida encima de la ciudad vieja. Desde allí tienes una bonita vista. Lo mejor de la fortaleza son las explicaciones del guía, que era muy simpático y te hacia ver las cosas.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Gut renovierte Burganlage
text: Diese Burganlage sticht unter den überschaubaren Sehenswürdigkeiten der Insel durch einen guten Renovierungszustand auf. es gibt auch einen Film über die Renovierung.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe

title: Point final d'une belle randonnée
text: Un joli chemin suit le fond de la ribeira. On peut ensuite monter jusqu'au plateau (petit village) et rejoindre le fort. L'accueil y est remarquable, la visite intéressante.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Très beau lieu
text: Le prix de l'entrée est de 500 escudos. La visite comprends un vidéo de 15 minutes en anglais et une visite guidée de 25 Minutes. Le tout n'étant pas très intéressant, il vaut mieux connaître l'histoire de se fort attaqué par le célèbre Sir Francis Drake et s'en inspirer. Il permet d'avoir une très belle vue sur Cidade Velha et je recommande la visite. Ma note est sévère car avec un tel lieu, de la promotion, rénovation sera bienvenu et aussi la création d'un musée serait très intéressant. A developper

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: The view alone of the ocean makes it worth while!
text:
We arrived there after going to the Kakum National Park and the view towards the ocean is just breath taking!
We had hired a tour guide with a driver, and it took alot of pressure off, we could just enjoy the sights.
The castle is a slave castle with every possible disgusting behavior towards the slaves that you could imagine being done in the 1890’s. Although slavery has been abolished, my perspective is that it just changed names and we call it now : human trafficking. I wish they would touch on that a little, but I guess that would not be too popular with the tourists!
All the same, a beautiful coast line, I don’t regret any moment of this sight!

title: Visit to the Cape Coast Castle
text: Had a wonderful black slavery historic tour experience for the first time at the cape coast castle with Worlanyo Tours. I loved it.

title: Qualcosa di nuovo per un italiano
text: Tra le cose da vedere sicuramente deve esserci il Castello di Cape Coast, una residenza coloniale da cui partivano gli schiavi per l'intera Europa. È toccante vedere le prigioni. È carino perché è comuqneu qualcosa di diverso per chi è abituato ai Castelli Europei. Nulla di eccezionale, ma racconta un po' di storia. C'è anche un piccolo museo all'interno.

title: Echoes from Africa's Tragic Past- The Slave Trade at Cape Coast, Ghana
text: This is a place which provokes in one a mixture of emotions that are difficult to describe. One can actually feel the anguish, fear and humiliation slave men and women must have felt in the dark slave dungeons. The slaves did not know any crime they must have committed to deserve such dehumanisation. Families were ripped apart, family history was lost, centuries old culture was lost and all sense of humanity was sacrificed for filthy lucre.

title: Guide group
text:
We visited here as part of a weekend rest from our project. Yes it was a standard tourist stop but great information in the museum plus a tour guide made our visit very interesting and informative.  Sadly we can’t turn back the clock and remake history but good to acknowledge it and make sure that in future respect for individuals and nations is paramount. 
Great views for photos too.

title: Incredible History
text: Visited with friends. A very intense and emotional tour which should be experienced by everyone. The guide was well prepared.

title: Cape Coast Castle
text: Though a Ghanaian and a guide anytime i get the chance to take people to the castle to learn about the slave trade it reminds me how far the world has come in abolishing such dehumanizing atrocities. The guides at the castle are professional, knowledgeable and great.

title: you will never be the same again.
text: Our tour guide was outstanding. It is very very heavy duty, emotional experience, and one that I will never forget. I am forever changed by this experience.

title: Castillo de esclavos
text: Toda la costa está sembrada de estos castillos, de tiempos coloniales donde el lucrativo negocio de los esclavos estaba en auge.

title: Worth to visit
text: You can read it history book but to see is a wow. Tour includes to entry price, 40ghs. You can visit old cell, torture rooms, market place, also there is museum.

title: Eens leuk om de lokale kunststukjes te bekijken
text:
Een leuk uitstapje. Je kan in dit kunstenaarsdorp de lokale kunstwerkjes bekijken en aankopen tegen een schappelijke prijs.
Hier vind je zeker een geschenkje of herinnering om thuis met heimwee terug te denken aan dit gastvrije land

title: Souvenir kingdom
text: Интересная деревушка по соседству с живописным пляжем с рыбачьими лодками.Сувениры на любой вкус-маски,фигурки,картины,красивое серебро,даже шкуры питона.Цены высокие,сразу надо опускать минимум вдвое.Местные ремесленники любят торговаться,картины яркие и профессионально нарисованные-такой местный Монмартр под деревом.Попросите гида познакомить вас с старейшиной посел��а,очень колоритный персонаж.Рекомендую посетить,тем более,что в Дакаре смотреть особо не на что.

title: Le calme au milieu du brouhaha ambiant
text: Le Village des Arts est un incontournable... Cet endroit paisible regroupe  des artistes de toutes tendances confondues. Vous pouvez y aller en toute confiance... Les artistes sont à votre disposition pour parler de leur arts sans vous "forcer la main"...

title: Belle visite, artistes intéressants dans leurs ateliers
text: J'ai beaucoup aimé cette visite dans un lieu qui avait beaucoup de charme, excellent accueil des artistes présents , très belle galerie avec une expo de qualité, ai pu discuter avec plusieurs peintres, avec un photographe talentueux (qui fait bcp de très beaux flous).. j'ai été agréablement surprise par la qualité des ouvres présentées.

title: Деревня хандмейда
text: Ездили группой специально закупить побрекушки. Деревня жилая, местные ремесленники  зарабатывают только изготовлением и продажей. Торговаться не получилось, они сделали вид, что на не понимают)

title: Dommage !
text: Vraiment dommage que les rabatteurs et certains artisans se manifestent de façon aussi pressante, voire agressive !

title: Some of the most beautiful art I have ever seen is in this village
text: I was introduced to the head man who then took me around the village.  Be sure to tip.  They do not ask but it helps the village.  The artists were friendly and love showing their work.  It varies from folk to very sophisticated works and their is sculpture as well.

title: worth a trek out to it
text: Some really interesting artists out here. Much was of a high quality and the artists were very welcoming. Difficult to find though.

title: Obscure but interesting place, great to visit during the Biennual
text: This is an alternative place where artists have their working spaces. It was very nice during the Biennale Dak Art because all artists working there were exposing their work.

title: Un peu de tout
text: Bijoux, vêtements, tableaux, breloques, sacs...Difficile de ne pas acheter. Se faire accompagner par "quelqu'un qui connaît" pour négocier les prix souvent excessifs

title: Un fouillis un peu triste!
text: J'ai entendu parler du Village des Arts de Dakar, en France. Je me faisais une joie de le visiter et de rencontrer les artistes ayant exposé en France. Las! Je suis tombé dans un fouillis où quelques peintres désœuvrés traînaient de ci de là! Quelques belles rencontres tout de même, heureusement!

title: Artwork is not that interesting, unfortunately
text: We should have realized that this was not going to be a great place to view or buy art when our taxi driver could not find the place and then actually left us at the wrong place. The place seemed to be in a torpor, with only some artist workshops open and the art museum closed. It did not seem like many tourists visited this place, which was a bit rundown.  We saw just one other tourist while we were there, visiting with a local artist. Most of the artwork was not of high quality. We had hoped to purchase a mask for our collection, but alas, did not.

title: Its where we can find all the amazing of craft arts, no question that is perfect for good shopping in Dakar
text: Going to Dakar and not pass by this Village Artisanale how they cal it its for sure a big mistake, we can find so much and so beautifull pieces. definatelly a important place to visit

title: for art lovers
text: I was the only visitor. This is a real artists colony. Each artist has his/her own space where they work and sell their art. There is also an exhibition hall that was featuring the art of a single painter when I visited. The whole place is shaded by mango trees. Art lovers will feel at peace here. Bring money. Buy art. Prices are very reasonable and the art is quality and unique.

title: Génial
text: Vous tomberez sur le charme de bon nombre de petit souvenir voire chef d'oeuvre qui viendront orner votre intérieur à votre retour de vacances. De nombreux petits cadeaux à petit budget. Enormement de concurrence sur ce site aartisanal, alors restez zen et surtout n'hésitez pas à marchander les prix.

title: Real Art Camp with Attaya
text:
If in Dakar, one of the not so crowded inspiring places to visit. Interact directly with famous artists such as ElHadj Sy, Ibou Kebe, or emerging ones like Kara.
You can explore large sculptures wooden or metallic made as well as all works of artists who exhibited in Korea, New York, Paris or Tokyo. Really amazing place!
Good for family day- just bring your drinks along.

title: Full of touristy knick knacks with a couple interesting items
text: Although it is a pleasant outdoor place to shop for crafts, most items here are made for mass consumption and are available almost anywhere else in Africa.  Therefore, if you are looking for a unique and valuable piece of Africana art or crafts, this is not the place.  One shop has an impressive collection of genuine African masks, but the shop is cluttered, dingy and dirty and many pieces have not been restored.  One leather shop was selling incredible full length anaconda skins and crocodile hides.  Other than that there is nothing to buy here.

title: La richesse des artistes sénégalais en un lieu
text: Sculpture, peinture, et les ateliers des artistes avec des rencontres passionnantes sur leur art en direct quand ils sont là.

title: Go to the Village des Arts a Yoff
text:
People below are mixing up two places:

Village des arts next to football stadium at Yoff is perfect. The original artists are here.

Village des arts next to fish market at Soumbedioun is less interesting.

title: Look at the sculpture!
text: Not too many artists were around when I was there, and the gallery was locked. However the scene was intriguing, and the many big sculptures were there to see.

title: Dodgy stairs
text:
Not a lot to see to be honest although I never bothered venturing upstairs, one of our party who did fell down them with quite a bump.

Don't go out of your way for this.

text: En engelsman bjöd in mig att bo i en av hans hyreslägenheter ute på Mindelo. Vi tog bussen in till centrum och vandrade runt i Mindelo under en hel dag ! Jag gillade staden och kan rekommenders andra att vandra runt i just Mindelo och se dess sevärdheter.

text: Dizem que e uma replica da Torre de Belém nao achei parecida, e um edifico que ao passar na rua principal de Sao Vicente ve logo. La dentro nao tem nada para ver.

title: À faire
text: Il faut visiter la tour de Belem est son musée. En plus, si vous avez le courage de monter tout en haut vous aurez une vue magnifique sur la ville.
