title: high above Cidade Velha
text:
Travelling by taxi from Praia it makes sense to branch off to the right first, before descending to Cidade Velha proper. Soon one arrives at the Fortaleza de São Filipe. Only here, at a small information center, one can buy a ticket for 500 Esc (5 €) per person, valid also for the other sights down in Cidade Velha.

At the information a 15-minutes video is shown about the fort. We then walked around its outer fortifications, before going to a closed gate, which the man in charge at the information center had to open for us.

The Fortaleza, once built in the 16th century as a defense against pirate attacks, sits about 120 meters above Cidade Velha. A footpath leads down towards the village by the sea. Since Cidade Velha and its fort had been completely destroyed by a French pirate in the 17th century and were then given up in favour of Praia, not much had been left up here, until Portugal decided - at the time of Salazar, who was keen to glorify Portugal's past in all the colonies - to reconstruct the whole fortification. Thus what one sees dates mainly from 1960, although all was done to stay as close as possible to the original.

More than the fortress itself, we enjoyed the views to the achada and the mountains to the west and down to Cidade Velha and out over the sea. In the middle of the fort is a cistern with a dome, which one can enter and then descend on a spiral staircase made of iron. Near the information center is a also a small bar, where one can buy something to drink.

title: Schon der Aussicht wegen
text:
Für Geschichtsinteressierte ein Muss, auch die Aussicht auf cidade velha ist perfekt. Man schaut sich zuerst einen gutgemachten Film an, dann besucht man die renovierte Anlage, dann gibt es dort noch Getränke und Snacks. Die Burg ist für Europäer nichts besonderes. Interessant ist die Geschichte. Nachdem wieder einmal europäische Piraten die Gegend überfallen, geplündert und dort gemordet hatten gab Philipp II im 16. Jahrhundert den Auftrag zum Bau dieser Burg, wobei das Baumaterial von Europa herangeschafft wurde.
Bis 1712 war die Burg ein Schutz für die Bewohner der Umgebung. Dann schaffte es wieder ein Freibeuter, die Burg und die Umgebung zu zerstören.

title: Historically Preserved
text: This was a beautiful experience. After visiting the Pelourinho, the Convento and the churches, we decided to stop here on the way out of Ribera Grande. Entrance fee is 500 escudos per person and includes a 15 minute introduction video. You will then be escorted to the entrance gate in the fort and you are free to walk around within its boudaries. There are posts with information about the preservation project and a bit of the history about the area; they are written in Spanish and Portuguese. Amazing views of Cidade Velha and the waterfront from up top and you can see the mountains to the west and north behind you. Wonderful spot for a picture and to feel the fresh, nonstop ocean breeze. Safe travels! A bus ride back to Praia is about 70 escudos per person from here. And the cab with range, but no more than 1000 escudos to drive you back to your location.

title: Start your visit of Cidade Velha here, for the views
text: This is a must see if in Praia.  Give yourself an hour to drive here on your way to or from the airport.  As the ancient city was the first city built by Europeans in Africa, it’s worth a visit.  There is an ancient fort built atop a hill overlooking the old town with an amazing view up and down the ravine/valley next to which the old town was built, as well as an amazing view out to see.  There is no need to pay to enter the fort, but a look from its walls was nice.  Continue down into the town to see the ancient slave whipping post, an ancient street dating back to the 1400s, ruins of the first cathedral in Africa, and the oldest remaining and operating church in Cape Verde.

title: Wonderful historic monument
text:
I've visited this place during my free time while on business trip in Praia.
If you're planing a trip to Cidade Velha, you should definitely plan the visit to the fort as well. To get there take a right turn from the main road Praia - Cidade Velha just before the road starts descending towards the town.
There is a small bar and souvenir stand in front of the fort and a bit left of it is the visitors center where you can buy admission tickets (500 CVE per person) and watch a 15 minute movie describing the history and restoration of the fort and nearby church called "Convento de São Francisco".
Once you enter the fort itself you will be amazed with the view it offers and you can easily imagine how it looked back in 16th century serving as the main coastal and land defense against privateers, pirates and other invaders.
Sadly the information board within the fort are in Portuguese only and not well maintained (some are barely readable due to sunlight exposure) but none the less, the views you get to see pay off for this.

title: Best market in Dakar
text: Yes the vendors can be pushy, but much less than many of the other markets, especially Goree' (hate the vendor there!).  I bring all the newbies here.  I feel much less stress than other places, it's not as crowded, the people are nicer, and the pickpocket threat is lower.  Lots of good art to be had, many manufactured on site.  Don't be afraid to say no - they'll live.  Whatever price they come in at, you can expect to settle for 1/3 if you bargain hard.  Even if you pay too much, though, at least you know it's going to feed their families.  Senegalese are good people - support the arts and the people too.

title: Imperdibile per l'arte
text:
Si trova a Route de l'aeroport
Yoff Dakar, vicino allo Stadio di calcio. È facile da visitare ma se volete approfittare di parlare con gli artisti dovete dedicare mezza giornata.
Ogni artista ha il suo atelier che usa spesso anche come abitazione. C'è anche una galleria comune che li rappresenta ed espone opere di tutti.
È una splendida occasione per conoscere l'arte contemporanea del Paese. Prezzi ottimi!
Per veri appassionati!

title: village des arts e non mercato dell'artigianato
text:
leggendo le recensioni mi sono accorto che la maggior parte delle persone ha recensito il mercato dell'artigianato che è tutt'altra cosa in tutt'altro luogo.
village des arts è un piccolo rione in cui in un edificio centrale c'è una mostra collettiva di tutti gli artisti che lavorano li, poi girando ci sono i vari studi dei vari artisti in cui si può entrare, guardare e chiaccherare con loro. Nessuna pressione per vendere, ambiente molto rilassato, a me hanno offerto un caffè e poi in un altro studio un te e si parla di arte. Ci sono quasi esclusivamente pittura, bronzi e ceramiche. Belle opere e, a differenza del mercato dell'artigianato, vera arte e non cose create in serie per i turisti. 
E' davvero una bella idea riunire gli artisti in un villaggio così in pochi metri si possono conoscere tutti. 
Va visitato anche se un po' fuori mano (vicinissimo allo stadio Leopold sedar senghor)

title: bell'artigianato sì, ma con poca originalità

come biglietto da visita c'è il solito degrado, baracche trasandate e sudicio in giro, è mai possibile non tenere all'ordine e alla pulizia neanche dove si tengono i propri manufatti e dove si ricevono clienti? Comunque a parte questo ci sono bei dipinti e bell'artigianato che però poi ritrovi replicato in tutto il mercato. E' anche un problema curiosare perchè come ti soffermi ti viene subito proposta la vendita. 
Abbiamo fatto un acquisto che solo di contrattazione ci è costato più di un'ora di tempo, ovvio che per tentarne un secondo bisogna proprio essere motivati, anzi di più!

title: El lugar de compras para turistas en el Centro de Dakar. Regateo 100%.
text:
Artesanía local, cuero, telas, collares, pulseras, imanes, bronce, cinturones, carteras...y un largo etcétera de artículos para turistas a precios asequibles, si se sabe regatear, pero de una calidad mejorable.
Aún así se pueden encontrar objetos en determinadas tiendas que pueden ofrecer cierta calidad, como son los bolsos de señora de imitación, en cuero, piel de cocodrilo o de avestruz. En algunas ocasiones, los dueños de las tiendas, al paso del turista despistado pueden llegar a ser un poco insistentes, nada que no pase en otras partes del mundo. Aún así puede ser una experiencia buena, como parte del encanto a la visita dakaroise.
El regateo es parte de la costumbre a la hora de cerrar el trato. Pero que nadie se equivoque, el visitante nunca ganará en este negocio. Como mucho se llevará una buena oferta si es insistente y habla algo de francés.

title: Wonderful artistic colony in Dakar
text: Dozens of individual artists studios located in former barracks. Sculptors, painters, photographers. Many artists do found objects art pieces. Integration of different arts form recycling of old metals. All fascinating. Loved especially the studio of Kara Fall, who paints abstract works inspired by Dogon masks.

title: Museu do Mar
text:
Next to the lively and very worthwhile to visit Fish Market is the small replica of Lisbon's Torre de Belem, housing since 2014 the interesting 'Museo do Mar'. There are no opening hours mentioned and the entry fee is only 1 € (100 Esc). The museum is on 3 floors and with an observatory rooftop, and has no elevator.

Many different aspects of the sea in connection with Cape Verde are presented here. I liked the not too long, but informative boards in Portuguese, French and English in relation to each subject. 

One theme is Porto Grande, the big protected harbour of Mindelo with all its not too long, but important history, a lot related to the times of the British Empire. Underwater Archeology is also represented with finds from shipwrecks around the Cape Verde islands. 'Music and the Sea' is a theme in the city of Cesaria Evora with her song 'Mar Azul'.

Many Capeverdian seamen were once working on whaling ships from New England and later went to live there. This connection is well documented, especially with New Bedford. The whale itself and and the marine biodiversity in general are also paid attention here.

At the end of the visit it makes sense to go up to the rooftop to overlook one of the most beautiful harbours in the world.

text: In the centre of Mindelo, near the fish market and beach where you can watch the catch bring gutted (eels arrive in wheelbarrows!), lies the tower. The area was buzzing with local traders, ladies walking with bowls of anything on their heads, men waiting for work, car mechanics, bicycles and more fish.  This is a commercial port, not a tourist trap and all the better for it. Beware the wind whipping up sand from the beach and throwing it in your eyes. Never go before 11am artists like to sleep and quite a few have their Ateliers here with a bed…I have always enjoyed the exhibitions, and my last visit I was privileged to meet two young European Artists who were having an Art sabbatical in Dakar…if you love Art start your visit to Dakar here!

text: The shop owners can be somewhat pushy, but if you don't engage them you will be fine. The prices are to be bargained down. First price is never the last price. All in all a fun experience.

title: Must visit!
text:
I went to the Village des Arts this weekend to pick up an art piece I fell in love with while it was on exhibit elsewhere. The Villege is right next to the football stadium. Apparently, the stadium wax constructed by Chinese laborers who resided in the dorms. Once the stadium was built, the government gifted the dorms to artists.

It was quite an experience!  It's not an exhibition space, but rather a collection of studios for diverse Senegalese artists. They span all ages, from young people in their early twenties, to graybeards, some of the country's most reknown artists, working in different media. Senegal's foremost tapestriy weaver Mahmadou Wade, has a studio there, as does  El Sy, one of the country's leading artists. He actually created a piece for the World Cup in Brazil last year.  I also met a female artist, of which there are few, as it's apparently really tough for women  to be artists here. And in a couple of cases,  fathers and sons were working out of the same space. In one case, a man and two of his sons were using the same studio. You could tell from their different styles that it wax more than one person creating the art there. Ionly saw a small percentage of the art as most of the artists were out, their studios closed. I think that's to be expected as I went on a Saturday afternoon....what better time to wait prospective clients than that?

The art itself is powerful. I had to hurry out of some of the studios, as I sensed a very strong, and to me, disturbing presence (I'm pretty sensitive in these respects). If you want to buy exceptional Senegalese art, go here FIRST, before you go to Sambedioune. Qualitatively, there is no comparison!

A bargaining tip: whatever price they quote, slash at least in half, then haggle. Note that Senegal is a very relational society, so you can't just walk in and out of an artist studio. You chat with them, they want to know a bit about you. As El Sy said, "I don't sell my art, I only cede it". 

If only for the unique experience of meeting many artists, representing different styles, traditions and age groups do go. And hopefully like me, you'll bring home a little something extra!

title: Face to Face with World Class Artists!

title: The ideal place for your last day shopping
text: Yes, we spent good money in different shops in less than one hour (including a nice mask now hanging in my living room wall). Everyone tries to sell you his goods but they do not harass you as in other places. And just a few steps away there is the Soumbedioune beach where you can see the fishermen bring their catches in the afternoon and all the business around that industry. Happy pictures!

I did not like the experience at all. However, these is a good selection of local ware, wood carvings, jewellery, T-shirts, though one must be prepared to negotiate in order to get a good deal.

title: Definitely go to visit the artists' studios
text: We hae ben here many times and purchased art from the artists. It is definitely the best place to meet the artists as they are in their ateliers, working and welcome you politely and willing to talk if you so desire. We have been seduced by several and have a small collection for when we "crack" and purchase beautiful pieces. They have their own stories and it is well worth listening to them as you can learn so much about art, the international art scene (yes, almost all sell in US, Europe, Asia). Don't miss this village !

title: Not bad
text:
If you have nothing else to do on a Saturday in Accra, check the museum. It is right in the city center. There are some interesting things and it will give you something to do for an hour or so.
Most important, of course, is the whole part about the slave trading. Heart wrenching! If you are the sensitive kind, take a pack of tissue with you.
However, I found it was an excellent documentation of this major event in history. 
Worth the visit.

title: history
text: i love the museum so much, i was able to see things i have been told stories about. i really explored Ghana on this trip....... cant wait to get back. i couldn't get any photos last time. this time i will get lots.....

title: Ghanaian heritage
text: Quite interesting. I learnt about a lot of people who have come to Ghana over the years. However this museum is by no means world class considering it is a National Museum, was hoping and expecting for more

title: A Must see
text: whenever you travel to a new place, going to their museums first is a great place to begin to understand their cultures and histories. Ghana is made up of many families and each have a story to tell. Go see and learn!

title: Something to do for an hour
text:
I was expecting to see more history about the country before the Europeans arrived but to be honest there is very little on display about this time.
It isn't the largest museum so you only need an hour or so to go around.

title: Knowledgeable
text: A knowledgeable guide and an excellent introduction to Ghana. Go here first to learn about the country's history and culture.

title: História
text: O NAtional Museum of Ghana é passagem obrigatória em ACRA. Conta toda a História e mostra a Cultura deste pais Africano. Muito bom.

title: Too hot but very interesting
text: We went in the hottest time of the year, but it did get so hot that I found it hard to concentrate on what the tour guide was saying sometimes. But other than that, it was very informative and interesting

title: Ghanian History and Artefacts
text: You would enjoy every bit of it...make sure you ask for a guide! You would witness tit bits of Slave trade and the traditional kitchen. There is an attempt to exhibit the major cultures of Ghana as well as its natural resources.

title: Nice place to visit
text: Great museum and very informative. It has no AC so bring water and be prepared for the heat though. Plan to spend at least an hour, maybe 2 to look at all the exhibits. Definitely worth a trip.

title: Historical & Cultural Highlights
text:
A relatively small museum, the curators have managed to pack a great deal into the building. The museum provides an overview of significant Ghana history and also includes cultural touches about food, clothing, music and more.

I found the exhibit about the slave trade especially well done; it includes models, artifacts, and visuals that communicate this tragic chapter in world history.

There is a worthwhile sculpture garden on the museum grounds.

title: Pequeno e vazio, mas interessante
text: O museu é pequeno e estava vazio quando o visitei. Lá encontramos uma pequena coleção de achados arqueológicos e ítens que fazem parte da cultura e história de Ghana, como utensílios tribais, informação sobre a rota de tráfico negreiro, etc.... Não há audioguia disponível.

title: Excellent Overview of Ghana History and Culture
text: This Museum does an excellent job of familiarizing the visitor with the anthropology, history and culture of regions throughout Ghana.  The staff is friendly and knowledgable and will offer to personally guide you at no extra charge (though tips are appreciated).  Ask for Gloria.  Gift shop here has very competitive prices.  No AC.

title: Best guide ever
text: As we visited during a weekday, we were the only two people there. At first I thought is would be boring as it's not exactly the largest museum I'd ever been in, but we had a personal guide who was very informative. She spoke clearly and one could sense the emotion in her voice when she showed us the slave trade exhibits on display. this was my main reason for visiting anyway, but i found it a moving experience and would recommend this tour.

title: Interesting place
text:
We spent about an hour here and there was some decent displays.  Nothing crazy good.  Probably worth your time.  They did have fans on and it was an OK temperature.  The staff were very friendly.  Probably the most interesting display, for me, was on the slave trade.

The price is going up from 20 Cedi to 40 next month.

title: アフリカを学びました
text: なかなか大きくてテーマ別に展示がわかりやすくしてあります。結構長い時間楽しめました。有料ですがツアーで説明してくれる人がいるといいです。特に奴隷貿易の展示はよくできていました。後でケープコーストにいって奴隷城行く人は

title: An interesting hour, but expensive
text:
I went her with my family on New Year's Day. Firstly we were impressed that the museum was open on a public holiday, when most other things were closed!

The museum has some interesting artifacts and information on Ghanaian cultures as well as slavery. If you have already been to Elmina or Cape Coast this is a nice addition. However the first floor seemed to be a collection of things they couldn't fit anywhere else, with very little information. As other readers have said there were also no fans on the first floor and it was really hot!

The small shop is really worth a visit - some small items very reasonably priced without having to haggle at the market.

title: More than expected
text: The museum did present interesting exhibits about Ghana's history and customs and is worth the visit. Depending on your interests 2 hours should be enough time to browse the exhibits. I found it unfortunate that even the locals don't know where their national museum is located. Upon locating the museum there were only a handful (4-5) other patrons inside, all non-Ghanaian. I was particularly attracted to the slave trade/slave route maps as well as the exhibits on stools and kente cloth weaving.

title: Good place for antique lover
text:
This is a good place to visit for an antique lover, specially for those who are really interested in art and craft work. One should always know and understand each activity. 

The guide present guided us practically with all the details in the museum.

title: If you really have nothing else to do with 30 min.
text: I generally like museums and am interested in the history of Ghana. But this is really not worth the time and money. The sculpture garden is virtually ruined and the museum itself is a big room with some pictures in it and very few exhibits. Not to mention the fact that it is not air-conditioned....The only interesting part is about the slave trade and specifically one slave ship that left Ghana. I wish the Ghanaian people that some money will be invested in preserving their heritage and history.

title: Une superbe vue sur la vallée !
text:
Difficile de monter...mais le déplacement vaut la peine.
Une superbe vue sur la ribeira d'une part, et sur le village et la mer d'autre part.
On a du mal à imaginer qu'une bande de pirates ait pu anéantir cette place forte.
La réhabilitation du lieu est particulièrement réussie.

title: うーん。
text:
プライアにビザ取りで滞在しており、世界遺産ということで行ってみました。
街から乗り合いバスで1時間、観光客はわずかにいるばかりで、正直あまり行く価値は無いかと。
ただ、逆に観光地っぽくなく、地元の人たちと触れ合えるローカルな場所という意味では、良かったかな。

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: 景色はいいです
text: プライアからバスというか乗り合いバンで1時間ほど。シウダーベリャの町の上の丘にあるポルトガル時代の要塞跡。入口が町はずれにあって、歩いて行ったら結構へばりました。世界遺産なので期待してきましたが、うーん、景色がいいだけであんまり遺跡っぽさがない。

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Maravilloso lugar
text:
Lugar con mucha historia , para maravillarse con la estructura, 
Muy turístico, una vista espectacular, mucha cultura , hay que pagar para ingresar, solo para los turistas es la tarifa , pero vale la pena cancelarlos.
Recomendado al turista que gusta de historia y cultura.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: muito interessante
text: local extremamente interessante, muito bem recuperado, com imenso significado histórico, vale sem dúvida uma visita

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Indispensable pour comprendre l'histoire du Cap Vert
text:
Prendre le temps de visionner le film (en français!) expliquant l'histoire de Cidade Velha, ancienne capitale de Santiago et ainsi l'histoire de la colonisation par les hommes de l'archipel du Cap Vert.
Restauration exemplaire. Point de vue à couper le souffle. Un des rares vestiges du passé qu'il est indispensable de visiter.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: warto zobaczyć !
text: Do fortecy doszłyśmy z katedry, drogą a właściwie ścieżką przez wieś. Zakup biletu za 5 euro, potem film o fortecy i innych zabytkach w Cidade Velha. Na koniec najważniejsze bo zwiedzanie fortecy. Na jej terenie stare działa, mury. Mnie najbardziej podobał się zbiornik z wodą, który znajduje się na dziedzińcu.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Forteresse Real de San Felipe
text: Belle forteresse avec vue sur la mer. Avant d entrer, cela vaut la peine d aller regarder la projection du film qui donne un aperçu historique de la ville et des différents sites à visiter. Nul besoin de guide, un bon chauffeur de taxi suffit.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Im Paket mit Cidade Velha empfehlenswert
text:
Wer geschichtlich interessiert ist, wird hier seine Freude haben. Es gibt einen Film in diversen Sprachen, danach kann man auf eigene Faust die Ruine erkunden und das Wissen aus dem Film hilft dabei sehr!!!

Der Ausblick ist beeindruckend, es gibt saubere Sanitäranlagen und auch Snacks und Getränke kann man hier kaufen. 

Wer mag folgt dem steilen Weg hinunter nach Cidade Velha, wo es viel zu entdecken gibt. Außerdem gibt es einen schönen, ruhigen und sauberen Strand mit einer kleinen Strandbar und einem Handwerksmarkt. 

Versuchen sie herzukommen, wenn nicht gerade die Touristenscharen der Aida einfallen, denn dann ist es überlaufen und ungemütlich. Es empfiehlt sich früh am Tag oder kurz vor Sonnenuntergang.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: forteresse au dessus de ciudade velha
text:
belle et ancienne forteresse situee au dessus de la vieille ville, prendre un guide parlant francais
possibilite de restauration simple a l entree du fort
le fort est le point de depart d une magnifique promenade de plus de deux heures sur le plateau puis descente au fond d une vallee luxuriantes avec tres beaux baobabs entre autres. bonnes chaussures de marche conseillees pour la descente caillouteuse.
on arrive ensuite dans la vieille ville au bord de mer

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Vistas impresionantes sobre la Ciudad y sobre la Ribeira
text: Puedes subir andando desde Cidade Velha, desde la parte alta donde está la catedral sigues subiendo por el medio de la Ciuf¡dad, no por la carretera de entrada, pregunta a cualquier lugareño y te lo indicarán , son muuuuy amables, mejor hacerlo cuando el sol no apriete demasisado, yo subí aslas cinco mas o menos. Otra posibilidad es que el Hiace te deje en el desvío para la Fortaleza y después bajas andando.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Nur der Ausblick ist schön.
text: Das Fort ist eigentlich langweilig, zu mindestens für mich. Aber der Blick auf das Tal Ribeira Grande und die alte Hauptstadt Cidade Velha ist sehr beeindruckend. Draussen löst man ein Ticket bei einem lustigen Mann. Zu essen und trinken gibt es hier oben nichts. Das gab es wohl mal, so steht es in den Reiseführern.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Monumento com muito interesse
text: Um dos monumentos do séc XVI, entretanto bem reabilitado, que vale a pena visitar. O guia é excelente, culto, mesmo quando de sai do tema principal. A vista é magnífica

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Amazing place that must be visited
text:
We arrive to Cidade Velha with a collective bus, it cost 100 CVE each, great experience with local people.
Once in the main square we walk up to the cathedral ruins, you cannot see that much here.
Then took a street an walk up to the Fortaleza, it's an easy walk and quick. Locals will help you if you cannot find it.
It cost 500 CVE to get in and it worth it. Fortaleza is an amazing place and Tino will explain you how is was distributed and the history, slaves, pirates...

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: History and nice vistas
text:
Enough of the fort is still there to imagine the history of the past. They also show a video to further enhance it. With the nice views of the old town it is eady to picture the importance of the buildings and all the work that went into it.
Well worth the 500 ESC:)

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Património classificado
text: Reerguido graças à cooperação com entidades espanholas e integrado no plano de reconhecimento da Cidade Velha como Património Mundial da Humanidade, este forte permite uma vista deslumbrante do que resta da antiga capital,  Ribeira Grande de Santiago, hoje Cidade Velha, sobre a ribeira de Maria Parda e, com alguma sorte em dias límpidos, pode ainda ver-se, para oeste, o vulto da Ilha do Fogo. A entrada é paga e o bilhete serve ainda para poder visitar o convento de S. Francisco na Cidade Velha.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Lieu historique à visiter
text: La visite de la Forteresse Sao Filipe de Cidade Velha (ex Ribeira Grande) fait rappeler aux forteresses déjà visitées tel que : Goré (sénégal), Cape Coast et Elmina (ghana). Malgré sa position dominante avec une belle vue imprénable et romantique sur le village et sur la vallée de l'ancienne place de Ribeira Grande et comme les autres, cette forteresse laisse imaginer tout le travail effectué et les souffrances subirent par nos frères qui étaient en captivité. Visiter ce lieu permet de revisiter l'histoire et de mieux comprendre ce qui s'est passé.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Recommended visit to this historic Portuguese fort. Good, short guided tour included in entrance fee.
text: Historic Portuguese fort high on a hill above Cidade Velha on Santiago Island, Cape Verde. Modest entrance fee included a dated 10 minute video in Spanish, about half of which had subtitles in English. Entrance fee also included a free guided tour by a not-so-official-looking local guy. He took us around the fort and showed us the major buildings and dwellings and also gladly took some group pictures for us. We tipped him an extra couple dollars. The view from the fort is quite amazing. Definitely a worthwhile stop.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Una storia ai più sconosciuta
text: Posto ricco di storia e paesaggisticamente stupendo, il primo posto da non perdere a Capo Verde. Da visitare con guida (prezzi contenuti) per cogliere a pieno quanto questo posto meriti di essere patrimonio dell'umanità dell'Unesco. Da non perdere anche la visita a Cidade Velha.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Celestino my new friend :-)
text:
Seriously, just take the guides tour. Celestino will give you some great insight not only about the fort, but also about the old city and cv history.
We were lucky to visit the fort in the afternoon when there was no one else around. Great experience and phenomenal panorama and views.

placeInfo.name: Fortaleza Real de San Felipe
placeInfo.address: Rua de Forteleza, Cidade Velha, Santiago 7629 Cape Verde

title: Worse than in Cape Coast or Elmina
text: If you have visited Elmina and Cape Coast castle, you won't be impressed. The Castle was built buy Danish in 1650-ies. As many castles on the Gold Coast, the Osu castle was used for slave trade. Right now it is a presidential palace and photos outside of the Castle are not allowed. The entry fee with a guided tour is 40 cedis.

title: A wonderful, if not sometimes sad, sense of history.
text:
The layers of history and architecture here is facinating, through early traders, the slave trade, the presidential palace, royal visits and the like.
It's a shame that it's not well-maintained as some lovely pieces of furniture, chandeliers etc. are being ravaged by time. One part of the gardens is a 'bone-yard' for wrecked government vehicles! :(

title: visite ?
text: Il nous a été impossible de savoir si on pouvait visiter. Après être allé sur place et avoir demandé à des ghanéens et à des résidents, nous n'avons pas eu le mot de la fin.

title: Castle with interesting history
text: You can only visit with guided tour. There is no official entry fee but you are expected to make a donation after visiting. The tour itself was interesting and you have nice ocean views from the castle.

title: Great disappointment!!
text:
Arrived to visit and was told that visitors had particular days to visit. As I am from the UK....Friday is the day. Unsure that this is correct as I saw lots of activities happening ...maybe an official function ? Who knows.!!
Was unable to return, so hoping to visit when i am back in Ghana.

title: Maintenance needed
text: The castle has the potential to be a great tourist attraction with a little care and maintenance. The courtyard has a beautiful garden unfortunately it also had many junked presidential escort vehicles on the grounds. This becomes a major eyesore and distraction to the visitors.

title: Ok tour but rather limited
text: I think it’s free to get in but it’s all a bit vague. The tour with the guide seems quite restricted in where you can go.

title: Impressive
text: It was very organised. The guide was very knowledgeable, professional and kind. I think her name was Matilda. There was a lot to see. A lot of history and well preserved. My experience was very different from some of the reviews that I have read here. I could not believe that it was actually free! I am glad that it will be undergoing extensive renovation over the next 2 years. Thanks for the history.

title: Historical
text: The castle has a lot if history around slave trade. It is a sad place because of the unpleasant history but it can make more money from tourists if better managed. Our guide was still learning and therefore could not answer most of our questions, but worth a visit.

title: A stupendous place.
text: An exhaustive guided tour of the renovated ,half-luxurious, half-deserted castle on a cliff overlooking the waves...And through the appalling slaves' confinement rooms leading to the "door of no return".

title: Osu Castle-An Empty Monument
text:
We were told the place was going to turned intoi a tour center where guests could go in to visit.
The politics went in a way over who should take charge.Who should run it.Museum and Monuments Board? A separate and autonomous body? MPs,chieftains,from distances eyed for ir becvause of their connections with the slave trsade.In a book I published I emphasized that Europeans can visit to see one of their monumental architectural edifices here.Boulders were put on board a ship,the Friedinsbourg,a slave liner to bring them down.The construction took over ten years.It was the seat of government.Very few people ever entered in.It had a beautiful garden inside. A mystery edifice built by the Danes during King Christian's tenure.It is full of hysory spanning over 200 years.My book,The Christansborg Castle,Basel Mission 21 and the Mulatoes of Osu,descendants of the few children left behind when the settlers were ordered to come home or face beheadment on the abolishing of the slave trade by Denmark.

title: Piece of astonishing history
text: I was in Accra for a conference and we came here as a group that had been arranged for. Perhaps my superb experience may not be realistic for the one or two enexpected individual tourists who rock up unexpected. But judged on what I had I would say that it's a compulsory place to go to - especially if you are an African and care a great deal for history. The castle itself has changed hands many time between the Danes, the Dutch, the British and ultemately the Ghanaians. You also have had post independence presidents some preferring to stay there as their presidential houses and some wondering how on earth could a president of a nation comfortable live and dine at a place of that was a major slave point for your people! But I liked the guide. I think his name is Samuel. He was very knowledgeable and objective in his commentary. We were a group of Africans, Europeans and Americans. I thought he was briliant in balancing sensitivity with the need to give out objective information of tourist value. But yes, the place urgently needs to be restored and it is clear a lot of money would be neccessary to do so. Otherwise, don't go there if you are an emtional black historical African. Great place. Very significant tourist attraction conveniently located on a beach in Accra.

title: the actual castle was great
text: a beautiful visit - the castle is worth going to, the view fantastic and the guide was so knowledgable and interesting. I learnt a lot.

title: Easy and important place to visit
text: My friends and I walked from the Mausoleum to the Independence Arch to Geese Park and finally to Osu Castle. We were happy to find a tour group to join and learned a ton. I was especially impressed with how the tour guide answered questions. He had a deep knowledge that helped me understand more than just what was presented at this one castle. I was later able to see Elmina castle and seeing two castles helps you understand how slavery functioned. The tour guide works on tips. Pay what you think it is worth.

title: Don't waste your time
text: Staff here are rude and unhelpful.  Came on a Tuesday, they said the place was closed, and to come back on Saturday.  Came on Saturday, they still said it was closed.  Realized they will say anything just to get you to go away.  This place could be a nice tourist attraction in a city that doesn't really have many; it's a shame they don't treat it as such.

title: Depressing dungeons .. Bad maintenance
text: So sad to see that the place is not well maintained .. A little TLC and this could attract a serious amount of tourists

title: very interesting place to visit
text: we visited Osu castle and it totally changed our view. We were not aware of how the slavery trade functioned in Ghana and this tour graphically show the stark conditions they were kept in. they are currently renovating the castle to include an exhibition of Ghanaian people who have influenced others through sport, literature, arts etc. worth the visit

title: Great Building
text: I had a chance to visit Osu castle in an official capacity.  I had a meeting with a minister on a certain regional matter.  While there, I took the opportunity to tour the place.  The castle has a lot of history which I will not repeat here, but it was great to see it in person.

title: Open to the Public at last!
text: Having visited Elmina and Cape Coast Castles, this was the missing piece of the key slave trade forts. A guide for a free tour is provided and a gratuity at the end is more or less expected. It is early days for this attraction – some of the steps are dicey but you do see enough to make it worthwhile. Seeing the ex-President’s office was unexpected. Be sure to look for the setting for the picture on the 50 cedi bill which is as you arrive/leave the compound, a value added architectural feature pointed out by our pleasant guide who coincidentally received a tip of precisely that denomination.

title: Castle in development
text:
I know the castle is not open for visitors for that long and that made us liking the castle, but we were not deeply impressed. The guide told me they're still working in opening some rooms. 

Personally I think they can do more with decoration, maybe they have access to old pieces they can show. That might build the story behind the castle a bit more. A shop with drinks and maybe souvenirs would be very cool. 

Anyways, the castle is very pretty and the location is amazing. I liked the guides they were very nice. I would recommend someone to see the castle!

title: family visit
text: historical interest, great educational the exit for the slave from West Africa. culture show and a lot of souvenir

title: 負の遺産の一つ
text: ガーナの原宿、オスの沿岸にあり、17世紀にデンマーク人によって築かれた城です。奴隷や金の貿易に使われた城であり、様々な西洋国家が代わる代わる占領した城です。現在は観光地として一般公開するために整備中ですが、無料で見学をすることも可能です。ガイドもおり、声をかければ城の中を案内してくれます。

title: Miss
text: I was guider by William, the caretaker of Osu castle, and he gave me a tour around the Castle and tid surroundings. The castle is of special interest for me because it started by Swedes. I recommend a visit!

title: We liked this stop
text: We were looking for another spot when we came upon Osu Castle. Our guide was knowledgeable, friendly, and not too pushy. We enjoyed this experience and are telling others they should go.

title: New
text: This just opened up for tourism and is opening up to many visitors now. It is the third of three castles in Ghana. If you don't want to go far to Cape Coast for a slave tour, it will be your best bet to learn more about the trade.

title: Historic Castle in Accra, worth a visit
text: Located seaside and not far from Independence square and the Accra Sports stadium, Osu Castle seems over-looked to tourist in Ghana. Yet it is rich in history – going back to around 1696 and housing the government of Ghana from 1957 until circa 2013. You can visit Jerry Rawling’s office – with his actual desk and chair. The gardens are nicely maintained. It is reportedly soon to be turned into a premier museum by the Ministry of Tourism.

title: il était une fois Sandaga ...
text: Ce marché qui a connu des heures de gloire de par son architecture et son ambiance est devenu un lieu d'arnaque ! prix prohibitifs, agressivité des vendeurs, très très loin de la fameuse Teranga ! reportez vous aux petits marchés de quartier vivants et colorés.

title: Be ready to be "helped"
text: A market to get your souvenirs, make sure you haggle with them about prices.  The fabric building which is where the tailors can make your custom clothing.  The textiles are expensive here compared to other places but the tailoring is a good price (10 USD a shirt)

title: Cauchemardesque
text:
Ayant eu plusieurs bonnes expérience dans les marchés locaux en Afrique de l'ouest, j'ai entraîné mon mari au marché de Sandaga. Quelle erreur!!! A peine descendu du taxi que nous nous faisions accoster par des vendeurs, la plupart sympathiques, pas plus collant que dans les autres marchés. Mais un monsieur sortait du lot. Il n'arrêtait pas de nous parler de son association 'les enfants du coeur' et comme quoi on devait les aider... bref on a été polis mais 5 minutes après il était toujours là juste à côté. Il commençait a être plus agressif en disant que le Sénégal c'est le 'terranga' le pays de l'hospitalité et que nous manquions de communications. Mon mari lui a gentiment dit que nous souhaitons visiter ce pays et son marché en paix... quelle boulette! Apparemment on a du lui faire ressortir un traumatisme d'enfance car là, il nous insultait de racistes (mon mari est blond et moi chinoise et surtout on est à Dakar...mouais faudrait qu'il m'explique sa logique) c'est là que mon mari a décidé de passer à l'autre côté de la rue en espérant qu'il allait lâcher l'affaire. .. eh non! Mon mari, assez vigilant, a pu voir que deux personnes avec des capuchons nous suivaient. Alors on rebrousse chemin en zig zagant pour éviter que les mecs nous suivent de trop près. Dès que l'on se rapprochait d'un étal les vendeurs reculaient carrément ! je vois déjà la catastrophe. .. heureusement on a sauté dans un taxi et lui a demandé de foncer. 3000 pour rentrer à l'hôtel, sans discuter aucun soucis. On se retourne et nous voyons le 'bon samaritain' entrain de consulter ses, pas 2 mais 4 collègues en pointant dans notre direction. Bon dieu!
Je reste dans ma cage dorée en attendant mon retour!

title: Chaotic, crowded, overwhelming
text:
This is a big crowded, chaotic market.  On the upside, you can find bout anything your looking for there.  Clothes, baskets, carvings, masks...you name it, its probably there.  You can get a good price too if you haggle.  Keep in mind when negotiating, there is a toobab price (local price x3) and a tourist toobab price (local price x10).  

On the down side, I went by myself and I almost regretted it because immediately three or four young guys surrounded me, each competing to "show me around".  They wouldn't take no for an answer, no matter how many times I repeated "no thank you" in both French and Wolof.  They followed me like they were glued to my hip pocket.  To be clear, I never felt unsafe, but it was a little overwhelming.  Knowing French is helpful with negotiating, Wolof might be a little better, but not at all necessary.

All in all, this is a pretty good experience if you really want to experience Dakar.  If you're looking for some good souvenirs and don't mind a little adventure, this is definitely the place.  Just go in with a sense of humor and keep a very close eye on your wallet.

title: Un des marchés les plus animés de Dakar
text: Le marché dispose de très nombreux petits "stands" où vous pourrez trouver du tissu, des habits, des livres...Il permet de voir l'animation dakaroise et de trouver souvenirs ou tissues pour vous confectionner des habits sur mesure.

title: è un immenso manicomio!
text:
non si può andare a Dakar senza visitare il mercato di Sandaga! E' una gran fatica però, se ti fermi a curiosare a un banco non ti mollano più, devi guardare dove metti i piedi perchè ci sono buche e sconnessioni varie, ogni tanto ti senti sfiorare da una moto a tutto fuoco o da un carretto pieno di mercanzie e a volte gli spintoni che ti arrivano servono a evitarti di essere investito. 
Ovviamente ci ha avvicinato un ragazzo con lo scopo di farci da guida, molto carino e cortese. Abbiamo cercato di evitarlo ma ci ha accompagnato  molto educatamente per un bel tratto di strada senza essere invadente, anzi allontanando gli scocciatori. Dopo un po' se ne è aggiunto un altro. Insomma per farla breve li abbiamo accettati tacitamente entrambi, Alì e Abdul, ci hanno scortato nel grande mercato. Abbiamo un po' conversato e alla fine ci hanno condotto nel grande magazzino delle stoffe. Questo posto è pazzesco, una palazzina zeppa di stoffe, con tante stanzette soffocate dai tessuti o bui sgabuzzini dove ragazzi chini su macchine da cucire confezionano senza sosta abiti su misura. Lì abbiamo fatto alcuni acquisti, sapendo di far guadagnare qualcosa ad Al' e Abdul, ma che fatica...la contrattazione è di rito e non la puoi evitare dal momento che ti chiedono tre volte il valore. A dire il vero non ho trovato poi molto da comprare, ma il pensiero di dover perdere tanto tempo a contrattare è stato un vero deterrente. 
Al momento di lasciare i ragazzi della "scorta" abbiamo dato loro una piccola mancia e i saluti sono stati sentiti e sinceri. Sono ragazzi semplici questi senegalesi e il loro ricordo è sicuramente un valore aggiunto al ricordo di questa splendida vacanza.

title: La les bornes ont été dépassées
text: Ce matin a Sandaga, en ballade avec un copain Francais et un ami Sénégalais, en famille. Mon ami rentre dans une boutique et demande le prix d'une robe. Le vendeur répond 150.000 Francs cfa ce qui correspond à 20 fois le prix environ. Nous déclinons l'offre. Le ton monte. Le Marchand finit par agresser physiquement notre ami Sénégalais, a 5 contre un. Certes c'est le première fois que que cela arrive en une dizaine de visites. Mais si c'est une tendance, les affaires vont devenir moins bonnes a Sandaga. Ami commerçant, fait attention, Internet is watching you !!

title: Un mercado mas. Nada fuera de lo comun.
text:
Interesante. Si. Bonito No. 
Un lugar corriente donde se vende de todo un poco. Sin clase ni cordura. El area es apretada y angosta. Hay que estar muy pendiente de las cosas personales. 
Si se esta en el centro vale la pena la visita. De lo contrario no amerita.

title: Heeeerlijk
text:
Het dynamische hart van Dakar 
Ik vind het altijd heerlijk om daar rond te struinen, al die kleuren al die geuren 
Mijn eerste keer vond ik de vele gidsen die zich aanboden best wel vervelend. Ik raad iedereen dan ook aan als toerist iemand mee te nemen die in Dakar woont
Inmiddels na vele bezoeken durf ik zeker in mn eentje de markt op te gaan, maar ik spreek inmiddels ook wel redelijk wolof de lokale taal. en weet ik precies hoe om te gaan met opdringerige verkopers, negeren heeft vaak geen zin, zeg vriendelijk nee bedankt big smile en vaak laten ze je dan wel met rust. vergeet niet dat voor vele verkopers een dag niets verkocht/ ook een dag niet eten betekent..Afdingen op de prijs is prima, er worden vaal enorme bedragen gevraagd, maar met gode onderhandeling kan er een prima deal worden gesloten. ding wel af met respect naar de verkoper, zij moeten er vaak een hele familie/gezin van onderhouden

title: TOUBAB! TOUBAB!
text:
Une expérience unique à condition de parler Wollof et de ne pas suivre aveuglément les amis qui connaissent des amis qui ont entendu des amis dire qu'ils ont des amis qui ont ce que vous cherchez...
Le meilleur moyen de se perdre dans les ruelles de Dakar et de finir plumé comme un pigeon.
Deux expressions à connaitre:
Dedet et Bayi ma!

title: Big, bustling market
text:
Sandaga is a big, bustling market, similar to many markets I have been to in West African countries, but if you are in Dakar, its a fun place to go to experience a facet of Senegalese life and culture...or to pick up some souvenirs to take home! 

If you are a "toubab," be prepared to get pulled in every direction by people trying to sell you things.  Don't take this personally, but if someone is bothering you, just be firm with them...although this does not always ensure that they will leave you alone.  Also, be prepare to bargain hard if you want a fair price!  If you are unfamiliar with the prices, or do not know French or Wolof, it may be best to bring a local along with you...it will likely make things a bit easier on you!

title: comme des mouches
text: à voir le marché sandaga, mais attention aux picpoket, tres habiles. sinon les pseudo vendeurs vous collent comme des mouches si vous etes toubab. meme en habitué.

title: Accrochez vous
text: Une expérience unique, mais en ces temps de crise touristique au sénégal les vendeurs ne lachent pas les toubabs ! Mais c'est à voir, on n'oublie pas cette visite.

title: Paradis
text:
C'est le premier endroit ou j'ai travailler à Dakar avec des Senegalais.
C'est un endroit merveilleux et très intriguant on y trouve tout ce que l'on veut c'est un lieu étonnant ou vendeurs, Senegalais, Toubabs, étc... Se côtoient toute la
Journée ! 

Lieux incontournable du plateau de Dakar

title: Dakar
text: Incontournable à Dakar la visite de l'île de Gorée et celle du marché de sandaga, il ne faut pas avoir d appréhension et se laisser embarquer dans les immeubles ou se trouve les boutiques et ateliers de fabrique

title: A faire par les touristes
text:
Si on visite Dakar, on ne peut pas rater le marché de Sandaga ! Marché atypique. Malheureusement les touristes ne sont pas épargnés et on ressort de cet endroit fatigué.
Tout se négocie et les prix peuvent être très différents selon la tête du client...donc méfiance !

title: A voir : la cour des orfèvres
text:
Selon notre chauffeur,  le marché a été démantelé car il empietait trop sur la circulation,  nos avons quand même trouvé un endroit nommé la cour des orfèvres (angle armand angrand et blaise ndiaye), avec un vendeur de peintures sous verre de grande qualité (prix annoncés moitié moins chez sur la côte des almadies), je vous le recommande !
Nous avons trouvé un grand marché local très agréable rue blaise ndiaye; attention,  il n'y a rien destiné aux toubabs dans ce marché,  il permet juste de s'imprégner de la vie locale.

title: You can find anything here, really!
text: I've been here searching for a carjack, paintings, costumes for a 1980s costume party, and I never leave disappointed.  If you're a taubab, you'll be approached when you arrived for someone to carry your things that you buy.  This is worth having someone do for you as it means everyone else will leave you alone in this otherwise hectic market.

title: Сувениры
text: За сувенирами и\мы поехали на этот самый рынок. Рынок большой, но покупателей, особенно из числа платежеспособных туристов там немного. Поэтому там будут разрывать вас на части. Многие продавцы говорят по английски. Зайдя в одну из многочисленных лавочек вы получите предложение раз в пять превышающее максимальную цену для изделия. В ходе торговли цена сбивается, наращивается количество экземпляров того же сувенира за эту же цену. Попытка уйти некупив будет сопровождаться преследованием, а также "Брат, ты же обещал купить...". Вообщем место оригинальное и судя по всему не совсем безопасное. Лучше всего появляться с местными друзьями.

title: Enorme
text: Um sítio enorme onde se encontra de tudo a toda a hora. Vale a pena visitar. Comprem as caixas de jóias a pele que são lindas.

title: Go to the second floor, it is more interesting
text: In the first floor you can see west african traditional equipments without any explanation (in French only). The second floor is more interesting as they show different Senegalese wrestles and their lucky charms they buy from their marabou aka voodoo..

title: Insightful cultural tour
text: Fantastic learning afternoon inside the IFAN Museum. The guide was knowledgeable and very thorough in taking us around the museum display.

title: vestige
text: une architecture coloniale superbe, bien entretenue en plein centre ville - peu de manifestations. le Musée d'art africain ne présente pas un grand intérêt et les pièces présentées sont mal entretenues - lieu exceptionnel pour les grandes expos, mais trop rares.

title: Das Gebäude ist interresant
text: Aber die Objekte, die noch vorhanden sind, zeigen, dass die guten Stücke illegal verkauft und unterschlagen wurden. Ein paar Masken wurden zur "Diebstahlssicherung" mit langen Schrauben durch die Nase an der Wand befestigt. Viel Sammler dieser Welt werden sich in ihrem Kämmerlein an den gestohlenen guten Stücken erfreuen können

title: Musée
text:
Je l'ai visité il y a longtemps, il faut y aller régulièrement car les expositions changent.
C'est une autre façon de découvrir la culture Africaine à travers tous ces objets, mises en scène, etc.

title: Visited the Dakar Women's Art Show
text: A wonderful place to visit, filled with light, and some very interesting art works..enjoyed the experience.

title: Not so impressive
text: Quite small collection of some typical West African artefacts, also from other countries than Senegal. In the second building there are thematical exhibitions - worth checking whats is going on at the moment.

title: Leider ausgeplündert
text: War früher das ethnographische Zentralmuseum für ganz Westafrika. Leider fast keine guten Stücke mehr da.

title: small but interesting
text: We went to IFAN to see examples of African Art. The museum was small but we enjoyed it. The first floor was devoted to African art from the region, while the second floor was devoted to wrestling

title: Small collection af West African traditional art
text: Big impressive building from the outside. Not that much inside. Liked the traditional masks and sculptures. Better than many other museums in Africa!

title: visite
text: tres leger , exposition permanante tres peut fournie  , peux de moyen et peux de volonté de faire mieux

title: Agradable resumen de la cultura y arte africanos
text: Es un museo pequeño, bastante bien organizado, y que permite una buena introducción a cultura y arte africano. Me gustó mucho la exposición que contrapone los utensilios tradicionales africanos con sus sustitutos de plástico, y el problema que generan estos últimos.

title: Da andare, ma che vergogna...
text: L'Ifan, recentemente ristrutturato, venne edificato negli anni Trenta e costituisce un bel complesso architettonico, uno dei primi realizzati in Africa dai francesi ispirandosi alle culture locali. Si tratta di due grandi stanze, con reperti provenienti dall'Africa occidentale, tutti molto interessanti. Malgrado la recente ristrutturazione le pulizie lasciano molto a desiderare, le teche sono coperte di polvere, i pavimenti sporchi e la signora "adetta" dove essersi disturbata alzandosi dalle sedie (tre in fila) sulle quali è abitualmente sdraiata riesce a farvi pagare il biglietto di ingresso, per poi tornare al suo meritato "riposo", senza dare nessuna spiegazione e senza fare il minimo sforzo per tenere puliti gli ambienti.

title: Wonderful African Art
text: If you have an interest in African Art, don't miss this place! They have a fantastic collection well appointed.

title: Curioso
text: En alguna de sus sales hay alguna cosa interesante, pero no relevante, aunque es curioso verlo y ver las diferentes facciones de la cultura e historia senegalesa por encima

title: Nice museum in Dakar
text: There aren't too many functional museums in Dakar. This one, now known as the Musee Theodor Monod, focuses broadly on ethnohistorical objects--masks, statuettes, etc.--than on art. It's well lit and has nicely presented objects and beautiful grounds. There is a thought-provoking exhibit on the top floor that looks at the impact of widespread plastic use in Senegal and how plastics have replaced more traditional naturally degradable materials in everyday life. Plastic use and the lack of an infrastructure that can deal with waste of any sort much less materials that do not decompose over time are huge problems in Senegal. It was nice to see a museum space dedicated to teaching kids and adults about how personal choices impact the environment.

title: Tres bien.
text: Visite interessante, de jolies pieces exposees et des expositions pertinentes, mettant en evidence la vie africaine

title: Good museum, worth visiting
text: You can cover this museum in 2 hours (or much less, if you don't read everything).  It's worth going and is educational, pretty well organized, and interesting.  Maintenance could be better, but they don't get a lot of visitors, I think.  It's a great perspective, however, on how fast Senegalese culture has changed and how much it has stayed the same in the past few decades.

title: Mi opinon del museo fue en otra atracciòn
text: Por favor leer la de Le Monument de la Renaissance Africaine .Me equivoque en situarla .Disculpas .Este monumento es muy interesante si se ha leído antes sobre su creación puesno hay ningun guia ni folletos

title: Bravo
text: Quel joli musé mais trop petit, il me semble que le Sénégal pourrai avoir un musée des arts bien plus grand, le tour du coup en est vite fait et pourtant des pépites s'y trouve, des masques, des lances, plein d'objets un effort à faire par le gouvernement pour que Dakar est un musée qui mérite ce nom

title: A quick look around, getting jumped at
text: Visited the Artisanal Center to look at some souvenirs. A lot of small shops with handcrafted masks, jewellery, etc. A a caucasian you get more than enough attention, insect repellant does not work here ;-)

title: L'art dans toute sa splendeur
text: Ce centre artisanal est situé en pleine ville de COTONOU au Bénin, entre la Bourse du Travail et le Hall des Arts. On y trouve de belles œuvres d'art. Il est recommandé de faire ses achats à cet endroit pour plus de garantie afin d'éviter d'acheter du faux, les vendeurs étant sur place. Je vous conseille de bien négocier les prix.

title: Very Good Artisanal Place
text:
I was there in May 2016. There you will have all you search like artisanal works: different kinds of collars, African, tambours, pictures and pieces of arts, traditional shoes.
And I can tell you the persons who work there know how to call and how to sell things, so if you are not interested just get away and look for what you came for.

title: Un bon resumé des activités artisanal du Bénin
text: Dans ce centre vous trouvez une grande collection des objets artisanals très jolies et bien faits. Les prix sont un peu élevés, mais avec un peu de temps vous pouvez battre les prix et obtenir des souvenirs superbes.

title: Handwerker- und Künstlerdorf
text: Wie überall in Afrika sind die Händler für den europäischen Geschmack eher aufdringlich - wären wir auch, wenn wir von der Hand in den Mund leben würden. Benin ist kein touristisch erschlossenes Land. Es kommen wenig Touristen oder Rucksackreisende, die nicht viel Platz im Gepäck haben. Das Land ist bitter arm und es ist gut, diese organisierten Kunsthandwerker zu unterstützen.  Auf einem großen Areal sind alle Arten von afrikanischen Handwerkern und Künstlern vertreten. Fangen Sie allerdings ganz hinten im Dorf an. Die dortigen Künstler bekommen selten Kunden, denn die Leute geben ihr Geld schon vorne aus. Ein geschützter Bereich. Hier kann man gut parken. Das Areal ist sauber und einladend.

title: Presque tout...dans un seul lieu
text:
Beaucoup de boutiques (et un restaurant) qui vendent un peut les mêmes produits, mais qui sont de bonne qualité.
Endroit parfait pour récupérer des adresses d'artisans ou autres qui se trouvent dans le pays, (donc à faire en début de voyage).

title: Few items for my son
text: One good piece of advice: go with a local you will get some good deals. The items are typical you bring from Cotonou Bénin and they are nicely done. They will not reap you off.

title: Patiente et longueur de temps font plus que force ni que rage
text:
On trouve de tout, de beaux articles artisanaux comme des articles dont la provenance est douteuse.
Attention, il faut casser jusqu'à 4/6 fois le premier prix annoncé chez certaines boutiques.
Il faut prendre son temps, s'armer de patience et ne pas hésiter à comparer, on peut y trouver des trésors. Dommage que certains vendeurs racontent n'importe quoi sur la provenance des objets.... Demander une facture pour prévenir les soucis à la douane si l'article quitte le pays.

title: Le cpa
text:
Le centre de promotion de l'artisanat est le plus grand centre dédié aux artistes à Cotonou.  Des bijoutiers, des sculpteurs,  des tresseurs de tissus y ont  trouvé leurs places.  Vous pourrez trouver votre objet souvenir dans cet endroit.
On y vend aussi  de  tableaux, des masques, des réalisations sur bois, ...

title: Grand choix de fabrication artisanales
text: Toute l'Afrique est représentée dans ce grand centre artisanale. Il y a des objets vieux et récents. On trouve donc son bonheur.

title: Üblicher Krimskrams
text:
Auf einem riesigen Gelände reihen sich Shop an Shop. Ich habe nicht wirklich etwas Besonderes erblickt, auch fand ich die Verkäufer nervig. Komm hier, Schau da.
Aber es gibt dort eine kleine Bar, wo man der Mittagshitze im Schatten entfliehen kann.
Die Metallwerkstatt war mein Highligt; nicht nur die Produkte, auch weil die Handwerker dort nicht so aufdringlich waren.

title: Bel endroit
text: Pour rencontrer des artisans  et artistes du pays, attention aux prix démesurément multipliés par rapport à ceux pratiqués à l'intérieur du pays

title: sympa
text:
un marché arisanal ou on trouve les mêmes articles dans toutes les boutiques
les vendeurs sont vraiment sympas, même s'il faut marchander

title: Centre de Promotion de l'Artisanat
text: Peu de promotion, tendance plutôt au "harcèlement" du touriste égaré. Beaucoup d'art nigérian (statues en bronze...), des toiles d'Abomey, du travail du bois, des bijoux... Le CPA montre un p;eu tout ce qui se fait au Bénin et un peu dans la sous-région

title: A faire
text: Si vous séjournéz à Cotonou ça vaut le detour.. Ici c'est l'endroit d'acheter vos souvenirs et cadeaux. Pourtant j'avoue que j'étais légèrement déçu par la diversité des stands. Il y a des nombreux points de vente, mais à part 2 ou 3 exceptions c'est les mêmes objets on trouve partout.. Mais à faire, c'est agréable

title: Sympa mais trop de pressiln
text:
J'avais très envie de venir pour en avoir beaucoup entendu parler mais finalement l'oppression des vendeurs dans les premières boutiques à presque failli me faire fuir.
Par contre je conseille de poursuivre sa route et d'aller voir les artisans en plein travail sur métiers à tisser ou sculptant du bois et autre.
C'est vraiment beau et intéressant.
Comme dit dans les commentaires précédents il faut absolument marchander oui car les vendeurs n'hésitent pas à augmenter les prix à la tête du client...

title: great center for crafts--- definitely don't miss
text: This center offers lots of little shops with various artisans selling their (and other) crafts.   Highly recommended.    Remember to negotiate.

title: Beaucoup d'artiste réunis, mais ne vous arrêtez pas aux premiers!
text: Centre subsidié pour le développement des différentes formes locales d'art. Il y a moyen de faire des achats intéressants sur place si vous savez négocier et surtout commencer par les échoppes situées au fond...

title: centre artisanal.
text: très beau centre artisanal reprenant  tout ce qui se fait comme artisanat au Bénin. Ne pas hésiter à très fort marchander car ils essaient de vous vendre leurs objets au prix fort. ne pas hésiter à changer de marchand et à faire jouer la concurrence

title: Great for souvenirzzzzz!
text: Conveniently located in downtown Cotonou. Numerous shops with a great variety of basic and more upscale items to chose from! You should obviously bargain, after which you will take home a nice piece for a more than fair price!

title: Great variety in one location
text: The atmosphere is calm and it is nice that the traders don't jostle you. I was able to get a good variety of goods- from a carved chair to Ankara purses. It was nice to have a one stop shop.

title: Total rip off.
text: Avoid this totally high pressure rip off site, most of the artwork and sculpture is imported from other African countries and the aggressive haggling needed to purchase anything here for a reasonable price. Personal I'd browse through the place and then send a local you trust to negotiate the price for any item you realy want.

title: interesting sight
text: all sorts of arts and craft here to admire and purchase if you feel like it. the pple here, amiable.

title: Nice
text:
Was my visit to the arts and crafts Centre and I have been visiting Abuja for years.
It's a nice place for all kind of arts and crafts. Even the shops are built in a traditional style with lovely traditional wood windows.
Went there to see a Taylor.
It's an open style plan with loads of small shops and African restaurants.
It is a must visit while in Abuja especially to get gifts for friends back home.

title: El mejor lugar para comprar artesanías locales a buen precio
text: Es el lugar apropiado para comprar souvenirs a precio local. Recomiendo sin embargo ir siempre acompañado de un local porque los precios pueden variar para el turista e incluso estar sujeto a timos o engaños. También es importante vigilar sus pertenencias al caminar.

title: Real great atmosphere for bargaining and many items to choose from
text: I visit this quaint place often and I never get tired of the cute bargains. The sellers are very friendly and easy to get along with. I always leave there very happy. I always go with someone who can bargain and banter in Hausa.

title: Nice place to buy African art
text: Nice pieces but a lot of the same stuff. Some of them are a bit pricey though. Definitely get leather, wood or any of the bead work while there. I didn't like the fabrics- ready to wear clothes, they were cheap looking and run when washed.

title: Wgood collection of arts and crafts
text: For anyone who wants to leave Abuja with an armful of Nigerian arts and crafts , this is a good place to be. They have everything, from flower vases to beaded jewelry to big terracotta figures and everything in between you will find it here. However, The prices are specially hung with foreigners in mind so if you want a good bargain, you either visit the place with your Nigerian friends or you haggle nicely.

title: quite an interesting place to visit
text: Your visit to Abuja is not complete without a visit to home of Art, clothes made with Nigeria and African styles, leather etc A one stop place for beautiful artistical souvenirs

title: A great place to get presents
text:
The Abuja Arts & Craft village is always my go to place for presents, I have been there countless times. If you are looking for accessories such as beads (necklaces and bracelets), bangles, bags, paintings, sewn fabrics for male and female, wallets and other things made from leather etc, you will find a good variety of all these. It is also a great place for souvenirs.
One other thing to know is how to negotiate/bargain, that way you'll get a good deal on whatever you buy.

Anyone visiting Abuja should check this place out before leaving.

title: Finto mercato tipico africano
text: Ricostruzione finta e malriuscita di un mercato dell'artigianato tradizionale africano. Sicuramente tappa obbligata in quanto Abuja non ha molto da offrire in termini di attrazioni, ma non aspettatevi nulla di che. Solo un'accozzaglia di souvenirs.

title: Hombre, que te diría yo. ....
text: Después de haber pateado un poco de África, me sigue gustando pasar por este tipo de mercados. Y casi indefectiblemente, acabo un poco decepcionado. Si se viene por primera vez, se disfruta, pero las mercancías son las mismas en todos los puestos, lo que hace pensar en que su origen artesano, no lo es tanto. Incluso se diría que son las mismas que en otros países, y algún producto de la artesanía local, tiene un aroma a Made in China, que tira de espaldas. Hay que verlo, la gente se porta bien, no son pesados , los precios están correctos, o sea, que sí.

title: If you love arts and crafts, visit here!
text: If you are an artist or art lover, don't leave Abuja without visiting this place. Good parking space, tailors and souvenir shops available. Every visit is unique as the art works on display keep changing...

title: Excellent shopping for authentic Nigerian culture artifacts
text: This Arts and Crafts Village is literally its own village. It is large and winding with articles from clothing to leather goods to jewelry (stones unfinished too) to wood work of all kinds. Allow plenty of time, or plan to return. There is little shade, unless you are in one of the craft huts. I was there at the end of dry season; 105 degrees F with no shade was a long afternoon. But the crafts and bargains are well worth any time spent. Know the language or take someone local with you to bargain. If you don't barter, you will be paying inflated prices. The local sellers expect bargaining to be done. Allow yourself a set amount of money before you go; the feeling for me was like gambling! Just one more item, just one more hut to explore! Many of the huts have business cards available. Keep them with any gifts; they are interesting to give along with the gifts you give.

title: Typical place for tourist
text:
What is surprising is that many taxi drivers ignore this place. 
Typical place where tourist can find something to buy.

title: Research
text: Had fun the place is awesome.chek it out this is arts and crafts awsom stuff 😀😀😀👍👍😎everything in side a village.

title: Bons preços e ótimo atendimento
text: Muito bom para compras de artesanato e roupas africanas,um lugar com bom espaço e diferentes peças, todas feitas ali mesmo e com ótima qualidade preços satisfatório.  atendimento excelente.

title: Creativity at it's peak.
text: Lovely arts and professionals, creativity is at its peak here as there are so many creative and professional artists around to display their work.

title: Quaint .........................
text:
This place is nice for walking around and experiencing local culture. The items for sale are wonderful to look at but are also wonderfully overpriced. It's the centre of town and a visitor/tourist hub hence the exorbitant pricing. If you are willing to adventure a little further a field you will find the same items at a fraction of the cost, over 80% cheaper.
If for security reasons you are unable to do so, buyer beware.

title: Average African craft stuff...So sad to see the illegal animal skins!
text: Went wit ha group. Most of the crafts are typical of what I normally see even in Kenya. Some neat art though! The venders don't attack you to make a sale like in some places. Very sad to see the illegal leopard, giraffe, and other animal skins in the back of the village. Very much a touristy type of place.

title: cap vert
text: bien sur,nous savions que cette tour emblematique n etait qu une pale copie de la superbe tour de belem,mais le panorama en haut est tres beau et permet de s orienter dans la ville.

text: This small tower stands out along the seafront, and is in good condition. But it is a reminder of the Island's colonial past, and looks unusual where it is situated. It does however house a small maritime museum, which can be visited for a small fee.

text:
Un petit musée de la peche à la baleine
N'oubliez pas de donner 100 escudos à la dame en entrant

text: Vale muito a pena porque dá uma vista espetacular da cidade, com, inclusive, várias passagens pela poesia e arte local.

text: Cette réplique de la Tour de Belem de Lisbonne offre surtout l'intérêt de voir la ville de haut à partir d'un endroit central et agréable surtout en fin de journée vers 17H. Les plus téméraires monteront l'échelle (est-ce autorisé ?). L'accueil est agréable, et la petite exposition mérite d'y jeter un oeil.

text: Known as Capitania dos Portos, this a replica but smaller version of the Torre de Belem in Lisbon and stands out on the seafront near the Fish Market. Well worth a visit and the top gives good views of the town and harbour.

title: lugar onde mindelo revive a sua identidade
text: replica muito bem concedida ficou muito bem depois do restauro deveria ter mais intereçao e animaçao neste espaco relembrando hestoria que se passou nesta baia

title: Vale a pena...
text: O valor da entrada são 100$00 (1,00 €) por pessoa. Tem vários andares, cada anda tem o seu tema. Pode ir até ao ultimo, a vista é espectacular. Vale a pena...

title: Yachts on one side, barbers and cafes on the other.
text: If this is the road I'm thinking of it is the road that connects the beach tot he market along the water front. It definatley needs to be walked along if you are visiting Mindelo, there luxury yachts on oneside and the post office and tourist information on the other, if you continue your amble you will come across the outdoor market selling tourist souvenirs as well as fish, fruit and some veg. There are cafes along the way that deserve to be looked into especially the ones that don't look so inviting as they will be the best with local food and impromptu guitar playing.

text: Não achei de visita obrigatória, contudo com algum interesse para quem pretende conhecer um bocadinho mais do mundo subaquático no que diz respeito às espécies em São Vicente.

title: LOCAL VIEWPOINT

title: Get a better understanding of Ghana

title: Museum Visit
text:
The National Museum of Ghana, Accra is situated on the Barnes Road and within the precincts of the famous Holy Spirit Cathedral of the Catholic Church, and the Psychiatric Hospital,  Asylum Down-Accra.

This museum is now a shadow of its former glorious self(when one could spend a half-day there);
all the same, the museum has still got some collections in place, especially for those who will like to know more about Ghana's history. It is still an ideal place to visit especially for foreigners who will like to be little more curious about "Ancient Ghana". 

It is a place to visit, again, for those students and researchers of History ;and the Museum been adjacent to the "National Archives" Building, one will have a lot to study, and definitely, for research works.

title: Very interesting in a quaint sort of way
text: If you are looking for the Louvre or the British Museum you will be disappointed. However, this collection of authentic Ghanan history is well with half a day of your time. The guide we had was a young college student and very knowledgeable and rightly proud of her country.

title: Surprisingly informative

title: Make this your first stop
text: Make this your first stop. The museum is not the best in the world, but extremely informative about the history of ghana. There are truly amazing artifacts on display. They are going the best they can with what they have. Really worth spending some time here and take a journey through their rich history. Be prepared to be totally shocked and appalled to see what slavery and the western culture did to these people who lived on total harmony with nature. It's worth the visit.

title: Small but some interesting exhibits
text: This is a small museum that is pretty basic. There is no air conditioning, a very small gift counter, and the layout is rather hap-hazard. It does however contain some interesting exhibits on the history of Ghana (as well as some less interesting ones). The exhibit on slavery is worthwhile in understanding the history of the country. The descriptions attached to the exhibits are pretty basic but do provide the information needed to understand them. The guide we had was very useful.

title: Underappreciated and underutilized
text: I went on a weekday while travelling and had the museum all to myself. Very inexpensive entry, and well worth the quite low cost. Although the museum is not very large, it does present a wide number of interesting artifacts and exhibits. Don't miss the wooden thrones - they are hidden under a stairwell and easy to miss if you aren't looking for them, but they have the thrones/seats of the first President of Ghana as well as the chair of the Governor of the British Gold Coast Colony and the Portuguese Gold Coast. Very interesting and beautifully preserved. Most of the museum offers more of a pan-African history, with masks and artifacts from Egypt and throughout the West Coast countries, but there are uniquely Ghanaian pieces here and there that are worth exploring.

title: Just simply a poor effort!
text: Please dont waste your time. I'm sure there are many better places than this in Ghana. It just seemed like a room full of random collections of things with no real educational or historical emphasis. Go to a mall or just roam the streets and you're likely to have a better time!

title: Significant
text: Great location and space, with actively curated exhibitions. Also, home to the Dak'art Biennale. The garden often has sculptural installations.

title: Wonderful Masks
text: I agree with most of the previous comments...both positive and negative. I was disappointed that we didn't see more West African objects and that the information provided was only in French...including the videos. But the masks were my favorite part and I thought they made the visit worthwhile. But, do know that admission is expensive for the number of objects on display. However, we know that most museums these days do need more money to operate...so the money went to a good cause. There are two floors and stairs, but no elevator. We had the place to ourselves. No photos allowed. The top floor features plastic and we didn't know enough French to decipher exactly what message they were espousing with the displays of plasticware mixed in with ceramics, etc. But we did notice that Senegal has less plastic lying around on the streets than some of the nearby countries.

title: Disappointing
