title: Buona l'idea, ma...
text:
Solo per la grandezza, per il colpo d'occhio e per l'idea meriterebbe sei stelle in luogo delle cinque previste al massimo, ma...se si è curiosi, come sono io, e ci si addentra un po' più nelle cose si scoprono cose che fanno scendere il valore di quella che, ripeto, sarebbe stata davvero un'ottima occasione per magnificare il bisogno di rinascenza dell'Africa. La statua è davvero impressionante (53 m di altezza sono davvero tanti) e il posizionamento su una collina la fa diventare ancor più maestosa. Seconda per altezza alla Statua della Libertà, con i suo oltre 90 m, è considerata la prima completamente visitabile al suo interno (non credo per l'altezza, quanto per l'esistenza di locali "abitabili" adibiti a piccolo museo della statua stessa e di alcuni cimeli della recente storia del Senegal). Ho tuttavia scoperto che è stata costruita da una società...coreana! Ma come, la "rinascenza africana" creata da un altro popolo? Ci sono poi le critiche degli antropologi locali che dicono che la struttura fisica dell'uomo non corrisponde ai parametri fisici africani e le critiche dei religiosi islamici decisamente contrari alla rappresentazione umana in generale e, a maggior ragione, a quella femminile con pochi abiti. Insomma, come ho intitolato questa recensione, una bella idea, ma...  
Il prezzo di ingresso è differenziato a seconda che si voglia visitare il museo e arrivare sino al belvedere (ricavato nella "corona" che gionge il capo dell'uomo), o meno: 10 € per la visita completa (non ho purtroppo preso nota dell'altro prezzo).

title: Vendeurs insupportables!!!
text:
Il y a de tout sur ce marché artisanal, beaucoup d'arnaques mais quelques beaux objets.
Les prix sont nettement supérieurs à ceux pratiqués sur les autres places touristiques du Bénin, mais négociables. 
Par contre la pression des vendeurs est insupportable. On est assailli dès l'arrivée et il est impossible de regarder tranquillement dans les boutiques. Dès qu'on a le malheur de porter de l'intérêt à un objet, on est harcelé par tous les vendeurs qui le proposent.
Résultat : alors que nous étions prêts à négocier plusieurs objets, nous sommes partis sans rien acheter, histoire d'avoir la paix!

title: Zekers langs gaan als je in Cotonou komt.
text: Om geschenkjes te kopen voor het thuis front voor toeristen , mensen zijn wel sympathiek maar er word teveel van het zelfde aangeboden.

title: Good selection
text: I liked the selection and quality of handicrafts. Prices were high and vendors could be annoying. Very pushy.

title: Interesante
text: Una variada exposición de la artesanía de Benin. Los comerciantes suelen ser amables y serviciales, pero atento a comprar "antigüedades", que alguno también intenta colarte.

title: Génial
text: Un lieu à visité à tout prix avec des objets de toute création du savoir faire des artisans du Bénin

title: Vendeurs oppressants
text: C'est un très bon lieu pour acheter des souvenirs (marchandage obligatoire !), on y trouve de tout, mais pas forcément très artisanal ... Par contre à chaque mètre un nouveau vendeur s'approche pour nous faire rentrer dans sa case de façon beaucoup trop insistante, c'est pourquoi je n'y retournerai pas.

title: A ne pas manquer
text: Découverte de la culture et de l'art béninois. Possibilité d'acheter différents objets et cadeaux à faire. Les artisans sculpteurs vous proposent des œuvres magnifiques. Les heures s'arrêtent pour y passer le temps que vous voulez. N'hésitez pas à vous munir d'un boubou pour la visite et même pour séjourner à Cotonou.

title: Neat crafts, most vendors friendly
text: The vendors are all set up in a shaded area, making the shopping pleasant. Most of the vendors were pleasant, although some were a bit aggressive. There is a good selection of wood, bone and stone carvings, purses, cloths, jewellery, etc. Prices were reasonable.

title: poco convincente. troppo turistico
text: troppo turistico. all'interno del Benin si può trovare di meglio sia come oggettistica che come prezzi!Gli oggetti in vendita sono gli stessi di altri mercati. non ho trovato nulla di davvero originale.

title: Pleasant experience & high quality souvenirs
text: This artisanal market has very high quality goods. The prices are higher than the other market I visited in Cotonou but the quality of the products justifies the higher price tag. The environment is really nice and it is an overall very pleasant experience. I highly recommend visiting the artisanal center during your stay in Cotonou.

title: Comprare regali!!!!!
text: trovato ciò che cercato e a un prezzo ragionevole. certo, con i beninesi bisogna sempre trattare, ma ce l'ho fatta.

title: LE centre artisanal de Cotonou
text:
C'est LE lieu de Cotonou où vous devez acheter vos souvenirs. 
Pleins de petites boutiques sont toutes centrées au même endroit. Il ne faut pas hésitez à circuler entre chacune même si vous ne pourrez pas toutes les faire malgré le côté très insistant des vendeurs qui sont tous très gentils. N'hésitez pas non plus à négocier les prix avec eux car eux n'hésite souvent pas à les exagérer.

title: Véritable centre culturel africain
text: Vous y trouverez des articles très variés de l'art africain à des prix très intéressants. Conseil: il faut toujours négocier les prix afin d'éviter d'acheter trop cher ou de vous faire avoir. Eviter les marchands ambulants.

title: qqs beaux objets
text: UN centre artisanal variés avec pas mal de choses et des vendeurs , certes un peu collant mais de façon très raisonnable. il suffit de dire qu on n a pas de sous

title: le centre artisanal de Cotonou
text:
Bonjour à toute et à tous.
Si vus ne me connaissez pas sachez que je suis blogueur et que j'ai visité le bénin. Je me suis rendu au centre artisanal de Cotonou il y a quelques temps et je viens vous annoncés que c'est un lieu qu'il ne faut pas manqué de visiter si vous effectuez un voyage au Bénin.
Sur place, vous aurez des magnifique masques africain, des colliers de tout genre et aussi beaucoup d'autres choses à voire et à rapporter d'u voyage au bénin en guise de cadeau pour la famille.

title: Centre de promotion de l'Artisanat à Cotonou, visite obligatoire
text:
Situé en plein centre-ville, sur le boulevard Saint-Michel, dans un parc ombragé bien agréable de 3 hectares, ce village alternant les huttes de pailles et bâtiments d'exposition vous plaira à coup sûr.
Vous y trouverez des objets allant de la simple breloque, à des magnifiques statues ou sièges en bois, et bien d'autres choses, notamment des bronzes superbes. Je ne pourrais pas tout décrire tant il y en a…
L'accueil est des plus sympathique et non pesant, si vous dîtes n'être pas intéressé, aucune insistance. N'oubliez pas de négocier, c'est la règle, mais si vous proposez trop bas, la négociation s'arrêtera, tout simplement.
Prévoir quand même deux ou trois heures pour avoir un bon aperçu de l'artisanat local, et la bouteille d'eau… BernardO

title: ベナンのお土産探しに便利です
text:
お土産を買いたい人は、ここが便利だとおもいます。しかし、クオリティは、期待しすぎないようにしてください。芸術品というよりも、お土産品が中心です。ですが、ときどき、掘り出し物がありますよ！
個人的に、好きな場所ですが、お店の呼び込みがうるさいので、星３つにしておきました。

title: Leuke prullaria
text: Leuke Afrikaanse markt, waarvan kooplui hun waren aanbieden. Het bekende houtsnijwerk us hier in overvloed aanwezig. Verder zijn er volop schilderijen te koop wat eveneens een leuke herinnering is. Tevens zijn er kleermakers die je een op maat gemaakte Afrikaanse snit kunnen aanmeten.

title: Schöne Andenken!
text: Optimal für alle, die sich ein schönes Andenken an Lagos besorgen wollen. An die Märkte von Abuja gewöhnt, fand ich es total entspannend hier ein bisschen zu shoppen, die anfangspreise sind moderater und man wird als "oyibo" nicht so angegangen.

title: Market mainly for souvenirs
text: Its a popular place for tourist and residents to buy souvenirs in much cheaper prices than some "luxury"shops in the town. Its hot,stinky,dusty,etc.place. Please dress very simple,no jewellery on you (that immediately will shout you are a "fresh fish" and the price will jump to sky), don't show you have money, arrange small notes in different pocket,have hat&water,sunblock on you. If you see your piece,prepare to bargain. Usually 3 times less the price they ask. Remember,bargain is a must. Even if the seller is not agree,don't be disappointed,just walk away and believe me,they'll run after you. Better is to go with somebody who knows the place-friend,driver,local or resident with experience ......Thirsday mornings usually is sanitations(cleaning time)for markets,so will not be open till noon. Saturday is full with expats,if this will make you to fill better. People are friendly,if you smile,but I'll not go there alone for sample.

title: A good shopping centre
text:
It was quite a good place to shop for variety of household items including grocery, fresh fruits, utensils, etc.
I was more happy to see wide options of good pearls, corals. I enjoyed shopping here.

title: Lekki Market for Tourists
text:
You find all kind of artifacts and local stuff ranging from clothes, bangles, souvenirs.

The market is a bit unorganised, but you find everything you are looking for to remind you of the different cultures of the Nigerian people

title: A typical market where you can buy everything - not in a good way
text: If you are looking for a bunch of trashy souvenirs to buy this is the place to go. It's also the place to go if you want to bug random animals that are caged up and tortured. Then again it's a typical market where you have lots of sellers and buyers in an ambiguous location. In all honesty, there are some good items to buy here but I would recommend hiring a local to barter for you and take you around. Overall, good fabrics and local crafts, but some of the sellers just left a bad taste in my mouth.

title: Treasure everywhere
text: Love this place. Full of local talent and wonderful pieces. Haggling met with smiles but be prepared to be approached constantly. Fabrics, furniture and art my favourite things here. No toilets. Can be muddy.

title: INDIGENOUS NIGERIAN ARTS & CRAFTS MARKET
text:
Excellent market for buying all sorts of Nigerian Arts, Crafts, Fabrics, Leatherware, Carvings etc,
Be ready to haggle and negotiate like a pro to get good bargains.
The market also has a section for fresh vegetables and fruits.
Relatively safe but like any market you need to keep your money safe and your bag in front of you

title: Absolutely must visit!
text: One of the top places to visit in Lagos.  Full of character and interesting things to see and buy.  From art and antiques to fruit and veg.  The stall holders are friendly and helpful and are willing to barter the prices.  However, just beware of the flock of young boys who greet you as you arrive who want to be the ones to show you around and take you to the best deals, and who expect to be paid (a small amount) for the privilege.

title: Great for local art
text: Hard to find, down a horrible dirt road, hidden behind local market, is a very large artisan market.  It's not well marked, our local driver had to ask several times for where it was located.  When w did arrive I didn't believe it and walked into the area before it changed to art.  It's worth the trip not only do you get some local color, but the art is quite good and many of the stall are populated by the artist.  I saw some of the reviews complain about the hard sell.  Well we didn't experience any of that and I've gone to most artisan markets in the region of West Africa.  This one was quite laid back in comparison.  there are local young adults when you walk in that will try to attach themselves to you. Either ignore, or as we did pick one and if they know what your looking for will take you to specific stalls.  The place is not small so allow yourself some time, and barter you'll be surprised hoe inexpensive things are.  We got some excellent masks and had a good time interacting with the artisans.  Felt very safe.

title: Un endroit Exceptionnel
text:
Si vous vous recherchez l'ambiance, ne dépassez pas les 1000 premiers metres.
Sivous recherchez la tranquilité franchissez les 1000 premiers metres
Si vous recherchez la liberté et la verdure, osez franchir les 2000 premiers metres.
Si vous n'etes pas encore satisfait continuer votre route lentement,
Là-bas,un peu plus loin vous découvrirez unepetite et belle ville chargée D'histoire.
Là, le dimanche ne vous suffira plus car,
là, les merveilles s'enchainent au point de vous faire esclave.
Bienvenue à Ouidah,où des milliers d'africains ont transiter pour les Amériques.
La plage de Fidjrossè, est comme un entonnoir,
Elle vous accueille à l'étroit et quelques metres plus loin s'ouvre à vous.
Ne manquez pas l'occasion d'un dimanche si vous vous rendez à Cotonou.

title: Gigantesque
text:
Superbe endroit à visiter et profiter des explications des guides. 
Chaque étages est rempli d'histoires à decouvrir. Le 15e étage offre une splendide vue .

title: À faire !
text: C’est un site à ne pas rater quand on est de passage à Dakar. De près c’est encore plus impressionnant que sur les photos et on a une vue imprenable sur la ville. L’entrée est gratuite mais il y’a un musée payant au pied du monument.

title: Impresiona
text: Nuestro hotel se encontraba muy cerca del monumento y aprovechamos para acercarnos. Impresiona tanto de día como de noche,  que está iluminado. Su construcción fue objeto de una fran controversia, tanto por el dinero que costó como por las quejas de la comunidad islámica por la vestimenta poco decorosa que viste la mujer de la escultura. Acceder al museo cuesta 10 euros por persona pero no entramos,  nos pareció excesivo

Great views of the city.

title: INTERESTING
text: I was there with my family and there are lots of interesting African artifacts that i hadn't seen before. Very creative in designs and concepts. Sellers beckon you in with welcoming smiles, explaining the concept and designs from various parts of Nigeria.

title: Güzel bir şehir
text: Şehir merkezinde elektirik, su gibi temel ihtiyaçlar olmasına rağmen arka sokaklarda maalesef insanlar çok fakir. Benzin çok ucuz ama temin etmek zor. Şehir merkezinde alışveriş imkanı var. Özellikle ahşap eşyalar çok popüler. Mutlaka pazarlık yapın. Güvenlik sorunu şehir merkezinde yok. Trafik biraz karışık mutlaka taksi veya yerel şöfor kullanın.

title: Торгуйтесь и еще раз торгуйтесь!!!
text: Небольшой рынок с местными сувенирами разного толка... ничего особенного вы там не найдете (особенно если в Африке уже не первый раз) набор стандартный - безделушки из черного дерева, кожи, национальная одежда... цену на понравившуюся вещь  можно и нужно сбивать до 50%... а то и больше

title: Intéressant
text: On peut trouver beaucoup de choses comme souvenir, des objets de décoration, les trucs utiles...  Il faut toujours discuter les prix!

title: Perfect souvenir shopping spot
text: I enjoyed all of the arts/crafts by local artists... shop to find everything from jewelry and art work, to masks and baskets! I definitely took an extra bag full home. I found it easy to negotiate prices - although I did keep in mind local economy and just how much I was attempting to bargain for (was it worth 1-2$ less? Or worth supporting local artists and craftsmen...?). The answer is easy - enjoy!

title: Souvenirs 😆😆😆
text: The arts and crafts village is centrally located in abuja. It is just behind sheraton hotel wuse. A good place to pick souvenirs especially for foreigners. Inside the compound is a restaurant called madiba. It is highly recommended for their traditional dishes and especially the palm wine. Music is good and the staff is friendly. Overall, if you are a visitor to Nigeria I recommend you visit this place in the daytime  (the A&C village) and at night  (madiba).

title: Beautiful sunny abuja
text: Naira land, this is where you get anything crocodile.there is that real skin looking crocodile which is scary but beautiful.you can get a painting of your choice instantly.prices thou are usually multiplied by 4.if someone says 10000 naira ,just know it's about 2000.in the meantime if you like something insist on your price,should they say it's not possible just walk away knowing you will find it in another chalet if not they will call you back to take your price.shopping in this market requires that you carry your water bottle.the heat is unbearable

title: Lovely Place
text:
In a country where the local tradition, culture and art are ignored for foreign ones, it is really nice to have a place like the Arts and Crafts village, to have a glimpse or an idea of what the tradition is and the popular crafts.
The quality of the craft were really good and for those with any interest in art or just an enthusiast, it should be on that checklist. I really enjoyed my walk in the little village. Its really sad that it is not being promoted as i did notice a few already shut down restaurants. The environment is lovely though.

title: A must visit location in Abuja
text:
the "Abuja arts & crafts village" is an arts and craft market.
the market has a lot of goods to ofer from painting to wooden arts.
if you ever go to Abuja you must go visit. I guarantee to you that you will find your cup of tea.

title: Regular marketplace with different
text: Regular market with usual stuff for sale, just surroundings are more original and tribal. Still nice place to visit

title: It's cool
text: Got to see creative paintings with high quality canvas. Traditional Nigerian clothes and costumes for occasions and photo shoot.

title: AWESOME!!!
text: LOVED this place, absolutely did not want to leave.  Wonderfully talented artisans there that make and sell truly amazing things!  Be prepared to spend all of your money quick.  You'll want to buy everything!

title: Art place in the city centre
text: It's a nice place sandwiched between Sliverbird Entertainment Centre/Mall and Sheraton Hotel. It's a good place to pick art work, traditional cloths, drawings and furniture. You can pick up nice items after shopping or watching a movie at Sliverbird and if you are staying at Sheraton,its just a walk to your hotel. Perfect for people who want to pick souvenirs  for people after a trip to Abuja.

title: Nice African hub
text:
The place is right next to Shoprite and there is also an access from Sheraton Hotel.
The crafts village is actually bigger than we had imagined. It was nice to see plenty African art works, jewellery and wood carvings on display.. It's worthwhile to remember that haggling is part of the Nigerian culture... Don't always pay the asking price...

title: Madiba Restaurant
text: It was a great evening in Madiba restaurant at the art and craft village. If you are a lover of fresh palm wine then visit Madiba restaurant. The African setting is so inviting cos it has the memories of late Madiba in it. They serve good food and drinks in a comfortable environment. If you love fried yams with peppered sours, you'll get it there. Then inside the art and craft village you'll find some beautiful african stuff in the hots with good tailors. Try it.

title: Nice place. Must bargain.
text: There are different arts&crafts to choose from. If you are a tourist you will be given special prices which are about 2x (if not more) higher than what they charge if you are local. Look around there are plenty to choose from and bargain hard! If you know someone local go together.

title: Nice place to find Nigerian Crafts
text: It was a good place to visit and find Nigeria art crafts. Normally they'll charge you more for being a tourist but after barging you could get a good price. I recommend to go with a local so tyou can get better prices!

title: Mercato dell'artigianato "falsamente tipico ma realmente africano"
text: Come specificato anche nel titolo questo mercato, benché offra tutta quella serie di prodotti dell'artigianato tipico di quel grande continuum artistico-culturale dell'Africa occidentale, manca di quel tocco di tipicità presente invece in altri contesti della stessa area geografica. Probabilmente ciò è da imputare alla giovane età della città, che rende il tutto meno "caotico" ma anche meno "tipicamente africano". Merita tuttavia di essere visto, anche perché, tralasciando questo mercato, non è che le attrazioni di Abuja siano poi molte.

title: Interesting place for local arts and crafts
text: The site has a local rural village themed setting.Where you can obtain souvenirs in different forms of arts and craft representing all the tribes in Nigeria. It is a place you'd love to explore every time you remember the experience.

title: Art works
text: Good experience with Nigerian artwork. Lots of art pieces to see. I was impressedwith the diversity of representation of the various tribes in Nigeria. It also offers children the opportunity to develop their art skills.

title: Relics Told Me Ghana's Past
text: Check in is ok with an old counter as old as the independece of Ghana. Some times tour guides are not ready.

title: Excellent but also disturbing
text: This small but excellent museum is a good introduction to Ghana but also the extent of the slave trade.  A must see in Accra.

title: Schön
text:
Der Museum in Ghana ist sehr hübsch und Talentiert da sind so viele Coole Sachen und Kreative Sachen ich frag mich nur wer das gemacht hat??? und wer das Gemacht hat ist ganz,ganz.
,ganz doll Kreative

title: Average for African museums
text: Africans really don't do Museums well.  Sure there are pieces of history that one can glean from a walk through this place, but one does get tired of looking at pieces of pottery.  The most interesting story for me was the engagement of a group of Danish young people with some folks from Ghana discussing their common history around slave trade.  The Danes were not a world power but they did have a fort in Ghana and were an active participant in the slave trade.

title: Nothing very special
text:
Interesting place with some nice pieces but nothing very special.
The area concerning the slaves is very interesting , the rest is ok.

title: Der Anfang ist gemacht ! Weiter so !
text: Es ist schon verwunderlich, dass aus der Historie des Landes so wenige Exponate ausgestellt sind. Wahrscheinlich haben die Kolonialmächte  damals  alles mitgehen lassen  oder es fehlt an der Professionalität  der Direktion. Acu  ist keine Museumsstruktur zu erkennen. Dennoch ! Das Museum wird von vielen Schulklassen besucht und engagierte Lehrer erklären anhand der Ausstellungstücke die Geschichte ihres Landes. Und das ist schon mehr als nichts. Der kritische Museumsbesucher  wird dennoch ausf seine Kosten kommen. Die Geschichte des Sklavenhandels ist umfangreich und nachvollziehbar erklärt. U nd so bleibt zumindest für ihn, den weißen Europäer, dass er neben der Nachdenklichkeit sich auch noch für diese damaligen Verbrechen schämen kann.

title: Worth a visit
text: The building was designed by Maxwell Fry and is very interesting. The exhibits and how they are displayed are uninspiring, though, and the museum would benefit from being run and staffed by people who are interested in the country's history and heritage.

title: My first port of call in Accra
text: Is very interesting place and not far from Niagara hotel where I lodged in Accra. I paid 6cedis and was taken round by one Elizabeth. The museum tells a lot on the history of Ghana,its culture, people and of course the pathetic story of slave trade. Whenever you are in Accra dont miss going to the Musuem it is very interesting.

title: Small, but Interesting
text: Limited explanation of items exhibited and not very well preserved; however, it was interesting to see the different wood carvings, fabrics, photos, and artifacts. 13 Ghanaian cedis to get in. Extra fee for taking photos, which I didn't do so I'm not sure how much it was. Gift shop was small with the usual trinkets.

title: History Lesson
text: We were treated to a trip round the museum by a very knowledgeable guide.   This was a very good history lesson about Ghana.   Gift shop selling good quality gifts.

title: Huge potential but in need of an upgrade
text: I was actually really excited to visit this museum and was blown away by the rich content of it. However, very serious consideration needs to be given to how the information is portrayed and upgrading the now poor facilities. Was sad to see the presidential car rusting under an old car cover in the park lot. I must say that the guides were particularly good though.

title: Rich but scanty!
text: I hardly visit museums but out of boredom I decided to visit the National Museum of Ghana in Accra. I did not regret it. It was quite interesting and one thing I gained from this visit is the fact that Palongo, a dance step which was very popular in the 1960s in Lagos did not originate from Nigeria but Ghana. It was really celebrated in the museum. It also occurred to me that the Azonto dance steps which also originated from Ghana sometimes in the last three years may actually have its origin from Palongo. Nice one. Saw some artifacts and some history of the Asante dynasty and stool. Not a bad visit, but for a National museum, I felt it was a bit scanty, not really much to show.

title: In Serious Need of an Upgrade
text: I know Ghana is a developing country, but this poor, little museum ought to get a serious facelift. It's quite shocking to see a museum in this shape, but what they do have is lovely, in terms of older artifacts. Like many attractions, there is a $10 USD fee to take photos. Save your cidi on that front.

title: Interesting Museum
text:
This museum gives an interesting intro to Ghanian tribal culture, with artifacts, fabric making, dance and music being explained on signboards and with guides available for hire.  (We chose to not hire a guide as we didn't have much time.)  As with some other museums in Ghana, one needs to pay an additional fee for taking photos.  We saw one tourist who chose to not pay, but snapped away with their phone.  The museum staff didn't take kindly to that.

There is a bit of a gallery within the museum where one can view/buy oil and watercolor paintings, batik fabric or clothing and other pieces made by skilled craftspeople.

By western standards, this museum may not rank high, but it does cover some interesting cultural history of the country. Like much of Africa, this museum shows the challenge of a maintenance-lacking mentality.  The grounds have some interesting sculptures, but these are not easily accessed, nor brought to the attention of tourists.  This could be a great museum, but the grounds and exhibits could use some TLC.

title: do it anyway
text: Not much to see but glad we went anyway.  There were photos and some write-ups of leaders and history since 1957 and the country's independence.

title: good to go back time to time
text: a little bit small but still it worth it to visit and learn the culture and history... the souvenir shop is really interesting, you can browse there also :)

title: Dusty and half-forgotten, but interesting
text:
The National Museum building is a typical 60ies "modern" one (opened in 1957), designed by British architects, now in need of a restoration.Ont my visit, I saw a forlorn cattle egret circling around the large, rotund space - but could not figure out how could it sneak in? There were windows open but only partially. Anyway, that was something really unique... The exhibits likewise - it has an "old, forgotten museum" feel, with dusty displays, faded labels, and undecipherable logic. The objects themselves are very interesting, and include some fine textiles, carvings, bronze objects, ceramics and overall deserve better display conditions. I wonder whether the museum has research staff, and if so, what are they doing? 
The little museum shop has some fine objects and rare-to-find books at reasonable prices. Photography has a steep fee - more than the ticket itself (C20, while the ticket for a foreigner is C13)

title: Nice smaller museum with local art for sale
text: This museum had interesting exhibits and also provided a nice break from the heat after going to the nearby Makola Market (although like pretty much everywhere else in Ghana there is no air conditioning!). There was also a section of the museum selling art by local artists for negotiable prices, as well as a gift shop with some nice souvenirs.

title: In need of much improvement
text:
The museum is pretty basic, displays are not chronological and some lack explanation. Also, it would be good if they would offer information in other languages (French, for instance, since they neighbour francophone countries). The objects displayed awake the interest for more information, which is not always available. The upstairs floor was poorly ventilated which made one not want to stay to view the artifacts. The art section has an overwhelming display of one painter. Although Isaac seems to be the current artistic pride of Ghana, a larger array of art styles would be appreciated.

The entrance price was affordable ($3.5) however to take pictures was an outlandish additional $10. Who will pay that? I guess they made such a price to boost sales in their limited gift shop.

title: Well done

title: Оборонительный рубеж

Расположенный на вершине скалы, он был практически недосягаем, зато с него можно было обстреливать как океанское побережье, так и равнину со стороны острова. Недаром именно здесь была основана первая столица на острове.

title: Kapverdische Geschichte live
text: Wer sich für Geschichte interessiert und tatsächlich die Kapverden besucht, kommt an der Cidade Velha und ihren im Unesco Weltkulturerbe verzeichneten Sehenwürdigkeiten nicht vorbei. Die alte Festung mit ihrer wechselvollen Geschichte aus Sklavenhändlern, Freibeutern, Piraten und Kolonialherren könnte kaum wechselvoller sein. Heute beeindruckt sie vorallem durch die alte Zisterne und durch ihre tollen Blicke, zum einen hinein in die Schlucht - von den Kapverdianern auch gerne "ihr" Grand Canyon genannt mit vielen Bäumen, aber auch hinüber auf die Insel Fogo. Für uns war der Blick dorthin umso spektakulärer, war doch der Pico de Fogo zwei Tage zuvor ausgebrochen. Man sah zunächst hinunter die Küste Von Santiago entlang, auf die alte Hauptstadt mit ihrer zerstörten Kathedrale, dann hob sich der Blick und ein fast schon surreales Bild zeichnete sich ab. Die Insel Fogo selbst war kaum zu erkennen, umso besser eine Wolkenschicht etwa auf halber Höhe des Pico de Fogo mit seinen stattlichen fast 4000m und darüber ein rauchender Gipfel. Wir sind bereits viel gereist aber einen rauchenden Vulkan haben wir auf all den Reisen bisher nicht zu Gesicht bekommen. Besonders war dies weil dieser Vulkan auf den wir blickten gerade erst ausgebrochen war. Fast meinte man den Lavaströme sehen zu können, doch das war am hellichten Tag nur eine Einbildung, nachts jedoch soll man diese von Santiago aus sehen. Die Festung selbst ist beschwerlich zu begehen und nicht wirklich etwas für Personen mit Geheinschränkung, wenig ist tatsächlich touristisch erschlossen, am meisten haben und die Kanonen mit der Tudor-Rose des Freibeuters Francis Drake erstaunt, die wir dort sicher nicht erwartet hätten. aber so ist nun einmal Geschichte, durchaus überrraschend. Viel zu sehen gibt es sonst nicht, aber die Ausblicke sind schon bestechend schön.

title: Well intentioned, but neither well presented nor maintained
text:
Our tour group arranged an afternoon visit to Ghana's National Museum, but were rather surprised at the diminutive size and the condition of the country's flagship museum.  As other reviewers have noted non-residents pay a larger entrance fee, and the 20 cedis charge for photographs is absurd in today's world.  The exhibits are old, indifferently translated, and most seriously of all, the artifacts are not stored in climate-controlled exhibits.  Indeed, there is no air-conditioning in the building, and the second level is especially hot.  There are large floor fans, but they are of little help.  Our guide was knowledgeable and helpful, but the other staff looked bored. The washrooms were clean.

The building is not accessible to people with disabilities.  

We spent only one hour in the museum, then left, and did not think that we had missed much else.  

The museum is worth a visit, as there is something to be learned regarding Ghana's history, but it is a pity that the country does not do more to protect and present its historic heritage.

title: Museum
text: Foreigner has to pay 7cedis and Locals 2 cedis for the entrance fee. If you wish to take photos in the museum, you will have to pay another 20cedis. However, the stuff shown in the museum is interesting and worth every minute of my time! However, the place is hard to locate as the signboard at the entrance is pretty small!

A little small compared to other national museums but worth the admission price of less than 4 US dollars.  Items in their gift shop were quite reasonably priced, a pleasant surprise.  Start on the first floor as the second floor exhibits are somewhat limited.

text:

А крепость на краю цивилизации стоит!

Немного разочаровало, что не стали проходить внутрь. Местный гид не советовал, т.к. стоимость входа большая, а разница в видах внутри бастиона и снаружи небольшая.

title: Пушки с острова палят, кораблям пристать велят...
text:
Стариннейшая португальская церковь - форпост гео-политической экспансии и построения мировой империи с 15-го века!

Форт Сан-Фелиппе является одной из основных достопримечательностей столичного острова Сантьяго (в основном, по тем же причинам, что пирамиды остаются в семёрке чудес света - как наиболее сохранившийся артефакт эпохи географических открытий), и потому является одним из пунктов, обязательных к посещению, раз уж Вы добрались до такой дали как Кабо Верде. Под склонами холма расположился "Старый город" - Сидаде Велья - старинная португальская столица, торговавшая рабами. Столица настолько древняя, что средневековый кафедральный собор, знавшие времена расцвета, уже несколько сот лет как разрушен - напоминание о бывших (и промелькнувших) цивилизациях.

Стены форта построены преимущественно из местных вулканических пород, но остов крепости (ключевые угловые обтёсанные камни) построен из европейских камней - по комментарию местного гида, корабли приходили со строительным гранитом в качестве балласта, а уходили в Бразилию (и обратно в Европу) заполненные "чёрным товаром"...

title: Interesting Reconstruction, Great Views
text: This fort was built by the Portugese around 1590 and sits on top of a hill that is above the "old city" and original capital of Cape Verde.  The fort has been reconstructed in many areas more recently to give a good perspective on what the fort would have been like in earlier times but had fallen into disrepair.  The fort was used to protect this area from the numerous pirates that operated in this area during the 16th and 17th centuries.  The fort itself, after the entrance has a very large open area that you cross to walk up steps to the fort's walls and ramparts which give tremendous views of the water and surrounding area.  Outside of the fort is a small cafe where you can get a drink and enjoy some of the other views.

title: Necessario ricordare...
text:
Gorée, solo un nome? Molto di più e non perché dal 1978 sia inserita nel Patrimonio dell'Umanità UNESCO, ma perché l'umanità ricordi quanti uomini, donne, bambini siano partiti da quest'isola incatenati solo per arrivare, i più fortunati, in un altro mondo, in una nuova terra dove l'annientamento del loro essere umani era metodo, dove l'essere umano era assimilato ad un qualsiasi animale da vendere a peso.
Ben 28 pare fossero le Case degli Schiavi su Gorée, poco più che uno scoglio in mezzo al mare di Dakar, ma oggi ne sopravvive solo una. E poco importa se anche gli studiosi locali si interroghino sul reale impiego proprio di questa casa come punto di partenza delle navi negriere che solcavano l'Oceano, o che il Senegal e Gorée non siano stati tra i principali Paesi dell'Africa fornitori di schiavi. E' un dato di fatto che l'infame mercato è passato anche da qui e se anche un solo uomo, una sola donna o, peggio, un solo bambino sono partiti da qui per scomparire nell'immensità dell'Oceano, o della grande terra d'America, meritano il nostro ricordo e un monumento che ben può essere questa "Casa degli Schiavi".
Un altro, mondo, un altro secolo, un'altra guerra, ma forse anche qui il grido di Primo Levi può levarsi spaventosamente aderente: "Voi che vivete sicuri nelle vostre tiepide case, voi che trovate tornando a sera il cibo caldo e visi amici: Considerate se questo è un uomo che lavora nel fango, che non conosce pace, che lotta per mezzo pane, che muore per un sì o per un no...."

title: L histoire

title: 一番の見どころ
text: セネガルで一番の見どころなのではないでしょうか。島にはその他にも色々あります。確かに悲しい歴史ですけど、繰り返さないためには学べきです。実際の場所を訪れることによりより歴史がわかります。

title: Poignant
text:
L’île de Gorée regorge d’une histoire peu reluisante, mais a su garder un sacré charme, et les lieux touristiques sont bien entretenus !

Attentions aux commerçants en haut de la “montagne”, il faut négocier de manière aggressive...

title: A voir, mais...
text:
Il faut le faire, mais honnêtement le site n'est pas très bien conservé...
Le guide (optionnel) en fera des tonnes sur le rôle de Gorée dans le triangle d'or alors que les autres sites ont bien plus contribué à l'esclavage... L'émotion est malgré tout présente et nous avons un devoir de mémoire !

title: Sobrecogedor
text: Sobrecogedor todo lo que se explica y todo lo que significa. Muy buenas las explicaciones del guía. Imprescindible.

title: Incontournable....
text: Lieu historique, où se mêle émotion et tristesse. Néanmoins le devoir de mémoire prend le dessus sur ce lourd passé.... à visiter et à revisiter....

title: Forgive without forgetting
text:
One of the many slave houses that were found on Gorée Island. Well preserved and still undergoing improvements. 
The museum representative is both eloquent and interesting. 
Short 20 minute ferry ride from the port of Dakar. 
A must if visiting Sénégal.

title: Was here in January 13 2018
text: I learned more of the history of west Africa here than I had learned at any point of my entire life. I love that this place has been preserved for education and of course rememberance. We had the best tour guide.

title: Un isola ed un museo pieno di significato da visitare...
text: Si raggiunge facilmente con traghetto ed è  un isola ben sviluppata sotto ogni punto di vista.Il museo merita una visita e successivamente un attenta riflessione...

title: Incroyable et terrible

Mention spéciale à la porte du voyage sans retour

title: Deroutant
text: Et dire que se sont des blancs qui ont fait cette chose immonde, mettre en cage les femmes d un côté, les hommes de l autres les enfants, les handicapés, séparer des familles par bateaux et se faire de l argent sur la misere

title: Moving memorial of human greed and depravity
text: La Maison des Esclaves is a shocking memorial of the horrors of slavery. From Goree Island 8 million slaves were sold over a period of 312 years. This is one of the few slave houses still open to the public - the rest are now occupied by local residents.

title: Passé mais cette fois dans le respect !
text: Surtout ne pas rater, visite à faire, pour le recueillement indispensable en pensant à tous ces gens qui ont souffert et on connu la mort dans des conditions impensables...

title: Très belle expérience et île
text: Une île vraiment magnifique, on coupe de l'agitation de la ville. En prenant un guide, on découvre toutes les histoires de l'île. La maison des Escales est petite mais chargée d'histoire, à faire vraiment !

title: Impressionante
text: Sicuramente è una tappa obbligatoria. Per conoscere, non dimenticare e non ripetere. La storia atroce dello schiavismo è racchiusa nel memoriale degli schiavi. Ma l’isola è anche un luogo pieno di colori, profumi e vita. Merita una visita di mezza giornata con un pranzetto in uno dei locali affacciati sul mare.

title: Retour de mes ancetres
text:
En tant qu'afro descendante je suis déçu de la visite que j'ai pu faire sur ectte ile haute en histoire . Je ne comprends pas que la ville puisse faire payer l'accès à l'ile une fois débarqué et faire de surcroit payer l'entrée de la maison.
Mon expérience dans cet endroit me laisse un gout amer car ils ont réussi malgré ma vigilance a me voler .
J’étais avec des Sénégalais et ils m'ont payer 3 places au prix ou sous touriste . Je m'en suis apercu bien plus tard . Je n'y retournerais pas ou sous d'autres conditions.
Que mes ancêtres reposent en Paix

title: Reif für die Insel
text:
Ich kam nicht als Tagesgast, wie die meisten der internationalen Touristen, sondern hatte mich für drei Wochen bei CHEZ COUMBIS eingemietet. So hatte ich genügend Zeit und Muße, die autofreie Insel mit ihren freundlichen und aufgeschlossenen Bewohnern näher kennenzulernen.

Über die unbedingt zu besuchenden und geschichtsträchtigen Orte wurde hier bereits ausführlich berichtet . Es lohnt sich aber auch ein Bummel abseits der Touristenströme durch die pitoresken Gassen, in denen man immer wieder neue Eindrücke gewinnt. 

Die freundlichen und aufgeschlossenen Insulaner sind immer für ein nettes, kurzes Gespräch zu haben, Anschluss ist schnell gefunden.

Während meines Aufenthaltes konnnte ich den Umzug aus Anlaß des Weltfrauentages, Dreharbeiten zu einem Musikvideo und einen einwöchigen Markt am Platz in der Nähe des Fähranlegers besuchen.

 In einem der zahlreichen netten und preiswerten Restaurants habe ich fast täglich dem Treiben von/zur Fähre zugeschaut. 

Der Urlaub war für mich ENTSCHLEUNIGEN PUR.

title: Une page de l histoire
text:
Une visite agréable dans ce lieu chargé d histoire. On ne peut qu imaginer la souffrance présente pendant plusieurs siècles.  
L île est plus propre que sur le continent

title: Unforgettable experience
text: It is advisable to get a guide to take you around and give you a commentary of the history of the island.  The salve building is a very humbling and emotional experience but well worth the visit.  The rest of the island is beautiful and nice to walk around.  Extend you time so you can have lunch in one of the excellent restaurants near the ferry stop.  The people there are also very friendly and helpful.  A lovely experience.

title: Incontournable

title: entspannter Ort
text:
Endlich ein relativ ruhiger Ort in Dakar.
Bevor man den Hafen betritt muss man den Pass zeigen bzw. irgendein Ausweisdokument. Zuerst muss eine Fee 500cfa entrichtet werden. Die Fähre kostet 5200 cfa (hin- und zurück). Die Überfahrt dauert ca. 30 Min. Auf der Insel gibt es ein paar Restaurants, die vergleichsweise teuer sind. Natürlich wird man wie überall gleich "überallen" und auf ein Souvenirmarkt gezogen. Die Preise sind zum Teil eine Unverschähnmheit (ein Magnet knapp 10 Euro), aber man kann den Preis herunter handeln. Die Insel hat man in 1,5h gesehen. Das Haus der Sklaven konnten wir leider nicht betreten, weil Promis auf der Insel waren.
Ansonsten ist es schön durch die Gassen zu schlendern und mit Blick auf das Meer entspannt etwas zu trinken/zu essen.

title: Feels a world away from Dakar
text:
Very nice little island in Dakar bay. Many colourful houses and baobab trees. Up on the hill people have converted the old war bunkers into houses, which was interesting. The house of slaves is not that interesting to visit, but still of historical significance.
It feels like a world away yet Easily accessible from the Dakar port, although it can get busy queuing up for tickets as ferries are not that regular, so come 30 min in advance.
It’s very tourist with many sellers

title: Île décevante  et délabrée
text: Île déjà visitée  il y a une quinzaine d'années. Hélas,  elle a perdu beaucoup de son charme passé. Dès  l'embarcadère,  le harcèlement par de pseudo guides commence. Certains sont très  agressifs pendant la traversée. Sur place, à  la descente du bateaux  c'est la ruée vers la maison des esclaves. Le personnel à  l'accueil de ce musée,  est très  désagréable notamment la personne chargée  du contrôle des billets. Elle confond manifestement visiteurs et bétail. Le musée est intéressant en tant que mémorial et lieu de mémoire contre l'esclavage  même  si les historiens s'accordent pour considérer que cette maison n'a probablement  jamais servi à cela. Les guides locaux semblent l'ignorer. La visite du reste de l'île  peut se faire rapidement. Avec les années,  les lieux se sont beaucoup délabrés faute d'entretien,  les ordures jonchent les rues. Un peu partout, des vendeurs tentent de vous attirer dans leur boutique. Une visite dont on peut se passer en lui préférant  la beaucoup plus charmante et vivante, île  de N'GOR.

title: A must if visiting Senegal
text:
If you have limited time in Senegal I would suggest a visit to Goree island. We took a tour from Pointe Sarène with Nouvelles Frontiers. The ferry from Dakar which was a short 20min journey. 

I was surprised how pretty and colourful the buildings were, made me feel as those I was back in Europe. 

We visited the main museum, the exhibits were written in French but our guide translated. 

We went to the house of slaves, it was chaotic in there, as they were just ramming people in to the point you couldn’t even move. Very poorly organised. 

The ferry on the way back was badly organised, 30 min wait in the baking sun with no shade. 

The street vendors can be very pushy, one woman grabbed my arm and tried to pull me into her shop.

Overall I enjoyed my visit and would highly recommend, learning about this dark period of history.

title: Superbe visite
text: Incontournable lors d'un voyage au Sénégal. Superbe journée passée sur l'île.de Gorée. Nous avons fait le bon choix en prenant les services d'un guide (8000 fcfa) poir connaître toute l'histoire de cette île. L'esprit de cette île est sifferent de.tous les autres endroits du Sénégal. A faire sans hésiter.

text: The whole Island is a tourist market. For the ferry they charge different prices. The foreigner pays the highest price. Everything is a money issue on the island. My advice: don't go

text: Mooi eiland met onmenselijke wrede verhalen  ,zijn met een privé gids door El Goree gestapt ,om 10 uur de eerste Ferry genomen ,lekker rustig nog ..de verhalen die we hoorden waren wreed ….

title: Survendu !
text:
Cette Ile, souvent placée parmi les « incontournables » de Dakar est très nettement « sur-vendue ».
Certes, le site n’est pas désagréable mais l’omniprésence des « enquiquineuses », rend la visite insupportable.
Certaines de ces vendeuses, aux noms de stars françaises du cinéma, vous mettent une pression excessive qui vire parfois au harcèlement pour ne pas dire à l’agression.
Quand une de ces « vendeuses » vient vous déranger durant votre déjeuner en vous reprochant de ne pas vous être arrêté dans son échoppe, je ne vois pas d’autre mot que « agression » pour qualifier sa démarche.
Dommage, cette attitude vient vous faire oublier le côté évidemment historique du lieu et vous empêche de prendre toute l’ampleur des drames qui se sont joués ici.

title: Interesting and enjoyable visit to Goree
text: We visited primarily for the House of Slaves but didn’t realise there was so much to see on this small island. Well worth a couple of hours of your time to admire everything it had to offer. A great couple of hours on foot exploring all that Goree Island has to offer. It’s colourful houses and vibrant atmosphere hides a dark and brutal past.

title: Goree UNESCO world heratige site 1978 -  Dirty History Behind Goree
text:
Goree an island only 1 mile long by 1/2 mile wide carries with it 400 year of dark history of colonial era crimes & sins comitted agasinst humanity by the portuguese dutch english & the french. Durch & French called the Island "Goree" - meaning "Good harbour" but the name did not match with what went on this tiny island between 16th & 19th centuries when wooden ships sailed from here with humans being chained in their holds across the Atalntic "They called these Cargo-ships". Goree was choosen for its historic location being the closest point in African continent to America & was the cheapest passing through-point for estimated 30 million Africans shipped as "Slave-Cargo". African-Slaves were kept in "Maison des Esclaves" chained on the floor for three months waiting for the arrival of the ship. Its now a pilgramige for Africans. The cells are a chilling reminder of the atrocities of the past & its impossible to stand in a dungeon like this & not imagine the rapes of virgin girls by the traders, the violence, the overcrowding, the deaths & the uncertainty of being shipped across the ocean for lifetime enslavement.
Reading through some of the reviews I get the feeling that some tourists come to Goree for a nice day out, not realizing that this is where "African holocaust" took place. The "African Cultural Genocide" "The distruction of African family structure", the father could be sent to US, wife to Brazil & children to Haiti, the destruction was total. Today this dark history of Goree is being repainted by Sand artists trying to repaint over the Sins of the past, but every grain of Goree's soil still RESONATES the AFRICAN HOLOCAUST of the past that took place here.
I hope one day someone like Sheik Bamba will open the debate on Modern-day accountability for the Colonial era crimes & recognizing the injustices of the past & commemorate this each year like these countries commemorate the victims of 2nd world war each year instead of arguing "All this past should be layed to rest"

title: Our self tour of this 1978 UNESCO site.
text:
We departed the Novotel/ibis complex at 9:15AM by a Yellow Taxi(1500 CFA) for the 1.3km NW to the Dakar Port dropoff. Just 60m away, we purchased our ferry tickets(5,200 CFA each) & paid the city tax(500 CFA each), before waiting in the new Maritime Building with floor fans whirling in front of the wall TV’s. The sitting room was over capacity when the ferry arrived before 10AM. When the passengers departed, the guards opened the doors for us to board through the approach tunnels. After a beautiful calm sail through the active port of container ships, oil tankers and fishing trawlers, we arrived at the island at 10:30AM.  
Having decided on a self tour, we walked up the main street to see the 1830 St Charles Church before visiting the nearby House of Slaves(1500 CFA each). After this crowded and most important site, we strolled a few narrow lanes, crossing squares with large trees and passing the old Governor’s House to the 1856 Fort D'estrees where we toured their 8 section museum(500 CFA each). After using their clean restrooms, we returned to the center dock to wait in the shade for the late noon return ferry and getting back to the Dakar Port at 1PM.

title: Une tres belle ile
text: Une tres belle petite ile calme et tres colorees .appart lhorreur du commerce de l'esclave et certaines maison en ruine que letat du senegal doit aider a la restauration.la maison des esclaves lieu de martyrs .a faire
